B0 is a prespecified interpretable discrete-time cause-specific competing-risk model with one-year intervals through five years and covariates age at diagnosis, assessment-to-diagnosis timing, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, Charlson count and CRC subsite. B1 adds reserve components and missingness indicators. Both use exactly the same eligible participant set and split. Unknown cause remains a separate outcome in the primary model.

The substantive learned alternative is a CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazard model using the same one-year person-period rows, same outcomes and same B0/B1 inputs, with nonlinear reserve thresholds, reserve-by-timing interactions and missingness patterns. It is chosen to test whether clinically meaningful thresholds or component combinations are erased by the transparent scalar model, not to chase a small predictive gain. Fit only after B0 is frozen, with a fixed small hyperparameter grid selected on validation data.

The timing falsification repeats the prespecified analysis in 0-<2, 2-<5 and >=5 years from assessment, retaining >=2 years as primary. A signal confined to 0-<2 years or disappearing at >=5 years is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult disease/timing, not confirmation.

Compare CRC-specific, other-cancer, non-cancer and unknown-cause patterns. A non-cancer increment that persists beyond two years, is not reproduced for CRC death, and is stable under cause sensitivities is supportive of prognostic specificity. A similar or larger CRC-death signal is adverse to the proposed separation and is compatible with stage/tumour burden; it does not prove a mechanism.

Compare all incident cases with reserve-complete cases on age, sex, lag, BMI, smoking, centre/available demographic fields, comorbidity and diagnosis year; model reserve availability and use inverse-probability weighting as a sensitivity. Report missingness by lag and outcome. Material disagreement between complete-case, imputed and weighted analyses makes the result selection-sensitive. Fit the external-cause V01-Y89 negative-control endpoint with the same exposure and timing rules. A strong matching external-cause association suggests general frailty, volunteer selection or coding artefact and is adverse to cancer-specific interpretation.

Report paired-record discordance, duplicate eids, impossible orderings, tied dates, unknown causes and counts by source. Repeat with 41270/41280 inpatient diagnosis records where feasible. Compare the competing-risk analysis with naive censoring of competing deaths. Use fixed exposure permutation and outcome permutation negative probes only after the primary analysis is locked; retained signal indicates leakage.

Supportive results require a non-cancer reserve association and calibrated held-out improvement over B0 in the >=2-year primary cohort, compatible uncertainty, persistence in >=5 years, no material selection instability, and no matching external-cause or CRC-specific signal. This supports a prognostic regularity and motivates external validation or prospective reserve measurement; it does not establish treatment tolerance, causality or mechanism.

Adverse results are no incremental information, reversal of the differential contrast, CRC-dominant association, timing-only association, strong external-cause association, or coding/order instability. Report the relevant rival explanation and do not claim durable host reserve.

Inconclusive results are sparse events, an undocumented tau_source, wide intervals crossing clinically relevant effects, severe missingness, cause instability, failed calibration or unavailable B0+D. Do not call an imprecise null a refutation; defer to longer verified follow-up, registry linkage, expert cause adjudication or an independent cohort.

## Clinical advance and limits

If supportive, the study would define a clinically useful prognostic boundary: whether low-cost prediagnostic reserve adds information about competing non-cancer mortality after CRC diagnosis beyond routine variables and timing. This could motivate prospective geriatric/nutritional assessment and a treatment-planning study. It cannot justify withholding therapy, infer toxicity or dose tolerance, establish a biological pathway, or generalize beyond UKB. TNM stage, grade, treatment, toxicity, performance status, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation require linkage, expert review or another study.

## Exactly three inspected works

The inherited evidence set is reused unchanged; no fourth work is introduced. All three are abstract-only inspected in the parent branch, and no full text is claimed here.

[K1] Zhou H, Li W, Liu S, Zhang H, Huang Y, Hu Y, Hu Y. “Pre-frailty and frailty as predictors of mortality among colorectal cancer survivors: Evidence from the National Health Interview Survey (1997-2018).” Medicine (Baltimore), 2026. PMID 41686585. It supports frailty/mortality association but is survivor-selected and not a prediagnostic competing-risk test.

[K2] Zhao D, He F, Liu H, Qing X. “Impact of preoperative handgrip strength and frailty on early postoperative loss of independence in patients with colorectal cancer.” Frontiers in Oncology, 2026. PMID 42459304. It supports handgrip/frailty as a perioperative vulnerability marker but not long-term mortality or causal tolerance.

[K3] García-Aranda M et al. “Ten-Year Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer-Competing Risks and Patient Vulnerability: A Prospective Multicenter Observational Study.” Journal of Clinical Medicine, 2026;15:4389. PMID 42279250. It supports competing-risk separation of CRC and other mortality but does not establish a prediagnostic reserve effect or remove stage/treatment confounding.

The unchanged parent key-references.json and the three attached UTF-8 evidence snapshots are to be reused as supporting files. Their receipts and hashes must remain unchanged; this repair changes only the scientific data binding and outcome-boundary instructions.

This is a delivery repair only: the scientific question, incident C18-C20 cohort, >=2-year primary lag, outcome/follow-up readiness gate, competing-risk outcomes, baseline-versus-CPU-boosted alternative, falsification criteria and stated limitations are unchanged.

## Question, supported claim and falsifiable hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports an association between frailty/handgrip-related reserve and mortality or perioperative vulnerability in colorectal-cancer patients [K1, K2], and supports separating CRC-specific from non-CRC mortality with competing-risk methods [K3]. It does not establish that a prediagnostic, objectively measured reserve profile distinguishes durable host vulnerability from occult cancer decline.

Hypothesis: among incident C18-C20 cases, lower measured reserve at least two years before diagnosis is associated with greater five-year cumulative incidence of non-cancer death than CRC-specific death after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar time, comorbidity and CRC subsite; adding reserve improves locked-test non-cancer risk prediction over the same routine-data baseline. This is a prognostic/descriptive association hypothesis, not a causal treatment-tolerance, stage, recurrence or mechanism claim.

The leading rival is timing/selection: measurements close to diagnosis may capture occult cancer/cachexia, and UKB volunteer selection or missingness may create the signal. Lag strata, cause-specific comparisons, missingness/selection analyses and an external-cause negative-control endpoint can bound those rivals but cannot establish mechanism.

## Population, time and outcomes

Recruitment assessment date is `53-0.0`, restricted to 2006-01-01 through 2010-12-31. Exclude any valid paired C00-C97 cancer record on or before assessment. ## Exposure, estimand and missing evidence

Primary reserve uses maximum available instance-0 left/right grip, side-missing indicators, albumin, creatinine and cystatin C. Standardize grip, log albumin, negative-log creatinine and negative-log cystatin C within training data. Average available standardized components only under the prespecified minimum availability rule; report complete-four-component and training-fold imputation plus missingness-indicator analyses. Higher score means measured reserve, not validated biological reserve.

Covariates are age at diagnosis from `21022-0.0` plus assessment-to-diagnosis interval under a documented age convention, `31-0.0`, BMI `21001-0.0`, smoking `20116-0.0`, diagnosis calendar year, CRC subsite and dated pre-`t0` Charlson count from `41270-*`/`41280-*`, excluding the incident CRC. All transforms, code maps, imputation and fitting parameters are learned inside training folds.

The estimand is the five-year cumulative-incidence contrast and locked-test prediction error for non-cancer death between baseline and reserve-augmented models, with CRC-specific, other-cancer and unknown death competing. Report non-cancer-versus-CRC contrast; cause-specific and Fine-Gray outputs are descriptive associations, not causal effects.

Townsend deprivation is unavailable in the verified four-source binding: no verified `189-0.0` deprivation column is present, and diagnosis-array occurrences of 189 are not deprivation. No ethnicity, centre, education or BMI surrogate may be renamed deprivation. B0+D is readiness-gated and requires a separately admitted source column, namespace, path and hash. Results without it cannot support the stronger “incremental to deprivation” claim. Stage, grade, treatment, toxicity, performance status, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation are also unavailable or require additional linkage/expert review.

## Models, split and deliverable

B0 is an interpretable one-year discrete-time cause-specific competing-risk model through five years using age at diagnosis, timing, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, Charlson count and subsite. B1 adds reserve components and missingness indicators. Unknown cause remains separate. Both use the same eligible participants and split.

The substantive alternative is a CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazard model on the same one-year person-period rows, outcomes and B0/B1 inputs, with nonlinear reserve thresholds, reserve-by-timing interactions and missingness patterns. It is included to reveal clinically meaningful thresholds/component combinations lost by a scalar transparent score, not to chase a small predictive gain. Freeze B0 first; use a small fixed grid selected on validation data. A temporal sequence model remains deferred because no validated dated longitudinal reserve or treatment/stage sequence is bound.

Use a fixed participant-level 70/15/15 train/validation/locked-test split, seed 36, stratified by event type and diagnosis year after deterministic eid hashing. Never split person-period rows. Test is read once after locking. Report cause-specific CIF calibration, calibration-in-the-large/slope, horizon and integrated IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, paired participant-bootstrap uncertainty for B0 versus B1 and B0 versus boosted B1 at 1/3/5 years, one-SD lower-reserve associations, non-cancer-minus-CRC log-effect contrast, CIFs, event counts and learned feature-effect table.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted output: (1) cohort flow and one-row-per-participant analysis table with b, t0, lag, components, covariates, tau_source, follow-up and exclusion/event reason; (2) fitted model objects plus coefficients/feature effects; (3) locked-test predictions, CIFs, calibration, Brier/AUC and bootstrap intervals; and (4) falsification/interpretation report. Completion requires output-linked conclusions and uncertainty. This branch contains no fitted results. The discovery estimate remains 4-8 CPUs, 16-32 GiB RAM and under two hours after projection with 500 bootstrap resamples (unmeasured); future solver envelope remains up to 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds. GPU is not required.

## Falsification and interpretation

Repeat the analysis in 0-<2, 2-<5 and >=5 years. A signal confined to 0-<2 or absent at >=5 is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult disease/timing.

Compare CRC-specific, other-cancer, non-cancer and unknown-cause patterns. Support requires a persistent >=2-year non-cancer association not reproduced for CRC death, stable under cause sensitivities, calibrated held-out improvement over B0, compatible uncertainty, persistence at >=5, no material selection instability and no matching external-cause signal. This establishes at most a prognostic regularity and motivates external validation/prospective measurement; it does not establish mechanism, causality, treatment tolerance or a treatment decision.

Adverse results include no incremental information, reversal of the differential contrast, CRC-dominant signal, timing-only signal, matching external-cause association, coding/order instability or materially divergent complete-case/imputed/weighted results. Report the corresponding rival explanation.

Inconclusive results include undocumented `tau_source`, sparse events, wide clinically important intervals, severe missingness, cause instability, failed calibration or unavailable B0+D. Do not treat an imprecise null as refutation; defer to verified longer follow-up, registry linkage, expert cause adjudication or an independent cohort. Also report duplicate eids, paired-record discordance, impossible orderings, ties, unknown causes and counts by source; repeat inpatient diagnosis parsing where feasible, compare with naive censoring, and run locked fixed exposure/outcome permutation probes for leakage.

# Episode 6 evolution — UKB-36 follow-up/outcome audit child

Status: proposed, not fitted. Parent: `candidate-d2fb106edf9bb248bb63775b`. This is a substantive execution child, not a change in the scientific population or endpoint: it preserves the incident C18–C20 prediagnostic reserve-versus-CRC/non-CRC competing-risk question while making the readiness gate, paired outcomes, selection falsification and baseline/learned comparison deterministic.

## 1. Scientific opening, supported claim, and unresolved hypothesis

The inspected literature supports three bounded points. Frailty is associated with mortality among colorectal-cancer survivors [K1]; low preoperative handgrip/frailty is associated with postoperative complications and loss of independence [K2]; and CRC-specific and non-CRC mortality have distinguishable competing-risk patterns, with tumor stage/residual disease and patient vulnerability pointing in different directions [K3]. None of these abstracts tests whether an objectively measured reserve profile *before diagnosis* is associated with a durable non-cancer mortality pattern rather than merely recording occult cancer decline, age/comorbidity, or selection.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> Among UKB participants assessed in 2006–2010 who are free of valid paired C00–C97 cancer records at assessment and later develop incident C18–C20 cancer, lower assessment-time measured reserve, with diagnosis at least 730 days later, is associated with a larger five-year cumulative-incidence increase in non-cancer death than in CRC-specific death after prespecified age, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar-time, comorbidity and subsite adjustment.

This is a prognostic/descriptive association hypothesis. It is not a claim that low reserve causes death, identifies treatment intolerance, reflects a validated frailty construct, or explains a biological mechanism. A positive result would be a clinically relevant boundary test: it would justify external validation and prospective prediagnostic reserve measurement, not a treatment rule.

The leading rival is occult-cancer timing: near-diagnosis loss of reserve may be an early manifestation of cancer, cachexia or intensified observation. Other rivals are age/comorbidity confounding, volunteer/inclusion selection, exposure missingness, diagnosis/cause coding, and CRC stage/treatment. [K3] makes the last rival consequential, but the bound UKB data cannot adjudicate it.

### Deterministic follow-up readiness gate

Before any cohort fitting:

1. Verify each exact path, source ID, catalog table ID, SHA-256, namespace, key uniqueness, and required column list.
2. Inspect the frozen source README, catalog metadata and the relevant outcome-source documentation for an explicitly stated outcome-ascertainment cutoff `tau_source`, including its calendar date and provenance. A file mtime, campaign date, current date, observed maximum event date, or undocumented interpretation of `20191-0.0` is not `tau_source`.
3. If no such documented cutoff exists, emit a readiness failure with the missing evidence and stop before fitting. Do not report a null, a cohort result or a five-year estimate.
4. If a cutoff is documented, apply the same cutoff to all death/cancer ascertainment fields. For each case, require `t0 + DateOffset(years=h) <= tau_source` for h=1, 3 and 5; use an explicit leap-day rule and report the rule. The five-year primary analysis uses only cases satisfying h=5.
5. Report the observed maxima separately as an audit: in this snapshot, death dates observed in `40000-0.0/1.0` reach 2022-12-19 and cancer dates in `40005-*.0` reach 2022-06-01. These maxima do not establish completeness.

## 3. Population, paired outcomes and estimand

Set `b_i = 53-0.0` and retain assessment dates from 2006-01-01 through 2010-12-31. A cancer record is valid only if the same slot has a parseable `40005-k.0` date and a trimmed uppercase ICD-10 `40006-k.0` code. Report malformed, unpaired and discordant slots; never repair them by borrowing a neighboring slot. Exclude participants with any valid paired C00–C97 record on or before `b_i`.

For incident CRC, select the earliest valid post-`b_i` C18, C19 or C20 date as `t0_i`. Retain all tied earliest slots and use the lowest slot, then lexicographically smallest normalized code, only for deterministic subsite labeling. A source audit using this rule found 6,094 assessment-window participants with a valid paired cancer on/before assessment, 2,219 post-assessment CRC cases with no such prior cancer, and 329/493/1,397 of those cases in the 0–<2, 2–<5 and >=5-year diagnosis-lag strata. These are screening counts before reserve completeness and documented follow-up gating, not fitted estimates.

Primary eligibility is diagnosis lag `t0_i-b_i >= 730` days, valid reserve exposure under the prespecified missingness rule, and documented five-year follow-up support. The primary timing window is 2–<5 years plus >=5 years; the 0–<2-year stratum is an adverse reverse-causation check, and >=5 years is a prespecified durable-timing sensitivity, not a replacement for the primary.

Death must use the paired slot `40000-j.0` date and `40001-j.0` underlying cause. Parse valid dates, retain only deaths after `t0_i`, choose the earliest date, and on a date tie prefer a usable ICD-10 cause then the lowest slot while recording all tied slots. Unknown means missing, malformed or non-ICD-10 cause. Classify first death as: CRC-specific C18/C19/C20; other cancer C00–C97 excluding C18–C20; non-cancer outside C00–C97; or unknown. Unknown is a separate competing event in the primary analysis. Sensitivities classify unknown as non-cancer and censor at unknown death. V01–Y89 external-cause death is a separately reported endpoint-specific negative control, not automatically folded into target non-cancer death. Death on/before `t0_i` is an impossible ordering: exclude it from primary and report it.

The primary estimand is the adjusted five-year cumulative-incidence differential:
`Delta5 = [CIF_nonCRC(R=Q25) - CIF_nonCRC(R=Q75)] - [CIF_CRC(R=Q25) - CIF_CRC(R=Q75)]`,
with other-cancer and unknown death competing, Q25/Q75 fixed from training data, and standardization over the locked eligible population. Report the one-, three- and five-year CIFs, `Delta5`, and the difference between cause-specific reserve log-effects; use 95% participant-bootstrap intervals. A positive `Delta5` supports the stated differential association. These are standardized prognostic associations, not causal effects. Fine–Gray and cause-specific estimates are descriptive sensitivity parameterizations, not interchangeable causal estimands.

## 4. Exposure and covariates

Set `grip_max = max(46-0.0, 47-0.0)`, using one side if the other is absent and missing if both are absent. The four primary reserve components are grip_max, albumin `30600-0.0`, creatinine `30700-0.0` and cystatin C `30720-0.0`. Fit transformations and scaling within training data only: sex-stratified standardization of grip, log(albumin), negative-log creatinine and negative-log cystatin C. Primary R is the mean of available standardized components when at least three of four are present; record component count and every missingness indicator. Complete-four, grip-only, laboratory-only, and training-median-plus-indicators versions are mandatory sensitivities. Call R “measured reserve,” never validated biological reserve.

Adjustment uses age at diagnosis derived from `21022-0.0` plus exact assessment-to-diagnosis interval under a documented convention, sex `31-0.0`, BMI `21001-0.0`, smoking `20116-0.0`, diagnosis calendar year, CRC subsite, and a dated pre-`t0` Charlson count from `41270-*`/`41280-*`, excluding the incident CRC. No post-diagnosis variable is allowed. Townsend deprivation, ethnicity, centre, stage, grade, TNM, treatment, toxicity, performance status, recurrence, histology, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation are not in the verified binding. In particular, do not relabel diagnosis-array occurrences of 189 as deprivation.

## 5. Baseline versus learned alternative

Both models use the identical participant split, outcome construction, covariates, reserve components, missingness indicators and diagnosis anchor. The comparison tests whether reserve is adequately represented as an approximately linear scalar or instead has stable thresholds/component combinations; it is not a leaderboard exercise.

- **B0/B1 interpretable baseline:** one-year discrete-time cause-specific complementary-log-log hazards for CRC, non-cancer, other-cancer and unknown death through five years. B0 contains age using prespecified restricted cubic-spline knots, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, Charlson count, subsite and interval. B1 adds one linear one-SD R term and its pre-specified missingness indicators. Convert hazards to CIFs by the competing-risk recursion. Freeze B0/B1 before inspecting test predictions.
- **B2 learned alternative:** CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazard model over the same person-period rows and four outcome states, with the same B1 inputs plus the four reserve components, interval and prespecified reserve-by-diagnosis-lag interactions. Use a small fixed grid (200/400 trees, depth 2/3, learning rate 0.03/0.05) chosen on validation integrated Brier score only. Report endpoint-specific permutation importance and held-out accumulated-local-effect curves; do not treat them as mechanisms.

Use a fixed participant-level 70/15/15 train/validation/locked-test split, seed 36, assigned by deterministic eid hashing and stratified only after participant assignment by event type and diagnosis year. No person-period rows may cross splits. Fit scaling, imputation, tuning and Q25/Q75 on training/validation only; read the locked test once.

Report cause-specific CIF calibration intercept/slope, one/three/five-year and integrated IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, one-SD reserve effects, `Delta5`, event counts, model coefficients, learned effect tables and paired participant-bootstrap uncertainty with at least 500 resamples. Treat an absolute locked-test integrated-Brier improvement of 0.01 with an interval above zero as a pre-specified practically meaningful predictive improvement, but do not require B2 improvement to support a descriptive association if B1 is stable. A predictive improvement without a stable reserve endpoint contrast is only a prediction result.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted and output-linked: (1) cohort-flow and one-row-per-participant table with `b_i`, `t0_i`, lag, paired-record audit, reserve components, missingness, covariates, `tau_source`, support and exclusion reason; (2) fitted B0/B1/B2 objects and effect tables; (3) locked-test CIF, calibration, Brier/AUC and bootstrap outputs; and (4) a falsification report labeling the evidence supportive, adverse or inconclusive. No fitted result is asserted in this child.

## 6. Falsification and interpretation

Run each check once under a frozen specification and retain all adverse results.

1. **Occult timing:** repeat 0–<2, 2–<5 and >=5-year lag strata. A signal confined to 0–<2, or absent at >=5, is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult disease/observation timing.
2. **Age/comorbidity:** compare the prespecified flexible-age/Charlson model with age-only, age-plus-comorbidity, and age-band analyses (40–59, 60–69, >=70 where supported). Large attenuation or a reserve-by-age reversal indicates confounding or effect heterogeneity, not a host-reserve mechanism.
3. **Missingness/selection:** compare complete-four, min-three, imputed-indicator, grip-only and laboratory-only R. Model availability of complete R from assessment age, sex, BMI and smoking among all assessment-window participants; apply stabilized inverse-probability-of-observation weights only as a sensitivity and report overlap/extreme weights. Compare included incident cases with assessment-window participants and report missingness by event/lag. This tests measured availability selection; it cannot remove UKB volunteer selection or MNAR bias.
4. **Coding:** report every unpaired/malformed cancer or death slot, tie, unknown cause and impossible ordering. Compare paired `40005/40006` diagnosis anchoring with the earliest concordant pre-`t0` C18–C20 `41270/41280` occurrence where date/code are both usable. Material instability is adverse to the coding interpretation.
5. **Competing-risk and cause:** compare CRC, non-cancer, other-cancer, unknown and external-cause patterns; compare diagnosis-anchored competing-risk CIFs with naive censoring of competing deaths. A matching external-cause signal or CRC-dominant pattern weakens the proposed differential reserve interpretation.
6. **Leakage/permutation:** shuffle R within sex once, permute outcomes once with fixed seed, and run fixed exposure/outcome permutation probes. Retained held-out signal indicates leakage or coding contamination and invalidates the corresponding result.
7. **Stage/treatment boundary:** do not proxy stage or treatment with death cause, diagnosis lag, comorbidity or reserve. If the result is CRC-specific, disappears after timing checks, or differs by subsite, label stage/treatment as unresolved and do not reinterpret it as biology.

**Supportive:** readiness passes; in the >=2-year primary cohort lower R yields positive `Delta5` with an interval excluding zero; direction is compatible in >=5 years; the contrast is not reproduced for CRC death; cause, coding, missingness-weighted and complete/imputed analyses are materially consistent; and no matching external-cause signal or permutation leakage appears. **Adverse:** `Delta5` is zero/reversed, CRC death is at least as strongly associated, the effect is timing-only, it is driven by missingness or one assay, it tracks age/comorbidity, is unstable under paired coding/unknown-cause rules, or matches external-cause/permutation signals. **Inconclusive:** readiness fails; deaths/events are sparse; clinically important intervals are wide; causes or coding are unstable; test calibration fails; or weighted analyses lack overlap. Do not call this a null. Continuing requires documented linkage completeness, expert outcome review, stage/treatment linkage or an independent cohort.

Computationally checkable claims are source binding, paired parsing, cohort flow, lag counts, model outputs, calibration, uncertainty and interpretation-to-output consistency. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for histologic confirmation, cause-of-death validity, stage, treatment, recurrence, treatment tolerance, mechanism, causality and generalizability outside UKB.

# UKB-36 prediagnostic reserve and competing mortality

## Scientific objective

Status: proposed, not fitted. This is an open research task, not a reproduction of the demonstration papers.

The inspected evidence supports: post-diagnosis frailty is associated with mortality [K1]; preoperative handgrip/frailty is associated with postoperative vulnerability [K2]; and CRC-specific and non-CRC mortality have distinguishable competing-risk patterns, with tumor-related and patient-vulnerability predictors differing [K3]. Those findings do not establish that an objectively measured reserve profile *before CRC diagnosis* identifies durable non-cancer vulnerability rather than occult cancer decline, age/comorbidity, selection, or coding/observation artifacts.

Hypothesis: among people with incident C18-C20 colorectal cancer, lower measured reserve at least two years before diagnosis is associated with a larger five-year cumulative incidence of non-CRC death than of CRC-specific death, after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, smoking, diagnosis year, subsite and prediagnostic comorbidity. The primary target is the adjusted differential:
`Delta5 = [CIF_nonCRC(R=Q25)-CIF_nonCRC(R=Q75)] - [CIF_CRC(R=Q25)-CIF_CRC(R=Q75)]`.
A positive Delta5 is the prespecified direction. This is a prognostic association, not a causal effect, treatment-tolerance claim, stage claim, recurrence claim or mechanism.

The strongest claim this experiment can support is a reproducible, internally validated association/predictive regularity in this UKB snapshot. It cannot establish histology, cause-of-death validity, cancer stage, treatment, toxicity, recurrence, mechanism, causality, external validity or a clinical treatment rule. [K3] makes missing stage and treatment a consequential rival explanation; do not proxy either with diagnosis lag, reserve, comorbidity or cause of death.

## Data bindings and read-only joins

Use only the five exact read-only Parquet bindings in `bindings.json`. All joins are inner/left joins on `eid` within the `ukb672073` identifier namespace. Do not use managed aliases, the `ukb671626` namespace, Olink/dta data, raw CSVs, or an inferred crosswalk.

No post-diagnosis variable is allowed. Townsend deprivation, ethnicity, centre, stage, grade, TNM, treatment, toxicity, performance status, recurrence, histology, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation are unavailable in the verified binding.

Report adjusted 1-, 3- and 5-year CIFs, Delta5, the difference between cause-specific reserve log-effects, event counts and 95% participant-bootstrap intervals (>=500 resamples). Q25/Q75 must be fixed from training data. Fine-Gray and cause-specific analyses are descriptive sensitivities, not interchangeable causal estimands.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

Use one fixed participant-level 70/15/15 split, seed 36, assigned by deterministic `eid` hashing and stratified only after assignment by event type and diagnosis year. No person-period rows may cross splits. Fit scaling, imputation, tuning and Q25/Q75 only on train/validation; read locked test once.

B0 includes prespecified restricted-cubic-spline age, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, Charlson count, subsite and interval. B1 adds one linear one-SD R term and prespecified missingness indicators; recurse hazards to CIFs.

B2 learned alternative: CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazards over the same person-period rows and four states, same B1 inputs plus four reserve components, interval and reserve-by-diagnosis-lag interactions. Fixed grid 200/400 trees, depth 2/3, learning rate .03/.05 selected only by validation integrated Brier score. Report endpoint-specific permutation importance and held-out accumulated-local-effect curves as descriptive patterns, not mechanisms.

Compare calibration intercept/slope, one/three/five-year and integrated IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, reserve effects, Delta5 and uncertainty. An absolute locked-test integrated-Brier improvement of .01 with interval above zero is practically meaningful for prediction, but B2 improvement is not required for a stable descriptive association. Predictive gain without stable reserve endpoint contrast is prediction only.

Run each once under the frozen specification and retain adverse results:

1. Timing: a signal only at 0-<2 or absent at >=5 is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult disease/observation timing.
2. Age/comorbidity: compare flexible age/Charlson, age-only, age-plus-comorbidity and age bands 40-59, 60-69, >=70 where supported. Attenuation or reversal indicates confounding/heterogeneity, not mechanism.

# UKB-03 repaired proposal: MRI thigh fat infiltration and same-visit functional limitation

Status: delivery-ready hypothesis and Harbor experiment specification; not fitted. This is a repaired child of expert seed candidate-b8b73c60f7e389c61d45a2f7. It does not inherit the prior UKB-36 outcome question or use any non-Assessment_Center outcome linkage.

## 1. Scientific opening and actual deliverable

The clinically unresolved boundary is whether MRI-derived thigh muscle fat infiltration measures lower-limb muscle quality that is functionally informative beyond muscle quantity and hand-grip strength, or whether it is simply another correlate of age, body size, low grip and existing disability. This matters because a clinician deciding whether a patient with apparently preserved muscle mass needs additional functional assessment needs evidence that composition adds information rather than another measurement of the same reserve construct.

The strongest inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. A UK Biobank study reports that higher MRI-measured thigh muscle fat infiltration (TMFI) is associated with mortality and system-specific disease, but its abstract does not establish functional validity beyond quantity or grip [K1]. A review of imaging studies links myosteatosis with gait, balance, strength and physical function, while emphasizing depot definitions, cross-sectional confounding and the need for standardized imaging [K2]. The EWGSOP2 consensus treats strength as central, muscle quantity/quality as confirmatory, and poor physical performance as severe disease, motivating joint measurement but not proving incremental value for this specific MRI field [K3].

The unresolved claim is therefore:

> At the same Assessment_Center visit, among UKB participants with complete instance-2 MRI thigh measurements, posterior-thigh muscle fat infiltration has a positive, clinically material adjusted association with slow usual walking pace after muscle quantity, grip strength, age, BMI and body-fat percentage are accounted for; a concordant but secondary association is expected for any fall in the prior year.

This is a cross-sectional, descriptive/prognostic information claim about current or recalled functional limitation. It is not a causal effect, a diagnosis of sarcopenia, a claim about future falls, a treatment rule, or a mechanism.

Actual scientific deliverable: newly fit B0/B1/B2 interpretable models and B3 learned models on the locked participant split; output the cohort-flow and complete-case/missingness table, the MFI incremental risk contrast, calibration and held-out uncertainty for walking pace and falls, the instance-3 unpooled sensitivity, and the frozen falsification report. Completion requires output-linked estimates and uncertainty; no fitted result is asserted in this proposal.

## 2. Why this advances inspected work

[K1] establishes broad health relevance of TMFI in UK Biobank but leaves functional incremental validity open. [K2] motivates composition as potentially informative for function, yet notes that myosteatosis is heterogeneous and often confounded by age, disease, disuse and body size. [K3] gives a clinical framework that combines strength, quantity/quality and performance, but its consensus recommendation is not an empirical test of whether the additional MRI measure changes functional classification.

This experiment adds a deliberately narrow, falsifiable boundary test: identical-visit posterior-thigh MFI, bilateral thigh fat-free volume and bilateral grip are entered in nested models for two clinically interpretable outcomes. The key contrast is not a small predictive score improvement; it is the adjusted absolute risk difference for slow pace when MFI is set to the training-derived 75th versus 25th percentile, with quantity and grip retained. A null result would be useful: it would argue that, for this population and measurement, quantity and grip capture most of the available same-visit functional information. A positive result would justify external validation and prospective functional testing, not immediate clinical use.

Leading explanation: MFI reflects lower-limb muscle quality and retains a residual relationship with functional limitation after quantity and grip adjustment. Strong rivals are: (1) quantity/body-size confounding, so MFI attenuates after fat-free volume, BMI and body-fat adjustment; (2) common age, disease, inactivity, pain or neurologic limitation, so the association is non-specific or disappears in age/body-composition sensitivity analyses; (3) measurement/selection, because MRI attendees with complete fields differ from the broader cohort; and (4) hand-grip mismeasurement, because upper-limb pain or neuropathy makes grip an imperfect comparator. Same-visit data cannot separate MFI causing disability from disability/disuse causing MFI, and no bound field provides pain, physical activity, neurologic examination or raw-image QC.

## 3. Exact read-only source binding

The full catalog snapshot is ukb-completed-subset-20261002, catalog SHA-256 6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32. The dataset README lists 61 read-only source files. This proposal uses one table only:

## 4. Population, timing and missingness

Primary population: one row per unique eid with a parseable 53-2.0 date from 2014-01-01 through 2023-12-31, valid numeric values for both MFI sides, all four thigh fat-free-volume fields, both grip fields, age, BMI and body-fat percentage, and a valid walking-pace response. The audit observed dates from 2014-04-30 through 2023-03-12. There is no future follow-up window and no incident disease selection.

MFI_mean is the arithmetic mean of 23355-2.0 and 23356-2.0 after training-only scaling; thigh_quantity is the sum of the four fat-free-volume fields after training-only scaling; grip_max is the maximum of 46-2.0 and 47-2.0. The primary complete-case model requires all source components rather than silently substituting one side. Prespecified sensitivities use one-side-available MFI and grip, complete-four versus minimum-three MRI components, left/right MFI separately, and MFI side difference.

Walking pace is coded as slow (924 = 1) versus average/brisk (924 = 2 or 3) for the primary binary estimand; an ordinal 1<2<3 model is secondary. Falls is any fall (2296 = 2 or 3) versus none (2296 = 1); the ordinal three-level coding is secondary. Codes -7/-3 and nulls are missing and excluded from the primary outcome, not encoded as healthy or impaired.

Primary instance-2 audit facts: 39,443 complete for the six MRI fields; 38,070 complete for MRI plus both grip sides; 39,145 with MRI plus walking pace; 39,177 with MRI plus falls; and 37,830 with MRI, both grips and both functional outcomes. Instance 3 has 816 complete MRI records and 808 with both grips and both outcomes. These are source audit counts, not study results.

Missingness is part of the result. Report a flow diagram from all table rows to dated instance-2 rows, complete MRI, complete comparator, complete covariates, and each outcome. Compare included versus excluded participants on available same-visit age, BMI, body fat, visit date and field availability. As a sensitivity, model probability of complete MRI/comparator availability from those observed fields and use stabilized inverse-probability-of-observation weights only with adequate overlap; report extreme weights. Do not impute a missing outcome in the primary analysis. Multiple imputation of covariates is a secondary analysis only, with imputation fitted within training data.

## 5. Estimand and analysis

For the primary slow-pace outcome Y, let C be age, BMI, body-fat percentage and visit calendar year, Q be thigh_quantity, G be grip_max, and M be MFI_mean. The primary standardized information contrast is:

Delta_MFI = E[ P(Y=1 | M=Q75, Q, G, C) - P(Y=1 | M=Q25, Q, G, C) ],

where Q25 and Q75 are calculated from the training split only and the expectation averages over the locked eligible population's observed Q, G and C. This is a model-standardized association contrast, not an intervention effect. Report Delta_MFI in percentage points with a 95% participant-bootstrap interval and the corresponding B1-to-B2 contrast. The secondary estimand repeats this for any fall. Report one-SD MFI contrasts as well because quartile contrasts are scale-dependent.

Models are:

- B0: age, BMI, body-fat percentage and calendar year, with prespecified restricted cubic splines for age and BMI.
- B1 baseline: B0 plus thigh_quantity and grip_max. This is the quantity/grip comparator.
- B2 primary incremental model: B1 plus linear MFI_mean.
- B3 learned alternative: a shallow gradient-boosted binary model using the identical participants, split and information set, represented by the raw bilateral MFI, four quantity, two grip, age, BMI, body fat and calendar-year fields plus deterministic summaries. A fixed small grid is selected on validation log loss/Brier score only. It can reveal stable MFI thresholds, side asymmetry or interactions with quantity/grip that B2 erases; effect plots are descriptive and not mechanisms.

All models use a deterministic eid-hash 70/15/15 participant split into train/validation/locked test, with event/date-stratum balance only after participant assignment. No participant may contribute to more than one split. Scaling, spline fitting, quartiles, imputation, tuning and thresholds use training data only. The locked test is read once. Fit and report both outcomes under the frozen specification; do not select the primary endpoint after viewing results.

Report event counts and prevalence, complete-case flow, B1/B2 coefficients and standardized contrasts, B3 held-out calibration intercept/slope, Brier score and AUROC, and paired participant-bootstrap intervals (at least 500, preferably 1,000). A 0.01 Brier change is secondary and is not clinical evidence without a stable MFI contrast. Repeat the frozen analysis at instance 3 without pooling or retuning; because it may reuse participants and has only 808 fully observed rows, it cannot serve as independent validation.

## 6. Falsification and interpretation rules

Run once under the frozen specification and retain adverse results.

1. Quantity/grip attenuation: if MFI loses direction or material size after Q and G are added, the claim that MFI adds information is not supported.
2. Body-composition sensitivity: compare B2 with and without body-fat percentage and, where overlap permits, visceral fat volume. Large attenuation identifies body-composition confounding or overadjustment as unresolved; it does not prove a mechanism.
3. Age and calendar sensitivity: compare flexible age with age bands and visit-year adjustment. A signal confined to one age band or date period is a boundary/selection finding, not a general functional marker.
4. Measurement structure: compare bilateral mean, each side, side difference, complete-four and minimum-three rules. A signal driven by one side or one missingness rule is adverse to a stable MFI interpretation.
5. Comparator limitation: repeat with grip_max, both grips, and grip residualized on age/body size. A large change shows that grip is an imperfect or collinear comparator; it does not prove lower-limb biology.
6. Outcome coding: repeat binary versus ordinal walking pace and falls coding, retain -3/-7 exclusion counts, and report whether the same direction appears for the two distinct outcomes. A pace-only result is not evidence for falls.
7. Selection: compare complete MRI attendees with all dated instance-2 rows and apply the observation-weight sensitivity. Failure of weight overlap or material instability makes the result inconclusive for the source population.
8. Leakage/permutation: shuffle MFI within age/BMI strata and permute outcomes once with fixed seeds. Any retained locked-test signal invalidates the corresponding computational result.
9. Later visit: repeat at instance 3 as a sensitivity. Concordance is supportive of transport across visit instances but is not independent replication; discordance is a reason to investigate selection and measurement timing.

Supportive result: in the locked instance-2 analysis, Delta_MFI for slow pace is positive with a 95% interval excluding zero and the prespecified point estimate reaches at least 5 percentage points (a planning threshold for clinical materiality, not a validated MCID); the direction is not removed by quantity/grip/body-composition/missingness sensitivities; no permutation signal appears; and the secondary falls result is directionally compatible or explicitly reported as null. B3 may reveal stable nonlinear structure, but predictive improvement alone cannot turn an adverse B2 result into support.

Adverse result: Delta_MFI is zero/reversed, below the planning materiality threshold, is explained by quantity/grip or missingness, is confined to a coding/side/date subgroup, or the same signal appears under permutation. This supports the rival that MRI MFI is redundant, confounded or selected, and the incremental-functional-information claim should be abandoned or narrowed.

Inconclusive result: wide intervals, too few falls, failure of source/date or overlap checks, unstable coding, non-overlapping observation weights, or inability to verify MFI measurement validity. An imprecise null is not a refutation. Continuing would require expert review of MRI segmentation/QC and functional coding, validated clinical assessments, or an external cohort. Clinical adjudication is required for disability severity, physical examination, pain/neurologic causes, raw-image measurement validity and generalization. The computation can check source binding, same-instance joins, cohort flow, model outputs, uncertainty and whether conclusions match those outputs; it cannot establish causality, mechanism, future falls risk or treatment benefit.

## 7. Alternatives, compute and limits

The interpretable nested models are retained because they directly answer the incremental question and expose attenuation after quantity and grip. The learned alternative is retained because threshold and component interactions are scientifically substantive possibilities: a linear mean MFI term can lose a high-risk tail or side-specific pattern. Both use the same source fields, participant split, targets and uncertainty evaluation. A transformer/sequence model is deferred because this is a one-visit question and no repeated dated trajectory is needed. A mechanistic model is deferred because raw images, histology, physical activity, pain, neurologic findings and treatment are unavailable. Revisit either only after those dependencies are admitted and the question changes.

Full model fitting and bootstrap are unmeasured; plan 4-8 CPUs, 16-32 GiB and under two hours, within the future solver planning envelope of 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. No GPU is required or scientifically justified for these tabular models.

[K1] Zhang Y et al. “Integrative Analysis Uncover the Effects and Multi-Omics Features of Thigh Muscle Fat Infiltration.” Aging Cell. 2026;25(9):e70690. PMID 42675546, DOI 10.1111/acel.70690. Abstract-only inspection. Supports broad UKB TMFI-health association; does not establish incremental same-visit function beyond quantity/grip.

[K2] Roe LS, Zmuda JM, Miljkovic I. “Myosteatosis: an emerging biomarker of aging.” Frontiers in Aging. 2026;7:1868010. DOI 10.3389/fragi.2026.1868010. Relevant full-text passages inspected from the frozen provider source. Supports the plausible composition-function link and explicitly bounds it with depot, confounding, cross-sectional and standardization limitations.

# UKB-03: MRI thigh fat infiltration and same-visit functional limitation

## Scientific question and claim boundary

This is a proposed, not yet fitted, Harbor experiment. The unresolved question is whether posterior-thigh MRI muscle fat infiltration (MFI) carries clinically meaningful same-visit information about functional limitation after muscle quantity and hand-grip strength are already known.

The primary hypothesis is: among UK Biobank participants with complete instance-2 MRI thigh measurements, posterior-thigh MFI has a positive, clinically material adjusted association with slow usual walking pace after adjustment for bilateral thigh fat-free muscle volume, bilateral grip, age, BMI, body-fat percentage and visit calendar year. A concordant but secondary hypothesis concerns any fall in the prior year.

The evidence already supports only bounded claims. [K1] reports broad associations between UK Biobank MRI thigh MFI and mortality/system-specific disease, not incremental same-visit functional validity. [K2] links myosteatosis with gait, balance, strength and physical function but emphasizes depot definitions, confounding, cross-sectional limits and measurement standardization. [K3] places strength first, quantity/quality as confirmatory, and poor physical performance as severe sarcopenia. None establishes this posterior-thigh field's incremental value beyond quantity and grip. This task adds a narrow, falsifiable boundary test; it does not reproduce any demonstration paper.

This is a cross-sectional descriptive/prognostic information claim about current or recalled functional limitation. It is not a causal effect, sarcopenia diagnosis, mechanism, future falls prediction, treatment rule, or evidence of clinical utility. A positive result supports external validation and prospective functional testing; it does not justify clinical use.

## Actual scientific deliverable

The solver must newly compute, from the bound Parquet source:

1. Source and cohort audit: verify schema, one-row-per-eid handling, date range, complete-case flow, outcome counts, available-versus-excluded comparisons, and missingness/observation-weight diagnostics.
2. Primary instance-2 models for both binary slow walking pace and binary any fall: B0, B1, B2, and B3, with held-out uncertainty.
3. The standardized MFI information contrast, its B1-to-B2 change, calibration and discrimination summaries, paired participant-bootstrap intervals, the locked-test results, and frozen falsification checks.
4. The unpooled instance-3 sensitivity without pooling or retuning.

Completion requires output-linked numerical estimates and justified uncertainty for both outcomes. A schema/header audit or a plan without fitted estimates is not completion of the estimation task.

## Exact data binding (read-only; no joins)

Dataset snapshot: `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`; catalog SHA-256: `6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32`.

Q25 and Q75 must come from the training split. Average over the locked eligible population's observed Q, G and C. This is a model-standardized association contrast, not an intervention effect.

Models:
- B0: age, BMI, body-fat percentage and calendar year; use prespecified restricted cubic splines for age and BMI.
- B1: B0 plus thigh_quantity and grip_max.
- B2: B1 plus linear MFI_mean; this is the primary incremental model.
- B3: shallow gradient-boosted binary model using the identical rows, split and information set: raw bilateral MFI, four quantity fields, two grip fields, age, BMI, body fat, calendar year, and deterministic summaries. Select a fixed small shallow-tree grid by validation log loss/Brier score only. Use B3 to reveal stable MFI thresholds, side asymmetry or interactions that B2 may erase; effect plots are descriptive, not mechanisms.

Use a deterministic eid-hash participant split: 70% train, 15% validation, 15% locked test. Balance outcome/date strata only after participant assignment. No participant can cross splits. Fit scaling, splines, quartiles, imputation, tuning and thresholds on training data only. Open the locked test once.

For each outcome report event counts and prevalence; B1/B2 coefficients; standardized contrasts; B3 held-out calibration intercept/slope, Brier score and AUROC; and paired participant-bootstrap intervals. A 0.01 Brier change is secondary and is not clinical evidence without a stable MFI contrast. Use at least 500 paired bootstrap resamples. Repeat the frozen pipeline at instance 3 without pooling or retuning; it is not independent validation.

## Falsification and interpretation

Run the following once under the frozen specification and retain adverse results:

1. Check whether MFI attenuates or reverses after quantity and grip are added.
2. Compare body-fat adjustment and, if overlap permits, visceral-fat adjustment; large attenuation is a confounding/overadjustment warning, not proof of mechanism.
3. Repeat flexible age with age bands and calendar adjustment; age/date-confined signals are boundary or selection findings.
4. Compare bilateral mean, each side, side difference, complete-four and minimum-three rules.
5. Compare grip_max, both grips and grip residualized on age/body size; large changes show comparator limitation, not lower-limb biology.
6. Compare binary versus ordinal walking pace and falls coding; pace-only support is not falls support.
7. Compare complete MRI attendees with dated instance-2 rows; use observation weights only with overlap.
8. Shuffle MFI within age/BMI strata and permute outcomes once with fixed seeds. Any retained locked-test signal invalidates that computational result.
9. Repeat at instance 3 without pooling; concordance is transport sensitivity, not independent replication.

Interpretation must be tied to the computed outputs:
- Supportive slow-pace result: locked instance-2 Delta_MFI is positive, its 95% interval excludes zero, point estimate is at least 5 percentage points (a planning threshold, not a validated MCID), quantity/grip/body-composition/missingness sensitivities do not remove it, and no permutation signal occurs. Falls may be compatible or null; do not promote the secondary outcome.

The solver's conclusion must not claim causality, mechanism, diagnosis, future falls risk, treatment benefit, or general clinical utility. It cannot establish disability severity, physical examination findings, pain/neurologic causes, raw-image segmentation/QC validity, causal direction, future falls, treatment benefit, external validity or clinical adoption. # UKB-672073 diagnosis-anchored child: prediagnostic reserve and near-term CRC presentation

Status: proposed, not fitted. Parent: candidate-2b202f4d99e86bdc347d56e0. This child is a targeted repair of the parent’s follow-up gate. It does not claim a mortality or incidence result.

## 1. Scientific opening and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports three bounded observations. A mixed oncology cohort containing colorectal-cancer patients found that a patient-reported/comorbidity frailty index was associated with survival [K1]. A longitudinal immune study found physiological change up to four years before some cancer diagnoses, making occult disease timing a serious rival [K2]. A Swedish register study demonstrates that prediagnostic exposures can be related to CRC outcomes, but its stage, treatment and follow-up infrastructure are not present in the verified UKB binding [K3]. None tests whether objectively recorded preassessment reserve is associated with how soon a recorded CRC diagnosis follows assessment, or whether that pattern is CRC-specific.

The parent’s five-year competing-risk mortality question cannot pass its required readiness gate on the present snapshot: the registered Online_Follow_up derivative has only `eid` and `20191-0.0`, and the catalog/source notes do not document an outcome-ascertainment cutoff `tau_source`. Observed maxima are not completeness. Therefore this child will not use absence of a cancer/death record as survival, censoring or a five-year risk endpoint.

Hypothesis:

> Among UKB participants with a valid assessment in 2006–2010 who have a subsequently recorded incident cancer diagnosis, lower assessment-time measured reserve is associated with a greater probability that the first recorded CRC diagnosis occurs within 730 days of assessment rather than 730–1825 days, relative to the analogous timing contrast for non-CRC cancers.

This is a case-only, diagnosis-anchored prognostic/descriptive association. It asks whether reserve can discriminate a near-assessment CRC presentation among people whose cancer is recorded. It is not an incidence, screening-performance, stage, treatment, mortality, causal or mechanistic claim. It remains clinically useful as a boundary test for whether a baseline reserve signal could identify a short diagnostic window for future validation; it cannot justify changing screening or treatment.

The leading rival is occult-cancer timing/measurement: low reserve may be an early manifestation of an already developing cancer or may increase healthcare contact and recording. Other rivals are age/comorbidity, cancer-subsite mix, coding and missingness/selection. A reserve association that is equally strong for non-CRC cancer or only appears in the shortest lag stratum will not support a CRC-specific durable-reserve interpretation.

Key references: [K1] establishes post-diagnosis frailty-survival association but not this timing estimand; [K2] motivates the occult-timing falsification; [K3] bounds what a registry study with stage and complete follow-up can establish beyond this UKB adaptation.

# UKB-672073 diagnosis-anchored CRC timing: recordability-controlled repair

Status: proposed, not fitted. Parent: candidate-7508a649e73cc544ca5959e0. This is a substantive repair of the parent’s remaining ascertainment/selection objection. It does not restore the unsupported mortality or population-incidence endpoint.

## 1. Opening, supported claim, and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports three bounded observations. A mixed oncology cohort reported that a patient-reported/comorbidity frailty index was associated with survival after cancer diagnosis [K1]. A longitudinal immune study reported physiological change up to four years before some cancer diagnoses, making occult disease timing a serious rival to any reserve interpretation [K2]. A Swedish register study shows what stage, treatment and national-register follow-up can add, but those elements are not in the verified UKB binding [K3]. None tests pre-assessment reserve against CRC diagnosis lag or separates that pattern from generic recordability.

The strongest claim supported by the parent is only: among people with a subsequently recorded cancer, lower assessment-time reserve may be associated with shorter lag to that recorded diagnosis, with a CRC-versus-non-CRC contrast. This is not incidence, true diagnosis time, screening performance, stage, treatment tolerance, mortality, causality or mechanism.

The strongest unresolved rival is a recording process. Lower reserve/comorbidity may increase healthcare contact and opportunities for cancer coding; conditioning on ever having a recorded cancer may select on this process. The observed pattern could therefore be generic documentation timing, cancer-register ascertainment, unmeasured symptoms, or selection rather than CRC-specific biology.

**Repaired hypothesis:** among UKB participants with a valid 2006–2010 assessment and an observed paired cancer diagnosis after assessment, the CRC-versus-non-CRC near-assessment lag contrast associated with lower measured reserve remains after standardizing by pre-assessment dated non-cancer diagnosis history, and is not reproduced by a same-source negative-control timing endpoint for first recorded non-cancer diagnoses. This is a robustness claim about documented records, not a causal reserve or healthcare-contact effect.

Generic recordability predicts similar reserve-by-short-lag associations in CRC, non-CRC and non-cancer records, and attenuation after pre-assessment record-history stratification. # UKB diagnosis-anchored CRC timing: temporal record-history state transition child

Status: proposed, not fitted. Child of candidate-a403c72d4e353a7f9c5b0237. This is a complementary formulation of the documented-record question; it does not restore the failed mortality/incidence endpoint, convert diagnosis dates into encounter dates, or claim a fitted result.

## 1. Scientific opening and claim boundary

The inherited proposal makes the strongest available claim deliberately narrow: among people with a valid 2006–2010 assessment and a subsequently observed paired cancer record, lower assessment-time reserve may be associated with a shorter lag to that recorded diagnosis, with a CRC-versus-other-cancer contrast. Its dated non-cancer history count H is a useful control, but H compresses a temporally ordered record history into one scalar. A person with one recent code and a person with ten remote codes can have similar or different H categories despite very different observable record histories.

The unresolved question is whether the reserve-by-lag contrast is specific to CRC timing after representing the *temporal state of recorded diagnosis history*, or whether it is a general transition-to-documentation pattern. This matters clinically because a positive CRC-specific temporal contrast could justify an encounter-complete study of prediagnostic vulnerability and diagnostic proximity; a contrast that follows generic history recency/repetition would warn against presenting reserve as a CRC biological detector or screening signal.

Evidence already supports, but does not prove, three boundaries. [K1] reports a post-diagnosis mixed-oncology frailty-survival association. [K2] makes occult disease a plausible rival by reporting physiological change years before some cancer diagnoses. [K3] shows that stage, treatment and complete register follow-up can materially bound CRC interpretation, but those fields are not in this UKB binding. None establishes a CRC-specific prediagnostic reserve-to-recorded-lag mechanism.

The leading explanation is occult CRC or diagnostic proximity: lower reserve may be closer to an underlying CRC process, so its association should concentrate in CRC and the shortest lag window. The consequential rival is recordability: recent/recurrent documented diagnoses mark a participant whose conditions are more likely to generate coding opportunities, so reserve may associate with short lags for CRC, other cancer and non-cancer diagnoses alike. Age, comorbidity, symptoms, referral, screening and coding differences can produce either pattern. This experiment can separate observable timing patterns, not prove mechanism, healthcare contact, true disease onset or causality.

Hypothesis: conditional on an observed post-assessment paired diagnosis-history event, the reserve contrast in near-assessment lag is larger for first recorded CRC than for first recorded non-cancer diagnoses after standardizing to the same pre-assessment temporal history states; the CRC excess is concentrated in the near window and is not explained by the history-state gradient. If the contrast is equal across classes or disappears after state representation, generic recordability is the better-supported explanation.

# UKB diagnosis-anchored CRC timing: temporal record-history state transition

Status: proposed, not fitted. This is the frozen Lead design selected for compilation. It is a bounded adaptation, not a reproduction of any demonstration paper. The solver must compute the study and may conclude supportive, adverse, or inconclusive; it must not optimize for confirmation.

## Scientific question and claim boundary

Among participants with a valid 2006–2010 assessment and a subsequently observed paired diagnosis-history event, does lower assessment-time reserve associate with a shorter lag to a first recorded colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis more strongly than with a first recorded non-cancer diagnosis after standardizing the same pre-assessment temporal record-history states?

The inherited evidence supports only a conditional recorded-event association: lower reserve may be associated with shorter lag to an observed diagnosis, with a CRC-versus-other-cancer contrast. It does not establish incidence, mortality, cancer-free status, encounter completeness, true disease onset, symptoms, referral, screening, stage, treatment, causality, mechanism, or clinical benefit. [K1] reports a post-diagnosis mixed-oncology frailty-survival association, not this prediagnostic lag. [K2] supports occult physiology as a timing rival, not CRC-specific reserve. [K3] shows what stage, treatment, and complete register follow-up can add, but those data are not bound here.

Leading explanation: occult CRC or diagnostic proximity; a CRC-specific contrast should concentrate in CRC and the near window. Consequential rival: generic recordability; recent/recurrent diagnoses mark more opportunities for coding, producing similar short-lag contrasts for CRC, other cancer, and non-cancer. Age, comorbidity, symptoms, referral, screening, coding, selection, and measurement can produce either pattern.

Primary hypothesis: conditional on an observed post-assessment paired diagnosis-history event, the reserve contrast in near-assessment lag is larger for first recorded CRC than for first recorded non-cancer diagnoses after standardizing to the same pre-assessment temporal history states; the CRC excess is concentrated in the near window and is not explained by the history-state gradient. Equal class contrasts or attenuation after temporal-state adjustment favor generic recordability.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly computed, output-linked: cohort flow and malformed/tied-slot audit; state support and overlap; class-by-state-by-window counts; state-standardized contrasts with participant-bootstrap uncertainty; source concordance against 40005/40006; held-out B0/B1 calibration and scoring; fixed falsification checks; and an interpretation tied to those outputs. # UKB diagnosis-anchored CRC timing: full-cohort recorded-source selection audit

Status: proposed, not fitted. This is a substantive child of candidate-c4e6c5069a1aebfa629e3a2d. It does not claim encounter completeness, incidence, mortality, true disease onset, causality, or clinical benefit.

## 1. Scientific opening, evidence boundary and hypothesis

The parent’s strongest supported claim is narrow: among participants with a valid 2006–2010 assessment and a subsequently observed paired 41270/41280 diagnosis-history event, assessment-time reserve may be associated with the lag to the first recorded CRC relative to other recorded diagnoses. That is a conditional recorded-event association. It is not a population risk or an incidence estimate because a participant with no observed post-assessment event may have had no event, an event in an unobserved source, or insufficient observation.

The unresolved question is whether a reserve-by-recorded-CRC-lag contrast persists after directly characterizing the event-observation boundary in the full eligible assessment cohort. Two explanations remain observationally plausible:

1. **Occult timing/diagnostic proximity:** lower reserve is closer to an underlying CRC process, so the reserve contrast should be relatively CRC-specific, concentrated in the near-assessment window, and similar for CRC records that are concordant across the two available cancer-record streams.
2. **Observed-record selection:** reserve, age, comorbidity history and recent recorded history affect whether a diagnosis becomes visible in a particular source and when it is recorded. This predicts gradients in the full-cohort recorded-source categories, source-specific CRC capture, and the lag contrast’s dependence on source concordance. It can also generate a non-cancer recorded-history gradient.

[K1] supports reserve/frailty as a clinically meaningful construct in post-diagnosis oncology, but does not establish prediagnostic timing or UKB record capture. [K2] makes latent disease-related physiological change before diagnosis a plausible timing rival, but does not measure this UKB reserve or encounter observation. [K3] shows the additional evidence used in a consequential CRC register study—population-complete linkage, stage and cancer-specific outcomes—while those fields are unavailable here. None establishes a CRC-specific prediagnostic reserve-to-recorded-lag mechanism in this binding.

**Hypothesis.** Conditional on the same pre-assessment recorded-history state and available assessment covariates, a lower-reserve contrast in near-assessment lag will be larger for first recorded CRC than for first recorded non-cancer diagnosis, and this CRC excess will persist in the subset whose 41270/41280 CRC record has a paired 40005/40006 CRC record within 30 days.
