{"result": {"text": "# Reserve-by-recorded-CRC timing specificity after common-source controls

Status: proposed substantive successor of candidate-4a893e17e9a5f2ad59447d9d. This is a source-bound, unfitted design. It preserves the parent's paired-source audit and recorded-event boundary, but makes the primary estimand full-cohort rather than conditioning the main decision on a sparse selected CRC subset.

## 1. Scientific opening, supported claim, and unresolved hypothesis

The strongest available claim is narrow: among participants with an eligible 2006–2010 assessment and an observed paired diagnosis-history event, baseline reserve may be associated with whether a first recorded CRC date is near rather than late after assessment. The parent also showed that two UKB source streams can be compared by their recorded CRC dates. These facts do not establish incidence, true onset, encounters, screening, mortality, mechanism, causality, or clinical utility.

The unresolved question is whether the timing contrast is CRC-specific or is a generic property of recorded histories. A low-reserve participant may have a CRC record near assessment because disease biology produces an earlier record, because any active diagnosis is more likely to be recorded near assessment, because pre-assessment recorded history is more recent or recurrent, or because the two sources date the same process differently. [K1] supports clinical relevance of frailty-related measurement in oncology but is post-diagnosis and not a record-timing test. [K2] makes prediagnostic physiological change a plausible rival, but does not distinguish biology from record visibility here. [K3] shows the extra stage, treatment, and follow-up provenance available in a population register; those fields are absent from this snapshot.

Hypothesis: after adjustment for measured baseline covariates and an explicitly dated pre-assessment history state, a reserve-by-near-versus-late tilt for first recorded CRC will be larger than the corresponding tilt for first recorded non-cancer and other-cancer events in the same diagnosis-history source, and the CRC-versus-other-cancer difference will replicate in the paired cancer source. The result must remain when the full eligible assessment cohort is retained with “no qualifying recorded event” as an explicit outcome. This is a falsifiable specificity hypothesis, not a claim about occult disease or diagnosis onset.

The clinical decision relevance is whether reserve should be investigated as a CRC-specific warning or screening-workflow signal, or treated only as a general marker of recordability and health-service contact. A positive result would justify clinical adjudication and a prospective ascertainment study; a comparator-matched or source-heterogeneous result would argue against a CRC-specific interpretation.

## 2. Exact source binding, namespace, and catalog limits

The frozen dataset snapshot is ukb-completed-subset-20261002, catalog SHA-256 6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32. The full catalog and inherited source audit identify 502,370 rows, eid as the identifier, namespace ukb672073, ordinary Parquet files, and no archive members for these tables. All joins are on eid only within ukb672073. UKB-671626, Olink, and dta identifiers are not compatible namespaces and are not joined. Source files are read-only; parsed events, audits, model outputs, and bootstrap files are derived workspace outputs.

| Role | Exact read-only source and SHA-256 | Catalog table and member | Required fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assessment and reserve | [private-path]/ukb_d61ec821b81b9034.parquet; e69705f71f6a4f263371bec081d50a7d9482291d73cde09873634b327936a841 | UKB/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv (Parquet), table-6fc0a334db7f533b; ordinary file, no archive member | eid, 53-0.0, 46-0.0, 47-0.0, 20116-0.0, 21001-0.0 |
| Demographics | [private-path]/ukb_ce68812c3a782e09.parquet; d446c8288dfe59abc97e44a43027628aa7221a60f307d4da879a7c491b930299 | UKB/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv (Parquet), table-674bd55f4152a860; ordinary file, no archive member | eid, 31-0.0, 34-0.0, 21022-0.0 |
| Laboratory reserve | [private-path]/ukb_a19465be8f90accc.parquet; 9a62c73361094f4e12045082d8872efa84933e7bb86f596e9e8a49fc162a4ab0 | UKB/ukb672073_Biological_Samples.csv (Parquet), table-50f94f98137a2d88; ordinary file, no archive member | eid, 30600-0.0, 30700-0.0, 30720-0.0 |
| Paired CRC and diagnosis records | [private-path]/ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047.parquet; 36d0e32efc608dd0e324a6e66fd4211813e7542ec08b78213488ab8f52874ad8 | UKB/ukb672073_Health_Related_Outcomes.csv (Parquet), table-03f57283ab9ae48b; ordinary file, no archive member | eid; 40005-0.0 through 40005-21.0 and 40006-0.0 through 40006-21.0; 41270-0.0 through 41270-0.258 and 41280-0.0 through 41280-0.258 |
| Follow-up provenance audit only | [private-path]/ukb_c9f8c514956c9481.parquet; 42c0e50e9b3e270bb578a4c56f0d753c9a794ad69e56a221bae940dd9060b1d5 | UKB/ukb672073_Online_Follow_up.csv (Parquet), table-99ff3ee72fc403a0; ordinary file, no archive member | eid, 20191-0.0 |

The catalog records 22 40005/40006 slots and 259 41270/41280 slots. Values must be cast explicitly before date or numeric parsing. A code or date without its same-slot partner is not an event; a neighboring slot may not repair it.

## 3. Population and temporal boundaries

Let b_i be the parsed 53-0.0 assessment date. The eligible population U is constructed before any post-assessment event scan:

- one unique eid;
- 2006-01-01 <= b_i <= 2010-12-31;
- valid sex 31-0.0, age 21022-0.0, BMI 21001-0.0, and smoking 20116-0.0;
- at least three available components of the four-component reserve;
- no observed paired C00–C97 cancer code/date on or before b_i in either CRC source.

The last condition means no observed pre-assessment cancer record, never cancer-free. 20191-0.0 is not a censoring date, denominator, completeness proxy, or tau_source.

For source C, a valid same-slot pair is 40005[j] date with 40006[j] ICD-10 code, j=0,…,21. For source D, it is 41270[j] ICD-10 code with 41280[j] date, j=0,…,258. Normalize code strings without inventing prefixes; parse dates; discard malformed or unpaired fields; deduplicate exact code/date pairs. CRC is C18, C19, or C20. Other cancer is C00–C97 excluding C18–C20. Non-cancer is every other valid recorded ICD code in source D; it is not a control for healthy people.

The primary window is W_i=(b_i,b_i+1825 days], with lag L=t-b_i. Near is 0<L<730 days and late is 730<=L<=1825 days. Fixed boundary checks use near cutoffs 365 and 730 days and a late cutoff of 1460 days. Dates beyond 1825 days are descriptive only.

## 4. Full-cohort outcome and exact estimand

Source D supplies the primary common-source outcome for every U row:

- Y=CRC-near, CRC-late, other-cancer-near, other-cancer-late, non-cancer-near, or non-cancer-late when the first valid post-assessment event has that class and lag;
- Y=no qualifying recorded event when no valid paired event occurs in W_i;
- Y=multi-class same-date tie when distinct classes share the earliest valid date.

A tie is retained in the full-cohort target and reported separately; it is not assigned to a favored class. Unpaired/malformed fields are audit failures, not events. “No qualifying recorded event” combines no observed event with unavailable or unrecorded disease and is never called no disease. This construction prevents the primary analysis from being defined only by selected CRC cases, while preserving the recorded-event claim boundary.

Source C supplies an analogous cancer-only target: CRC-near, CRC-late, other-cancer-near, other-cancer-late, multi-class tie, or no qualifying recorded cancer event. It cannot manufacture a non-cancer event.

Reserve is inherited exactly: G=max(46-0.0,47-0.0); albumin 30600-0.0; creatinine 30700-0.0; cystatin C 30720-0.0. Fit sex-stratified grip standardization, log albumin, negative-log creatinine, and negative-log cystatin C on training rows only. R is the mean of available standardized components, with component count and missingness retained. Q25 and Q75 are training-derived reserve quartiles.

Before scanning post-assessment records, define source-D pre-assessment history S from valid non-cancer 41270/41280 pairs in [1900-01-01,b_i): S=0 none; S=1 remote (latest pair at or before b_i-730 days); S=2 recent-single (latest pair in the preceding 730 days and exactly one unique recent date); S=3 recent-recurrent (at least two unique recent dates). Retain raw unique-pair count, recent unique-date count, and days since the latest pair as measured history descriptors. S is a dated recorded-history state, not an encounter count, healthcare-contact measure, or completeness score.

For fitted model m, let p^m_{g,l}(r) be the predicted probability of the full-cohort source-D category g-lag after setting reserve to r and standardizing over the fixed supported distribution of S and baseline x=(age, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year). The standardization distribution is fixed from covariates in the locked test set; it uses no test outcomes. Define the full-cohort recorded timing tilt:

T^m_{g,D} = [p^m_{g,near}(Q25)-p^m_{g,late}(Q25)] - [p^m_{g,near}(Q75)-p^m_{g,late}(Q75)].

This is an absolute probability contrast among all eligible assessments, with no-event and tie categories retained in the fitted target. It is not a risk, hazard, incidence estimate, encounter probability, survival time, or causal effect. Positive T means lower reserve is more associated with a near than a late recorded event of class g in the observable data.

The primary specificity estimands are:

- D_NC = T_CRC,D - T_non-cancer,D;
- D_OC = T_CRC,D - T_other-cancer,D;
- D_comp = T_CRC,D - 0.5(T_non-cancer,D + T_other-cancer,D).

Equal weighting is fixed before fitting so the much larger non-cancer class cannot overwhelm the other-cancer comparator. The source-replication estimand is D_C = T_CRC,C - T_other-cancer,C, and H_spec=D_C-D_comp. Report T values, all three D values, H_spec, category probabilities, and denominators. For transparency, also report the inherited event-conditioned sensitivity A_{g,k}=P(near | first recorded class g, S,x,R=Q25)-P(near | first recorded class g,S,x,R=Q75), only where class support passes. A is secondary; D_comp is the primary full-cohort estimand.

The hypothesis is supported only if the primary gates pass, D_comp and both component contrasts are positive with 95% intervals excluding zero, D_C is positive with its interval excluding zero, and H_spec lies within a prespecified [-0.05,+0.05] consistency band. The band is a decision threshold, not clinical equivalence. If the primary full-cohort contrast is positive but the event-conditioned A is not, the result indicates a recordability/prevalence distinction and does not establish a timing signal.

## 5. History rival, adjustment ladder, and model alternatives

Use one deterministic participant split: hash eid with seed 1414 into 70% train, 15% validation, and 15% locked test. Assign participants before event construction and keep all rows for an eid in one split. Imputation, transformations, reserve quartiles, spline parameters, standardization weights, and tuning use train/validation only.

The adjustment ladder is part of the scientific deliverable:

- M0: age spline, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year;
- M1: M0 plus scalar reserve R, reserve component count/missingness, and a coarse history-count representation;
- M2: M1 plus the explicit S state, days since latest pre-assessment pair, recent unique-date count, and prespecified reserve-by-history and class-by-history terms.

The primary interpretation uses M2. M0/M1 are not alternate hypotheses chosen after results; they show how much the CRC-versus-comparator contrast depends on measured age, reserve construction, or temporal history representation.

B0 is an interpretable additive multinomial logistic model for the full-cohort outcome, with age spline and prespecified reserve-by-event-class/lag and reserve-by-S interactions. It is the primary explanatory baseline because its estimates can identify whether the distinction is attributable to measured age/history adjustment, class/lag specificity, or source capture.

B1 is a shallow gradient-boosted multinomial model on exactly the same rows, features, targets, and split, using a fixed validation grid of 200/400 trees, depth 2/3, and learning rate .03/.05. It is scientifically substantive because reserve thresholds or reserve-by-history-by-class interactions could be hidden by additive terms and could change D_comp or H_spec, not merely a prediction score. Select only by validation multiclass log loss and Brier score. Evaluate locked-test Brier score, log loss, calibration by class/lag, and the same estimands. A small predictive gain alone is not a scientific advance; B1 is retained only if it changes the specificity decision and survives fixed date/code checks. CPU is selected: 4–8 cores, 16–32 GiB RAM, and at most 2.5 future-solver hours for selected reads, event construction, fits, locked evaluation, and 500 bootstrap replicates. This is a planning estimate, not a measured fit. GPU and sequence models are deferred because they cannot resolve missing encounter provenance; revisit only if B1 reveals reproducible nonlinear structure that a new validated dataset can test.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, output-linked evidence: source/schema/hash audit; U flow and class/lag/tie counts; history and reserve support; locked predictions and calibration; M0–M2 contrasts; B0/B1 D_NC, D_OC, D_comp, D_C, H_spec and event-conditioned A sensitivities; 500 participant-bootstrap intervals; fixed boundary, measurement, source-concordance and permutation checks; and a conclusion that points to these outputs. No fitted result is claimed here.

## 6. Support gates, uncertainty, and falsification

Before fitting, emit a machine-readable audit of every source path/hash/table ID, namespace, ordinary-file status, required columns, same-slot parseability, malformed and unpaired values, duplicates, pre-assessment exclusions, first-event ties, reserve availability, history-state support, U flow, outcome counts, split counts, source concordance, and confirmation that 20191-0.0 was not used for follow-up.

The primary full-cohort analysis requires all six source-D class/lag cells to have at least 100 participants overall and at least 20 in each split; each required history state must have at least 30 participants in U and at least 10 in each split; Q25/Q75 reserve support must overlap every primary class/lag category. Source-C CRC and other-cancer near/late cells must each have at least 30 participants overall and every split must be nonempty for source replication. These gates are checked before interpretation. If a gate fails, the corresponding contrast is inconclusive, not merged or rescued after inspecting results. A single predeclared fallback may combine S=2 and S=3 as “recent” if the combined state passes the same gates; no other state or class merging is allowed. State-specific A contrasts require at least 30 participants per class/lag/state and are secondary, so sparse states do not define the main estimand.

Use 500 participant bootstrap replicates, sampling eids within the locked test set and preserving split membership. Compute percentile 95% intervals for all primary contrasts and report failed replicates. Locked-test scoring is conditional on fitted models; bootstrap intervals do not repair missing clinical ascertainment.

Falsification and boundary checks are locked before fitting:

- Generic specificity: if non-cancer or other-cancer T is similar to CRC T, or D_NC/D_OC are near zero, the signal is generic recorded-history timing.
- History rival: strong attenuation or reversal from M1 to M2 supports dependence on temporal recordability/history, not a biological mechanism.
- Source rival: material H_spec, opposite source directions, or movement under exact-date versus ±30-day CRC concordance indicates source/date dependence.
- Temporal boundary: repeat near cutoffs at 365 and 730 days and late cutoff at 1460 days. A shortest-window-only effect is a boundary result, not durable reserve biology.
- Measurement/confounding: complete-four versus minimum-three reserve, grip-only, laboratory-only, age-only, age-plus-scalar-history, and missingness strata. Attenuation is evidence of dependence, not proof of a mechanism.
- Class permutation: within history state and lag, permute event class labels among eligible first-event rows once with a locked seed. A comparable specificity contrast after permutation invalidates the class computation.
- Source permutation: permute source labels only among paired eligible CRC records. A reproducible source contrast under that permutation invalidates the source comparison.
- Full-cohort capture: retain the inherited O0–O4 CRC audit on all U: O0 neither source records CRC, O1 source D only, O2 source C only, O3 both with first dates within 30 days, O4 both with dates differing by more than 30 days. A reserve/history gradient in O1–O4 is adverse to source-independent biology but does not prove a healthcare-contact mechanism.

Supportive results mean all gates pass; D_comp, D_NC, D_OC and D_C are positive with prespecified intervals; H_spec is within the band; the effect is not confined to the shortest window; source dates/codes are stable; generic classes do not match CRC; capture categories show no material reserve/history gradient; calibration is adequate; and permutations are null. This supports a reproducible association between reserve and the timing/class of recorded diagnosis transitions across two sources, with CRC specificity bounded by the observed fields.

Adverse results include comparator-matched timing, attenuation after M2, source heterogeneity, unstable date concordance, capture gradients, measurement dependence, or a permutation signal. These support generic recordability, source/date artifact, measured confounding, or coding error and should abandon the CRC-specific warning interpretation.

Inconclusive results include failed class/source overlap, sparse states, wide intervals crossing both decision regions, failed calibration/bootstrap, unresolved parsing, or missing provenance. An imprecise null is not refutation. Do not change windows, classes, or subgroup rules after viewing results.

## 7. Clinical limits and deferred evidence

The design cannot distinguish true onset from first recording, a diagnosis encounter from an administrative date, or an unrecorded event from no event. It lacks symptoms, referral, screening participation, healthcare-contact intensity, stage, histology, treatment, mortality, clinical adjudication, complete follow-up provenance, and an ascertainment-complete external cohort. The follow-up field 20191-0.0 is therefore audit-only. No association surviving adjustment identifies a biological mechanism or causal reserve effect. [K3] is a boundary example of what additional registry provenance could support.

The multi-omics and Olink branches remain deferred: no validated molecular CRC endpoint, stage, treatment, or compatible crosswalk to the ukb672073 eid namespace is bound here. A future continuation needs encounter-level dates and symptom/screening context, clinical diagnosis-date adjudication, stage/treatment linkage, a verified observation boundary, or an independent cohort. Computational checks can establish parsing, joins, support, fits, predictions, uncertainty, and conclusion-to-output consistency; clinical adjudication and another study are required for the stronger claims.

It supports a biological-proximity rival but is not CRC-specific and does not measure this reserve or healthcare contact.

[K3] Lu SSM et al. “Prediagnostic Prescription Antibiotics Use and Survival in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Swedish National Register-Based Study.” Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 2023. DOI 10.1158/1055-9965.epi-23-0340. Abstract-only inspection. It bounds the missing stage, treatment, and follow-up evidence; it does not validate UKB dates as onset or complete encounters.

The complete receipt file is key-references.json. The attached inspected UTF-8 Europe PMC metadata-and-abstract snapshots are support-K1-epmc.json, support-K2-epmc.json, and support-K3-epmc.json. Their exact SHA-256 values are 9dc1401edf4cb431a219369de0f913fe8039485c4d1599c60f112c4c455d5a30, 7a16fa36256a2172b8dac686188d5ec5db482dce15ac7f4c7333da1337e05166, and 712bf8fffd73f5ac83009ca3d1352e25ab0a2ed5bf4ffdc8e07b7708e5521f3b, respectively. [K1] supports clinical relevance of frailty-related measurement in oncology but is post-diagnosis and not a record-timing test. [K2] makes prediagnostic physiological change a plausible rival, but does not distinguish biology from record visibility here. [K3] shows the extra stage, treatment, and follow-up provenance available in a population register; those fields are absent from this snapshot.

Hypothesis: after adjustment for measured baseline covariates and an explicitly dated pre-assessment history state, a reserve-by-near-versus-late tilt for first recorded CRC will be larger than the corresponding tilt for first recorded non-cancer and other-cancer events in the same diagnosis-history source, and the CRC-versus-other-cancer difference will replicate in the paired cancer source. The result must remain when the full eligible assessment cohort is retained with “no qualifying recorded event” as an explicit outcome. This is a falsifiable specificity hypothesis, not a claim about occult disease or diagnosis onset.

The clinical decision relevance is whether reserve should be investigated as a CRC-specific warning or screening-workflow signal, or treated only as a general marker of recordability and health-service contact. A positive result would justify clinical adjudication and a prospective ascertainment study; a comparator-matched or source-heterogeneous result would argue against a CRC-specific interpretation.

## 3. Population and temporal boundaries

Let b_i be the parsed 53-0.0 assessment date. The eligible population U is constructed before any post-assessment event scan:

- one unique eid;
- 2006-01-01 <= b_i <= 2010-12-31;
- valid sex 31-0.0, age 21022-0.0, BMI 21001-0.0, and smoking 20116-0.0;
- at least three available components of the four-component reserve;
- no observed paired C00–C97 cancer code/date on or before b_i in either CRC source.

The last condition means no observed pre-assessment cancer record, never cancer-free. 20191-0.0 is not a censoring date, denominator, completeness proxy, or tau_source.

For source C, a valid same-slot pair is 40005[j] date with 40006[j] ICD-10 code, j=0,…,21. For source D, it is 41270[j] ICD-10 code with 41280[j] date, j=0,…,258. Normalize code strings without inventing prefixes; parse dates; discard malformed or unpaired fields; deduplicate exact code/date pairs. CRC is C18, C19, or C20. Other cancer is C00–C97 excluding C18–C20. Non-cancer is every other valid recorded ICD code in source D; it is not a control for healthy people.

The primary window is W_i=(b_i,b_i+1825 days], with lag L=t-b_i. Near is 0<L<730 days and late is 730<=L<=1825 days. Fixed boundary checks use near cutoffs 365 and 730 days and a late cutoff of 1460 days. Dates beyond 1825 days are descriptive only.

## 4. Full-cohort outcome and exact estimand

Source D supplies the primary common-source outcome for every U row:

- Y=CRC-near, CRC-late, other-cancer-near, other-cancer-late, non-cancer-near, or non-cancer-late when the first valid post-assessment event has that class and lag;
- Y=no qualifying recorded event when no valid paired event occurs in W_i;
- Y=multi-class same-date tie when distinct classes share the earliest valid date.

A tie is retained in the full-cohort target and reported separately; it is not assigned to a favored class. Unpaired/malformed fields are audit failures, not events. “No qualifying recorded event” combines no observed event with unavailable or unrecorded disease and is never called no disease. This construction prevents the primary analysis from being defined only by selected CRC cases, while preserving the recorded-event claim boundary.

Source C supplies an analogous cancer-only target: CRC-near, CRC-late, other-cancer-near, other-cancer-late, multi-class tie, or no qualifying recorded cancer event. It cannot manufacture a non-cancer event.

Reserve is inherited exactly: G=max(46-0.0,47-0.0); albumin 30600-0.0; creatinine 30700-0.0; cystatin C 30720-0.0. Fit sex-stratified grip standardization, log albumin, negative-log creatinine, and negative-log cystatin C on training rows only. R is the mean of available standardized components, with component count and missingness retained. Q25 and Q75 are training-derived reserve quartiles.

Before scanning post-assessment records, define source-D pre-assessment history S from valid non-cancer 41270/41280 pairs in [1900-01-01,b_i): S=0 none; S=1 remote (latest pair at or before b_i-730 days); S=2 recent-single (latest pair in the preceding 730 days and exactly one unique recent date); S=3 recent-recurrent (at least two unique recent dates). Retain raw unique-pair count, recent unique-date count, and days since the latest pair as measured history descriptors. S is a dated recorded-history state, not an encounter count, healthcare-contact measure, or completeness score.

For fitted model m, let p^m_{g,l}(r) be the predicted probability of the full-cohort source-D category g-lag after setting reserve to r and standardizing over the fixed supported distribution of S and baseline x=(age, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year). The standardization distribution is fixed from covariates in the locked test set; it uses no test outcomes. Define the full-cohort recorded timing tilt:

T^m_{g,D} = [p^m_{g,near}(Q25)-p^m_{g,late}(Q25)] - [p^m_{g,near}(Q75)-p^m_{g,late}(Q75)].

This is an absolute probability contrast among all eligible assessments, with no-event and tie categories retained in the fitted target. It is not a risk, hazard, incidence estimate, encounter probability, survival time, or causal effect. Positive T means lower reserve is more associated with a near than a late recorded event of class g in the observable data.

The primary specificity estimands are:

- D_NC = T_CRC,D - T_non-cancer,D;
- D_OC = T_CRC,D - T_other-cancer,D;
- D_comp = T_CRC,D - 0.5(T_non-cancer,D + T_other-cancer,D).

Equal weighting is fixed before fitting so the much larger non-cancer class cannot overwhelm the other-cancer comparator. The source-replication estimand is D_C = T_CRC,C - T_other-cancer,C, and H_spec=D_C-D_comp. Report T values, all three D values, H_spec, category probabilities, and denominators. For transparency, also report the inherited event-conditioned sensitivity A_{g,k}=P(near | first recorded class g, S,x,R=Q25)-P(near | first recorded class g,S,x,R=Q75), only where class support passes. A is secondary; D_comp is the primary full-cohort estimand.

The hypothesis is supported only if the primary gates pass, D_comp and both component contrasts are positive with 95% intervals excluding zero, D_C is positive with its interval excluding zero, and H_spec lies within a prespecified [-0.05,+0.05] consistency band. The band is a decision threshold, not clinical equivalence. If the primary full-cohort contrast is positive but the event-conditioned A is not, the result indicates a recordability/prevalence distinction and does not establish a timing signal.

## 5. History rival, adjustment ladder, and model alternatives

Use one deterministic participant split: hash eid with seed 1414 into 70% train, 15% validation, and 15% locked test. Assign participants before event construction and keep all rows for an eid in one split. Imputation, transformations, reserve quartiles, spline parameters, standardization weights, and tuning use train/validation only.

The adjustment ladder is part of the scientific deliverable:

- M0: age spline, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year;
- M1: M0 plus scalar reserve R, reserve component count/missingness, and a coarse history-count representation;
- M2: M1 plus the explicit S state, days since latest pre-assessment pair, recent unique-date count, and prespecified reserve-by-history and class-by-history terms.

The primary interpretation uses M2. M0/M1 are not alternate hypotheses chosen after results; they show how much the CRC-versus-comparator contrast depends on measured age, reserve construction, or temporal history representation.

B0 is an interpretable additive multinomial logistic model for the full-cohort outcome, with age spline and prespecified reserve-by-event-class/lag and reserve-by-S interactions. It is the primary explanatory baseline because its estimates can identify whether the distinction is attributable to measured age/history adjustment, class/lag specificity, or source capture.

B1 is a shallow gradient-boosted multinomial model on exactly the same rows, features, targets, and split, using a fixed validation grid of 200/400 trees, depth 2/3, and learning rate .03/.05. It is scientifically substantive because reserve thresholds or reserve-by-history-by-class interactions could be hidden by additive terms and could change D_comp or H_spec, not merely a prediction score. Select only by validation multiclass log loss and Brier score. Evaluate locked-test Brier score, log loss, calibration by class/lag, and the same estimands. A small predictive gain alone is not a scientific advance; B1 is retained only if it changes the specificity decision and survives fixed date/code checks. CPU is selected: 4–8 cores, 16–32 GiB RAM, and at most 2.5 future-solver hours for selected reads, event construction, fits, locked evaluation, and 500 bootstrap replicates. This is a planning estimate, not a measured fit. GPU and sequence models are deferred because they cannot resolve missing encounter provenance; revisit only if B1 reveals reproducible nonlinear structure that a new validated dataset can test.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, output-linked evidence: source/schema/hash audit; U flow and class/lag/tie counts; history and reserve support; locked predictions and calibration; M0–M2 contrasts; B0/B1 D_NC, D_OC, D_comp, D_C, H_spec and event-conditioned A sensitivities; 500 participant-bootstrap intervals; fixed boundary, measurement, source-concordance and permutation checks; and a conclusion that points to these outputs. No fitted result is claimed here.

## 6. Support gates, uncertainty, and falsification

Before fitting, emit a machine-readable audit of every source path/hash/table ID, namespace, ordinary-file status, required columns, same-slot parseability, malformed and unpaired values, duplicates, pre-assessment exclusions, first-event ties, reserve availability, history-state support, U flow, outcome counts, split counts, source concordance, and confirmation that 20191-0.0 was not used for follow-up.

The primary full-cohort analysis requires all six source-D class/lag cells to have at least 100 participants overall and at least 20 in each split; each required history state must have at least 30 participants in U and at least 10 in each split; Q25/Q75 reserve support must overlap every primary class/lag category. Source-C CRC and other-cancer near/late cells must each have at least 30 participants overall and every split must be nonempty for source replication. These gates are checked before interpretation. If a gate fails, the corresponding contrast is inconclusive, not merged or rescued after inspecting results. A single predeclared fallback may combine S=2 and S=3 as “recent” if the combined state passes the same gates; no other state or class merging is allowed. State-specific A contrasts require at least 30 participants per class/lag/state and are secondary, so sparse states do not define the main estimand.

Use 500 participant bootstrap replicates, sampling eids within the locked test set and preserving split membership. Compute percentile 95% intervals for all primary contrasts and report failed replicates. Locked-test scoring is conditional on fitted models; bootstrap intervals do not repair missing clinical ascertainment.

Falsification and boundary checks are locked before fitting:

- Generic specificity: if non-cancer or other-cancer T is similar to CRC T, or D_NC/D_OC are near zero, the signal is generic recorded-history timing.
- History rival: strong attenuation or reversal from M1 to M2 supports dependence on temporal recordability/history, not a biological mechanism.
- Source rival: material H_spec, opposite source directions, or movement under exact-date versus ±30-day CRC concordance indicates source/date dependence.
- Temporal boundary: repeat near cutoffs at 365 and 730 days and late cutoff at 1460 days. A shortest-window-only effect is a boundary result, not durable reserve biology.
- Measurement/confounding: complete-four versus minimum-three reserve, grip-only, laboratory-only, age-only, age-plus-scalar-history, and missingness strata. Attenuation is evidence of dependence, not proof of a mechanism.
- Class permutation: within history state and lag, permute event class labels among eligible first-event rows once with a locked seed. A comparable specificity contrast after permutation invalidates the class computation.
- Source permutation: permute source labels only among paired eligible CRC records. A reproducible source contrast under that permutation invalidates the source comparison.
- Full-cohort capture: retain the inherited O0–O4 CRC audit on all U: O0 neither source records CRC, O1 source D only, O2 source C only, O3 both with first dates within 30 days, O4 both with dates differing by more than 30 days. A reserve/history gradient in O1–O4 is adverse to source-independent biology but does not prove a healthcare-contact mechanism.

Supportive results mean all gates pass; D_comp, D_NC, D_OC and D_C are positive with prespecified intervals; H_spec is within the band; the effect is not confined to the shortest window; source dates/codes are stable; generic classes do not match CRC; capture categories show no material reserve/history gradient; calibration is adequate; and permutations are null. This supports a reproducible association between reserve and the timing/class of recorded diagnosis transitions across two sources, with CRC specificity bounded by the observed fields.

Adverse results include comparator-matched timing, attenuation after M2, source heterogeneity, unstable date concordance, capture gradients, measurement dependence, or a permutation signal. These support generic recordability, source/date artifact, measured confounding, or coding error and should abandon the CRC-specific warning interpretation.

Inconclusive results include failed class/source overlap, sparse states, wide intervals crossing both decision regions, failed calibration/bootstrap, unresolved parsing, or missing provenance. An imprecise null is not refutation. Do not change windows, classes, or subgroup rules after viewing results.

## 7. Clinical limits and deferred evidence

The design cannot distinguish true onset from first recording, a diagnosis encounter from an administrative date, or an unrecorded event from no event. It lacks symptoms, referral, screening participation, healthcare-contact intensity, stage, histology, treatment, mortality, clinical adjudication, complete follow-up provenance, and an ascertainment-complete external cohort. The follow-up field 20191-0.0 is therefore audit-only. No association surviving adjustment identifies a biological mechanism or causal reserve effect. [K3] is a boundary example of what additional registry provenance could support.

The multi-omics and Olink branches remain deferred: no validated molecular CRC endpoint, stage, treatment, or compatible crosswalk to the ukb672073 eid namespace is bound here. A future continuation needs encounter-level dates and symptom/screening context, clinical diagnosis-date adjudication, stage/treatment linkage, a verified observation boundary, or an independent cohort. Computational checks can establish parsing, joins, support, fits, predictions, uncertainty, and conclusion-to-output consistency; clinical adjudication and another study are required for the stronger claims.

It supports a biological-proximity rival but is not CRC-specific and does not measure this reserve or healthcare contact.

[K3] Lu SSM et al. “Prediagnostic Prescription Antibiotics Use and Survival in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Swedish National Register-Based Study.” Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 2023. DOI 10.1158/1055-9965.epi-23-0340. Abstract-only inspection. It bounds the missing stage, treatment, and follow-up evidence; it does not validate UKB dates as onset or complete encounters.

The complete receipt file is key-references.json. The attached inspected UTF-8 Europe PMC metadata-and-abstract snapshots are support-K1-epmc.json, support-K2-epmc.json, and support-K3-epmc.json. # Reserve domains, reverse causation, and specificity of recorded CRC timing

Status: unfitted substantive child of candidate-be2d73bd0508251fa8cbf015, prepared for episode 17 branch A. This preserves the parent’s full eligible cohort, exact ukb672073 bindings, paired code/date rules, two-source audit, and recorded-event boundary. The substantive repair is a sharper temporal and biomarker test of the leading clinical rival: low reserve at assessment may be a consequence of occult disease approaching diagnosis, rather than an independent CRC-specific warning; alternatively, the apparent timing pattern may be generic recordability or comorbidity.

No cohort fit, effect estimate, prediction, or clinical result is claimed.

## 1. Scientific opening and falsifiable hypothesis

The strongest claim supported by the inspected evidence and inherited source audit is narrow: in participants with a valid 2006–2010 assessment and an observed paired diagnosis-history record, baseline reserve can be compared with the lag to a first recorded CRC event. Available fields support comparisons with other recorded cancers and non-cancer diagnoses, and two UKB streams can be checked for date/code concordance. They do not establish cancer incidence, biological onset, symptoms, screening, referral, encounters, stage, treatment, mortality, mechanism, causality, or clinical utility.

[K1] supports clinical relevance and feasibility of frailty-like summaries in oncology, but is post-diagnosis and survival-focused. [K2] makes a biologically serious rival plausible: systemic physiology can change before a cancer diagnosis. [K3] shows why a register with stage, treatment and prediagnostic provenance can support stronger CRC claims than a first recorded code/date. None of these works tests this UKB recorded-event estimand.

The unresolved question is whether, after measured baseline covariates, dated pre-assessment recorded history, and a predeclared separation of laboratory and functional reserve, lower reserve is associated with a CRC record in an early or intermediate post-assessment band rather than a late record, and whether that contrast is larger than the corresponding timing contrast for other recorded classes.

The strongest rivals make different predictions.

1. Occult disease/reverse causation: an unobserved CRC process already present at assessment lowers reserve or its laboratory components and produces a record soon afterward. The contrast should be largest in the early band, attenuate when the lab domain is represented separately, and be weaker in intermediate-versus-late timing. This study cannot prove occult disease; it can only identify this pattern as adverse to an independent warning interpretation.

2. Generic recordability/comorbidity: low reserve marks recent or recurrent recorded illness and healthcare contact. The same reserve-by-lag pattern should appear for non-cancer and other-cancer records, attenuate after dated pre-assessment history adjustment, and vary with source capture. A CRC-specific claim is not supported by a generic pattern.

3. CRC-specific recorded timing compatible with, but not proving, a clinically useful warning: after those controls, the CRC contrast remains in the intermediate-versus-late comparison, exceeds both comparator contrasts, replicates in the paired cancer source, and is not explained by capture or date instability. This would support a reproducible association with the timing/class of recorded CRC transitions only. It would not identify onset or mechanism.

Hypothesis H_spec: in the full eligible assessment cohort, the reserve-by-intermediate-versus-late tilt for first recorded CRC is positive and exceeds the equal-weighted average of the non-cancer and other-cancer tilts after pre-assessment history and domain-resolved reserve controls; the CRC-versus-other-cancer contrast replicates in the paired cancer source. The early-versus-late contrast is a prespecified reverse-causation diagnostic, not the sole success criterion.

A positive result could justify clinical adjudication and a prospective ascertainment study asking whether symptoms, screening, referral, stage and true diagnosis onset explain the signal. A comparator-matched result would redirect the work toward recordability and comorbidity. An early-only, lab-sensitive result would discourage treating reserve as an independent CRC warning and prioritize occult-disease/measurement investigation.

## 2. Exact available data and source audit

All values must be cast explicitly before parsing. A date or code without its same-slot partner is not an event; a neighboring slot may not repair it. 20191-0.0 is never a censoring date, denominator, completeness proxy or source observation boundary.

## 3. Population, dates and event construction

Let b_i be parsed 53-0.0. Construct U before scanning any post-assessment record:

- one unique eid;
- 2006-01-01 <= b_i <= 2010-12-31;
- valid 31-0.0, 21022-0.0, 21001-0.0 and 20116-0.0;
- at least three available components among grip, albumin, creatinine and cystatin C;
- no observed valid paired C00–C97 code/date on or before b_i in either source.

The last exclusion means no observed pre-assessment cancer record, never cancer-free. It does not mean occult cancer was absent.

For source C, pair 40005[j] date with 40006[j] ICD-10 code for j=0,...,21. For source D, pair 41270[j] ICD-10 code with 41280[j] date for j=0,...,258. Normalize code strings without inventing prefixes; parse dates; discard malformed or unpaired values; deduplicate exact code/date pairs. CRC is C18, C19 or C20. Other cancer is C00–C97 excluding C18–C20. Non-cancer is every other valid recorded ICD code in source D and is not a healthy control.

The primary observation window is W_i=(b_i,b_i+1825 days]. Locked lag bands are early E (0<L<=365), intermediate I (365<L<=730), and late L (730<L<=1825). Dates after b_i+1825 days are descriptive only. The primary calendar boundary is the 2006–2010 assessment range and the participant-specific five-year window; assessment year is in every model. Fixed sensitivities use the alternative near cutoffs 730 days and late cutoff 1460 days, plus the sharper early boundary of 180 days. These are executed once with locked rules, not chosen after results.

Within each source, select the first valid post-assessment event by date. If distinct classes share the earliest date, assign a multi-class tie rather than favoring CRC. Duplicate pairs within a class do not create a tie. Malformed/unpaired slots are audit failures, not events.

## 4. Full-cohort outcome and estimands

The source-D outcome for every U row has 11 mutually exclusive categories: CRC-E, CRC-I, CRC-L; other-cancer-E, other-cancer-I, other-cancer-L; non-cancer-E, non-cancer-I, non-cancer-L; no qualifying recorded event in W_i; and multi-class same-date tie at the earliest valid event. The main denominator is all U, not selected CRC cases. No qualifying recorded event combines no observed event with unavailable or unrecorded disease and is never called no disease. Intermediate events remain in the target even when an estimand contrasts E or I with L.

Source C has the analogous cancer-only outcome with CRC-E/I/L, other-cancer-E/I/L, no qualifying recorded cancer event and tie. It cannot manufacture a non-cancer outcome.

### Reserve and biomarker-functional decomposition

The inherited composite reserve is retained as the descriptive primary exposure. On training rows only:

- G: sex-stratified standardized maximum grip, max(46-0.0,47-0.0);
- A: log-transformed albumin, 30600-0.0;
- C: negative-log creatinine, 30700-0.0;
- Y: negative-log cystatin C, 30720-0.0.

Composite R is the mean of available standardized components, with component count and missingness retained. Training-derived Q25 and Q75 are used only after fitting transformations.

The sharper pre-assessment control uses no unbound field. Laboratory reserve R_lab is the mean of available standardized A, C and Y, with laboratory count and missingness. Functional reserve R_grip is G, with grip availability. The biomarker-control model contains R_lab, R_grip, their prespecified product, component counts/missingness, and the same age, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year and history variables. Missing values are training-median imputed with missingness indicators; this is a computational rule, not evidence that a biomarker was normal.

Because U requires three of four components, each row has at least one measurable domain. The audit reports exactly how many rows have at least two lab components and/or grip. The primary full-cohort estimand remains all U. Domain-conditional contrasts are reported only if support gates pass. A secondary residual check fits, on training rows only, grip as a function of R_lab, age, sex, BMI, smoking and assessment year; the cross-fitted residual is not called a new clinical biomarker and is used only to ask whether a functional signal remains after measured laboratory state.

For model m, let p_m(g,b,z) be the standardized probability of source-D category g-band b after setting the specified reserve representation z to a training-derived low or high value and averaging over the fixed supported distribution of locked-test covariates, history and missingness. No test outcome is used.

For composite R:
T_m(g,E-L) = [p_m(g,E,Q25)-p_m(g,L,Q25)] - [p_m(g,E,Q75)-p_m(g,L,Q75)].
T_m(g,I-L) = [p_m(g,I,Q25)-p_m(g,L,Q25)] - [p_m(g,I,Q75)-p_m(g,L,Q75)].

These are absolute probability contrasts among all eligible assessments. Positive means lower reserve is more associated with an earlier than a late recorded event. They are not risks, hazards, incidence, survival times, encounter probabilities or causal effects.

Primary specificity contrasts are:
- D_NC,I-L = T_CRC,I-L,D - T_non-cancer,I-L,D;
- D_OC,I-L = T_CRC,I-L,D - T_other-cancer,I-L,D;
- D_comp,I-L = T_CRC,I-L,D - 0.5(T_non-cancer,I-L,D + T_other-cancer,I-L,D);
- D_C,I-L = T_CRC,I-L,C - T_other-cancer,I-L,C.

Report all T values, both E-L and I-L contrasts, class-band probabilities, denominators and the full outcome flow. The key biomarker control reports D_comp,I-L under the lab-plus-grip model, plus conditional R_lab-low/high-at-fixed-grip and R_grip-low/high-at-fixed-lab contrasts. These feature-setting contrasts are descriptive, not independent causal effects.

Primary support requires all nine source-D class-band cells have at least 100 participants overall and 20 per split; source-C CRC and other-cancer E/I/L cells each have at least 30 overall and nonempty splits; each history state has at least 30 U participants overall and 10 per split; and low/high support overlaps every required cell. One locked fallback may combine H2 and H3 as recent if it passes the same gates. No class or lag is merged after estimates are seen.

Support requires all gates, D_comp,I-L, D_NC,I-L, D_OC,I-L and D_C,I-L positive with 95% intervals excluding zero, and H_spec,I-L = D_C,I-L - D_comp,I-L within a prespecified [-0.05,+0.05] consistency band. The E-L contrast may be positive, but E-L alone is not supportive of a persistent CRC-specific warning. The band is a decision threshold, not clinical equivalence.

## 5. Pre-assessment history, adjustment and model comparison

Define source-D history before post-assessment scanning from valid non-cancer 41270/41280 pairs in [1900-01-01,b_i): H0 no pair; H1 latest pair at or before b_i-730 days; H2 exactly one unique recent date in (b_i-730,b_i); H3 at least two unique recent dates there. Retain raw unique-pair count, recent unique-date count and days since latest pair. These are dated recorded-history descriptors, not encounter counts, healthcare-contact intensity or completeness scores.

Use one deterministic participant split, assigning all rows for an eid together: hash eid with seed 1414 into 70% train, 15% validation and 15% locked test. No event construction, preprocessing or tuning uses test outcomes. Transformations, imputation, splines, Q25/Q75, residuals and hyperparameters use train/validation only.

The adjustment ladder is an output:
- M0: age spline, sex, BMI, smoking and assessment year;
- M1: M0 plus composite R, component count/missingness and coarse history count;
- M2: M1 plus H0–H3, days since latest history date, recent unique-date count and reserve-by-history terms;
- M3, the primary rival control: M2 non-reserve covariates plus R_lab, R_grip, their product, and domain missingness/count indicators.

B0 is a transparent additive multinomial logistic model for the 11-category full-cohort outcome. It uses prespecified age-spline terms, main effects, reserve-by-band/class interactions, reserve-by-history terms and the M3 domain decomposition; no outcome-driven interaction search is allowed. It is the primary explanatory baseline because coefficients and standardized contrasts show how specificity changes after measured history and laboratory/functional separation.

B1 is a shallow gradient-boosted multinomial model on exactly the same U rows, outcome categories, features and participant split as B0. Its fixed validation grid is 200/400 trees, depth 2/3 and learning rate 0.03/0.05. It can reveal reproducible reserve thresholds or reserve-by-history-by-class nonlinearities that an additive form misses. It is not justified by a small prediction gain alone. Select by validation multiclass log loss and Brier score only; evaluate locked-test log loss, Brier score, class-band calibration and all D, H_spec, temporal and domain contrasts. If B1 changes the specificity decision, inspect its prespecified feature-grid interaction summaries; do not call them mechanisms.

CPU is selected for the future solver: approximately 4–8 cores, 16–32 GiB RAM and up to 2.5 hours for selected-column reads, parsing, fits, locked evaluation and 500 bootstrap replicates. This is a planning estimate, not a measured fit. A GPU is not required for this 502,370-row tabular comparison; it would not supply missing encounter or stage evidence. Revisit a neural or multi-omics alternative only after a validated molecular/clinical linkage exists or B1 reveals a reproducible nonlinear pattern that an adjudicated study can test.

The actual deliverable is newly fitted, output-linked evidence: immutable source/schema/hash audit; U flow and event/tie counts; E/I/L support; history and reserve-domain support; locked B0/B1 predictions and calibration; M0–M3 contrasts; composite, lab-controlled and functional-residual contrasts; source concordance; 500-eid bootstrap intervals; fixed falsification checks; and a conclusion naming those output files. This proposal contains no fitted result.

## 6. Uncertainty, source concordance and falsification

Use 500 participant bootstrap replicates from the locked test set, sampling eids and preserving participant-level split membership. Recompute standardized contrasts and percentile 95% intervals; report failed replicates. Bootstrap uncertainty does not correct missing clinical ascertainment.

Before fitting, emit an audit containing every source path/hash/table ID, namespace, required column, same-slot parseability, malformed/unpaired values, duplicates, pre-assessment exclusions, first-event ties, reserve-domain availability, history support, U flow, outcome counts, split counts, source concordance and confirmation that 20191-0.0 was unused for follow-up.

Lock these checks before results:
- Occult-proximity: report E-L, I-L and fixed 180/365/730-day alternatives. A large CRC E-L contrast that attenuates to null for I-L after M3 is adverse to an independent persistent warning and compatible with reverse causation or early ascertainment.
- Biomarker decomposition: compare composite, lab-domain and grip-domain contrasts. Attenuation after separate lab control is evidence of dependence on measured physiology, not proof that occult CRC caused it. A residual grip pattern is not a mechanism.
- Generic recordability/comorbidity: if non-cancer or other-cancer I-L contrasts are similar to CRC, or D_comp,I-L is near zero, the signal is generic. Strong M2 attenuation favors the measured-history rival.
- Source concordance: retain all-U CRC capture categories O0 neither source, O1 source D only, O2 source C only, O3 both first dates within 30 days, O4 both differing by more than 30 days. Recompute paired contrasts under exact dates and a predeclared +/-30-day concordance rule. Material H_spec, opposite source directions or capture gradients are adverse.
- Temporal/calendar boundary: repeat near cutoffs 180, 365 and 730 days and late cutoff 1460 days; report assessment-year strata if support passes. An effect confined to one shortest window or calendar period is a boundary/ascertainment finding.
- Measurement: compare complete-four with minimum-three rows, grip-only, laboratory-only, composite, missingness strata and the residual check. Instability is measurement dependence, not proof of a mechanism.
- Class permutation: once, within history state and lag band, permute class labels among eligible first-event rows with a locked seed. A comparable CRC specificity contrast after permutation invalidates class construction or inference.
- Source permutation: permute source labels only among paired eligible CRC records. A reproducible source contrast after permutation invalidates the source comparison.
- Calendar audit: preserve assessment-year adjustment and event-year/assessment-year cross-tabs; never treat 20191-0.0 as an end date.

Supportive results require all gates, positive primary I-L contrasts with intervals excluding zero, source consistency, no material capture gradient, no generic comparator match, no permutation signal, acceptable calibration and a signal beyond the shortest window. They support a reproducible association between reserve-domain state and timing/class of recorded CRC transitions across the two source streams. They do not establish occult disease, true onset, screening benefit, causal reserve effect or a clinical decision rule.

Adverse results include comparator-matched contrasts, M2/M3 attenuation, an early-only or lab-sensitive CRC effect, source/date heterogeneity, capture gradients, measurement instability or permutation signal. These favor generic recordability, comorbidity, reverse causation/proximal physiology, source/date artifact or coding error and should abandon the CRC-specific warning interpretation.

Inconclusive results include failed support gates, sparse domain/history cells, wide intervals spanning both decision regions, failed calibration/bootstrap, unresolved parsing or contradictory source coverage. An imprecise null is not refutation. No lag, class, subgroup or fallback rule may change after viewing estimates.

## 7. Clinical limits and deferred directions

This design observes first valid recorded code/date, not disease onset. It cannot distinguish an occult tumor from a new diagnosis, a diagnosis encounter from an administrative date, screening/referral from routine care, or an unrecorded event from no event. It lacks symptoms, screening participation, referral, healthcare-contact intensity, stage, histology, treatment, mortality, encounter-level dates, complete observation boundaries and clinical adjudication. No surviving association identifies a biological mechanism.

The Olink/multi-omics direction and expert-seed branches remain deferred, not rejected as biologically uninteresting: no validated molecular CRC endpoint, stage/treatment outcome or compatible crosswalk to the ukb672073 eid namespace is bound here. They cannot be added to this child without changing population or namespace. Revisit requires a verified crosswalk and an adjudicated molecular/clinical endpoint with observation dates. An external or linked register study is required to distinguish true onset, stage and healthcare contact.

## 8. Three inspected works

[K1] Mathew D, Lane H, Ward D, Saunders R, Millar L, Etherton-Beer C. “Development and application of a frailty index derived from patient-reported outcome measures and comorbidities in oncology patients.” Internal Medicine Journal, 2026. DOI 10.1111/imj.70599. Abstract-only inspection. It supports clinical relevance of a frailty construct but does not establish prediagnostic CRC timing or recordability.

[K2] Chen G et al. “Age-dependent cytokine surge in blood precedes cancer diagnosis.” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2025. DOI 10.1073/pnas.2420502122; PMID 40117305; PMCID PMC11962427. Abstract-only inspection. It supports a prediagnostic systemic-physiology rival, but not this reserve, CRC specificity, UKB coding or healthcare contact.

[K3] Lu SSM et al. “Prediagnostic Prescription Antibiotics Use and Survival in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Swedish National Register-Based Study.” Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 2023. DOI 10.1158/1055-9965.epi-23-0340; PMID 37490284; PMCID PMC10543975. Abstract-only inspection. It bounds the additional stage, treatment and register provenance needed for stronger prediagnostic CRC claims.

key-references.json records receipt hashes. Attached UTF-8 provider snapshots are K1-mathew-2026-epmc.json, K2-chen-2025-epmc.json and K3-lu-2023-epmc.json. They contain Europe PMC metadata/abstract responses; no inaccessible full text or supplementary method is claimed.

# Within-person reserve change versus baseline reserve for recorded CRC timing

Status: proposed independent substantive child of `candidate-b83ae091e4d4f83fa628b4de`; no scientific fit or outcome estimate has been run. The only observed result below is a bounded repeat-field support audit.

## 1. Scientific opening, supported claim and unresolved hypothesis

The parent established a sharper recorded-event question: in a full cohort with a valid 2006–2010 UKB assessment, baseline reserve can be compared with the lag and class of a first subsequently recorded diagnosis, while other cancer and non-cancer recorded diagnoses provide specificity controls. That source-bound observation does not establish incidence, disease onset, encounters, symptoms, screening, referral, stage, treatment, mortality, mechanism, causality or clinical utility. The strongest evidence outside this dataset also bounds the question rather than answering it. [K1] shows that frailty-like constructs can be clinically relevant after cancer diagnosis, but not that pre-assessment reserve changes predict CRC timing. [K2] makes a serious reverse-causation rival plausible because systemic physiology can change before cancer diagnosis. [K3] shows the stage, treatment and register provenance needed for stronger prediagnostic CRC interpretation, none of which is bound here.

The remaining clinically important boundary is whether a subsequent within-person decline or stability pattern contributes information beyond a low or high baseline snapshot. This matters because the next clinical decision differs: a stable low reserve could mark longstanding vulnerability or generic recordability, whereas a decline close to a recorded CRC could be a proximal preclinical signal—or simply selection into a repeat assessment and variable measurement interval. The available repeat fields permit a bounded test of the *recorded-timing* version of that boundary.

Hypothesis H_change: after baseline reserve, dated pre-baseline recorded history, demographic/health covariates, repeat-observation selection and repeat interval are accounted for, an annualized decline in reserve between the baseline and matched instance-1 repeat assessment is associated with a larger CRC-than-comparator contrast in the intermediate-versus-late lag of the next recorded event. The decline signal must remain after separating laboratory and grip slopes, and must not be explained by repeat selection, interval length, source capture or a generic non-cancer/other-cancer pattern.

This is a falsifiable descriptive/transported association hypothesis. It is not a causal claim that changing reserve causes cancer or that a decline is a screening rule.

The leading rival explanations make different predictions:

1. Occult preclinical timing/reverse causation: decline is concentrated near the repeat assessment and the earliest post-repeat recorded event, especially in laboratory measures; it attenuates in the intermediate-versus-late comparison or after excluding/flagging records between baseline and repeat. This would be adverse to an independent warning interpretation, although the available records cannot prove occult disease.

2. Assessment selection and generic recordability: participants who return for repeat assessment, or whose records contain later diagnoses, differ in baseline health, prior recorded history and observation practices. Decline should predict repeat availability and comparator timing similarly; inverse-selection standardization should materially change the estimate. A CRC-minus-comparator contrast near zero favors this explanation.

3. Measurement interval/construct artifact: slope is partly a function of the long and heterogeneous interval (observed matched-panel median 1,617 days) or of field-specific missingness and repeat protocol. The signal should vary with interval, component availability and laboratory-versus-grip construction. A complete-case or interval-adjusted result that is unstable is not evidence of biology.

4. CRC-specific recorded timing compatible with a clinically useful warning: the CRC intermediate-versus-late contrast remains after these controls, exceeds both comparator tilts, replicates in the paired cancer source, and is not an early-only or capture-dependent result. That would support reproducible information in the recorded trajectory, not true onset, mechanism or clinical utility.

## 2. Bounded repeat-field verification

The configured snapshot is `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`, catalog SHA-256 `6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea411220157f0adedf32`. A read-only managed CPU audit read only the selected Assessment Center, Biological Samples and Population Characteristics Parquet columns and wrote `repeat-support-audit.json` (output SHA-256 `be79c5178e61d2a699f75c1e0c543556015a772e51144803676a89752446ac7e`). It took 7.36 seconds. It did not read outcomes or compute an association.

The audit found on the parent’s eligibility proxy (467,867 rows) that:

- 18,856 had a nonmissing `53-1.0` repeat date;
- 18,785 had repeat grip (`46-1.0` or `47-1.0`);
- 16,577 had at least two of `30600-1.0`, `30700-1.0`, `30720-1.0`;
- 16,523 had all three repeat ingredients before interval filtering;
- 16,504 had a repeat date strictly after baseline, 30–3,650 days apart, repeat grip and at least two repeat lab values;
- among valid repeat dates, the median interval was 1,617 days, the interquartile range 1,351–1,803 days, and no row was in the 30–730-day interval; 14,616 were 731–1,825 days and 4,238 were beyond 1,825 days.

These counts are not event counts and do not establish that instance 1 is a clinically identical visit across tables. Therefore the primary trajectory is the matched instance-1 panel, with the instance number and date retained; later `53-2.0/3.0` dates and later grip fields are a secondary grip-only description, not silently joined to missing lab repeats. No 30–730-day repeat stratum will be invented. The future fit must recompute all counts after exact paired-event construction, cancer-free-through-repeat restriction, and split assignment.

## 3. Exact source bindings and read-only limits

All joins below are `eid`-only within the `ukb672073` namespace. No UKB-671626, Olink or dta identifier is joined. All Parquet sources are ordinary files with no archive member; the original CSV table and the frozen Parquet derivative are not both read. Source files are read-only; audit, fitted models, predictions, bootstrap samples and reports are derived workspace files.

The `20191-0.0` field is retained only as an explicitly unused provenance audit. It is not a censoring date, observation boundary, healthcare-contact measure, completeness denominator or event-free guarantee. Same-slot code/date pairing is mandatory: `40005[j]` with `40006[j]`, and `41270[j]` with `41280[j]`. Unpaired, malformed or neighboring-slot-repaired values are not events.

## 4. Population and two outcome clocks

### Baseline full cohort U

Construct U before scanning post-assessment events:

- one unique `eid`;
- parsed `53-0.0` in 2006-01-01 through 2010-12-31;
- valid `31-0.0`, `21022-0.0`, `21001-0.0` and `20116-0.0`;
- at least three available baseline components among maximum grip (`46-0.0`, `47-0.0`), albumin (`30600-0.0`), creatinine (`30700-0.0`) and cystatin C (`30720-0.0`);
- no observed valid paired C00–C97 code/date on or before `53-0.0` in either outcome source.

This is not cancer-free in biology, not a complete population denominator and not a guarantee of follow-up.

For every U participant, source D’s primary baseline outcome is the first valid event in (b_i,b_i+1825], with early E (0<L≤365), intermediate I (365<L≤730), and late L (730<L≤1825). Categories are CRC-E/I/L (C18/C19/C20), other-cancer-E/I/L (C00–C97 excluding C18–C20), non-cancer-E/I/L (every other valid source-D ICD code), no qualifying recorded event, and a same-date multi-class tie. No event is not no disease. Source C has the analogous CRC/other-cancer cancer-only outcome and cannot create a non-cancer outcome. The first event is selected by date after exact pair parsing; class ties are retained.

The full-cohort baseline estimands are absolute standardized probability contrasts. For reserve representation (z), let T^0_{g,I-L}(z) = p(Y^0=g, I | z)-p(Y^0=g, L | z), and define the specificity contrasts (Delta^0_{NC}=T^0_{CRC,I-L}-T^0_{NC,I-L}), (Delta^0_{OC}=T^0_{CRC,I-L}-T^0_{OC,I-L}), and (Delta^0_{comp}=T^0_{CRC,I-L}-0.5(T^0_{NC,I-L}+T^0_{OC,I-L})). Report early-versus-late as a prespecified reverse-causation diagnostic. These are recorded-event probability contrasts, not incidence, hazards, or causal effects.

### Matched repeat landmark panel R

R is a subset of U requiring:

- a parsed `53-1.0` = r_i strictly after b_i, with 30 ≤ r_i-b_i ≤ 3650 days;
- at least one repeat grip value among `46-1.0`, `47-1.0`;
- at least two of `30600-1.0`, `30700-1.0`, `30720-1.0`;
- no observed valid paired C00–C97 event in either source in (b_i,r_i].

The last condition creates a recorded-event landmark, not a disease-free cohort. Its support, reasons for exclusion and outcomes between baseline and repeat are reported separately; conditioning on it can be a selection/collider problem.

For R, the repeat outcome (Y^1) is the first exact-paired source-D event in (r_i,r_i+1825], using the same CRC, other-cancer, non-cancer, no-event and tie categories and early/intermediate/late windows. Source C repeats the cancer-only outcome. This separate clock prevents the repeat measurement from being treated as a baseline predictor of an event that preceded it. It does not repair incomplete follow-up.

Secondary descriptive analyses use later grip fields `46/47-2.0/3.0` and dates `53-2.0/3.0` only when exact instance-specific fields are present; because the lab table exposes only instance-1 repeats for the primary components, these later records are not joined into a purported full reserve trajectory.

## 5. Reserve trajectory, estimands and selection transport

On training rows only, standardize the same four baseline components as the parent: sex-stratified maximum grip (G), log albumin (A), negative-log creatinine (C), and negative-log cystatin C (Y). Baseline (R_0) is their mean when at least three components are present. Repeat (R_1) uses the same transformation and requires repeat grip plus at least two repeat lab components. # Within-person reserve change versus baseline reserve for recorded CRC timing

Status: proposed independent substantive child of `candidate-b83ae091e4d4f83fa628b4de`; no scientific fit or outcome estimate has been run. The only observed result below is a bounded repeat-field support audit.

## 1. Scientific opening, supported claim and unresolved hypothesis

The parent established a sharper recorded-event question: in a full cohort with a valid 2006–2010 UKB assessment, baseline reserve can be compared with the lag and class of a first subsequently recorded diagnosis, while other cancer and non-cancer recorded diagnoses provide specificity controls. That source-bound observation does not establish incidence, disease onset, encounters, symptoms, screening, referral, stage, treatment, mortality, mechanism, causality or clinical utility. The strongest evidence outside this dataset also bounds the question rather than answering it. [K1] shows that frailty-like constructs can be clinically relevant after cancer diagnosis, but not that pre-assessment reserve changes predict CRC timing. [K2] makes a serious reverse-causation rival plausible because systemic physiology can change before cancer diagnosis. [K3] shows the stage, treatment and register provenance needed for stronger prediagnostic CRC interpretation, none of which is bound here.

The remaining clinically important boundary is whether a subsequent within-person decline or stability pattern contributes information beyond a low or high baseline snapshot. This matters because the next clinical decision differs: a stable low reserve could mark longstanding vulnerability or generic recordability, whereas a decline close to a recorded CRC could be a proximal preclinical signal—or simply selection into a repeat assessment and variable measurement interval. The available repeat fields permit a bounded test of the *recorded-timing* version of that boundary.

Hypothesis H_change: after baseline reserve, dated pre-baseline recorded history, demographic/health covariates, repeat-observation selection and repeat interval are accounted for, an annualized decline in reserve between the baseline and matched instance-1 repeat assessment is associated with a larger CRC-than-comparator contrast in the intermediate-versus-late lag of the next recorded event. The decline signal must remain after separating laboratory and grip slopes, and must not be explained by repeat selection, interval length, source capture or a generic non-cancer/other-cancer pattern.

This is a falsifiable descriptive/transported association hypothesis. It is not a causal claim that changing reserve causes cancer or that a decline is a screening rule.

The leading rival explanations make different predictions:

1. Occult preclinical timing/reverse causation: decline is concentrated near the repeat assessment and the earliest post-repeat recorded event, especially in laboratory measures; it attenuates in the intermediate-versus-late comparison or after excluding/flagging records between baseline and repeat. This would be adverse to an independent warning interpretation, although the available records cannot prove occult disease.

2. Assessment selection and generic recordability: participants who return for repeat assessment, or whose records contain later diagnoses, differ in baseline health, prior recorded history and observation practices. Decline should predict repeat availability and comparator timing similarly; inverse-selection standardization should materially change the estimate. A CRC-minus-comparator contrast near zero favors this explanation.

3. Measurement interval/construct artifact: slope is partly a function of the long and heterogeneous interval (observed matched-panel median 1,617 days) or of field-specific missingness and repeat protocol. The signal should vary with interval, component availability and laboratory-versus-grip construction. A complete-case or interval-adjusted result that is unstable is not evidence of biology.

4. CRC-specific recorded timing compatible with a clinically useful warning: the CRC intermediate-versus-late contrast remains after these controls, exceeds both comparator tilts, replicates in the paired cancer source, and is not an early-only or capture-dependent result. A first paired ICD code/date is a recorded event, not onset. Absence of a code is not absence of cancer. Conditioning on repeat assessment and no recorded cancer through the repeat can induce selection. No association surviving these checks identifies a mechanism or causal effect. [K3] Lu SSM et al. “Prediagnostic Prescription Antibiotics Use and Survival in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Swedish National Register-Based Study.” Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 2023. Do not read the corresponding CSV sources as well, and do not join UKB-671626, Olink, dta, genomics, or unbound clinical sources.

### Required new computation

The solver must produce, at minimum:

1. `/workspace/results/manifest.json`: runtime input targets, source hashes, table IDs, columns read, namespace, software/runtime versions, split seed, and actual row/field counts.
2. `/workspace/results/cohort_flow.json`: U and R construction flow, exclusions, repeat-selection strata, baseline-to-repeat event counts, missingness, interval distributions, and source/date parse audit.

# Full-cohort recorded-CRC specificity with a gated instance-1 reserve trajectory

Status: substantive crossover successor of `candidate-be2d73bd0508251fa8cbf015` and `candidate-28c77cf68b97ec3d05953fa4`. This is a source-bound, unfitted design. The repeat audit is readiness evidence only; no association, model fit, or clinical conclusion is claimed.

## 1. Scientific opening and falsifiable hypothesis

The strongest supported claim is limited: in an eligible UKB assessment cohort, baseline reserve can be compared with the timing and class of a subsequently *recorded* first diagnosis, using same-source non-cancer and other-cancer records as specificity comparators. The full-cohort design makes “no qualifying recorded event” and same-date class ties explicit rather than selecting only CRC cases. This does not establish incidence, true onset, encounter timing, symptoms, screening, referral, stage, treatment, mortality, mechanism, causality, or clinical utility.

The unresolved claim is whether a verified repeat reserve measurement at Assessment Center instance 1 adds information about the CRC-versus-comparator recorded-timing contrast beyond a baseline reserve snapshot. A stable low baseline may represent longstanding vulnerability or generic recordability. A within-person decline might be a proximal prediagnostic signal, but it might instead reflect repeat-assessment selection, a long and heterogeneous measurement interval, field-specific missingness, or disease already being recorded between assessments.

Hypothesis H_change: among the baseline-eligible cohort, the CRC-versus-comparator contrast in the lag of the next recorded event is larger for participants with a lower annualized reserve change between baseline and a verified instance-1 assessment than for participants with a higher change, after baseline reserve, dated pre-baseline recorded history, interval, repeat-selection variables, and laboratory-versus-grip slope decomposition are accounted for. The trajectory contrast must remain for the repeat-landmark outcome after the repeat clock begins, must exceed non-cancer and other-cancer comparator tilts, and must not disappear under prespecified selection, interval, source-concordance, or reverse-timing checks.

This is a descriptive recorded-event hypothesis. It is not a claim that reserve decline causes CRC, identifies occult disease, measures onset, or is a warning rule.

[K1] supports the clinical relevance of measuring frailty-like reserve in oncology but is post-diagnosis and does not test prediagnostic recorded timing. [K2] makes prediagnostic systemic change a serious reverse-causation rival, but does not validate these UKB fields or distinguish onset from first record. [K3] bounds stronger prediagnostic CRC interpretations by showing the value of register provenance and outcome context unavailable here. This crossover adds a separate post-repeat outcome clock, explicit selection tests, and a decision rule for deferring the trajectory claim when support is inadequate.
