## Feature construction and leakage controls

Construct all feature selection, category levels, medians, scaling, and model fitting separately within each outer training fold. Select the top 30 analyte keys by distinct eligible training-stay coverage, subject to at least 1% training-stay coverage. If fewer than 30 meet the rule, retain all and report the number. Never select analytes from held-out hospitals.

For V features, use age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight, and the latest finite numeric value per selected analyte in [0,360]. Do not carry values from outside the window. Impute a missing value with the training-fold analyte median; missingness is intentionally represented only in process models. Preserve unknown categories as explicit levels and learn category handling in training.

For aligned process P, add per-analyte result-present indicators, valid-result count, distinct-result-offset count, first and last valid-result offsets, overall valid-lab row count, and overall distinct-offset count. Counts use only rows meeting both result and revision timing rules. P represents observed result documentation/measurement, not confirmed testing orders.

For the temporal alternative, use three bins [0,120], (120,240], (240,360]. For each selected analyte and bin, use the last valid value, presence indicator, and valid-result count, plus the same static predictors. Fit a fixed elastic-net logistic model; training-fold medians and category rules only. This preserves temporal order that latest-value VP-GBM loses, while keeping process and value channels explicit.

A timing audit must verify that no source row with result or revision offset >360 enters any primary feature. A code-level manifest must show that discharge fields, hospital id/metadata, Apache fields, diagnosis, notes, therapies, and post-landmark events are absent from model matrices.

## Models and method alternatives

The simple additive baseline is V-Logit: elastic-net logistic regression with static predictors and 30 latest imputed values, fixed alpha and regularization chosen before fitting. It is transparent and tests whether conclusions depend on a familiar additive value model.

The parent’s capacity-matched nonlinear ablation is primary: V-GBM is a fixed histogram gradient-boosting classifier with only V; VP-GBM is the identical implementation, seed, preprocessing, class-weight policy, and hyperparameters with aligned P added. The paired VP-GBM minus V-GBM contrast is the main process attribution comparison. No held-out metric selects a model.

The scientifically substantive temporal/mechanistic alternative is T-Logit, not a generic larger neural model: separate 120-minute value/process channels test whether chronology and delayed documentation carry information lost by latest-value summaries. It can reveal whether an apparent process effect is concentrated in early versus late measurement and whether value trajectories explain the internal advantage. It is intentionally not used to rescue an unfavorable VP result.

A temporal neural sequence model was considered and deferred. It could preserve every event ordering and nonlinear interaction, but the available lab table lacks order/specimen/collection semantics, so it would learn the same ambiguous observation process with less attribution clarity. Revisit it only if T-Logit and VP-GBM show a reproducible timing signal and a readiness check demonstrates adequate events per hospital. This is a selection/deferral decision, not a categorical rejection of neural or GPU methods.

## Split and estimands

First retain hospitals with at least 100 eligible primary-cohort stays, using no outcomes or laboratory features. If fewer than five such hospitals remain, stop as infeasible. Sort hospital IDs by SHA-256 of eicu-transport-v2 + NUL + hospitalid and assign contiguous hospitals to five folds by greedy balancing of eligible stay counts. All stays from a hospital remain in one outer fold.

Within each outer training set, an internal 20% reference sample is selected by a deterministic hash of uniquepid, stratified only using training labels and grouped so all stays of an included patient are together. It is a reference for internal performance, not external validation. The primary transport estimand compares the same fitted model on this internal reference with its held-out hospitals.

For model m, define AUC deterioration D_AUC(m)=AUC_internal(m)-AUC_external(m). Define Brier deterioration as Brier_external(m)-Brier_internal(m), and calibration deterioration as the increase in absolute calibration-slope error externally versus internally. The primary paired process contrast is D_AUC(VP-GBM)-D_AUC(V-GBM); secondary paired contrasts use Brier and slope. Report direct held-out VP-GBM minus V-GBM metrics and per-hospital paired values.

Compute AUROC (primary discrimination), AUPRC, Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, reliability summaries without site recalibration, and decision-curve net benefit at 5%, 10%, and 20%. The modeled action is trigger senior review/goals-of-care and monitoring review, not a treatment recommendation. Use a hospital-cluster bootstrap with 2,000 resamples, preserving all predictions within sampled hospitals, for 95% intervals. Report event prevalence, fold/hospital counts, and effective hospital sample sizes; no patient bootstrap is the sole uncertainty method.

## Prespecified negative controls and time-shift falsification

### Within-hospital process permutation

Within every hospital in each outer training fold, randomly permute the complete aligned P vector across eligible stays, preserving that hospital's process distribution and the marginal analyte/event counts while breaking its patient-level alignment with V and Y. Use a recorded seed and permutation manifest. Fit the same VP-GBM to V plus P-permuted. For held-out hospitals, apply an independent within-hospital permutation to P before prediction, using no labels. This is a diagnostic, not a selected model.

If P-permuted retains internal signal and loses it at held-out hospitals, that is evidence that a hospital/process distribution can mimic an apparent patient process effect. If P-permuted loses incremental signal while aligned VP-GBM retains held-out value, the patient-state rival is strengthened. If both are unstable or intervals are wide, call the distinction inconclusive. This control does not prove a hospital mechanism because the same process vector can encode residual case mix.

### Time-reversal placebo

Within [0,360], replace each retained event offset t with 360-t before calculating first/last offsets and the three temporal-bin features; keep patient, analyte, numeric value, revision eligibility, and event count unchanged. Refit/predict the prespecified reversed-P and reversed-T diagnostics with no retuning. A large loss only for timing-sensitive features supports a chronology-dependent observation pattern; unchanged performance says timing order is not needed for the observed association. Neither result identifies why a test was obtained.

### Future-window positive leakage control

For stays with unitdischargeoffset >720, build a separate 360–720-minute process feature vector using rows with result offset in (360,720] and revision offset <=720. Fit the same fixed learner only as a code audit. Its predictions and metrics must never enter the primary cohort, model comparison, bootstrap, or conclusions. A large signal is expected because it is post-landmark and confirms why the 360-minute boundary matters; any accidental use of this feature in a primary model is a readiness failure. This is the required time-shift/label-timing falsification check, not evidence supporting the clinical hypothesis.

## Interpretation rules, limitations, and missing evidence

Supportive of documentation/workflow dependence: the primary paired deterioration contrast is positive with its 95% interval excluding zero, VP-GBM has worse held-out calibration or net benefit at at least two thresholds, and the permutation/time-reversal pattern is consistent with hospital-distribution or timing sensitivity. State only that observed process signals are transportability liabilities consistent with documentation dependence.

Adverse: VP-GBM is at least as transportable and useful, or its held-out advantage is retained while P-permuted collapses; this favors stable patient-state information or another explanation and revises the documentation claim. It does not prove biological stability.

Inconclusive: intervals span zero, too few hospitals/events, repeat-patient exclusion or analyte selection makes the cohort unstable, primary and negative-control patterns disagree, or calibration and discrimination point in different directions without a prespecified utility interpretation.

Remaining unidentifiable evidence includes test orders, specimen collection, canceled orders, interface outages, clinician rationale, bedside acuity not measured in labs, care pathways, end-of-life decisions, and a death timestamp. Hospital-held-out folds do not randomize testing practice and cannot eliminate case-mix or selection bias. Clinical adjudication is required to interpret individual missing results and workflow causes. Prospective silent deployment, external data with order/interface fields, and an impact study are required before clinical use.

## Feasibility, compute, and selection record

Measured bounded diagnostic: direct header/hash verification completed in 1.49 seconds and the first 100,000 lab rows were summarized in 1.08 seconds on the discovery shell. These are not full-study runtime measurements.

Unverified solver planning estimate: CPU only, 16 CPUs, 64–128 GiB RAM, and 2–6 hours for full lab feature extraction, five hospital folds, three primary models, negative controls, and 2,000 hospital-bootstrap replicates; reserve within the parent’s stated 8-hour/16-CPU/256-GiB planning envelope. V-Logit/T-Logit should fit in minutes to under an hour; V/VP-GBM and feature extraction dominate. No GPU is required because this is a tabular, fixed-feature experiment; an allocated GPU is not prohibited but would not resolve the missing order/documentation semantics. A future readiness job must measure one fold and confirm memory before full execution.

Selected T-Logit because it tests a substantive temporal explanation at low, inspectable cost. Deferred temporal neural sequence model because it requires a larger, less interpretable representation while the key missing dependency is clinical event semantics, not model capacity. Revisit only under the rule above. No result from either model is claimed here.

## Three inspected works

[K1] Rajkomar et al. reports multi-center mortality prediction with rich sequential EHR data. It supports the feasibility and importance of cross-center prediction, but not a testing-process mechanism. This child adds a prespecified patient-process ablation, hospital-held-out transport estimand, and negative controls.

[K2] Gao et al. reports predictive value of missing indicators and cautions that missingness shifts can impair transportability. It is single-institution CLABSI work; this child tests an ICU mortality outcome across held-out eICU hospitals and separates aligned from within-hospital-permuted process.

[K3] Hadler et al. reports external mortality validation despite fragmentation and improved local adaptation, with calibration and data-availability burdens. It does not isolate laboratory process or patient state; this child measures unadapted transport and explicitly avoids causal interpretation.

## Evidence attachments

The three inspected source excerpts and their structured receipts are attached as:

- work/episode2-evolution/K2-gao-2026-inspected-excerpt.txt
- work/episode2-evolution/K3-hadler-2026-inspected-excerpt.txt

The exact source binding and bounded diagnostic are attached as:

- work/episode2-evolution/bounded-schema-timing-diagnostic.md

Source excerpts are labeled provider/full-text extractions rather than claimed copies of unavailable original PDFs. Private source rows were not sent to public search.


## Harbor runtime contract

This readiness package preserves the frozen candidate above. The candidate is the scientific specification; no favorable result is supplied. The frozen receipt is copied byte-for-byte to `package/key-references.json`; its three inspected source excerpts remain private supporting evidence from the selected candidate and are not solver inputs. For a completed study, `results.json` must set `study_status` to `complete`, identify the primary outcome and estimand, list every required model and negative control, and link each conclusion to existing computed files. Each conclusion must be classified as `supportive`, `adverse`, or `inconclusive`, state the relevant estimate and uncertainty, and remain within the descriptive prognostic transportability estimand. A conclusion of “supportive” is not required: adverse and inconclusive outcomes are valid scientific results.

# Working proposal: discordant kidney recovery after ICU AKI

Status: Lead design for episode 2 repair; proposed Harbor experiment, not executed results.

## Scientific deliverable

The future Harbor solver must newly construct an index-ICU-stay cohort and fit two prespecified analyses on the same eligible population:

1. A transparent, standardized logistic-risk analysis estimating the 7-day risk difference between discordant and concordant recovery, with uncertainty and sensitivity analyses.
2. A substantive temporal alternative that fits a patient-level-split masked sequence model on the same pre-landmark data, then reports held-out calibration, Brier/AUROC, and the same discordant-versus-concordant risk contrast.

Completion requires a cohort flow and cell counts, phenotype definitions, adjusted risk difference with confidence interval, secondary outcome estimates, sensitivity/negative-control results, and model-comparison outputs linked to saved computed files. A readiness probe or a favorable-looking coefficient is not completion.

## Unresolved clinical question and hypothesis

After an ICU patient develops creatinine-defined AKI, clinicians may infer recovery when serum creatinine falls. The unresolved question is whether that inference is unsafe when urine output and recorded fluid balance do not improve at the same time.

Hypothesis: among adults with a first eligible ICU stay who develop creatinine-defined AKI, survive and remain in the ICU to a fixed 48-hour post-onset landmark, and show a prespecified creatinine fall, patients with low primary-set urine output or positive recorded-net-volume proxy at that landmark have a higher 7-day risk of hospital death or ICU-recorded incident kidney-replacement therapy than patients with both urine recovery and non-positive fluid balance. The primary estimand is the standardized prognostic risk difference, discordant minus concordant recovery.

This tests a falsifiable association. It does not claim that discordance causes death, that positive balance proves hemodilution or congestion, or that the patient has measured persistent renal dysfunction. The clinically consequential decision it could inform is whether a falling creatinine alone should be sufficient for de-escalating renal monitoring or transition planning after AKI. The result would be hypothesis-generating for a monitoring/intervention study, not a bedside rule.

## What is supported versus unresolved

The strongest inspected evidence supports three bounded propositions. Creatinine can overestimate measured kidney function after prolonged critical illness, in association with muscle loss [K1]. Urine output thresholds and their time windows materially alter prognostic discrimination when combined with creatinine, including in MIMIC-IV, but that work studies AKI staging rather than recovery discordance [K2]. Positive fluid balance around ICU AKI is associated with AKI and mortality in a prospective external cohort, although it is confounded by illness and treatment severity [K3].

The unresolved claim is narrower and new for this design: within a fixed post-AKI survivor landmark, does a creatinine fall accompanied by low charted urine output or positive charted net balance identify a reproducibly higher-risk recovery phenotype than creatinine plus physiologic recovery? Existing evidence does not establish that such a phenotype is present in this MIMIC snapshot, that its mechanism is dilution, muscle loss, congestion or tubular injury, or that changing treatment improves outcomes. [K1] is small and abstract-only here; [K2] does not establish mechanism or a treatment threshold; [K3] does not study this recovery comparison.

## Population, time origin and exclusions

Use the read-only MIMIC-IV 3.1 archive:

- source: [private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip
- source SHA-256: 0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09
- dataset snapshot: 5126591f768df4f9d981d97d94329fd65f78a1a0e1eb7cab0332454f888ab8b6
- catalog: [private-path]/completed-data.json
- catalog SHA-256: 9bc20153591045e19e908fc0b538d04a950f2fe75b85ba99c8de1fb3b2d750be

Select adults (hosp/patients.anchor_age >=18) and the first ICU stay per hospital admission, linked by (subject_id, hadm_id). Exclude invalid ICU intervals and admissions without a usable creatinine series. Define t0 as the earliest creatinine observation within 72 hours after icustays.intime that satisfies a KDIGO-like biochemical onset rule: at least 0.3 mg/dL above a creatinine value in the preceding 48 hours or at least 1.5 times the minimum valid value in the preceding 7 days. If no prior value supports the rule, use a separately labeled admission-baseline sensitivity; do not silently invent baseline. Exclude anyone with established RRT before t0.

Require survival and ICU presence through tL=t0+48 hours and a latest valid creatinine observation in [t0+36h,tL]. No exposure-defining record may have clinical time after tL. tL is the exposure landmark; do not use data after tL in exposure construction or baseline adjustment. The 7-day outcome window is [tL, tL+7 days), truncated at ICU end, hospital discharge or death as appropriate. Patient-relative timestamps are required because MIMIC deidentification preserves within-subject intervals but invalidates cross-subject calendar alignment.

Primary urine output uses only numeric mL values from the audited bedside set (226559 Foley, 226560 Void, 226561 Condom Cath, 226563 Suprapubic, 226567 Straight Cath), converted to mL/kg/h using the nearest valid weight at or before tL, requiring weight within 48 hours. Nephrostomy (226564/226565), OR/PACU urine (226627/226631), and mixed GU-irrigant channels (226566/227489) are excluded from the primary phenotype and labeled sensitivities. Exclude text estimate itemid=226713 and Apache-derived itemid=227519. Net balance is a recorded input-volume proxy minus direct urine output over [tL-24h,tL], retaining item-level composition, excluded/non-mL fractions and a missingness indicator. “Fluid improvement” is non-positive recorded net volume, never a claim about true fluid status. CVP is exploratory, never a validated fluid-status gold standard.

## Exposure phenotypes

Find the peak valid creatinine in [t0,tL] and define creatinine recovery as peak minus landmark creatinine >=0.3 mg/dL. A ratio sensitivity is landmark/peak <=0.8. Neither means normal kidney function.

Define urine recovery as >=0.5 mL/kg/h during [tL-24h,tL]. Among patients with creatinine recovery and complete primary physiology data:

- concordant recovery: creatinine recovery + urine recovery + net balance <=0;
- discordant creatinine-only recovery: creatinine recovery + low urine output or positive net balance;
- exploratory three-level phenotype: low urine only, positive balance only, both.

Patients without creatinine recovery are a descriptive reference group, not part of the primary discordant-versus-concordant contrast. Report all exclusions and missingness before outcome comparisons.

## Outcomes and analysis

Primary outcome Y7d is hospital death or first ICU-recorded incident RRT in [tL,tL+7d), using admissions.deathtime/hospital_expire_flag and procedureevents RRT items; do not count RRT before tL. Do not truncate hospital follow-up at ICU outtime; alive hospital discharge is censoring/competing event. Because procedureevents does not cover ward-only RRT, label the component ICU-recorded RRT and report a no-pre-tL-RRT sensitivity. Secondary outcomes are death alone, ICU-recorded RRT alone, ICU readmission during the same admission, and hospital death by dischtime. Report component-specific cumulative incidence and handle discharge/competing events descriptively or with cause-specific models; the composite is primary to avoid selecting a favorable competing-risk convention.

Primary estimand:
RD = P(Y7d=1 | discordant) - P(Y7d=1 | concordant)
among eligible creatinine-recovery patients. Fit a prespecified logistic model with restricted cubic splines or carefully bounded linear terms for age, baseline creatinine, AKI stage at t0, peak creatinine, recorded CVP, observation density and recorded-volume proxy, plus sex, admission type, and pre-landmark treatment/support summaries and missingness indicators. All adjustment is pre-tL; do not adjust for post-tL mediators or outcome proxies. Standardize predictions over the observed eligible population to obtain RD and percentile/bootstrap confidence intervals. Do not interpret adjustment as causal identification. Sensitivity analyses vary creatinine item (50912 versus 50912+52546), baseline window, urine item set, weight age, urine threshold (including K2-informed lower thresholds), balance scale, exclusion of early dialysis, and complete-case versus explicit missingness handling.

Falsification and integrity checks are prespecified:

- The direction and clinically relevant magnitude must persist across assay, urine-source, baseline, weight, recorded-volume, discharge/competing-event and missingness sensitivities to support a reproducible phenotype.
- A null with a confidence interval spanning clinically meaningful harm is inconclusive, not proof of no misclassification.
- If the association disappears after observation-density adjustment or is driven by missing weights/recording intensity, the leading clinical interpretation is not supported.
- A model using post-tL measurements, outcome proxies, or cross-patient leakage fails.
- A positive adjusted association does not establish hemodilution, congestion, intrinsic tubular injury, treatment effect or mechanism.

## Baseline versus substantive learned alternative

The simple baseline is the primary scientific analysis: fixed tL summaries of creatinine peak/slope, urine rate, net balance, weight, CVP, support/RRT, observation counts and missingness, fit with standardized logistic risk. It preserves interpretability and directly estimates the phenotype contrast.

The learned alternative is a masked temporal model over 6-hour bins from t0-24h through tL. Each bin includes creatinine, urine volume/rate, input/output volume, weight, CVP, RRT/support indicators and missingness/measurement-count channels. It targets the same Y7d outcome and uses patient-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test splits; all stays from a subject remain in one split. Compare calibration slope/intercept, Brier score, AUROC and held-out standardized phenotype contrast, with bootstrap uncertainty. A sequence can reveal whether the order and joint trajectory of creatinine, urine and balance contain information lost by the fixed-window baseline. It cannot identify mechanism.

Selection/deferral: retain the baseline as primary even if the learned model predicts better. Fit the learned model only if both phenotype cells have adequate event support and repeated measurements are sufficient; otherwise defer it. Revisit the learned branch only if it improves calibration or reveals a robust trajectory interaction replicated in held-out data, not for a small AUROC gain. GPU use is optional. A CPU tabular/sequence fit is expected to be feasible; the larger learned run is an unverified estimate of 4-16 CPU cores, 16-64 GB RAM, and 1-6 hours, or one allocated A100 for 1-3 hours if sequence batching is the bottleneck. These are planning estimates, not measured episode results. The solver envelope is 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB, up to 8 GPUs and 28,800 seconds; discovery itself used no GPU and did not train a model.

## Interpretation

Supportive result: a stable, clinically nontrivial excess 7-day risk in discordant recovery, with adequate cell support and calibration, would justify prospective validation of enhanced renal monitoring and an adjudicated study with measured GFR/biomarkers. It would still be a prognostic association.

Adverse result: no excess risk, reversal, or disappearance after adjusting observation intensity would weaken the claim that creatinine-only recovery identifies a clinically important discordant state and would redirect work toward other recovery measures. It would not prove creatinine is valid or that fluid/urine management is harmless.

Inconclusive result: sparse cells, wide intervals, unstable thresholds, or substantial unmeasured missingness would mean the available MIMIC data cannot resolve the question. It would justify a measurement study, not a favorable conclusion.

The configured data cannot adjudicate true measured GFR, cystatin-C discordance, tubular injury, true total-body volume, medication-versus-fluid intent, ward-only RRT, clinician intent, goals of care, complete urine collection, reliable pre-ICU baseline kidney function, or causal treatment effects. Those require additional biomarker/physiology data, chart adjudication, prospective monitoring, or external validation.

## Disposition of demonstrations and unused seed directions

- Delphi-2M/natural-history: inspected article text and methods guidance. A structured temporal model is a useful methodological analogue, but its UKB/Danish longitudinal population and disease-token task are not a reproduction target here; this proposal adapts only the idea that ordering can be tested against a fixed summary baseline.
- Oncoformer/cancer: only the supplementary material was available; the main article and complete STAR Methods were not inspected. Its chest-X-ray modality is unavailable in this MIMIC snapshot, so no multimodal claim is pursued. A lab/time-series adaptation would be a different question and is deferred.
- ALADYNOULLI/Bayesian: inspected article text and methods guidance. Its genetics, multi-biobank signatures and latent disease-hazard objective are not available or necessary for this acute ICU question; a latent trajectory model would not distinguish the proposed clinical rival better than the predeclared masked sequence alternative, so it is deferred.
- Other imported MIMIC seeds (asynchronous organ recovery, diuretic timing, antimicrobial de-escalation, glucose stress, sedation, lactate, transfusion, discharge instability and congestion) remain context. This episode selects AKI recovery because the exact creatinine/urine/fluid bindings and a non-causal falsifiable comparison are strongest. The antimicrobial and diuretic seeds need treatment-confounding and source-control adjudication; the cystatin/measured-GFR dependency in the AKI seed is unavailable but does not block this bounded prognostic adaptation.

Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2023;18(8):997-1005. doi:10.2215/cjn.0000000000000203. Abstract-only inspection; full-text acquisition failed.

[K2] Machado GD, Santos LL, Libório AB. Redefining urine output thresholds for acute kidney injury criteria in critically Ill patients: a derivation and validation study. Crit Care. 2024;28:272. doi:10.1186/s13054-024-05054-3. Full-text XML passages inspected.

[K3] Melo FAF, Burdmann EA, Macedo E, Mehta R, Zanetta DMT. Acute kidney injury developed in the intensive care unit: a population-based prospective cohort study in the Brazilian Amazon. Sci Rep. 2024;14:22954. doi:10.1038/s41598-024-74177-y. Full-text XML passages inspected.

Supporting evidence files and receipts: work/key-references.json; work/evidence/haines-2023-provider-excerpt.json.txt; work/evidence/machado-2024-derivation-excerpt.txt; work/evidence/melo-2024-fluid-balance-excerpt.txt.


## Episode 2 schema-audit repairs incorporated

The independent bounded schema/header audit found all listed archive headers matched their JSON schemas and verified the item labels/units. It identified and this child resolves: post-landmark creatinine leakage; mixed GU-irrigant contamination; input amount/totalamount double counting; blank labevents hadm_id risk; hospital follow-up incorrectly truncated at ICU end; and incomplete ward-RRT ascertainment. The audit also found storetime/charttime ordering anomalies, so documentation-time is a labeled sensitivity rather than an assumed availability truth. Fluid balance is explicitly a recorded-volume proxy requiring item-level composition and excluded/non-mL reporting. The audit was metadata/header/dictionary work only; no cohort or scientific result was executed.

# Harbor task: discordant kidney recovery after ICU AKI

This is an open-ended, readiness-mode research task. The proposal is frozen by the
Lead; do not replace its population, time origin, estimand, outcome, baseline,
alternative, or falsification criteria with a convenient prediction benchmark.
No scientific result has been supplied. A passing readiness check is not a result.

## Scientific question and deliverable

After an ICU patient develops creatinine-defined acute kidney injury (AKI), a fall
in serum creatinine can be interpreted as recovery. The unresolved question is whether
that interpretation is unsafe when urine output and recorded fluid balance do not
improve at the same time.

Hypothesis: among adults in a first eligible ICU stay who develop creatinine-defined
AKI, survive and remain in the ICU to a fixed 48-hour landmark, and have a prespecified
creatinine fall, patients with low primary-set urine output or positive recorded-net-
volume proxy at the landmark have higher 7-day risk of hospital death or ICU-recorded
incident kidney-replacement therapy (RRT) than patients with both urine recovery and
non-positive recorded balance. The primary estimand is the standardized prognostic
risk difference (RD), discordant minus concordant recovery.

This is an association hypothesis, not a causal claim. It does not say that discordance
causes death, positive recorded balance proves hemodilution/congestion, a creatinine
fall proves normal kidney function, or a model identifies a treatment effect. The
clinical decision it could inform is whether a falling creatinine alone is sufficient
for de-escalating renal monitoring or transition planning after AKI. Even a supportive
result would be hypothesis-generating for prospective monitoring and intervention
studies, not a bedside rule.

The solver must newly construct the cohort and fit both prespecified analyses on the
same eligible population:

1. The primary transparent analysis: a standardized logistic-risk model estimating
   the 7-day RD with confidence interval, cohort flow, cell counts, phenotype
   definitions, secondary outcomes, and all declared sensitivities/falsification
   checks.
2. A substantive learned alternative, conditional on adequate event support in both
   phenotype cells and sufficient repeated measurements: a masked temporal model over
   6-hour bins from t0-24 hours through tL. It uses patient-level 70/15/15
   train/validation/test splits, keeping all stays from one subject in one split.
   Report held-out calibration slope/intercept, Brier score, AUROC, and the same
   standardized discordant-versus-concordant phenotype contrast with bootstrap
   uncertainty. A CPU-compatible masked sequence implementation is acceptable; GPU
   use is optional.

Completion requires saved computed outputs linked to the reported conclusions:

- a cohort flow and counts at every exclusion, including missingness and cell sizes;
- exact t0, tL, creatinine-recovery, urine, balance, and outcome definitions used;
- the primary adjusted RD, uncertainty, model specification and standardization
  population;
- death, ICU-recorded RRT, same-admission ICU readmission, and hospital-death
  secondary estimates, with competing-event/censoring handling described;
- assay, baseline, urine-source, weight-age, balance, early-RRT, documentation-time,
  observation-density and missingness sensitivities as applicable;
- negative-control/integrity checks and an explicit post-landmark/leakage audit;
- the learned-model held-out metrics and contrast only if its predeclared support
  and measurement conditions are met; otherwise report a reasoned deferral;
- a conclusion classified as supportive, adverse, or inconclusive, with each claim
  tied to a computed file, estimate and uncertainty.

Do not report a favorable conclusion merely because it confirms the hypothesis. A
correct computation with an unsupported clinical interpretation is incorrect.

## Evidence boundary and interpretation

The inspected evidence supports only bounded prior propositions. Creatinine can
overestimate measured kidney function during prolonged critical illness in association
with muscle loss [K1]. Urine-output thresholds and time windows can change prognostic
discrimination when combined with creatinine, including in MIMIC-IV, but that work
addresses AKI staging rather than recovery discordance [K2]. Positive fluid balance
around ICU AKI has been associated with AKI and mortality in a prospective external
cohort, with confounding by illness and treatment severity [K3].

The experiment tests the narrower unresolved claim: within a fixed post-AKI survivor
landmark, does a creatinine fall accompanied by low charted urine output or positive
charted balance identify a reproducibly higher-risk phenotype than creatinine recovery
with physiologic recovery? No prior work cited here establishes that this phenotype is
present in this MIMIC snapshot, its mechanism, or benefit from changing care.

Interpret results as follows:

- Supportive: a stable, clinically nontrivial excess risk in discordant recovery with
  adequate cells, calibrated estimates, and persistence across the declared
  measurement/observation sensitivities supports prospective validation of enhanced
  renal monitoring and an adjudicated study with measured GFR/biomarkers. It remains
  prognostic association evidence.
- Adverse: no excess risk, reversal, or disappearance after observation-intensity
  adjustment weakens the claim that creatinine-only recovery identifies an important
  discordant state. It does not prove creatinine is valid or fluid/urine management is
  harmless.
- Inconclusive: sparse cells, wide intervals spanning clinically meaningful harm,
  unstable thresholds, or substantial unmeasured missingness mean MIMIC cannot resolve
  the question. Report a measurement study as the next step, not a favorable null.

The data cannot adjudicate measured GFR, cystatin-C discordance, tubular injury, true
total-body volume, medication-versus-fluid intent, ward-only RRT, clinician intent,
goals of care, complete urine collection, reliable pre-ICU kidney baseline, or causal
treatment effects. These require additional biomarkers/physiology, chart adjudication,
prospective monitoring, or external validation. An association surviving adjustment
does not establish a mechanism.

send source rows or notes to public search tools.

## Cohort and temporal rules

Select adults (`patients.anchor_age >= 18`) and the first ICU stay per admission.
Exclude invalid ICU intervals and admissions without a usable creatinine series. Define
t0 as the earliest valid creatinine observation within 72 hours after `icustays.intime`
that is at least 0.3 mg/dL above a valid value in the preceding 48 hours or at least
1.5 times the minimum valid value in the preceding 7 days. If no prior value supports
that rule, preserve a separately labelled admission-baseline sensitivity; do not invent
a baseline. Exclude established RRT before t0.

Require survival and ICU presence through `tL = t0 + 48 hours` and a latest valid
creatinine in `[t0+36h,tL]`. No exposure-defining or baseline-adjustment record may
have clinical time after tL. The outcome window is `[tL,tL+7 days)`, with follow-up
through hospital discharge/death and ICU movement recorded rather than silently
truncated at ICU outtime.

For labevents, retain selected-subject rows whose clinical `charttime` lies in the
selected ICU interval even if `hadm_id` is blank; when present, matching `hadm_id`
prevents cross-admission assignment. Keep documentation-time (`storetime`) checks as
a labelled sensitivity, not as an assumption that documentation equals availability.

## Exposure phenotypes

Use peak valid creatinine in `[t0,tL]`. Creatinine recovery means peak minus landmark
creatinine >= 0.3 mg/dL; landmark/peak <= 0.8 is a ratio sensitivity. Neither means
normal kidney function.

Primary urine is numeric mL from only the audited bedside items: `226559` Foley,
`226560` Void, `226561` Condom Cath, `226563` Suprapubic, and `226567` Straight Cath.
Convert to mL/kg/h using the nearest valid weight at or before tL, requiring a weight
within 48 hours. Exclude from the primary phenotype and label sensitivity analyses for
nephrostomy `226564/226565`, OR/PACU urine `226627/226631`, mixed GU-irrigant channels
`226566/227489`, text estimate `226713`, and Apache-derived `227519`.

Urine recovery is >= 0.5 mL/kg/h over `[tL-24h,tL]`. Recorded net balance is a proxy:
administered recorded input volume minus direct urine output in that window. Apply one
mutually exclusive rule per input row: never sum `amount` and `totalamount` from the
same row. Use interval overlap, retain unresolved/non-mL fractions and item-level
composition, and include a balance missingness indicator. “Fluid improvement” means
only non-positive recorded net volume, never true total-body volume. CVP `220074` is
exploratory and not a fluid-status gold standard.

Among patients with creatinine recovery and complete primary physiology data:

- concordant: creatinine recovery, urine recovery, and recorded net balance <= 0;
- discordant creatinine-only: creatinine recovery plus low urine output or positive
  recorded net balance;
- exploratory three-level report: low urine only, positive balance only, both.

Patients without creatinine recovery are a descriptive reference group, not part of
the primary discordant-versus-concordant estimand. Report exclusions and missingness
before outcome comparisons.

## Outcomes and analysis

Primary `Y7d` is hospital death or first ICU-recorded incident RRT in `[tL,tL+7d)`,
using admissions death fields and procedureevents RRT items. Do not count RRT before
tL. RRT item IDs are `225441` hemodialysis, `225802` CRRT, `225803` CVVHD, `225805`
peritoneal dialysis, `225809` CVVHDF, and `225955` SCUF. The component is explicitly
ICU-recorded: procedureevents does not ascertain ward-only RRT. Secondary outcomes are
death alone, ICU-recorded RRT alone, same-admission ICU readmission, and hospital death
by dischtime. Report component-specific cumulative incidence and describe discharge as
a competing/censoring event; the composite remains primary.

Estimate
`RD = P(Y7d=1 | discordant) - P(Y7d=1 | concordant)`
among eligible creatinine-recovery patients. Fit a prespecified logistic model with
restricted cubic splines or bounded linear terms for age, baseline creatinine, AKI
stage at t0, peak creatinine, recorded CVP, observation density and recorded-volume
proxy, plus sex, admission type, pre-landmark treatment/support summaries, and
missingness indicators. Standardize predictions over the observed eligible population
and obtain percentile/bootstrap confidence intervals. Adjustment is prognostic
standardization, not causal identification; never adjust for post-tL mediators or
outcome proxies.

Prespecify sensitivities varying creatinine assay (`50912` versus `50912+52546`),
baseline window, urine item set, weight age, urine threshold (including a K2-informed
lower threshold), balance scale, exclusion of early dialysis, complete-case versus
explicit missingness, documentation time, observation density, and discharge/competing-
event handling. Save the exact analysis dataset specification and random seeds.

Falsification/integrity rules:

- Direction and clinically relevant magnitude must persist across the declared assay,
  urine-source, baseline, weight, balance, discharge/competing-event and missingness
  sensitivities to support a reproducible phenotype.
- A null whose interval spans clinically meaningful harm is inconclusive, not proof of
  no misclassification.
- If the association disappears after observation-density adjustment or is driven by
  missing weights/recording intensity, the leading clinical interpretation is not
  supported.
- Any post-tL measurement, outcome proxy, cross-patient leakage, or pre/post split
  contamination fails computational integrity.
- A positive adjusted association cannot be reported as hemodilution, congestion,
  intrinsic tubular injury, treatment effect, or mechanism.

## Baseline versus learned alternative and resources

The fixed-landmark summary baseline uses creatinine peak/slope, urine rate, recorded
balance, weight, CVP, support/RRT, observation counts and missingness. It is primary
because it is transparent and directly estimates the clinical phenotype contrast.

The alternative uses the same inputs in 6-hour bins from t0-24h through tL, with values,
missingness/measurement-count channels, and support indicators. It can reveal whether
the order and joint trajectory of creatinine, urine and balance contain information
lost by fixed summaries. It must be evaluated on held-out patient-level data using
calibration, Brier, AUROC and the same phenotype contrast with uncertainty. It cannot
identify mechanism. Retain the baseline as primary even if the learned model predicts
better; revisit the learned branch only for a replicated trajectory interaction or
calibration improvement, not a small AUROC gain. Defer it if support or repeated
measurements are inadequate.

The future solver envelope is 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB, up to 8 GPUs, and 28800 seconds.

for 1-3 hours if batching is a bottleneck, is unverified planning information. Ordinary

# Episode 2 evolution: audited first-recorded-TACE question

Status: repaired working proposal; no scientific model result has been computed. The source audits below are bounded observations used to repair feasibility and falsification, not evidence that the hypothesis is true.

## Scientific question and claim boundary

Among patients with a first locally recorded TACE in the HCC snapshot, does a post-index liver-state trajectory contain prognostic information for a second locally recorded TACE in days 43--180 beyond pre-index severity and the opportunity to observe the patient?

The testable claim is descriptive/predictive: among patients with an auditable exact-code index TACE and an observable outcome status, assay-specific state values and their ordered change during days 7--42 improve held-out prediction of a day-43--180 repeat exact-code TACE beyond pre-index severity and observation-process features.

The leading rival is a care-process explanation: patients who are sicker, scheduled for planned retreatment, or more intensively followed have more laboratories, examinations and encounters. Greater measurement opportunity can create both an apparent dynamic signal and a repeat procedure without a biological response signal. Repeat TACE is an operational endpoint, not tumor response, progression, treatment failure, or a causal effect of TACE.

[K1] supports retrospective biomarker associations after TACE but does not distinguish state from observation process. [K2] supports that HCC response requires viable-enhancement/necrosis assessment and that response criteria have practical limits; this record has no validated mRECIST/LR-TR labels. [K3] bounds the rival that surveillance signals can lag heterogeneous biology and should be adjunctive. The substantive advance is an exact-code, observation-complete, held-out state-versus-process test, not a reproduction of any demonstration paper.

## Bounded source audit

All HCC files are ordinary CSV files, with no archive member. Use snapshot 3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521 and source hashes in datasets/hcc/README.md and metadata.json.

These dated rows represented 1,169 patients. Every dated patient's first strict row matched an encounters composite key in the bounded join audit. One patient/start-time duplicate occurred; exact duplicate starts are deduplicated for event counting and retained in the audit. The bounded endpoint audit found 112/1,169 dated strict-index patients with a later strict TACE in days 43--180; this is a source audit, not a fitted result.

A broad TACE/化疗栓塞 substring scan matched 78,067 rows and 1,740 names. This demonstrates coding heterogeneity, not equivalence. Chinese synonyms and combined procedure strings are not mixed into the primary cohort.

# Hospital-held-out patient-state versus documentation-process signal in eICU

Status: complete proposal child of candidate-20566d681c807e69fae39170. No fitted study result is claimed. This is a design and data-binding audit, not an executed study.

## Scientific opening and unresolved claim

The inspected evidence supports three narrower claims, not the central mechanism. Rajkomar et al. [K1] show that broad sequential EHR representations can predict mortality across two medical centers. Gao et al. [K2] report that missing-indicator information can be predictive and caution that changing EHR missingness can harm transportability; the inspected evidence is abstract-only. Hadler et al. [K3] show that an external mortality model can retain discrimination while local EHR patterns and data availability improve local calibration/performance. None isolates a laboratory-result process channel from patient state in ICU mortality, and none identifies a causal effect of ordering, recording, or missingness.

The unresolved question is: among adult first eligible eICU ICU stays observed beyond six hours, does adding early laboratory-result presence, frequency, and timing to laboratory values create a hospital-held-out transport penalty because it encodes hospital/documentation process, or does it add patient-aligned information about latent acuity/care intensity that remains useful in another hospital?

Leading explanation: the process vector P contains hospital-specific measurement/documentation practice. Its apparent internal value will be less transportable than value-only features, including absolute risk calibration and a prespecified flagging policy.

Strong rivals are: (1) P is mainly a proxy for patient state or care intensity not captured by selected values, so aligned P retains held-out value and within-hospital permutation removes its patient alignment; (2) case mix, hospital severity, or the six-hour landmark creates the gap independently of documentation, so value-only models show a similar gap or the gap remains after P is permuted conditional on coarse value risk; and (3) timing/label artifacts drive the association, so a time-reversal placebo changes timing-dependent features.

The strongest available evidence supports predictive process sensitivity as plausible, not a documentation mechanism. The falsifiable claim is:

> The process-aware model has greater internal-to-hospital-held-out deterioration than the value-only model, and a process-permuted model that preserves hospital-specific P distributions and coarse observed-value state reproduces a material part of that deterioration.

This is a descriptive transportability claim, not a causal claim about testing or documentation.

## Clinical importance and decision boundary

A hospital-held-out process liability matters before silent deployment: a score can retain ranking but misstate absolute risk or trigger too many reviews when the receiving hospital records tests differently. A supportive result would justify site-specific measurement review, external calibration, and considering a value-only deployment specification. An adverse result would justify retaining process information only with prospective measurement validation; it would not prove biological stability.

The modeled action is a hypothetical flag for senior review/goals-of-care discussion and monitoring review. Thresholds 0.05, 0.10, and 0.20 are policy-scenario thresholds, not validated clinical decision thresholds. Net benefit is NB(t)=TP/N−FP/N×t/(1−t), with no assumed treatment benefit, harm, or resource valuation. These outputs describe alert/false-positive tradeoffs only; they cannot establish clinical utility, recommend treatment, or select a bedside threshold. Clinical adjudication and an impact study are required for those claims.

## Substantive design repair

The inherited proposal evaluated an internal 20% reference sample after fitting on the entire outer training hospitals. That makes its internal metric optimistic and can manufacture the internal-to-external deterioration used to support a documentation interpretation.

Repair: in each outer hospital fold, make a deterministic patient-grouped 80/20 split within outer training hospitals before feature selection or fitting. Fit each model only on the 80% development portion. Score the untouched 20% internal reference and held-out hospitals with that same fit, without recalibration. Feature selection, imputation medians, category levels, scaling, model fitting, and permutation strata are learned from the 80% development portion only. If the grouped split cannot be formed, stop rather than return an optimistic result.

A second bounded diagnostic sharpens the remaining rival. In addition to unconditioned within-hospital P permutation, permute P within hospital and five coarse bins of the fitted value-only V-GBM risk score. Bin cutpoints come from development predictions; cells under 10 are merged with an adjacent bin by a fixed rule. For held-out hospitals use development cutpoints and independently permute P within hospital-by-bin cells, without labels. This preserves hospital P marginals and coarse observed-value risk while breaking exact patient alignment. It does not remove unmeasured severity or prove workflow causality, but is more discriminating than unconditional permutation.

## Population, time zero, horizon, and outcome

Time zero is ICU admission; eICU offsets are minutes relative to ICU admission. Include a patient row only when patientunitstayid, uniquepid, hospitalid, unitdischargeoffset, and unitdischargestatus are nonmissing; unitvisitnumber=1; unitstaytype=admit; age parses numerically and is at least 18 (retain eICU >89 as adult); and unitdischargeoffset>360. Audit duplicate patientunitstayid rows. Exclude every uniquepid with more than one otherwise eligible primary stay in this snapshot, so a de-identified person cannot occur in development and a held-out hospital. Report the excluded-repeat count descriptively only. If uniquepid cannot support this grouping, stop as infeasible.

Y=1 is unitdischargestatus=Expired and Y=0 is a non-Expired ICU discharge. This is ICU-discharge mortality, not 24-hour or complete hospital mortality. Discharge fields are eligibility/label fields only. Join apachePatientResult by patientunitstayid to audit actualicumortality and report discordance descriptively; do not replace the primary label or use any Apache field as a feature. A discordance audit cannot create a death timestamp. The estimand is conditional on remaining under observation beyond 360 minutes and on first eligible admit stay.

## Exact data binding and revision handling

Retain hospitals with at least 100 eligible primary-cohort stays, using no outcome or laboratory feature; require at least five hospitals. Sort hospital IDs by SHA-256 of UTF-8 eicu-transport-v2 + NUL + hospitalid and assign contiguous hospitals to five folds by greedy eligible-stay balancing. All stays from a hospital remain in one outer fold.

Within each outer training set, select a deterministic patient-grouped 20% reference by uniquepid hash, with hospital representation and outcome strata only to stabilize prevalence; fit on the remaining 80%. Reference labels are not used in fitting, selection, threshold choice, or calibration. Record any deterministic small-cell merge and stop if the split cannot be formed.

Select up to 30 analyte keys by distinct development-stay coverage, requiring >=1% development-stay coverage. If fewer qualify retain all and report the number. Repeat selection separately in each outer fold using only development rows. V features are age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight and latest finite value per selected analyte in [0,360]. Impute missing values with development-fold medians and learn unknown category levels in development. P features are per-analyte presence, valid-result count, distinct-result-offset count, first/last valid-result offsets, overall valid-lab row count and overall distinct-offset count. P describes observed recording/measurement, not confirmed orders. No identifier, hospital/site field, discharge field, Apache field, diagnosis, note, treatment, or post-landmark event enters a model matrix.

T features use [0,120], (120,240], (240,360] and per analyte/bin last value, presence and valid-result count plus static predictors, with the same revision rule and development-only preprocessing.

For stays with unitdischargeoffset>720, a separate positive leakage audit may form a 360–720-minute P vector from labresultoffset in (360,720] and revision offset <=720. It never enters primary fitting, predictions, metrics, bootstrap or interpretation; any appearance in primary matrices is a readiness failure.

## Models, estimands, uncertainty, and outputs

V-Logit is fixed elastic-net logistic regression on V. V-GBM is a fixed histogram gradient-boosting classifier on V. VP-GBM is the identical learner, seed, preprocessing, class-weight policy and fixed hyperparameters on V+P. The primary process comparison is VP-GBM versus V-GBM. T-Logit is the prespecified temporal alternative.

Fit each model on the 80% development portion and predict both reference and held-out hospitals. No held-out metric selects a model or threshold. Define D_AUC(m)=AUROC_internal−AUROC_external; D_Brier(m)=Brier_external−Brier_internal; and D_slope(m)=absolute calibration-slope error_external−absolute calibration-slope error_internal. The main contrast is D_AUC(VP-GBM)−D_AUC(V-GBM); Brier, slope and policy-scenario net-benefit contrasts are secondary. Report direct held-out VP-GBM−V-GBM metrics and per-hospital paired values. Compute AUROC, AUPRC, Brier, calibration intercept/slope, reliability without site recalibration, and net benefit at 0.05/0.10/0.20. Use 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap replicates over paired hospital-level prediction contributions and report effective hospital counts; patient bootstrap alone is insufficient.

Unconditioned P permutation permutes complete P vectors within hospital in each development set, fits the same VP-GBM, and independently permutes P within hospital for reference/external prediction using recorded seeds/manifests. State-matched P permutation uses development-derived V-GBM risk-score quintiles; permute within hospital-by-bin cells, merge cells under 10 only by a fixed adjacent-bin rule, and independently apply the same rule without labels to reference/external hospitals. Time reversal replaces each event offset t with 360−t before first/last and T features, preserving analytes, values, revisions and counts; refit/predict without retuning.

The solver must output a frozen cohort/fold/development-reference manifest; V/P/V+P/T features; predictions for V-Logit, V-GBM, VP-GBM, T-Logit, both permutation controls and time reversal; seeds/manifests; prohibited-field/future-window audit; per-hospital metrics; bootstrap intervals; calibration and policy-scenario net-benefit tables; and an interpretation report linking every conclusion to exact computed outputs. Completion is these outputs with uncertainty, not a favorable result.

## Interpretation and unavailable evidence

Supportive of a documentation/workflow-consistent liability requires: positive primary process deterioration with a 95% cluster interval excluding zero in at least one primary metric; worse held-out calibration or net benefit for aligned VP-GBM at at least two policy thresholds; no equally large value-only deterioration; and state-matched permuted-P retaining a material development process signal or transport penalty while exact patient alignment is broken, without the pattern being solely time-reversal. This means only that observed process signals are transportability liabilities consistent with documentation dependence.

Adverse: aligned VP-GBM retains held-out incremental value and state-matched permutation collapses to V-GBM; this favors patient-aligned information or another explanation, not proof of biological stability. Inconclusive: intervals span zero, too few hospitals/events, unstable repeat exclusion or analyte selection, equal value-only deterioration, discordant controls, or incompatible discrimination/calibration/threshold patterns. A wide interval is imprecision, not refutation. Conclusions must cite prediction, metrics and bootstrap files; readiness is not evidence.

Unavailable evidence includes orders/cancellations, specimen collection time, interface outages, clinician rationale, unmeasured bedside acuity, care pathways, end-of-life decisions, death timestamp and complete narrative notes. Hospital-held-out folds do not randomize practice or eliminate case mix, severity, selection or measurement bias. Clinical adjudication, external order/interface data, prospective silent deployment and impact evaluation are needed for workflow, causal or clinical-benefit claims.

## Methods, compute, and alternatives

The selected study is CPU tabular. Readiness is one fold first, then plan 16 CPUs and 128–256 GiB within the 28,800-second/16-CPU solver envelope. Streaming the 516 MB compressed lab source, five outer fits, controls and manifests is estimated at 2–8 hours; the full estimate is unverified. Bootstrap replicates do not refit. GPU allocation is available but unnecessary: fixed tabular summaries do not require it and GPU capacity cannot supply absent event semantics.

V-Logit is the simple baseline and loses nonlinear interactions and chronology. VP-GBM is the substantive learned alternative with identical target/split/uncertainty; its information gain is value-by-process interaction, not a leaderboard gain. T-Logit uses explicit early/late bins with identical target/split/uncertainty and can reveal timing information lost by latest-value summaries at low inspectable cost. A neural event-sequence model is deferred because missing order/specimen/interface/rationale semantics make extra capacity uninformative for the key ambiguity; revisit only if T-Logit and time reversal show reproducible chronology and one-fold readiness shows adequate events per hospital. The detailed comparison and deferral record is method-alternatives.md. No model result is claimed.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Rajkomar et al. supports multi-center EHR mortality prediction and sequential representations, but not a laboratory-process mechanism. This proposal adds a hospital-held-out value/process ablation and falsification controls.

[K2] Gao et al. supports predictive missingness and transport risk from shifted EHR patterns, but is abstract-only and single-institution CLABSI work. This proposal tests the analogous eICU ICU-mortality question with state-matched permutation.

[K3] Hadler et al. supports the deployment importance of external calibration and data availability, but does not isolate workflow from patient state or case mix. This proposal makes that decomposition explicit while retaining an observational transport estimand.

Exactly three receipts and attached UTF-8 excerpts are in key-references.json and K1-rajkomar-2018-inspected-excerpt.txt, K2-gao-2026-inspected-excerpt.txt, K3-hadler-2026-inspected-excerpt.txt. Binding and matched-method audits are source-binding-audit.md and method-alternatives.md.

## Features, folds, and leakage controls

Retain hospitals with at least 100 eligible primary-cohort stays, using no outcome or laboratory feature; require at least five hospitals. Sort hospital IDs by SHA-256 of UTF-8 eicu-transport-v2 + NUL + hospitalid and assign contiguous hospitals to five folds by greedy eligible-stay balancing. All stays from a hospital remain in one outer fold.

Within each outer training set, select a deterministic patient-grouped 20% reference by uniquepid hash, with hospital representation and outcome strata only to stabilize prevalence; fit on the remaining 80%. Reference labels are not used in fitting, selection, threshold choice, or calibration. Record any deterministic small-cell merge and stop if the split cannot be formed.

Select up to 30 analyte keys by distinct development-stay coverage, requiring >=1% development-stay coverage. If fewer qualify retain all and report the number. Repeat selection separately in each outer fold using only development rows. V features are age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight and latest finite value per selected analyte in [0,360]. Impute missing values with development-fold medians and learn unknown category levels in development. P features are per-analyte presence, valid-result count, distinct-result-offset count, first/last valid-result offsets, overall valid-lab row count and overall distinct-offset count. P describes observed recording/measurement, not confirmed orders. No identifier, hospital/site field, discharge field, Apache field, diagnosis, note, treatment, or post-landmark event enters a model matrix.

T features use [0,120], (120,240], (240,360] and per analyte/bin last value, presence and valid-result count plus static predictors, with the same revision rule and development-only preprocessing.

For stays with unitdischargeoffset>720, a separate positive leakage audit may form a 360–720-minute P vector from labresultoffset in (360,720] and revision offset <=720. It never enters primary fitting, predictions, metrics, bootstrap or interpretation; any appearance in primary matrices is a readiness failure.

## Models, estimands, uncertainty, and outputs

V-Logit is fixed elastic-net logistic regression on V. V-GBM is a fixed histogram gradient-boosting classifier on V. VP-GBM is the identical learner, seed, preprocessing, class-weight policy and fixed hyperparameters on V+P. The primary process comparison is VP-GBM versus V-GBM. T-Logit is the prespecified temporal alternative.

Fit each model on the 80% development portion and predict both reference and held-out hospitals. No held-out metric selects a model or threshold. Define D_AUC(m)=AUROC_internal−AUROC_external; D_Brier(m)=Brier_external−Brier_internal; and D_slope(m)=absolute calibration-slope error_external−absolute calibration-slope error_internal. The main contrast is D_AUC(VP-GBM)−D_AUC(V-GBM); Brier, slope and policy-scenario net-benefit contrasts are secondary. Report direct held-out VP-GBM−V-GBM metrics and per-hospital paired values. Compute AUROC, AUPRC, Brier, calibration intercept/slope, reliability without site recalibration, and net benefit at 0.05/0.10/0.20. Use 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap replicates over paired hospital-level prediction contributions and report effective hospital counts; patient bootstrap alone is insufficient.

Unconditioned P permutation permutes complete P vectors within hospital in each development set, fits the same VP-GBM, and independently permutes P within hospital for reference/external prediction using recorded seeds/manifests. State-matched P permutation uses development-derived V-GBM risk-score quintiles; permute within hospital-by-bin cells, merge cells under 10 only by a fixed adjacent-bin rule, and independently apply the same rule without labels to reference/external hospitals. Time reversal replaces each event offset t with 360−t before first/last and T features, preserving analytes, values, revisions and counts; refit/predict without retuning.

The solver must output a frozen cohort/fold/development-reference manifest; V/P/V+P/T features; predictions for V-Logit, V-GBM, VP-GBM, T-Logit, both permutation controls and time reversal; seeds/manifests; prohibited-field/future-window audit; per-hospital metrics; bootstrap intervals; calibration and policy-scenario net-benefit tables; and an interpretation report linking every conclusion to exact computed outputs. Completion is these outputs with uncertainty, not a favorable result.

## Interpretation and unavailable evidence

Supportive of a documentation/workflow-consistent liability requires: positive primary process deterioration with a 95% cluster interval excluding zero in at least one primary metric; worse held-out calibration or net benefit for aligned VP-GBM at at least two policy thresholds; no equally large value-only deterioration; and state-matched permuted-P retaining a material development process signal or transport penalty while exact patient alignment is broken, without the pattern being solely time-reversal. This means only that observed process signals are transportability liabilities consistent with documentation dependence.

Adverse: aligned VP-GBM retains held-out incremental value and state-matched permutation collapses to V-GBM; this favors patient-aligned information or another explanation, not proof of biological stability. Inconclusive: intervals span zero, too few hospitals/events, unstable repeat exclusion or analyte selection, equal value-only deterioration, discordant controls, or incompatible discrimination/calibration/threshold patterns. A wide interval is imprecision, not refutation. Conclusions must cite prediction, metrics and bootstrap files; readiness is not evidence.

Unavailable evidence includes orders/cancellations, specimen collection time, interface outages, clinician rationale, unmeasured bedside acuity, care pathways, end-of-life decisions, death timestamp and complete narrative notes. Hospital-held-out folds do not randomize practice or eliminate case mix, severity, selection or measurement bias. Clinical adjudication, external order/interface data, prospective silent deployment and impact evaluation are needed for workflow, causal or clinical-benefit claims.

## Methods, compute, and alternatives

The selected study is CPU tabular. Readiness is one fold first, then plan 16 CPUs and 128–256 GiB within the 28,800-second/16-CPU solver envelope. Streaming the 516 MB compressed lab source, five outer fits, controls and manifests is estimated at 2–8 hours; the full estimate is unverified. Bootstrap replicates do not refit. GPU allocation is available but unnecessary: fixed tabular summaries do not require it and GPU capacity cannot supply absent event semantics.

V-Logit is the simple baseline and loses nonlinear interactions and chronology. VP-GBM is the substantive learned alternative with identical target/split/uncertainty; its information gain is value-by-process interaction, not a leaderboard gain. T-Logit uses explicit early/late bins with identical target/split/uncertainty and can reveal timing information lost by latest-value summaries at low inspectable cost. A neural event-sequence model is deferred because missing order/specimen/interface/rationale semantics make extra capacity uninformative for the key ambiguity; revisit only if T-Logit and time reversal show reproducible chronology and one-fold readiness shows adequate events per hospital. The detailed comparison and deferral record is method-alternatives.md. No model result is claimed.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Rajkomar et al. supports multi-center EHR mortality prediction and sequential representations, but not a laboratory-process mechanism. This proposal adds a hospital-held-out value/process ablation and falsification controls.

[K2] Gao et al. supports predictive missingness and transport risk from shifted EHR patterns, but is abstract-only and single-institution CLABSI work. This proposal tests the analogous eICU ICU-mortality question with state-matched permutation.

[K3] Hadler et al. supports the deployment importance of external calibration and data availability, but does not isolate workflow from patient state or case mix. This proposal makes that decomposition explicit while retaining an observational transport estimand.
