Do not use Apache scores, predicted/actual mortality, LOS, ventilation, or any other Apache field as a feature or replacement outcome.

All four sources are read-only. Do not modify or publish source rows. No other eICU table, archive member, clinical note, diagnosis, treatment, vital-sign, or ventilation field enters the primary matrices.

## Feature construction and leakage controls

Within each outer training partition, select at most 30 analyte keys by distinct-stay coverage in [0,360], requiring >=1% development-stay coverage. Selection is development-only and is repeated per outer fold. Fit all value scaling, category handling, medians, thresholds, and model parameters on development stays only.

For each selected analyte, derive from [0,360] the latest finite value, first and last valid offsets, valid-result count, distinct valid-result-offset count, and presence. Define a development-only robust scale as max(IQR, a fixed positive numerical floor). For analytes with an early value, derive a clipped robust-deviation component and, where at least two early values exist, a clipped first-to-last change component. Define the early lab-observed stress score `S` as the mean of available components across observed selected analytes, omitting an unavailable change component only and renormalizing weights. Do not use clinical reference ranges absent from eICU. Define high stress using the development 75th percentile of `S`, fixed for reference and held-out hospitals; retain continuous `S) in models.

The primary late exposure is `G=1` for zero valid lab-result rows in (360,720] and `G=0` for at least one. A secondary exposure uses the count of valid rows and distinct valid offsets with prespecified log1p scaling. Construct the complete late process vector from the selected analytes and overall late counts/offsets, but do not use late values as physiologic predictors unless explicitly recorded as process features in the prespecified matrix. No post-720 value, offset, revision, or process feature enters a primary matrix. Audit duplicate stay keys, missing joins, and future-window contamination.

## Hospital-held-out analysis

Retain hospitals with at least 100 dynamic-cohort stays based only on eligibility and early/lab availability, and require at least five hospitals. Use five greedy balanced outer folds with every hospital in one fold. Reproduce the parent’s frozen convention: sort hospital IDs by SHA-256 of UTF-8 `eicu-transport-v2` + NUL + `hospitalid), then assign contiguous hospitals greedily to balance eligible-stay counts. Record the exact fold manifest.

Within each outer training partition, form the deterministic patient-grouped 80/20 internal reference split before analyte selection, scaling, stress thresholding, fitting, or permutation. Group by `uniquepid); use only development for fitting and all preprocessing. Score the untouched internal reference and held-out hospitals without site recalibration. Record deterministic seeds and all manifests.

The simple baseline is an elastic-net logistic model using age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight, early latest values, early process counts/presence, continuous `S`, `G), and a prespecified high-stress-by-`G` interaction. It is the primary interpretable model-standardized contrast. The substantive learned alternative is a fixed histogram gradient-boosting classifier on the identical development rows, outcome, preprocessing, split, and uncertainty procedure, with `S), late process counts, and their nonlinear interaction available. The alternative is retained to reveal a clinically meaningful nonlinear stress-by-gap boundary that a logistic interaction can miss, not to chase a small leaderboard gain. A neural event-sequence model is deferred because the available sources lack order, specimen, interface, and clinician-rationale semantics; reconsider only if a bounded readiness fold shows sufficient repeated sequences and the simple/GBM timing pattern remains reproducibly unexplained.

For both models, report AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, calibration intercept/slope, calibration-in-the-large, per-hospital metrics, and standardized predicted-risk contrasts for `G=1) versus `G=0), separately by high/low stress. Report hypothetical monitoring-review net benefit at 0.10 and 0.20 only as alert tradeoffs; these are not validated clinical thresholds and no treatment benefit or test burden is assumed. Use 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap replicates with paired model/control contributions for 95% intervals; patient-only bootstrap is insufficient.

The primary contrast is the held-out high-stress standardized risk contrast minus the corresponding low-stress contrast, with the logistic interaction as transparent confirmation. The transport contrast is the difference between development-reference and hospital-held-out contrasts. Every interpretation must link to frozen predictions, contrast tables, metrics, and bootstrap files.

## Falsification, controls, and interpretation

The state-matched falsification reassigns complete late process vectors within hospital and development-derived early-stress quintile, preserving hospital process distributions and coarse early state while breaking patient-to-late-process linkage. Use a deterministic recorded seed and manifest, apply the same rule to reference and held-out predictions without using their labels, and report effective cell sizes. If a cell cannot support a nontrivial reassignment, preserve it as an identity control and report the affected cells; do not silently pool across hospitals or stress strata.

Supportive evidence for a patient-linked monitoring-gap pattern requires all of: (a) a positive held-out high-stress contrast with a 95% hospital-cluster interval excluding zero; (b) the high-minus-low interaction in the prespecified direction; and (c) attenuation toward the early-state model under the state-matched permutation. A model-only improvement without this pattern is insufficient.

The documentation/site rival is supported if the original held-out contrast is positive but the matched permutation retains a similar contrast, or if a process-only model transports similarly while early state adds little. That result motivates interface/workflow audit, not an alert or automatic testing.

An adverse result is a precise near-zero or negative high-stress contrast, no high-minus-low interaction, and no calibration or policy-scenario advantage for the gap flag. It would favor the broader transportability question or indicate that recorded-result density is not a useful dynamic decision marker; it would not prove testing is adequate.

The result is inconclusive when hospital/event counts are inadequate, the zero-result exposure is too sparse, analyte selection or the stress threshold is unstable, cluster intervals span clinically relevant values, the original and permutation controls disagree, or the label audit is materially discordant. A wide interval is imprecision, not refutation. Concentration in the 12–24-hour stay band is a selection/terminal-discharge warning, not evidence of benefit; duration-stratified analyses are sensitivity descriptions because duration is post-landmark and may be a collider.

All submitted conclusions must be supported by computed outputs and uncertainty. Correct computation cannot license causal, mechanistic, clinical-benefit, or “hypothesis confirmed” language.

## Required outputs and actual scientific deliverable

Write these paths under `/workspace/results/`:

- `cohort_fold_manifest.json`: cohort counts, exclusion counts, hospital eligibility, five-fold assignments, internal-reference assignments, seeds, and source hashes.
- `predictions.csv`: row-level held-out/reference predictions for baseline, learned alternative, and state-matched control with stay/hospital IDs, split, outcome, stress stratum, exposure, and model/control labels.
- `metrics.csv`: AUROC, AUPRC, Brier, calibration, per-hospital metrics, standardized contrasts, transport contrasts, and policy-scenario summaries.
- `bootstrap_intervals.csv`: 2,000 hospital-cluster paired bootstrap estimates and 95% intervals for the primary and secondary contrasts, with effective hospital counts.
- `interpretation.json`: supportive/adverse/inconclusive status, exact claims, uncertainty, evidence-file links, unavailable-evidence limits, and required next study.

The actual deliverable is newly fitted cross-hospital baseline and GBM models, the original and state-matched-permutation predictions, frozen cohort/fold/reference and feature manifests, uncertainty tables, leakage and Apache label audits, and a cautious interpretation. A readiness pass only checks imports, bindings, headers, and tiny synthetic logic; it does not execute the study or establish scientific truth.

## Unavailable evidence and follow-up

The configured data do not provide laboratory orders/cancellations, specimen collection time, interface outage/audit trail, missingness reason, vital signs, treatment/ventilation, clinician rationale, goals-of-care decisions, death time, complete notes, clinical reference ranges, or independent adjudication of whether a test was indicated. The patient discharge offset is not a death timestamp. Conditioning on 12-hour observation and early recording selects a survivor/measurement subset. Hospital-held-out folds do not randomize care or remove case mix, severity, treatment, terminal-decision, or interface bias.

A supportive retrospective result requires clinical review of sampled records plus external order/interface data, then prospective silent-alert validation and an impact study measuring mortality, false alerts, test burden, and harms. No bedside testing recommendation follows from this package alone.

## Compute and selection record

The planned solver envelope is 16 CPUs, 128–256 GiB RAM, and at most 28,800 seconds (8 hours), using CPU tabular extraction and fits; bootstrap replicates do not refit. The earlier 4-CPU/16-GiB availability diagnostic was discovery-only and its counts are not study results. The full 2–8 hour scan/fit estimate is unverified. The deployment exposes A100 GPUs, but no GPU is scientifically required for these fixed tabular summaries, and GPU capacity cannot supply absent clinical semantics.

The simple baseline is preferred for the primary interaction and transport contrast because it is transparent. The GBM is retained because its nonlinear stress-by-gap surface could reveal a clinically meaningful boundary that the baseline loses. A temporal binned logistic alternative is deferred unless timing remains unexplained; a neural event-sequence model is deferred for the missing-semantics reason above. Revisit those alternatives only with a bounded one-fold diagnostic showing adequate repeated event sequences and a reproducible residual chronology. Complexity, GPU use, and predictive gain are not evidence of clinical value.

## Compact bibliography

[K1] Rajkomar A, Oren E, Chen K, et al. “Scalable and accurate deep learning with electronic health records.” npj Digital Medicine. 2018;1:18. DOI: 10.1038/s41746-018-0029-1. Inspected abstract-only. Supports multi-center mortality prediction and temporal EHR representation; does not establish laboratory-process mechanism or intervention benefit.

[K2] Gao S, Albu E, Stijnen P, Rademakers F, Cossey V, Debaveye Y, Janssens C, Van Calster B, Wynants L. “Comparing methods for handling missing data in electronic health records for dynamic risk prediction of central-line associated bloodstream infection.” BMC Medical Research Methodology. 2026;26:128. DOI: 10.1186/s12874-026-02819-y. Inspected abstract-only via Europe PMC. Supports predictive/transport-sensitive information presence; does not establish ICU mortality, ordering behavior, or causality.

[K3] Hadler RA, Lakamana SK, Moorman T, Bozkurt S. “Testing Transferability of a Mortality Risk Model for Interhospital Transfer Using Real-World Electronic Health Records: External Validation and Model Enhancement.” Critical Care Explorations. 2026;8(9):e1442. DOI: 10.1097/CCE.0000000000001442. Inspected abstract and external-validation excerpt. Supports the importance of external validation, calibration, and local data availability; does not identify testing-process effects or distinguish causal monitoring mechanisms.

# Residual physiologic instability immediately before ICU discharge

Status: Lead-repaired Harbor proposal; planned experiment only. No cohort scan, model fit, or clinical result was run during discovery.

Parent: candidate-9952f4a2f3f7965944f4511f (itself a repair of expert seed candidate-42ec85fd895f7d68293404be). The prior selected AKI-recovery candidate-53d7d556112d78b21903acbd is contextual only; this is a distinct discharge-safety question.

## Scientific opening and unresolved hypothesis

ICU readmission or death soon after ICU dismissal is clinically consequential, but a discharge-time risk score does not show that a patient was discharged too early or that delaying discharge would help. [K1] supports the importance of discharge-time respiratory/neurologic impairment while explicitly leaving the intervention question open. [K2] shows that learned discharge-risk models can lose performance outside their development setting. [K3] shows that MIMIC measurements are modular, sparse and partly generated by care processes.

The strongest available claim is therefore only that discharge-time abnormalities can be prognostic in some cohorts. The unresolved, falsifiable claim is:

> Among adults discharged alive from an ICU to a non-ICU destination after at least 24 hours, persistent oxygen-support or repeated abnormal vital-sign bins in the final 24 clinical hours are associated with higher first-event risk of ICU readmission or hospital death within 48 hours than an observed-stable state, after adjustment for measured context and explicit tests of destination, treatment-limitation documentation and observation intensity.

This is prognostic, not causal or mechanistic. A positive result would motivate prospective discharge/monitoring studies; it would not prove that discharge timing caused the event.

## Actual scientific deliverable

The future Harbor solver must newly construct the eligible cohort and produce:

1. A flow table with every exclusion and exposure-state count.
2. An item-label/unit audit, four six-hour-bin feature table, and missingness/observation table.
3. Unadjusted and context-adjusted 48-hour cumulative-incidence estimates and standardized risk difference for persistent versus observed-stable states, with separate ICU-readmission and death outcomes and uncertainty.
4. A transparent fixed-summary baseline and a masked temporal alternative fitted on the same patient-level split, including held-out calibration, Brier score, discrimination, uncertainty and exposure-state risk summaries.
5. Destination, observed-code-status and observation-density sensitivities, plus supportive/adverse/inconclusive interpretation records linked to computed output files.

Readiness, a coefficient, AUROC, or favorable direction is not completion.

## Population, joins and temporal boundaries

Use the first valid ICU stay per hospital admission (earliest `icu/icustays.intime`) with `intime < outtime`, `los >= 1 day`, and `hosp/patients.anchor_age >= 18`. Join `icu/icustays` to `hosp/admissions` on `(subject_id, hadm_id)` and to `hosp/patients` on `subject_id`. Keep all admissions for one `subject_id` in one train/validation/test split.

Set the landmark `tL = icu/icustays.outtime`. Require the first `hosp/transfers` row with `eventtype='transfer'` and `intime >= tL` to have a non-ICU `careunit`; classify careunits containing ICU, CCU, CSRU, SICU or TSICU as ICU. ICU-to-ICU moves are excluded. Missing or unclassifiable immediate destinations are excluded from the primary cohort, counted in the flow table, and analyzed only in a labeled sensitivity using `hosp/admissions.discharge_location`. Destination is a context/selection variable, not the exposure.

Require `admissions.deathtime` to be null or strictly after `tL`. If `hospital_expire_flag=1` lacks a usable death time, timing is unresolved and the stay is excluded rather than reconstructed. Use patient-relative intervals because MIMIC timestamps are deidentified with within-person intervals preserved but cross-person calendar alignment invalid.

Primary features are limited to `[tL-24 hours, tL)`. For `icu/chartevents`, include only rows with `charttime < tL` and `storetime <= tL`; no post-landmark destination, discharge, death, later-stay or other outcome information is an input. Partition the window into four fixed six-hour bins. Measurements are summarized by clinical `charttime`; `storetime` is only an availability screen and a documentation-timing sensitivity.

## Verified residual-instability exposure

The primary item audit was inspected from `datasets/mimic/table-d1023acc404fd1d4.json` and the attached d_items extract. Use only these verified `icu/d_items` labels and IDs in `icu/chartevents`:

- 220045 Heart Rate (bpm)
- 220210 Respiratory Rate (insp/min)
- 220052 Arterial Blood Pressure mean and 220181 Non Invasive Blood Pressure mean (mmHg)
- 220277 O2 saturation pulseoxymetry (%)
- 223834 O2 Flow and 227287 O2 Flow (additional cannula) (L/min)

Do not use unverified FiO2 or oxygen-device item IDs in the primary or required sensitivity. If a future solver discovers an additional label, it must report it as exploratory and separately audited, not silently add it.

For each stream and bin, calculate median, count, valid-value mask and abnormality. Fixed, pre-outcome boundaries are HR <50 or >110 bpm; RR <8 or >25/min; MAP <65 mmHg; SpO2 <92%; and oxygen flow >=4 L/min. A bin is abnormal if any valid stream crosses a boundary; a respiratory-support bin is positive if either verified oxygen-flow item crosses its boundary.

Exposure states are: observed stable (at least 3 of 4 bins have all required streams, with no abnormal or support bin); persistent instability (at least 2 bins abnormal or support-positive); intermittent instability (exactly 1); and insufficient observation (fewer than 3 qualifying bins or no valid required stream). The primary contrast is persistent versus observed-stable. Keep intermittent and insufficient states visible; do not impute missingness to normal. Report component-specific burden and the number of qualifying bins.

## Outcomes and estimands

Follow from `tL` for 48 hours, bounded by same-admission `hosp/admissions.dischtime`. Define mutually exclusive first events:

- ICU readmission: a distinct subsequent `icu/icustays.stay_id` with the same `(subject_id, hadm_id)` and `tL <= intime < tL+48h`.
- Hospital death: `admissions.deathtime` in `[tL,tL+48h)), before any readmission.
- Alive hospital discharge before 48 hours: `dischtime < tL+48h`, with no earlier readmission or death.
- Event-free at 48 hours otherwise.

If death and readmission have identical recorded times, death is first by a fixed tie rule and the tie is reported. An expiration flag without death time is unresolved, not silently converted.

The primary estimand is the 48-hour cumulative incidence of composite readmission/death with alive discharge competing, and its standardized risk difference (persistent minus stable) over the eligible population. Secondary estimands are cause-specific cumulative-incidence contrasts for readmission and death. These are associations among ICU survivors discharged to non-ICU care, not treatment effects or principal-stratum effects.

## Baseline, alternative and method choice

The primary baseline is a transparent fixed-summary cause-specific competing-risk analysis using the four-bin summaries, exposure state, age, sex, admission type, ICU length of stay, first/last careunit, time from admission to ICU entry, qualifying-bin count and component burdens. Report crude risks before adjustment. Fit cause-specific first-event models or an equivalent multinomial first-event model, then standardize risks by exposure state. Use patient-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals with a fixed seed (target 1,000 resamples; if the solver envelope forces fewer, record the prespecified reduction).

The substantive alternative is a small masked temporal GRU-D-style model on the same four bins, with the same streams/context, value masks and time-since-last-observation, fit only on training patients, early-stopped on validation and evaluated once on a locked patient-level test set. It targets the same first-event states, not a different outcome. It can reveal ordering, persistence, co-movement and informative observation gaps that fixed medians/counts lose. The scientific comparison is whether those temporal features change persistent-versus-intermittent risk interpretation and held-out calibration, not whether a neural model wins a small AUROC. Report calibration slope/intercept, Brier, event-specific AUROC/AUPRC, calibration by exposure state/destination, patient-bootstrap or five fixed-seed uncertainty, and all seeds.

The baseline remains primary because its estimand is auditable. The temporal model is retained because it tests substantive information loss. A latent mechanistic model is deferred: the snapshot lacks adjudicated respiratory diagnoses, verified delivered-device settings, work-of-breathing assessments and reliable treatment intent. Future planning estimates, not measured discovery results, are 1–3 CPU hours for extraction/fitting, 2–4 additional CPU hours for bootstrap/artifact checks, and 2–6 hours on one allocated A100 for the small temporal model. The future envelope is 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB, up to 8 GPUs and 28800 seconds. No GPU or solver study was run here.

## Rival explanations, falsification and interpretation

Add the immediate non-ICU destination as a sensitivity. Add last eligible `chartevents` values for verified code-status IDs 223758 and 228687 only when text explicitly indicates DNR, DNI, comfort, hospice or no escalation; unknown remains unknown. This is a documentation proxy, not a goals-of-care adjudication. Compute vital/oxygen row counts, distinct bins and non-vital/non-oxygen chart counts in the same window. If the contrast attenuates with observation density or a process-only gradient is comparable, surveillance/recording is a stronger explanation.

Supportive evidence is a directionally consistent, clinically nontrivial persistent-versus-stable risk difference with uncertainty excluding a negligible range, persistence across destination/code-status strata, no comparable process-only gradient, and adequate calibration. Temporal improvement supports added ordered information only if held out and stable; it does not establish physiology or causality.

Adverse evidence is null/reversed or unstable contrast, risk concentrated in insufficient observation, attenuation after observation adjustment, disappearance within destination/code-status strata, or a temporal gain that fails held-out evaluation. This favors residual severity, discharge selection, treatment limitation or surveillance artifacts.

Inconclusive evidence is sparse events, wide intervals spanning meaningful harm, high missingness, unresolved timing, poor calibration, or inadequate strata. It warrants replication/measurement work rather than a favorable conclusion. True oxygen need, clinician intent, appropriateness of discharge, mechanism, causal benefit of delayed discharge, and transportability require expert adjudication, prospective monitoring/delay studies or an external hospital.

## Exact source bindings and archive provenance

Read-only source: `[private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip`, SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`.

Required archive members and schema files:

- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/icustays.csv.gz`, `datasets/mimic/table-7d5c8feb0fb0dbd4.json`: `subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,first_careunit,last_careunit,intime,outtime,los`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/admissions.csv.gz`, `table-e8ec3e6e4c428559.json`: `subject_id,hadm_id,admittime,dischtime,deathtime,admission_type,discharge_location,hospital_expire_flag`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/patients.csv.gz`, `table-9154f8c46cade9af.json`: `subject_id,gender,anchor_age,anchor_year,anchor_year_group,dod`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/transfers.csv.gz`, `table-685b6b74d0d7c547.json`: `subject_id,hadm_id,transfer_id,eventtype,careunit,intime,outtime`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/chartevents.csv.gz`, `table-8208609a785ea7e8.json`: `subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,caregiver_id,charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valuenum,valueuom,warning`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/d_items.csv.gz`, `table-d1023acc404fd1d4.json`: `itemid,label,abbreviation,linksto,category,unitname,param_type,lownormalvalue,highnormalvalue`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/outputevents.csv.gz`, `table-a7ad1c4cdcdbfe0a.json`: `subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,caregiver_id,charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valueuom`; optional observation-density sensitivity only.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/inputevents.csv.gz`, `table-d193e854c19eb4ba.json`, and `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/procedureevents.csv.gz`, `table-f6493e8403a0abe7.json`: available time fields are starttime/endtime/storetime; not primary exposure inputs and only allowed in declared, pre-landmark sensitivities.

Only documented identifier namespaces are joined: ICU-to-admission on `(subject_id,hadm_id)`, ICU-to-patient on `subject_id`, and subsequent ICU stays on `(subject_id,hadm_id)` with distinct `stay_id`. Do not join incompatible IDs or shifted calendar dates.

## Demonstration dispositions and deferred alternatives

- Natural-history/Delphi: the structured sequence idea is a bounded adaptation through the secondary masked temporal comparator on the verified ICU chart streams; no UKB trajectory reproduction or external Danish validation is claimed.
- Cancer/Oncoformer: the full multimodal image experiment is unavailable because local imaging payloads are absent; it is not used as a topic constraint. A lab-only adaptation is unnecessary for this discharge question.
- Bayesian/ALADYNOULLI: the latent trajectory idea was considered but deferred because mechanism-relevant clinical labels and genetic inputs are unavailable; adding latent complexity would not separate the stated rivals.

These are ordinary references, not evidence that this study has been executed. The other configured datasets remain directly accessible read-only but are outside this MIMIC-specific estimand.

## Key references

[K1] Gajic et al. (2008) establishes discharge-risk importance but not causality or this phenotype. [K2] Shi et al. (2022) bounds learned-model claims through external performance loss. [K3] Johnson et al. (2023) supports explicit missingness/process safeguards for MIMIC. The attached `key-references.json` and three UTF-8 excerpts are the only key-reference evidence package; all receipts/hash mappings are preserved. No computed result is claimed.

4. A transparent fixed-summary baseline and a masked temporal alternative fitted on the same patient-level split, including held-out calibration, Brier score, discrimination, uncertainty and exposure-state risk summaries.
5. Destination, observed-code-status and observation-density sensitivities, plus supportive/adverse/inconclusive interpretation records linked to computed output files.

Readiness, a coefficient, AUROC, or favorable direction is not completion.

## Population, joins and temporal boundaries

Use the first valid ICU stay per hospital admission (earliest `icu/icustays.intime`) with `intime < outtime`, `los >= 1 day`, and `hosp/patients.anchor_age >= 18`. Join `icu/icustays` to `hosp/admissions` on `(subject_id, hadm_id)` and to `hosp/patients` on `subject_id`. Keep all admissions for one `subject_id` in one train/validation/test split.

Set the landmark `tL = icu/icustays.outtime`. Require the first `hosp/transfers` row with `eventtype='transfer'` and `intime >= tL` to have a non-ICU `careunit`; classify careunits containing ICU, CCU, CSRU, SICU or TSICU as ICU. ICU-to-ICU moves are excluded. Missing or unclassifiable immediate destinations are excluded from the primary cohort, counted in the flow table, and analyzed only in a labeled sensitivity using `hosp/admissions.discharge_location`. Destination is a context/selection variable, not the exposure.

Require `admissions.deathtime` to be null or strictly after `tL`. If `hospital_expire_flag=1` lacks a usable death time, timing is unresolved and the stay is excluded rather than reconstructed. Use patient-relative intervals because MIMIC timestamps are deidentified with within-person intervals preserved but cross-person calendar alignment invalid.

Primary features are limited to `[tL-24 hours, tL)`. For `icu/chartevents`, include only rows with `charttime < tL` and `storetime <= tL`; no post-landmark destination, discharge, death, later-stay or other outcome information is an input. Partition the window into four fixed six-hour bins. Measurements are summarized by clinical `charttime`; `storetime` is only an availability screen and a documentation-timing sensitivity.

## Verified residual-instability exposure

The primary item audit was inspected from `datasets/mimic/table-d1023acc404fd1d4.json` and the attached d_items extract. Use only these verified `icu/d_items` labels and IDs in `icu/chartevents`:

- 220045 Heart Rate (bpm)
- 220210 Respiratory Rate (insp/min)
- 220052 Arterial Blood Pressure mean and 220181 Non Invasive Blood Pressure mean (mmHg)
- 220277 O2 saturation pulseoxymetry (%)
- 223834 O2 Flow and 227287 O2 Flow (additional cannula) (L/min)

Do not use unverified FiO2 or oxygen-device item IDs in the primary or required sensitivity. If a future solver discovers an additional label, it must report it as exploratory and separately audited, not silently add it.

For each stream and bin, calculate median, count, valid-value mask and abnormality. Fixed, pre-outcome boundaries are HR <50 or >110 bpm; RR <8 or >25/min; MAP <65 mmHg; SpO2 <92%; and oxygen flow >=4 L/min. A bin is abnormal if any valid stream crosses a boundary; a respiratory-support bin is positive if either verified oxygen-flow item crosses its boundary.

Exposure states are: observed stable (at least 3 of 4 bins have all required streams, with no abnormal or support bin); persistent instability (at least 2 bins abnormal or support-positive); intermittent instability (exactly 1); and insufficient observation (fewer than 3 qualifying bins or no valid required stream). The primary contrast is persistent versus observed-stable. Keep intermittent and insufficient states visible; do not impute missingness to normal. Report component-specific burden and the number of qualifying bins.

## Outcomes and estimands

Follow from `tL` for 48 hours, bounded by same-admission `hosp/admissions.dischtime`. Define mutually exclusive first events:

- ICU readmission: a distinct subsequent `icu/icustays.stay_id` with the same `(subject_id, hadm_id)` and `tL <= intime < tL+48h`.
- Hospital death: `admissions.deathtime` in `[tL,tL+48h)), before any readmission.
- Alive hospital discharge before 48 hours: `dischtime < tL+48h`, with no earlier readmission or death.
- Event-free at 48 hours otherwise.

If death and readmission have identical recorded times, death is first by a fixed tie rule and the tie is reported. An expiration flag without death time is unresolved, not silently converted.

The primary estimand is the 48-hour cumulative incidence of composite readmission/death with alive discharge competing, and its standardized risk difference (persistent minus stable) over the eligible population. Secondary estimands are cause-specific cumulative-incidence contrasts for readmission and death. These are associations among ICU survivors discharged to non-ICU care, not treatment effects or principal-stratum effects.

## Baseline, alternative and method choice

The primary baseline is a transparent fixed-summary cause-specific competing-risk analysis using the four-bin summaries, exposure state, age, sex, admission type, ICU length of stay, first/last careunit, time from admission to ICU entry, qualifying-bin count and component burdens. Report crude risks before adjustment. Fit cause-specific first-event models or an equivalent multinomial first-event model, then standardize risks by exposure state. Use patient-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals with a fixed seed (target 1,000 resamples; if the solver envelope forces fewer, record the prespecified reduction).

The substantive alternative is a small masked temporal GRU-D-style model on the same four bins, with the same streams/context, value masks and time-since-last-observation, fit only on training patients, early-stopped on validation and evaluated once on a locked patient-level test set. It targets the same first-event states, not a different outcome. It can reveal ordering, persistence, co-movement and informative observation gaps that fixed medians/counts lose. The scientific comparison is whether those temporal features change persistent-versus-intermittent risk interpretation and held-out calibration, not whether a neural model wins a small AUROC. Report calibration slope/intercept, Brier, event-specific AUROC/AUPRC, calibration by exposure state/destination, patient-bootstrap or five fixed-seed uncertainty, and all seeds.

The baseline remains primary because its estimand is auditable. The temporal model is retained because it tests substantive information loss. A latent mechanistic model is deferred: the snapshot lacks adjudicated respiratory diagnoses, verified delivered-device settings, work-of-breathing assessments and reliable treatment intent. Future planning estimates, not measured discovery results, are 1–3 CPU hours for extraction/fitting, 2–4 additional CPU hours for bootstrap/artifact checks, and 2–6 hours on one allocated A100 for the small temporal model. The future envelope is 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB, up to 8 GPUs and 28800 seconds. No GPU or solver study was run here.

## Rival explanations, falsification and interpretation

Add the immediate non-ICU destination as a sensitivity. Add last eligible `chartevents` values for verified code-status IDs 223758 and 228687 only when text explicitly indicates DNR, DNI, comfort, hospice or no escalation; unknown remains unknown. This is a documentation proxy, not a goals-of-care adjudication. Compute vital/oxygen row counts, distinct bins and non-vital/non-oxygen chart counts in the same window. If the contrast attenuates with observation density or a process-only gradient is comparable, surveillance/recording is a stronger explanation.

Supportive evidence is a directionally consistent, clinically nontrivial persistent-versus-stable risk difference with uncertainty excluding a negligible range, persistence across destination/code-status strata, no comparable process-only gradient, and adequate calibration. Temporal improvement supports added ordered information only if held out and stable; it does not establish physiology or causality.

Adverse evidence is null/reversed or unstable contrast, risk concentrated in insufficient observation, attenuation after observation adjustment, disappearance within destination/code-status strata, or a temporal gain that fails held-out evaluation. This favors residual severity, discharge selection, treatment limitation or surveillance artifacts.

Inconclusive evidence is sparse events, wide intervals spanning meaningful harm, high missingness, unresolved timing, poor calibration, or inadequate strata. It warrants replication/measurement work rather than a favorable conclusion. True oxygen need, clinician intent, appropriateness of discharge, mechanism, causal benefit of delayed discharge, and transportability require expert adjudication, prospective monitoring/delay studies or an external hospital.

Read-only source: `[private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip`, SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`.

# Day-42 recorded-assay signal: transportability across observation and care-process strata

Status: substantive transportability child of candidate-7b0d258c95e246598f0e6a3d. No model has been fitted and no clinical result is claimed.

## Scientific deliverable and decision boundary

The new deliverable is a prespecified transportability analysis of the inherited day-42 HCC landmark experiment. It must produce a frozen cohort and timing audit; development-only stratum cutpoints; held-out hazards and patient-level losses for every baseline/learned channel model; all-source censoring and assay-observation support audits; stratum-specific and partial-pooled assay increments; horizon and calendar interactions; negative controls; uncertainty intervals; and a claim-to-output map. Completion is demonstrated by these computed outputs and their provenance, not by readiness or a favorable result.

The clinically consequential question is:

> Among patients with a first dated locally recorded exact-code TACE who are observable at day 42 and have no exact-code repeat before day 42, is the incremental information in recorded assay state at day 42 stable enough across measurement opportunity, order availability, encounter intensity, care-process intensity, calendar period, and early versus late follow-up that it could be validated as a reusable recorded-state signal for a later operational repeat TACE?

The falsifiable claim is not “assays identify tumour response” or “repeat TACE benefits patients.” It is that the held-out improvement from (S) over (M0+P_{obs}+P_{care} is present and not materially different across supported workflow strata after all-source IPCW and cross-fitted assay-observation weighting. I will call this transportability claim supported only if every prespecified supported stratum has a positive primary loss increment, the partial-pooled heterogeneity estimate is below the predeclared computational margin, and the direction survives the timing, calendar, split, and negative-control checks. The margin is an operational separation rule—not a clinical minimal important difference, which is unavailable in this snapshot.

The strongest rival is a care-process/timing explanation: high-intensity encounters, orders, assays, or planned retreatment pathways create both more recorded assay values and more exact-code repeat TACE. A second rival is incompletely measured current severity. Under these rivals, the (S) increment will be concentrated in high-opportunity/high-order/high-care strata, disappear after observation weighting or process adjustment, be strongest only in days 43–90, vary across calendar periods, or be reproduced by timing/value permutations. A stable increment would support reusable recorded information for this operational event; it would not identify a biological mechanism. A null or adverse result would be clinically useful because it would argue against spending effort on assay-only transport and redirect the next study toward imaging, intent, and workflow linkage.

### Three inspected works and the unresolved advance

[K1] Dai et al. inspected full-text passages from a selected three-center CT/radiomics/deep-learning repeat-TACE cohort. It supports the strongest existing claim available here: treatment-adjacent recorded information can predict outcomes in a selected repeat-TACE imaging cohort, while external performance fell and the authors noted small-sample, scanner, and generalization limitations. This child adds a routine longitudinal EHR test with explicit observation and care-process strata; it does not reproduce the imaging study.

[K2] Tsurusaki et al. was inspected at the abstract level. It bounds the endpoint: HCC treatment response uses necrosis-aware mRECIST/RECICL concepts, not a procedure code or an uncalibrated laboratory value. [K3] Minh et al. was also inspected at the abstract level; its documented response comparison was sensitive to undocumented imaging outcomes, ascertainment, exposure classification, and treatment-selection confounding. The advance here is a falsifiable boundary test for whether a recorded-assay signal is portable across those observable recording processes, while explicitly refusing a response or causal claim.

The proposed result cannot establish tumour response, progression, TACE benefit/harm, treatment necessity, assay causality, or mechanism. Those require expert imaging and intent adjudication, validated assay units/reference ranges, mortality/outside-care/transplant ascertainment, and an independent cohort.

## Disjoint features and prespecified transport strata

Define elapsed time from the index start without date rounding. All feature cutoffs are day 42 unless stated otherwise.

- (M0): pre-index age, sex, department, encounter/admission history, diagnosis dictionary counts through matched encounters, procedure counts, and exact-assay summaries from [-365,0). All transformations and imputations are fold-fitted.
- (S): target-assay numeric values and qualitative/inequality flags in (0,42], plus assay-specific change from a valid pre-index observation in [-365,0). (S) contains no assay-request indicator or missingness indicator. Numeric missingness is imputed fold-wise by the frozen baseline/median rule; absence of an assay is represented only in (P_{obs}.
- (P_{obs}: dated encounter, examination, medication/order, and lab-observation counts, distinct-date counts/gaps, assay-label request/result counts, and availability/missingness indicators in (0,42], with no assay values, qualitative results, or state changes.
- (P_{care}: dated non-TACE procedure tokens, non-drug-order tokens, medication starts/ends, department/visit process marks, and their timing in (0,42], with no assay values. It is a competing operational explanation, not a causally adjusted confounder.

The transport axes are computed after eligibility but before any outcome fitting. Cutpoints are determined from the development partition only and frozen before untouched test scoring:

1. Measurement opportunity (G_{meas}): number of distinct elapsed calendar dates in (0,42] containing any valid encounter, examination, lab, medication, or order timestamp. Strata are zero, low-positive, and high-positive, with low/high split at the development median among positive values.
2. Order availability (G_{order}): number of distinct dates with a valid `开立时间` in (0,42]. Strata are no order, low-positive, and high-positive, split at the development median among positive values. An order with a later start/end time does not count as available before that time.
3. Encounter intensity (G_{enc}): number of distinct composite encounter IDs with at least one valid encounter timestamp in (0,42]. Strata are zero, low-positive, and high-positive using the development median among positive values.
4. Care-process intensity (G_{care}): number of distinct dated, de-duplicated non-TACE process marks from procedures, orders, medications, and encounter department/visit process marks in (0,42]. Strata are zero, low-positive, and high-positive using the development median among positive values. Exact-code TACE rows and all assay values are excluded.
5. Calendar period (G_{cal}): three equal-frequency index-date bins from the development partition, with breakpoints computed from index timestamps only and frozen before test outcome evaluation. The exact timestamp breakpoints are an output, not a post hoc choice.
6. Horizon (G_{hor}): fixed early [43,90] versus late [91,181) risk intervals; no fitted cutpoint.

The primary analysis estimates each axis one at a time to avoid sparse five-way cells. A secondary joint analysis uses only the supported 2×2 low/high (G_{meas}) by (G_{care}) cells; zero/positive categories remain separately reported. Any stratum that fails support is not collapsed into a neighboring stratum.

## Transport estimands and analysis

Let (A=M0+P_{obs}+P_{care}, (B=A+S), and let (L_i^{m}) be a patient-level integrated, all-source IPCW loss for model (m) over the intervals during which the patient is at risk. The primary stratum-specific incremental information estimand is
[
Delta_g^{LL}=E[L^A-L^Bmid G=g],
]
with positive values meaning that recorded assay state improves held-out weighted log loss. The secondary is (Delta_g^{Br}=E[Br^A-Br^Bmid G=g]). Report each within-stratum increment, its overall test-set standardization using the frozen test stratum proportions, pairwise stratum contrasts, and the difference between ordinary and observation-weighted estimates.

All-source right-censoring weights are fitted inside development folds from information available before each risk interval, with a frozen development-fold tail rule and support/effective-sample-size audit. For models containing (S), fit a separate cross-fitted day-42 assay-observation model for the probability of at least one valid target-assay value using (M0), pre-day-42 (P_{obs}, and (P_{care}. Use stabilized observation weights within each transport axis:
[
w_{obs,g}=Pr(S observedmid G=g)/Pr(S observedmid M0,P_{obs},P_{care},G=g).
]
The numerator and denominator are fold-fitted; weights are truncated only by the frozen development-fold rule. No extrapolation is permitted. The clinically consequential question is:

# Selection and censoring boundary for the eICU testing-process transportability signal

Status: proposed substantive branch-B child of assessed-valid `candidate-e57c426aadda72d3c9746477`. No model fit or hypothesis result is claimed.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The parent asks whether early laboratory-result presence, frequency, and timing add transportability-sensitive information beyond laboratory values. Its hospital-held-out process permutation breaks patient linkage, but it still leaves two consequential interpretations unresolved:

1. The six-hour landmark conditions on remaining in the ICU and observable long enough to accumulate results. ICU discharge, early death, or early transition to end-of-life care can select a subgroup whose documentation process is unusually informative.
2. A same-hospital permutation can preserve stable case mix and hospital recording density. It does not show that a process increment is dynamic deterioration rather than a stable severity/documentation mixture.

The strongest inspected evidence supports only bounded premises. Temporally ordered EHR data can predict mortality across centers [K1]. Information presence can be predictive and missingness patterns can threaten transportability, but the inspected Gao evidence is abstract-only [K2]. External mortality performance may retain discrimination while local adaptation changes calibration and requires harmonization [K3]. None establishes the eICU mechanism.

Primary falsifiable hypothesis: among adult first ICU stays eligible at six hours, the process-aware model's hospital-held-out transport penalty is not solely a consequence of measured landmark/discharge or early end-of-life selection. Specifically, the process increment should remain after (a) a prespecified >720-minute landmark sensitivity, (b) inverse-probability standardization for measured six-hour eligibility, and (c) restriction to stays without an early carePlanEOL record. A state-matched within-hospital process permutation should attenuate a genuine patient-state increment; if it does not, stable case mix or workflow/documentation remains a stronger explanation.

This is a descriptive transportability and selection-boundary hypothesis, not a causal claim that testing, documentation, or end-of-life care causes death.

## Clinical importance and decision boundary

If the process increment survives selection audits and is removed by state matching, it is plausible that repeated testing reflects dynamic recorded illness and can help a hospital-held-out early review score. If it disappears after the no-EOL or >720-minute boundary, apparent transportability may be driven by discharge/end-of-life selection and should not justify deployment. If it survives state matching and the null retains the increment, a site-specific documentation or stable case-mix explanation is more credible, supporting data-feed harmonization and recalibration rather than more testing.

The consequential modeled action is a senior review of monitoring adequacy and goals-of-care context when predicted ICU-discharge mortality is at least 10%; 5% and 20% are secondary thresholds. This is not authorization to alter treatment or end-of-life decisions. Report alert burden and decision-curve net benefit against treat-none and treat-all. A process model that adds net benefit only in the early-EOL stratum is not a validated decision aid: it may duplicate documentation and requires clinical adjudication.

## Scientific deliverable

The solver must newly produce:

1. A frozen cohort manifest, the six-hour eligibility indicator, early-EOL indicator, >720-minute sensitivity indicator, and deterministic five-fold hospital assignment.
2. Leakage-safe value and process features and predictions for V-Logit, V-GBM, VP-GBM, P-GBM, NC-State-GBM, and the selection-weighted/no-EOL/>720-minute sensitivity analyses.
3. A selection audit reporting counts and outcome prevalence by six-hour eligibility, discharge-length boundary, EOL6 status, hospital fold, and hospital.
4. AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, calibration intercept/slope and calibration-in-the-large, alert burden, and net benefit at 5%, 10%, and 20%, with paired 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap intervals.
5. A report linking every interpretation to saved predictions, contrasts, and uncertainty intervals. No fitted result is part of this proposal.

## Population, time, outcome, and estimands

The primary cohort is the parent's cohort:

- Include `patient` rows with `unitvisitnumber=1`, `unitstaytype=admit`, numeric `age >=18` (retain `>89`), nonmissing `hospitalid`, `patientunitstayid`, `unitdischargestatus`, and `unitdischargeoffset`; exclude duplicate unit rows, unparseable ages, and `unitdischargeoffset <360`.
- Retain hospitals with at least 100 eligible stays; stop if fewer than five remain. Preserve unknown gender/ethnicity as explicit categories.
- Time zero is ICU admission; the primary feature window is `W0=[0,360]` minutes. All offsets are ICU-relative.
- `Y=1` iff `patient.unitdischargestatus == "Expired"`; otherwise `Y=0` for non-Expired ICU discharge. The outcome is ICU-discharge mortality conditional on being observed beyond 360 minutes, not fixed-time mortality.
- Join `apachePatientResult` by `patientunitstayid` for an audit of `actualicumortality` only; do not replace `Y`, use Apache scores, or use discharge fields as predictors.

The primary estimand is the parent transport contrast:
`D_AUC = (AUC(VP-GBM, internal)-AUC(VP-GBM, external)) - (AUC(V-GBM, internal)-AUC(V-GBM, external))`.
Define the analogous contrasts for Brier error, calibration error, and net benefit, with signs oriented so positive means an increment or improvement as appropriate.

The selection audit has three prespecified boundaries:

- `S6 = 1(unitdischargeoffset >360)` is the primary landmark selection. On the full adult first-admission denominator, report `S6`, early discharge/death status, and EOL6 availability. Do not pretend that a post-360 outcome is defined for `S6=0`.
- `S720 = 1(unitdischargeoffset >720)` is a stricter descriptive landmark sensitivity using the same [0,360] features and outcome. Compare `D_720` to `D_AUC`; it is a selection boundary, not a new causal estimand.
- `EOL6` is an audit-only indicator: at least one finite `cpleolsaveoffset` or `cpleoldiscussionoffset` in [0,360]. Do not use `carePlanEOL` or `activeupondischarge` as predictors. Report `D_noEOL` among `EOL6=0` and `D_EOL` separately only if event and hospital counts support an interval. An EOL record is a documented care-plan event, not proof of a clinical decision time or death time.

For measured selection standardization, fit a training-fold-only logistic model for `S6` using admission fields `age`, `gender`, `ethnicity`, and `admissionweight`, with categories and medians learned in training folds. Use stabilized inverse-probability weights for S6=1, truncate only at prespecified [0.05,0.95] propensity bounds, report the fraction truncated and effective sample size, and use hospital-cluster bootstrap. This is a sensitivity estimand standardized over measured admission covariates; it cannot recover outcomes after early ICU discharge or correct unmeasured severity.

## Exact eICU bindings and availability

Catalog provenance: `[private-path]/completed-data.json`, SHA-256 `9bc20153591045e19e908fc0b538d04a950f2fe75b85ba99c8de1fb3b2d750be`. eICU snapshot: `896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476fe89543643c08b7df637a15ec`. Every source is a read-only ordinary gzip CSV; no archive member is used.

- Patient anchor: `[private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/patient.csv.gz`, source SHA-256 `2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b`; table `patient`, `datasets/eicu/table-ab037c09d7df9a3c.json`, schema SHA-256 `f354ea972ab3b4efa81556a02963dee7d9e2ccb0ab23cacb309059132e94b5a7`. Required fields: `patientunitstayid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, `uniquepid`, `hospitalid`, `unitvisitnumber`, `unitstaytype`, `age`, `gender`, `ethnicity`, `admissionweight`, `unitadmitoffset`, `unitdischargeoffset`, `unitdischargestatus`. Use `patientunitstayid` for all row joins and `hospitalid` for hospital folds; do not join incompatible identifier namespaces.
- Hospital stratifier: `[private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/hospital.csv.gz`, source SHA-256 `16684f45680921fb263fdd057ac9217093a9e81fc663228480e0d6a4665390a6`; table `hospital`, `datasets/eicu/table-811df7b2ef435e12.json`, schema SHA-256 `336091a45944fb9d4c39ec6b30af67e472b221df8877f9c555e3b444e1212811`. Required fields: `hospitalid`, `numbedscategory`, `teachingstatus`, `region`. Join only `patient.hospitalid=hospital.hospitalid`. Use only for reporting/stratification and never as predictors.
- Laboratory measurements: `[private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/lab.csv.gz`, source SHA-256 `91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a`; table `lab`, `datasets/eicu/table-79bdb33275339b1a.json`, schema SHA-256 `41b0cab77ecab75bb9746fd44812c7a574196be60bfdce26835f9805ae2c6925`. Required fields: `labid`, `patientunitstayid`, `labresultoffset`, `labtypeid`, `labname`, `labresult`, `labresulttext`, `labmeasurenamesystem`, `labmeasurenameinterface`, `labresultrevisedoffset`. Join only on `patientunitstayid`. Keep finite numeric `labresult`, `0<=labresultoffset<=360`, and blank or `labresultrevisedoffset<=360`. Use normalized `labname + labmeasurenamesystem`, falling back to interface if system is blank, only as analyte key; never use result text.
- End-of-life audit: `[private-path]/EICU 2.0数据/carePlanEOL.csv.gz`, source SHA-256 `8c776d15fd944507c0b57e3e7974db03ad87ac435d27b3f406b3d1afd046ecb0`; table `carePlanEOL`, `datasets/eicu/table-4a60395475cf75e7.json`, schema SHA-256 `cc6507907398acbb8bf7d7f13aef97d47e2fd96a3e04cca4272dbcad516707e0`. Required fields: `patientunitstayid`, `cpleolsaveoffset`, `cpleoldiscussionoffset`, `activeupondischarge`. Join only on `patientunitstayid`; use finite offsets in [0,360] for EOL6, and retain the raw first-offset audit. Do not use `activeupondischarge` in modeling.

The source catalog and schema files confirm all listed temporal fields and ICU-relative offsets. No available field supplies order status, specimen-collection time, interface outage, clinician rationale, or death time.

A bounded read-only availability scan, not an outcome or model result, observed 200,859 patient rows; before final repeat-`uniquepid` and fold exclusions, 146,842 adult first-admit rows with usable offsets, 140,777 with offset >360, 134,137 with offset >720, and 172 hospitals with at least 100 such rows. The EOL file contained 1,433 rows, 746 unique stays with an EOL offset in [0,360], and 171 unique stays with an offset in (360,720]. These counts only establish that the proposed audit inputs exist; the solver must recompute final counts under the exact cohort and must not treat them as study findings.

## Features and the stable-case-mix control

Within each outer training partition, select the 30 analytes with the largest distinct eligible-patient coverage among analytes with at least 1% coverage, using training hospitals only. For each selected analyte, retain the latest valid value and its original offset in [0,360], with no carry-forward. Impute values by training-fold medians. Value inputs are age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight, and the selected lab values. Process inputs are per-analyte presence, valid-row count, distinct-offset count, first/last result offset, and overall valid-row/distinct-offset counts. These are recording proxies, not confirmed orders.

The main models use the same feature definitions as the parent. NC-State-GBM changes only the null assignment of the complete process vector: within each hospital, sort by SHA-256(`"eicu-process-state-null-v1\\0"+patientunitstayid`) and cyclically assign the next vector within a coarse, training-defined state stratum. The state stratum is the quintile of a value-only risk score from V-GBM, calculated out-of-fold for training stays and by the fold-fitted value model for held-out hospitals, with admission demographic/weight bins as tie-breakers. If a cell has fewer than 10 stays, use the prespecified adjacent-quintile merge and report the merge. Keep the original values, outcome, and hospital; use no process or outcome in the assignment.

This control is stronger than an unrestricted same-hospital permutation for the stable-case-mix rival, but it is not a causal adjustment: a value-only score is an imperfect state summary, and within-cell documentation can remain correlated with unmeasured severity. Retain the parent's unrestricted NC-GBM and cyclic offset-shift TS-GBM as secondary controls when feasible; the state-matched audit is the new primary mechanistic boundary.

## Models, split, uncertainty, and alternative selection

V-Logit is the interpretable elastic-net logistic baseline using demographics and value features. V-GBM is the capacity-matched value-only histogram gradient booster. VP-GBM is the identical booster with original process features; P-GBM is process-only. NC-State-GBM uses the same learner and hyperparameters as VP-GBM but the state-matched process vector. TS-GBM shifts only process offsets by t-180 when t>=180, otherwise t+180, as the parent's timing placebo. Categories, medians, analyte selection, class policy, seeds, and hyperparameters are learned within outer training folds only.

The primary split holds out hospitals. Sort hospital IDs by SHA-256(`"eicu-transport-v1\\0"+hospitalid`) and greedily balance eligible stays into five contiguous folds. Within training hospitals, reserve a fixed 20% patient-stratified internal sample using SHA-256(`"eicu-internal-v1\\0"+patientunitstayid`). No patient-only split is called external validation. The same folds, outcomes, prediction rows, bootstrap cluster indices, and uncertainty metrics are used for every model and sensitivity boundary.

For model m and evaluation e, let `I(m,e)=AUC(m,e)-AUC(V-GBM,e)`; orient Brier and calibration contrasts so positive means better performance or smaller error. Report `D_AUC`, `D_720`, `D_noEOL`, and weighted `D_IPW`, plus direct held-out differences. Use 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap resamples with identical indices across paired models. Report per-hospital estimates, prevalence, event counts, effective sample sizes, propensity truncation, and missing EOL strata.

Baseline versus learned alternative reasoning: V-Logit is scientifically useful because its coefficients and calibration show whether a process increment is directionally consistent and interpretable under the same outcome and hospital split. V-GBM versus VP-GBM is the capacity-matched learned alternative: nonlinear value-process interactions can reveal whether process dependence occurs only in state-dependent combinations that a linear baseline misses. NC-State-GBM, not a larger model, is selected because it directly tests the stable-case-mix/documentation rival. Inputs are the same 0-360 demographics, values, and process summaries; the target is ICU-discharge mortality; evaluation is held-out-hospital discrimination, calibration, and 10% review net benefit with cluster uncertainty. CPU planning estimate: 16 CPUs, 64-128 GiB RAM, 2-6 hours for extraction, five-fold fits, selection sensitivities, and bootstrap; one-fold readiness should measure actual cost. This fits the configured planning envelope of 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB, and 28,800 seconds. GPU is not selected: the data are tabular, the GBM and bootstrap are CPU-feasible, and an A100 would not answer the selection mechanism. A temporal neural model is deferred because it would add representation complexity without improving this selection falsification; reconsider only if a bounded diagnostic shows summary features lose relevant temporal information. The estimate is planned, not measured, and does not authorize proposer/solver training.

## Interpretation and falsification

Support for a patient-state/dynamic-deterioration interpretation requires a positive, uncertainly precise primary process increment; attenuation of the process increment in NC-State-GBM relative to VP-GBM; and broadly similar D across no-EOL, >720-minute, and measured-selection-weighted boundaries. This remains descriptive evidence that process features carry patient-linked information, not proof of physiology or causality.

Support for selection/documentation is a positive primary D that materially attenuates after >720 restriction, no-EOL restriction, or IPW; concentration of net benefit or calibration change in EOL6 or near-landmark discharges; or retention of a similar process increment in NC-State-GBM. This establishes a boundary where process prediction is compatible with stable case mix or workflow/end-of-life documentation; it does not establish that documentation caused error.

Adverse to the process-aware claim is an upper confidence limit below zero for D with VP-GBM no better in calibration or 10% net benefit, provided technical checks and control penalties do not explain it. Mixed results arise when state matching and selection boundaries disagree. Results are inconclusive when intervals span clinically meaningful values, EOL6 is too sparse, propensity weights are unstable, hospital/event counts fail, analyte selection changes materially, or the label/audit discordance is substantial.

The verifier can check cohort construction, joins, offsets, fold isolation, null permutations, model parity, predictions, metrics, bootstrap intervals, and whether conclusions match those outputs. It cannot determine whether a result was clinically an order, an interface omission, an end-of-life decision, or a useful alert. Those claims require clinician adjudication, order/specimen/interface data, a death timestamp, and prospective silent deployment/impact evaluation. No result supports changing monitoring, treatment, or goals-of-care practice without those studies.

## [K1], [K2], [K3] inspected evidence and limits

[K1] Rajkomar et al. demonstrates temporally structured, cross-center EHR mortality prediction with a logistic comparator, but does not isolate testing process. This child adds discharge/EOL selection boundaries and state-matched process nulls.

[K2] Gao et al. (abstract-only inspection) supports the warning that information presence can be predictive and transportability can shift, but concerns one CLABSI setting and does not distinguish state from workflow. This child tests that distinction in eICU while preserving the limitation.

[K3] Hadler et al. supports external discrimination/calibration evaluation and local adaptation under fragmented EHR data, but cannot identify process mechanism. This child adds an explicit landmark/censoring audit and a within-hospital state-matched rival.

Bibliography:

- [K1] Rajkomar A, Oren E, Chen K, et al. “Scalable and accurate deep learning with electronic health records.” npj Digital Medicine. 2018;1:18. DOI: 10.1038/s41746-018-0029-1.
- [K2] Gao S, Albu E, Stijnen P, Rademakers F, Cossey V, Debaveye Y, Janssens C, Van Calster B, Wynants L. “Comparing methods for handling missing data in electronic health records for dynamic risk prediction of central-line associated bloodstream infection.” BMC Medical Research Methodology. 2026;26:128. DOI: 10.1186/s12874-026-02819-y. Abstract only.
- [K3] Hadler RA, Lakamana SK, Moorman T, Bozkurt S. “Testing Transferability of a Mortality Risk Model for Interhospital Transfer Using Real-World Electronic Health Records: External Validation and Model Enhancement.” Critical Care Explorations. 2026;8(9):e1442. DOI: 10.1097/CCE.0000000000001442.

Source evidence is attached byte-for-byte from the parent’s frozen, receipt-hashed excerpts and `key-references.json`; K2 remains explicitly abstract-only.

- `S6 = 1(unitdischargeoffset >360)` is the primary landmark selection. On the full adult first-admission denominator, report `S6`, early discharge/death status, and EOL6 availability. Do not pretend that a post-360 outcome is defined for `S6=0`.
- `S720 = 1(unitdischargeoffset >720)` is a stricter descriptive landmark sensitivity using the same [0,360] features and outcome. Compare `D_720` to `D_AUC`; it is a selection boundary, not a new causal estimand.
- `EOL6` is an audit-only indicator: at least one finite `cpleolsaveoffset` or `cpleoldiscussionoffset` in [0,360]. Do not use `carePlanEOL` or `activeupondischarge` as predictors. Report `D_noEOL` among `EOL6=0` and `D_EOL` separately only if event and hospital counts support an interval. An EOL record is a documented care-plan event, not proof of a clinical decision time or death time.

For measured selection standardization, fit a training-fold-only logistic model for `S6` using admission fields `age`, `gender`, `ethnicity`, and `admissionweight`, with categories and medians learned in training folds. Use stabilized inverse-probability weights for S6=1, truncate only at prespecified [0.05,0.95] propensity bounds, report the fraction truncated and effective sample size, and use hospital-cluster bootstrap. This is a sensitivity estimand standardized over measured admission covariates; it cannot recover outcomes after early ICU discharge or correct unmeasured severity.

These counts only establish that the proposed audit inputs exist; the solver must recompute final counts under the exact cohort and must not treat them as study findings.

## Features and the stable-case-mix control

Within each outer training partition, select the 30 analytes with the largest distinct eligible-patient coverage among analytes with at least 1% coverage, using training hospitals only. For each selected analyte, retain the latest valid value and its original offset in [0,360], with no carry-forward. Impute values by training-fold medians. Value inputs are age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight, and the selected lab values. Process inputs are per-analyte presence, valid-row count, distinct-offset count, first/last result offset, and overall valid-row/distinct-offset counts. These are recording proxies, not confirmed orders.

The main models use the same feature definitions as the parent. NC-State-GBM changes only the null assignment of the complete process vector: within each hospital, sort by SHA-256(`"eicu-process-state-null-v1\\0"+patientunitstayid`) and cyclically assign the next vector within a coarse, training-defined state stratum. The state stratum is the quintile of a value-only risk score from V-GBM, calculated out-of-fold for training stays and by the fold-fitted value model for held-out hospitals, with admission demographic/weight bins as tie-breakers. If a cell has fewer than 10 stays, use the prespecified adjacent-quintile merge and report the merge. Keep the original values, outcome, and hospital; use no process or outcome in the assignment.

This control is stronger than an unrestricted same-hospital permutation for the stable-case-mix rival, but it is not a causal adjustment: a value-only score is an imperfect state summary, and within-cell documentation can remain correlated with unmeasured severity. Retain the parent's unrestricted NC-GBM and cyclic offset-shift TS-GBM as secondary controls when feasible; the state-matched audit is the new primary mechanistic boundary.

## Models, split, uncertainty, and alternative selection

V-Logit is the interpretable elastic-net logistic baseline using demographics and value features. V-GBM is the capacity-matched value-only histogram gradient booster. VP-GBM is the identical booster with original process features; P-GBM is process-only. NC-State-GBM uses the same learner and hyperparameters as VP-GBM but the state-matched process vector. TS-GBM shifts only process offsets by t-180 when t>=180, otherwise t+180, as the parent's timing placebo. Categories, medians, analyte selection, class policy, seeds, and hyperparameters are learned within outer training folds only.

The primary split holds out hospitals. Sort hospital IDs by SHA-256(`"eicu-transport-v1\\0"+hospitalid`) and greedily balance eligible stays into five contiguous folds. Within training hospitals, reserve a fixed 20% patient-stratified internal sample using SHA-256(`"eicu-internal-v1\\0"+patientunitstayid`). No patient-only split is called external validation. The same folds, outcomes, prediction rows, bootstrap cluster indices, and uncertainty metrics are used for every model and sensitivity boundary.

For model m and evaluation e, let `I(m,e)=AUC(m,e)-AUC(V-GBM,e)`; orient Brier and calibration contrasts so positive means better performance or smaller error. Report `D_AUC`, `D_720`, `D_noEOL`, and weighted `D_IPW`, plus direct held-out differences. Use 2,000 hospital-cluster bootstrap resamples with identical indices across paired models. Report per-hospital estimates, prevalence, event counts, effective sample sizes, propensity truncation, and missing EOL strata.

Baseline versus learned alternative reasoning: V-Logit is scientifically useful because its coefficients and calibration show whether a process increment is directionally consistent and interpretable under the same outcome and hospital split. V-GBM versus VP-GBM is the capacity-matched learned alternative: nonlinear value-process interactions can reveal whether process dependence occurs only in state-dependent combinations that a linear baseline misses. NC-State-GBM, not a larger model, is selected because it directly tests the stable-case-mix/documentation rival. Inputs are the same 0-360 demographics, values, and process summaries; the target is ICU-discharge mortality; evaluation is held-out-hospital discrimination, calibration, and 10% review net benefit with cluster uncertainty. CPU planning estimate: 16 CPUs, 64-128 GiB RAM, 2-6 hours for extraction, five-fold fits, selection sensitivities, and bootstrap; one-fold readiness should measure actual cost. This fits the configured planning envelope of 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB, and 28,800 seconds. GPU is not selected: the data are tabular, the GBM and bootstrap are CPU-feasible, and an A100 would not answer the selection mechanism. A temporal neural model is deferred because it would add representation complexity without improving this selection falsification; reconsider only if a bounded diagnostic shows summary features lose relevant temporal information. The estimate is planned, not measured, and does not authorize proposer/solver training.

## Interpretation and falsification

Support for a patient-state/dynamic-deterioration interpretation requires a positive, uncertainly precise primary process increment; attenuation of the process increment in NC-State-GBM relative to VP-GBM; and broadly similar D across no-EOL, >720-minute, and measured-selection-weighted boundaries. This remains descriptive evidence that process features carry patient-linked information, not proof of physiology or causality.

Support for selection/documentation is a positive primary D that materially attenuates after >720 restriction, no-EOL restriction, or IPW; concentration of net benefit or calibration change in EOL6 or near-landmark discharges; or retention of a similar process increment in NC-State-GBM. This establishes a boundary where process prediction is compatible with stable case mix or workflow/end-of-life documentation; it does not establish that documentation caused error.

Adverse to the process-aware claim is an upper confidence limit below zero for D with VP-GBM no better in calibration or 10% net benefit, provided technical checks and control penalties do not explain it. Mixed results arise when state matching and selection boundaries disagree. Results are inconclusive when intervals span clinically meaningful values, EOL6 is too sparse, propensity weights are unstable, hospital/event counts fail, analyte selection changes materially, or the label/audit discordance is substantial.

The verifier can check cohort construction, joins, offsets, fold isolation, null permutations, model parity, predictions, metrics, bootstrap intervals, and whether conclusions match those outputs. It cannot determine whether a result was clinically an order, an interface omission, an end-of-life decision, or a useful alert. Those claims require clinician adjudication, order/specimen/interface data, a death timestamp, and prospective silent deployment/impact evaluation. No result supports changing monitoring, treatment, or goals-of-care practice without those studies.

## [K1], [K2], [K3] inspected evidence and limits

[K1] Rajkomar et al. demonstrates temporally structured, cross-center EHR mortality prediction with a logistic comparator, but does not isolate testing process. This child adds discharge/EOL selection boundaries and state-matched process nulls.

[K2] Gao et al. (abstract-only inspection) supports the warning that information presence can be predictive and transportability can shift, but concerns one CLABSI setting and does not distinguish state from workflow. This child tests that distinction in eICU while preserving the limitation.

[K3] Hadler et al. supports external discrimination/calibration evaluation and local adaptation under fragmented EHR data, but cannot identify process mechanism. This child adds an explicit landmark/censoring audit and a within-hospital state-matched rival.

Bibliography:

- [K2] Gao S, Albu E, Stijnen P, Rademakers F, Cossey V, Debaveye Y, Janssens C, Van Calster B, Wynants L. “Comparing methods for handling missing data in electronic health records for dynamic risk prediction of central-line associated bloodstream infection.” BMC Medical Research Methodology. 2026;26:128. DOI: 10.1186/s12874-026-02819-y. Abstract only.
- [K3] Hadler RA, Lakamana SK, Moorman T, Bozkurt S. “Testing Transferability of a Mortality Risk Model for Interhospital Transfer Using Real-World Electronic Health Records: External Validation and Model Enhancement.” Critical Care Explorations. 2026;8(9):e1442. DOI: 10.1097/CCE.0000000000001442.

Source evidence is attached byte-for-byte from the parent’s frozen, receipt-hashed excerpts and `key-references.json`; K2 remains explicitly abstract-only.
