| `pathology` | `[private-path]/data_病理_3292603985559017792.csv`; `7ad2d61c7254754b8528efe82a25af95473812b9734f1b1e5fb5e2cc5b2c3d41` | identifier/key audit only | no valid temporal column; excluded from longitudinal predictors |

The metadata confirms the many-to-one patient+visit relationships and the absence of images, raw waveforms, meaningful vitals and transfers. Exact duplicates are collapsed before counts. Names, identity numbers, phones, insurance/hospital numbers, file order and incompatible identifier namespaces are never used.

## Frozen review proxy and deterministic secondary gates

Normalize strings only by trim, Unicode case-fold and whitespace normalization. Do not use semantic substring lists, examination findings, diagnosis text or order text meaning.

For each eligible index, define within `(T0, T0 + 42]`:

- `E_any`: an examinations row with the same patient+visit key and valid `开始时间`;
- `O_open`: an orders row with valid `开立时间`;
- `O_done`: an orders row with valid `结束时间` and exact observed `医嘱状态 = 检查已完成`;
- `E_order_linked`: an examination/order pair at the same patient+visit with exact normalized equality `检查 = 医嘱(非药品)`, valid order `开立时间 <= 检查开始时间`, and, if valid, examination start no later than order `结束时间`. Missing order end cannot create a completed link.
- `W_packet=1`: `E_order_linked=1` or `O_done=1`; retain packet date, lag, counts and status-known indicator.

Only `W_packet` is the secondary proxy. `E_any` and `O_open` remain audit fields and a predeclared descriptive sensitivity, never substitutes. `P_plan` may summarize non-TACE procedure, order and packet counts in days 0–42 for process auditing, but no order is interpreted as planned TACE and no exact TACE row is included.

The W secondary is estimable only if, before any interpretation, both `W_packet=1` and `W_packet=0` have at least 100 test patients, 15 test primary events, 15 development primary events, finite weights and weighted ESS >= 100; the overall primary support gate must also pass. The planned W statistic is the overall state increment after exposing the exact proxy: `D_Wadj = L(A*) - L(B*)`, with `A* = M0 + W_packet +` process features after removing direct duplicate `E_any`/`O_open`/`O_done`/linked-packet components and `B* = A* + S`. It is not a causal adjustment or a W-stratum effect. No within-stratum refit, broad-proxy rescue or favorable-stratum selection is allowed. If either level fails, output `inconclusive_support_failure` for the complete W secondary; do not report a W-adjusted direction.

The NC secondary is estimable only if, before interpretation, there are at least 50 `Y_NC` events overall, 15 in the untouched test patients, 100 test patients, 15 development events, finite weights and weighted ESS ≥100. It uses the same A/B channels, split, censoring and evaluation, changing only the outcome to `Y_NC`. If any gate fails, output `inconclusive_support_failure`; do not substitute a non-TACE encounter, medication, laboratory or other event.

For either supported secondary, report the estimate and bootstrap interval, but classify it as discriminating only when the two-sided 95% patient-bootstrap interval has half-width ≤0.05 on log-loss contrast and ≤0.02 on Brier contrast, with finite calibration outputs. Otherwise report `inconclusive_precision_failure` even if the point estimate is favorable. These are precision rules, not clinical importance thresholds. Primary evidence is not withheld merely because a secondary gate fails.

## Models, patient-held-out estimand and weighting

The primary baseline is an elastic-net pooled-logistic discrete-time hazard with bins 43–90 and 91–180 (or one prespecified low-degree time spline, fixed before fitting). Use the inherited comparable channels:

- `M0`: demographics and permitted pre-index diagnosis/encounter summaries;
- `P_obs`: dated encounter, examination, medication/order/lab counts, distinct dates/gaps, assay-label request/result counts and availability indicators, with no assay values/results;
- `P_care`: non-TACE procedure tokens, non-drug order tokens, medication starts/ends, department/visit marks and timing, with no assay values/results;
- `S`: the inherited eight assay labels, audited quantitative/qualitative values, inequality/censoring flags and assay-specific pre-index changes, with no request/missingness indicator.

Fit at minimum `M0`, `A = M0 + P_obs + P_care`, `B = A + S`, `A*`, `B*`, and the supported NC counterparts. Exact channel definitions, cutoff and feature audits are frozen before fitting. The primary result is `D_state = L(A) - L(B)`, where positive means lower held-out loss from adding recorded assay state.

The matched learned alternative is a compact time-aware GRU over the same (-365) through (+42) stream: event category/label, audited numeric value, qualitative/inequality flags, relative time, elapsed time since prior event, decay and channel tag. It receives the same A/B and, if supported, W/NC ablations, target, split, weights, metrics and three fixed development seeds. The GRU can reveal nonlinear trajectories and order-to-exam timing patterns that elastic-net summaries lose; a GRU improvement is not evidence that the signal is clinical or state-specific. Elastic-net is primary because its channel increments and proxy exclusions are auditable; the GRU is retained as a matched sensitivity, not to chase a small score gain. Larger transformers and broad searches are deferred because they do not resolve the state/workflow ambiguity.

Generate one deterministic patient split before fitting: 80% development/20% test, stratified only on primary event indicator, seed 271828, with no patient crossing partitions. Freeze IDs, algorithm and counts in `frozen_patient_split.json`. Seeds 314159 and 161803 are fixed sensitivity splits and cannot select a favorable result. Fit all encoders, dictionaries, scaling, imputation, cutpoints, hyperparameters, proxy support summaries and weight models inside development folds; score the untouched test once.

The overall primary gate is at least 50 primary events overall, 15 test events, 100 test patients, 15 development events, completed timing/duplicate audits, finite weights and weighted ESS ≥100. All-source right-censoring weights are fitted inside development folds. Assay-observation weights are cross-fitted from M0, pre-day-42 `P_obs` and `P_care`. Report ordinary and observation-weighted estimates, weight tails and ESS. Bootstrap test patients with all their person-days and fixed weights for paired 95% intervals.

Report weighted log loss as the primary loss, Brier/integrated Brier and calibration slope/intercept as required secondary metrics, and AUROC/AUPRC only descriptively. The same held-out predictions and loss definitions must support every model/channel comparison.

## Multiplicity, falsification and interpretation

The one prespecified max-|t| patient-bootstrap family contains exactly three named state increments: `D_state`, supported `D_Wadj`, and supported `D_NC = L(A_NC) - L(B_NC)`. The support mask is frozen from the deterministic gates above before interpretation. An unsupported member is absent/NA with its exact gate reason; it is never imputed, relabeled or counted as a null result. Familywise intervals are reported for every estimable member, and the primary decision is still the overall member. GRU, alternate split, lead-time, permutation and complete-follow-up results are sensitivity outputs, not new confirmatory hypotheses.

Use the identical split, folds, weights, support rules and output schema for:

- assay/result timestamp permutations preserving patient assay/result multisets and process counts;
- quantitative assay shuffles within calendar and baseline-severity blocks;
- process-mark permutations within calendar and event-count strata;
- `W_packet` label permutations within patient and index-calendar blocks;
- removal of all process/assay records in days 36–42 and a process cutoff at day 28;
- alternate valid `obs_end` definitions and exclusion of undated strict-TACE histories;
- exact-code-only versus a separately frozen high-specificity alias sensitivity;
- development outcome-label permutation scored against untouched true-label test outcomes.

Supportive primary evidence requires: the overall gate passes; the familywise lower 95% bound for `D_state` is >0; ordinary and observation-weighted directions agree; A/B calibration is acceptable; the increment is not reproduced by assay value/time permutations; and it does not disappear under the seven-day lead-time control. This supports only reusable recorded information, not tumor biology, response, causality or benefit.

A supported W secondary that is substantially attenuated after exact `W_packet` exposure, or a supported NC increment comparable to the primary, is adverse to a state-specific interpretation and redirects data acquisition toward scheduling, intent, outside-care and severity review. If W or NC is unsupported or fails its precision rule, the result is inconclusive about that rival; it does not count against the primary. A positive W-adjusted increment with no NC increment is compatible with state-consistent information, but still not proof of biology. A primary increment reproduced by value/time permutation, process controls or near-day-42-only records is adverse to the claimed state interpretation. Mixed state/workflow evidence warrants adjudication, not a treatment rule. An imprecise null is not decisive refutation.

Every conclusion must link to a computed row in `decision_facing_summary.csv` and identify whether it is computationally checkable. Clinical response, treatment intent, assay units/reference ranges, outside care, mortality, harms, costs, mechanism, net benefit and treatment utility require unavailable evidence, expert adjudication or another study.

## Required solver outputs and deliverable

Require:

- `frozen_patient_split.json`, cohort/index/duplicate/early-repeat and `obs_end` audits;
- `review_workflow_proxy_audit.csv`, `proxy_definition_and_leakage_report.json`, `proxy_support_gate.csv`;
- `negative_control_endpoint_audit.csv`, `negative_control_support_gate.csv`;
- held-out predictions/losses for M0, A, B, A*, B* and supported NC models for both elastic-net and GRU;
- `state_workflow_contrasts.csv`, `proxy_adjusted_contrast.csv`, `negative_control_contrasts.csv`, `falsification_results.csv`;
- `multiplicity_familywise_intervals.csv`, `calibration.csv`, `weight_ess_audit.csv`, and `decision_facing_summary.csv`;
- `claim_output_map.md` mapping each prose claim to outputs, uncertainty and its computational/clinical status.

A supported secondary has a numeric estimate, interval, support counts, precision flag and exact definition. An unsupported one has no estimate and a deterministic `inconclusive_support_failure` row. No solver may silently drop a failed secondary or replace it with a broader proxy/endpoint.

## Alternatives, compute and selection/deferral record

The alternatives are scientifically comparable because both fit the same target, day-42 landmark, [43,181) outcome window, A/B channel ablations, patient-held-out split, IPCW/observation weights, support gates, metrics and falsification controls.

The elastic-net hazard is selected as the primary because it is transparent enough to audit whether assay information survives explicit workflow accounting. Planning estimate: 2–8 CPUs, 8–16 GiB, generally under one hour; this is unverified until solver execution. The compact GRU is the substantive learned alternative because it preserves irregular event order, assay trajectories and order-to-exam timing that summary features lose. Planning estimate: one allocated A100, 4–8 CPUs, 16–32 GiB, approximately 1–3 hours; unverified. A GPU is not required for the elastic-net. If a GPU is used for the GRU, the solver must request it through managed allocation and use the allocated `cuda:0`; an unallocated shell CUDA result is not a feasibility test.

Deferred: large transformers, broad hyperparameter searches, free-text examination NLP, semantic order interpretation and latent clinical-response modeling. These add complexity without resolving the named state/workflow uncertainty and require missing labels/clinical semantics. Revisit the GRU only if it changes the interpretation on the same held-out estimand, not for a small predictive gain. Revisit W/NC only with new data or a predeclared support change; never by post hoc substitution.

## Evidence limits and next decision

The HCC snapshot lacks imaging payloads and adjudicated mRECIST/RECICL response, treatment intent/scheduling, outside-care events, assay units/reference ranges, mortality, harms, costs and expert severity review. The examinations table has `检查所见` and `检查诊断`, but these are not a validated response adjudication and are excluded from response labeling and NLP. Therefore, even a fully supportive computational result justifies only a next study linking recorded assays to adjudicated imaging/intent and outside care; it cannot support a treatment rule.

Continue to imaging/intent/outside-care adjudication if the primary gate and controls support a residual recorded-state increment. Prioritize workflow/scheduling and severity data if the W or NC evidence is adverse. Defer interpretation if either secondary fails support/precision. Abandon the assay-state validation direction only after adequately supported, repeated timing and process controls reproduce or eliminate the increment. No fitted results are claimed here.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Dai Y, Zhao S, Wu Q, Zhang J, Zeng X, Jiang H. *A CT-Based Deep Learning Radiomics Scoring System for Predicting the Prognosis to Repeat TACE in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Cohort Study*. Journal of Hepatocellular Carcinoma. 2025;12:1647–1659. doi:10.2147/jhc.s525920. Relevant full-text HTML passages inspected; attached excerpt is bounded.

[K2] Tsurusaki M, Sofue K, Murakami T, Tanigawa N. *Radiological Assessment and Therapeutic Evaluation in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Differentiation and Treatment Response with Japanese Guidelines*. Cancers (Basel). 2024;17(1):101. doi:10.3390/cancers17010101. Relevant full-text XML passages inspected; attached excerpt is bounded.

[K3] Minh VL, Hung NV, Anh PT, Anh PT, Thong PM. *Recorded Early Imaging Responses After Transarterial Chemoembolization Plus Lenvatinib Versus Transarterial Chemoembolization Without Documented Lenvatinib for Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Vietnamese Cohort Study*. Journal of Clinical Medicine. 2026;15(17):6839. doi:10.3390/jcm15176839. Relevant full-text XML passages inspected; attached excerpt is bounded.

## Change from parent and rejected alternatives

This child preserves the parent’s exact index, day-42 landmark, early-repeat exclusion, [43,181) operational endpoint, source paths/hashes, joins, time fields, patient-held-out estimand, all-source IPCW/observation logic, elastic-net baseline and matched compact GRU. The substantive repair is interpretive and operational: the overall state contrast is the only primary decision; W is one exact proxy-accounting secondary rather than a set of selected proxy strata; NC is one exact endpoint secondary; both have deterministic support and precision gates, one max-|t| family, and no-substitution rules. Broad `E_any`/`O_open`, proxy-stratum selection, alternative care endpoints and response-text modeling are explicitly rejected or deferred because they dilute the minimum discriminating experiment or require unavailable clinical meaning. This is a narrower claim with clearer failure handling, not a claim that the data can adjudicate HCC response.

## Competing explanations and what the experiment can establish

The leading explanation is that measured assay values or qualitative states contain recorded information about patient state. The strongest rivals are:

- workflow/selection: an order, review, encounter or planned care pathway produces both an assay record and a subsequent procedure;
- lead time: records close to day 42 encode a near-term plan rather than a durable state;
- severity/measurement: unmeasured severity or access drives assay recording, review intensity and procedures.

The overall state contrast tests predictive/descriptive incremental information. A positive result is not a causal effect, tumor-response estimate, treatment-benefit estimate or treatment rule. The workflow secondary tests whether the increment attenuates after the exact review/completion packet is represented; it cannot remove all unmeasured workflow. The non-TACE secondary tests whether a similar increment follows generic procedure care; it cannot prove biological specificity.

A state-consistent pattern is a primary increment that remains directionally consistent under observation weighting, explicit `W_packet`, seven-day lead-time removal and assay value/time permutations, with a smaller or unsupported increment for `Y_NC`. A workflow-consistent pattern is attenuation after `W_packet`, concentration in its supported pathway, disappearance under the lead-time control, or a comparable `Y_NC` increment. Both patterns remain compatible with residual severity confounding.

# Support-ascertainment repair: observed-opportunity discordant AKI

Status: proposed substantive child of candidate-a9d5b8e26e4cae544423df9d; design only. No cohort scan, model fit, or scientific result was run.

## Change from the selected parent

The parent’s question is retained: after a six-hour lag, does creatinine recovery discordance with direct urine output and/or recorded input-minus-output predict short-term hospital death and ICU-recorded RRT? The audit changes the support interpretation and estimand in three consequential ways.

1. The local dictionary invalidates the inherited expected extubation ID 225795: it is “Dextran 40” in `icu/inputevents`. Extubation is `icu/procedureevents.itemid=227194`; `225792` is “Invasive Ventilation” and `225794` is “Non-invasive Ventilation.” The corrected definition is binding-critical.
2. A same-window support or “support-first” contrast is not a treatment comparison. Support can be triggered by the renal process, severity, or documentation intensity. It is therefore a prespecified temporal compatibility diagnostic, never a primary adjustment set, principal-stratum causal effect, or mechanism test.
3. The primary estimand is explicitly an observed-ICU prognostic estimand, with separate endpoint-specific risk sets and observed antecedent-support and measurement-opportunity strata. “No observed support” means no qualifying record, not no treatment. ICU-recorded RRT means only RRT recorded while in the retained ICU; it is not all-hospital RRT.

These are substantive repairs to estimand and decision criteria, not compiler fixes.

## Scientific opening and falsifiable claim

Creatinine recovery can be discordant with urine output and recorded balance. A leading explanation is that the discordance is a clinically useful prognostic marker of renal recovery not captured by creatinine alone. The strongest rival is a support/ascertainment process: observed vasopressors, ventilation, administered inputs, diuresis, renal testing, and ICU retention reflect severity and observation practice, while support can change urine and recorded balance. Missing ward RRT, treatment intent, insensible losses, muscle mass, and measured GFR prevent causal or mechanistic identification.

The evidence inspected supports only bounded premises. [K1] reports that creatinine-based eGFR can overestimate measured kidney function during prolonged critical illness as muscle is lost. [K2] shows that urine-output windows and persistence choices affect AKI classification and mortality prediction. [K3] reports AKI/mortality associations alongside vasoactive drugs, ventilation, and positive recorded balance, and states that KRT was discretionary and fluid balance omitted insensible losses. None establishes this MIMIC phenotype or a causal support effect.

Hypothesis:

> Among adults in a first eligible ICU stay who are alive, remain in that ICU, have no pre-landmark ICU-recorded RRT, and have a classifiable renal state at each landmark, the six-hour-lagged discordant recovery state has a reproducible seven-day prognostic contrast for hospital death and for ICU-recorded RRT versus concordant recovery; the contrast is not wholly reproduced by observed antecedent support history or by renal/input/output measurement opportunity.

The claim is noncausal. Supportive results establish only a reproducible association in the observed population and strata. They do not establish that renal dysfunction caused death, that support caused the phenotype, or that ICU-recorded RRT represents all RRT.

## Actual deliverable

The solver must newly estimate and save:

- a cohort flow from first eligible ICU stay through t0 and landmarks L in {24, 48, 72} hours;
- renal states: concordant recovery, low-urine-only, positive-recorded-balance-only, both, no recovery, and unknown/insufficient opportunity; the primary contrast is discordant (low urine OR positive recorded balance) versus concordant recovery, with mutually exclusive component contrasts;
- corrected support dictionary audit and event intervals;
- endpoint-specific seven-day Aalen–Johansen cumulative incidences, standardized risk differences and uncertainty for hospital death and ICU-recorded RRT;
- overall primary estimates and descriptive estimates in observed antecedent support-history and observed measurement-opportunity strata;
- risk-set counts, competing events, ICU-exit attrition, unknown opportunity, invalid times/units and sparse-cell decisions;
- fixed-summary and temporal alternatives on identical subjects, inputs and subject-level split;
- a manifest linking every output to source table, item definition, key, clinical time, interval, risk set, competing event and interpretation.

Completion requires all outputs and conclusions linked to computed tables. Readiness or a model coefficient is not completion.

## Population, clocks and exposure

Use MIMIC-IV adults with `hosp/patients.anchor_age >= 18`. Join `icu/icustays` to `hosp/admissions` on `(subject_id, hadm_id)`, retain valid `intime < outtime` stays overlapping the admission, sort by `intime, stay_id`, and retain exactly the first valid ICU stay per hospital admission. Keep all admissions from a subject in one split.

Use ICU-relative hours. Primary creatinine is `hosp/labevents.itemid=50912`; `52546` is sensitivity only. Require finite `valuenum`, compatible `valueuom), clinical `charttime) within the retained ICU, and median duplicate valid values at a charttime. `storetime` cannot move an observation earlier. t0 is the earliest eligible creatinine charttime in [intime, intime+72h) meeting the inherited AKI increase criterion: >=0.3 mg/dL over a valid preceding 48 hours or >=1.5 times the valid minimum in the preceding seven days, using same subject/admission and no future values. Exclude established ICU-recorded RRT before t0; label missing baseline, failed t0, invalid time and pre-t0 RRT separately.

For L in {24,48,72}, set Ltime=t0+L. Primary renal interval:
`A_L=[max(t0,Ltime-24h), Ltime-6h)`; washout `W_L=[Ltime-6h,Ltime)). Primary renal features cannot use W_L or later. The primary landmark risk set for death is alive at Ltime and still in the retained hospital episode; the primary RRT risk set additionally requires alive, still in the retained ICU, no ICU-recorded RRT before Ltime, and a classifiable renal state. A renal-unknown subject is retained in flow but not in the discordant-versus-concordant contrast. Do not impute unknown states.

## Corrected source bindings and support audit

The audit did not inspect patient rows or estimate prevalence. It verifies labels and bindings only.

## Renal state and observed opportunity

Use primary direct urine output itemids `226559,226560,226561,226563,226567` (Foley, Void, Condom Cath, Suprapubic and Straight Cath) from `icu/outputevents). Exclude nephrostomy, OR/PACU, mixed GU-irrigant, text-estimate and Apache-derived items as in the parent. Convert with nearest valid weight at or before Ltime within 48h using `icu/chartevents` weight itemids `224639,226512,226531`; verify units with `d_items). Empty bins are unknown, not zero. Require valid primary urine information in >=2 of 3 A_L bins; report all-three and >=1 sensitivities. Use the inherited frozen threshold; never optimize it on outcome.

For recorded balance, use `icu/inputevents` intervals overlapping A_L. Use exactly one of `amount) or `totalamount) per row, compatible mL units only, and retain composition, unresolved fraction, and input-minus-direct-primary-urine. This is recorded balance, not total-body balance. Require valid input and urine opportunity for a balance state.

Define observed measurement opportunity before inspecting outcomes:

- `O_L=complete): renal criteria met (>=2 urine bins and valid creatinine contribution) and balance input/urine are unit-valid in the required interval;
- `O_L=partial/unknown): a renal or input/urine requirement is not met or has invalid/missing timing;
- `O_L=ICU-truncated): the retained stay ends before the full A_L interval.

`O_L) is an observed data-quality/measurement stratum, not a counterfactual principal stratum. Complete opportunity does not mean complete bedside measurement. Primary contrasts are reported overall and, only when estimable, within O_L; the complete-opportunity analysis is a sensitivity to quantify ascertainment, not an adjustment that creates causal identification.

## Support history and endpoint-specific estimands

Define antecedent history `H_L=[t0,max(t0,Ltime-24h))), which is empty at L=24, and support interval `S_L=A_L). Use only valid intervals with `starttime<endtime), clipped to the retained ICU.

For H_L, define mutually exclusive observed support-history strata: no qualifying support record, one qualifying non-RRT class, multiple classes, and unknown/invalid timing. Qualifying classes are vasopressor, ventilation, administered-volume and diuresis. These are records of support/process, not treatment assignment. For L=24 the support-history comparison is structurally unavailable and must be labelled so.

For S_L, report support-first when the first qualifying support start precedes the first renal-defining observation, renal-first for the reverse, simultaneous/indeterminate for ties/missing times, and neither if no qualifying support record. This is a temporal compatibility diagnostic only. Positive balance ordering is indeterminate unless its contributing input interval starts before the first renal observation. Do not adjust for S_L, W_L, support recorded after Ltime, or any outcome-derived support state.

Primary estimand for each L and outcome is:

> The seven-day observed-ICU prognostic cumulative incidence difference between discordant and concordant renal states, standardized over the observed eligible risk set, separately for hospital death and ICU-recorded RRT, with descriptive estimates within predeclared H_L and O_L strata when those strata meet the sparse-cell rule.

For hospital death, causes are death and alive hospital discharge; alive hospitalized at seven days is administrative censoring. For the RRT endpoint, the risk set requires retained-ICU presence at Ltime; causes are first ICU-recorded RRT, alive ICU exit, and hospital death before RRT, with the earliest clock event winning. ICU-recorded RRT is not post-ICU or ward RRT. Report RRT only as an ascertainment-limited endpoint.

Estimate Aalen–Johansen seven-day cumulative incidences and risk differences, with six-hour cause-specific discrete hazards as an implementation check. Provide unadjusted and standardized estimates. Antecedent H_L may be included as a descriptive prognostic standardization block only for L>24; it is not a causal adjustment for support. No causal effect, mediation, principal-stratum effect or mechanism is estimated.

## Sparse-cell and interpretation rule

Freeze this rule before fitting:

- An overall discordant-versus-concordant estimate is eligible only if each state has at least 50 subjects and the endpoint has at least 10 total events across the comparison risk set.
- A component or H_L/O_L stratum estimate is eligible only if each compared state has at least 50 subjects and at least 5 endpoint events in that stratum. Otherwise output counts and exact event proportions only and mark the contrast “not estimable—sparse,” without pooling strata or changing landmarks.
- Any landmark with >40% unknown/partial opportunity, or a corrected-label/interval failure affecting >5% of support rows, is a feasibility warning; it does not justify post hoc outcome selection. If the primary state is too sparse at all landmarks, defer the renal-discordance claim and retain only the ascertainment audit.
- If uncertainty spans a clinically important range, call the result inconclusive, not adverse.

Supportive: an eligible contrast persists in at least two landmarks, in the complete-opportunity sensitivity, and is not materially reproduced by H_L support-only gradients or S_L ordering. This supports a reproducible prognostic association only.

Adverse: the contrast attenuates/disappears in complete-opportunity strata, is confined to support-first/documentation-dense records, appears only in the current-window sensitivity, reverses across landmarks, or depends on the former erroneous 225795 label. This favors support/measurement rivalry and weakens the renal interpretation. It does not prove normal renal function.

Inconclusive: sparse cells, large unknown opportunity, wide intervals, inconsistent event clocks, or endpoint-specific discordance without stable interpretation. A temporal model gain without a stable component-specific contrast is predictive information, not evidence of renal mechanism.

Computationally checkable: dictionary labels, joins, state construction, interval clipping, landmark/washout, risk sets, AJ counts, sparse rule, split integrity, calibration and held-out metrics. Clinical adjudication/another study is required for treatment intent, complete ward RRT, measured GFR, muscle mass, true fluid balance, goals of care, causal effects and transportability.

## Baseline and temporal alternative

Primary transparent baseline: fixed summaries from exactly A_L and H_L, with creatinine level/peak/recovery/slope, AKI stage, three-bin urine and masks, recorded input/output composition and balance, weight/CVP, support class/presence/duration, O_L and documentation counts. Fit separate six-hour cause-specific discrete-time competing-risk heads for hospital death/alive discharge and ICU-recorded RRT/ICU exit/death. No W_L or post-L input is visible.

Substantive same-question alternative: a temporal model on identical six-hour bins from t0 through Ltime-6h, with separate channels and missingness masks for creatinine, urine, input/output, weight/CVP, vasopressors, ventilation using corrected `227194) termination, administered volume, diuresis, RRT and observation counts. Use a causal-time mask to exclude W_L and post-L values. Separate endpoint heads predict the same causes. Auxiliary outputs may summarize support-first/renal-first/simultaneous/unknown and persistent/resolving discordance, but these are descriptive process labels, not mechanisms.

Fit both using a subject-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test split, all admissions from a subject in one split. Evaluate held-out endpoint-specific calibration, cumulative-incidence calibration, time-dependent Brier, cause-specific discrimination, support/opportunity-stratum calibration, and bootstrap intervals for risk contrasts. Selection is based on whether timing/persistence changes the renal-versus-ascertainment interpretation, not a small AUROC gain. The baseline is scientifically valuable because it exposes the contrast and strata; the temporal alternative can reveal whether persistence/order/transitions explain residual association that fixed summaries lose.

Future solver planning envelope: CPU-default, 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB, up to 28800 seconds; a bounded readiness probe may use <=600 seconds. An A100 is optional for repeated temporal fitting, not required. These are planning limits, not measured runtime; no full fit was run in this episode.

Deferred alternatives: causal treatment-effect/IPW or principal-strata analysis (missing intent, completeness, ward RRT and counterfactual opportunity); all-hospital RRT endpoint; single black-box primary model; post-L support adjustment; external validation without an adjudicated cohort. Revisit only with treatment-intent, complete-observation, or external clinical adjudication data.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Haines et al. motivates the creatinine measurement-artifact rival. [K2] bounds urine-output threshold/window and opportunity choices. [K3] motivates support/severity and incomplete-balance rivalry. The attached key-references.json and UTF-8 excerpts preserve the parent’s receipts and exactly these three distinct works. This proposal adds corrected local dictionary binding, an observed-opportunity estimand, endpoint-specific ICU ascertainment risk sets, and a frozen sparse-cell decision rule; it does not reproduce any cited work.

# UKB CBC cancer-type contrast: absolute-risk boundary for timing and clinical selection

Status: proposed substantive child of candidate-0abc2db8e1e021a786125005. No hypothesis test or full solver fit has been executed. This child preserves the parent's exact UKB namespace, paired-array rules, cancer classes and temporal design, and adds a prespecified decision-facing absolute-risk estimand and sharper source/selection classification.

## Scientific opening and claim boundary

CBC abnormalities are associated with cancer in primary-care records, and a recent longitudinal CRC study reports pre-diagnostic CBC trajectories. Those observations do not establish whether a CBC pattern is relatively CRC-specific rather than haematologic, whether a two-year delay removes near-diagnostic ascertainment, or whether the apparent contrast survives a different timed outcome source. The clinically consequential uncertainty is therefore interpretability: would the pattern represent a stable, cancer-type-specific risk contrast, or only registry timing, inpatient capture, or the selected subset who return for a repeat research assessment?

[K1] supports a broad primary-care CBC/cancer association but not cancer-type specificity or delayed UKB risk. [K2] motivates a 24-month longitudinal boundary but is CRC-only and explicitly investigational. [K3] shows why discrimination without calibration and external/temporal validation is insufficient for clinical claims. The inspected works are abstract-only; no unavailable supplement or full text is claimed.

The strongest evidence-supported claim is limited: CBC abnormalities and some longitudinal CBC summaries can associate with subsequent CRC-related or broad cancer outcomes in selected populations. The unresolved claim tested here is:

> Among UKB adults with a complete first CBC and no qualifying cancer at T0, the prespecified higher-platelet/lower-haemoglobin phenotype has a larger CRC than haematologic-cancer association in the delayed T0+2 to T0+5 interval, and that relative contrast has a clinically interpretable absolute-risk direction that is not produced by repeat-observation selection or by registry-specific timing/capture.

This is a descriptive, temporally ordered association. It is not a causal, cellular-mechanistic, diagnostic-accuracy, screening, clinical-utility, stage, treatment or referral-threshold claim. A result can support a next external validation without establishing that a clinician should act on an individual CBC.

## Exact data binding and inspected availability

All analysis uses the one read-only UKB source below; no participant join is performed.

- Dataset snapshot: `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`; catalog SHA-256 `9bc20153591045e19e908fc0b538d04a950f2fe75b85ba99c8de1fb3b2d750be`.
- Catalog/guide: `datasets/README.md`, `datasets/ukb/README.md`, and `datasets/ukb/table-5d49a6760e7ffdbd.json`; table `ukb671626.csv (Parquet)`, source ID `ukb_483356f97e1e8132_parquet`, 502,371 rows, unique key `eid`, identifier namespace `ukb671626`, ordinary file with no archive member.
- Read-only Parquet: `[private-path]/ukb_483356f97e1e8132.parquet`, SHA-256 `a7c03cf84cd951dec9fa013ae76e6e1a363f579506886f59a0f179beae15e23a`.
- Original lineage, not an analysis input: `[private-path]/ukb671626.csv`, SHA-256 `5875087f2fc05adb6c9a1e3826cd483171d81667a101107ee8b016fa1f6d628f`.
- Binding target: `/data/ukb_483356f97e1e8132_parquet/ukb_483356f97e1e8132.parquet`, same Parquet hash.

Required fields are physically present according to the inherited table/schema audit; the solver must recompute all completeness and validity denominators rather than importing audit counts:

- Key and landmarks: `eid`; `53-0.0` = T0, `53-1.0` = T1, `53-2.0` = T2. These are research-assessment dates, not laboratory order dates.
- CBC: `30000-{0,1,2}.0` WBC, `30020-{0,1,2}.0` haemoglobin, `30070-{0,1,2}.0` RDW, `30080-{0,1,2}.0` platelets.
- Baseline covariates: `31-0.0` sex, `21003-0.0` age, `21001-0.0` BMI, `20116-0.0` smoking, `30710-0.0` CRP, and calendar year derived from T0.
- Registry outcome arrays: pair same-index `40005-j.0` cancer date with `40006-j.0` ICD-10 code, j=0,...,21. Keep only parseable valid pairs and take the earliest qualifying event.
- Inpatient sensitivity arrays: pair same-index `41270-k.0` ICD-10 diagnosis code with `41280-k.0` first-inpatient-diagnosis date, k=0,...,258. This is a secondary ascertainment proxy, not a gold standard. Never cross indices and never pool the sources into one outcome date.
- Death: `40000-0.0`; `40001-0.0` is audit-only. Death is a competing event, not a cancer-type proxy.

Classify CRC as C18-C20, haematologic cancer as C81-C96, and other primary malignant cancer as C00-C97 excluding those two families and secondary C77-C79. Report invalid dates, missing pair members, duplicate eids, date ties, impossible date ordering and all code-family denominators.

The source does not contain symptoms, reason for testing, laboratory order date/source, primary-care contacts, ferritin/iron, reticulocytes, FIT, smear, marrow/pathology adjudication, stage, treatment, imaging, transfusion context, healthcare utilisation, or expert cancer adjudication. The inpatient source is selectively observed through hospitalization and may itself be severity- and healthcare-use-dependent.

## Population, windows and estimands

### Primary first-CBC population

Include unique nonmissing `eid` with parseable T0 and complete instance-0 WBC, haemoglobin, RDW and platelets. Exclude any valid qualifying registry cancer on or before T0. Do not require T1 or T2.

For the 0-2 year analysis, follow from T0 to the first CRC, haematologic cancer, other primary cancer, death, administrative censoring at 2022-12-31, or T0+2 years. For the delayed analysis, enter the risk set only if alive and free of all qualifying cancer at T0+2; follow to the first event, censoring, or T0+5 years. Events before T0+2 therefore do not become delayed events and their exclusions/counts are reported. This is a conditional delayed-risk estimand, not an unconditional five-year population risk.

### Relative D estimand

Standardize each baseline CBC variable using development-only means and scales. Fit separate cause-specific models for CRC and haematologic cancer, with other cancer and death as competing causes, using the four CBC values, age, sex, BMI, smoking, CRP and T0 calendar year. In window w:

`D_s(w) = (beta_platelet,CRC,s,w - beta_Hb,CRC,s,w) - (beta_platelet,HEME,s,w - beta_Hb,HEME,s,w)`

where s is registry (R) or inpatient (I) outcome source. Positive D means the platelet/haemoglobin contrast is relatively more CRC-associated. Report the component coefficients, `D_R(0-2)`, `D_R(2-5)`, and the corresponding inpatient values; do not treat D as a risk ratio, causal effect or mechanism. The primary relative claim is delayed `D_R(2-5)>0), with 0-2 as a near-diagnostic/timing comparator.

### Absolute-risk / decision-facing estimand

Define two fixed, prespecified CBC profiles in development standard-deviation units:

- `g_CRC`: platelets +1 SD, haemoglobin -1 SD, WBC and RDW at their development means.
- `g_HEME`: platelets -1 SD, haemoglobin +1 SD, WBC and RDW at their development means.

For every individual in the relevant risk set, retain their observed age, sex, BMI, smoking, CRP and T0 year, replace only the two platelet/haemoglobin values by each profile, and standardize the resulting model-based competing-risk predictions over that same risk set. Let `P_s(c,g,w)` be the Aalen-Johansen/model-standardized cumulative incidence of cancer class c during w under source s and profile g. The primary decision-facing contrast is the absolute-risk difference-in-differences:

`A_s(2-5) = [P_s(CRC,g_CRC,2-5) - P_s(CRC,g_HEME,2-5)] - [P_s(HEME,g_CRC,2-5) - P_s(HEME,g_HEME,2-5)]`.

Report the four component risks and the two class-specific risk differences as percentage points, not just A. Positive A means that the fixed profile ordering shifts absolute incidence toward CRC rather than haematologic cancer. Report the same estimand in 0-2 years and under the repeat-selection strata. A is a model-standardized association contrast; it is not an individual's diagnostic probability or a clinical action threshold.

Because the source has no validated decision threshold, the proposal uses an explicit descriptive effect-size boundary rather than inventing a referral rule: `delta_A=0.01` (one percentage point) for the delayed-window A contrast, with 95% bootstrap intervals. Decision-facing labels are prespecified as:

- decision-scale supportive: both source-specific intervals are entirely above +1.0 percentage point, D has the prespecified positive direction, and the registry/inpatient qualitative classification agrees;
- relative-only or inconclusive: D is positive but at least one A interval overlaps [-1.0,+1.0] percentage points, or there are too few paired events for source comparison;
- adverse to the proposed interpretation: either source interval is entirely below -1.0 percentage point, a source changes from above +1.0 to below -1.0, or the D direction reverses precisely.

This boundary is a transparent reporting boundary, not evidence that a one-percentage-point difference would justify testing, referral or treatment.

## Registry-versus-inpatient timing and selection falsifications

### Source bridge

Derive registry and inpatient event series independently from the exact paired arrays. Run the same cohort, delayed entry, covariates, competing events, standardization, D, A and temporal split under each source. Keep outputs side by side; do not select the source based on favorable final performance and do not average them.

Among participants with valid same-class events in both sources, report inpatient-date minus registry-date displacement by cancer class: median, IQR, quantiles, event count, and the fraction whose source date crosses T0+2 or T0+5. If fewer than 50 same-class paired events are available for a class, that class's displacement and source-robustness conclusion is inconclusive. A disagreement can reflect different clinical capture, not which source is correct.

Call the delayed interpretation source-sensitive if any prespecified condition holds: D direction reverses; the delayed A classification crosses the ±1 percentage-point boundary; `|D_R(2-5)-D_I(2-5)|>0.20` log-hazard units; the absolute delayed contrast differs by >1 percentage point; or a source-by-T0-calendar-era interaction is present with a 95% interval excluding zero. Concordance is only compatibility with robustness because registry and inpatient coding may share errors. Registry-positive/inpatient-negative is adverse to registry robustness, not proof that CBC biology is absent. Sparse overlap is inconclusive.

### Clinical/repeat-observation selection

Define `R=1` before using any cancer outcome as a complete T1 assessment strictly after T0 and within 2-8 years, with all four instance-1 CBC fields observed; `R=0` is otherwise. R is a future-attendance indicator for a sensitivity comparison, not a baseline predictor. The repeat-CBC cohort additionally requires no qualifying cancer or death on/before T1 and uses baseline CBC, four changes, gap and baseline covariates; T2 is sensitivity-only.

For the first-CBC population, report D and A separately for R=1 and R=0 under each source, fixed 2-8-year gap strata, T0 calendar-era strata, and two-year near-diagnostic displacement. Fit an R-observation model using only baseline T0 covariates and use stabilized inverse-probability weights only as a selection stress test. Report overlap/positivity and compare weighted with unweighted estimates; do not call this a causal correction because symptoms, indication and healthcare use are unmeasured. A change across R strata or a large weighted/unweighted shift is adverse to generalizing the repeat-CBC finding to all first-CBC participants. If the weighted analysis has poor positivity or delayed events are sparse, report inconclusive rather than trimming until favorable.

Required negative controls/falsifications are: other-primary-cancer specificity; CRC-versus-haematologic label permutation preserving dates/censoring; source-specific calendar-era interaction; gap strata; repeat-era strata; paired-array integrity; and a near-diagnostic check showing whether a signal disappears or reverses after excluding the first two years. A cancer-type permutation collapsing toward zero checks implementation and type specificity, not biology.

## Equal-input method comparison

The actual scientific deliverable requires new fitting, not readiness: source-specific cohort/event audits; 0-2 and 2-5 D and A estimates; class-specific absolute risks; date displacement; R-strata and weighted selection diagnostics; permutation/other-cancer controls; and a conclusion labelled supportive, adverse or inconclusive.

A. Transparent baseline: separate cause-specific Cox models for CRC, haematologic cancer, other primary cancer and death, with the same four CBC predictors and covariates above. Use robust intervals, proportional-hazard/time-window diagnostics, and Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence. The Cox model makes D and the absolute profile standardization auditable, but it can lose nonlinear platelet/haemoglobin ranges, interactions and time-varying type-specific hazards.

B. Same-input learned alternative: a CPU gradient-boosted discrete-time multi-task competing-risk model with yearly intervals and separate hazards for CRC, haematologic cancer, other cancer and death. Use exactly the same people, inputs, paired outcome source, landmark, windows, competing-risk definitions and fixed profiles as A; only the functional form changes. It can reveal nonlinear Hb/platelet effects, interactions and time-varying hazards hidden by additive Cox. It cannot reveal clinical indication or mechanism.

Sort by T0: earliest 70% for development and latest 30% for final temporal holdout, keeping participants intact. Fit standardization, missingness decisions, weights, tuning and calibration only inside development. On the locked holdout compare both methods using target-specific calibration intercept/slope, calibration plots, 2- and 5-year cumulative-incidence Brier and log scores, the fixed-profile A contrast and participant-bootstrap uncertainty; AUC/Uno C-index is secondary. Use 500 participant bootstrap replicates, preserving failed fits. If a final holdout has fewer than 50 haematologic events, learned type-specific metrics and model superiority are inconclusive. A learned model that improves ranking but not calibration or the fixed-profile A contrast does not establish a scientific advance.

Resource estimate: 8-16 CPU cores, 32-64 GiB RAM, approximately 2-4 hours including selected-column parsing, fits and bootstrap; unmeasured in this branch. The solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. GPU is not required for this tabular experiment; available A100 capacity does not add scientific value unless a measured implementation shows otherwise.

## Bounded unused metabolic/liver direction and revisit rule

A concrete alternative in the same `ukb671626` table is the low-ApoB/low-albumin liver-risk direction: `30640-0.0` ApoB, `30600-0.0` albumin, `30620-0.0` ALT, `30710-0.0` CRP, with HCC C22, biliary C23-C24, other primary cancer and death from paired `40005/40006`, plus optional K70-K77 inpatient liver-disease sensitivity from paired `41270/41280`. # UKB CBC cancer-type contrast: absolute-risk boundary for timing and clinical selection

Status: proposed substantive child of candidate-0abc2db8e1e021a786125005. No hypothesis test or full solver fit has been executed. This child preserves the parent's exact UKB namespace, paired-array rules, cancer classes and temporal design, and adds a prespecified decision-facing absolute-risk estimand and sharper source/selection classification.

## Scientific opening and claim boundary

CBC abnormalities are associated with cancer in primary-care records, and a recent longitudinal CRC study reports pre-diagnostic CBC trajectories. Those observations do not establish whether a CBC pattern is relatively CRC-specific rather than haematologic, whether a two-year delay removes near-diagnostic ascertainment, or whether the apparent contrast survives a different timed outcome source. The clinically consequential uncertainty is therefore interpretability: would the pattern represent a stable, cancer-type-specific risk contrast, or only registry timing, inpatient capture, or the selected subset who return for a repeat research assessment?

[K1] supports a broad primary-care CBC/cancer association but not cancer-type specificity or delayed UKB risk. [K2] motivates a 24-month longitudinal boundary but is CRC-only and explicitly investigational. [K3] shows why discrimination without calibration and external/temporal validation is insufficient for clinical claims. The inspected works are abstract-only; no unavailable supplement or full text is claimed.

The strongest evidence-supported claim is limited: CBC abnormalities and some longitudinal CBC summaries can associate with subsequent CRC-related or broad cancer outcomes in selected populations. The unresolved claim tested here is:

> Among UKB adults with a complete first CBC and no qualifying cancer at T0, the prespecified higher-platelet/lower-haemoglobin phenotype has a larger CRC than haematologic-cancer association in the delayed T0+2 to T0+5 interval, and that relative contrast has a clinically interpretable absolute-risk direction that is not produced by repeat-observation selection or by registry-specific timing/capture.

This is a descriptive, temporally ordered association. It is not a causal, cellular-mechanistic, diagnostic-accuracy, screening, clinical-utility, stage, treatment or referral-threshold claim. A result can support a next external validation without establishing that a clinician should act on an individual CBC.

## Exact data binding and inspected availability

All analysis uses the one read-only UKB source below; no participant join is performed.

- Dataset snapshot: `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`; catalog SHA-256 `9bc20153591045e19e908fc0b538d04a950f2fe75b85ba99c8de1fb3b2d750be`.

- Read-only Parquet: `[private-path]/ukb_483356f97e1e8132.parquet`, SHA-256 `a7c03cf84cd951dec9fa013ae76e6e1a363f579506886f59a0f179beae15e23a`.
- Original lineage, not an analysis input: `[private-path]/ukb671626.csv`, SHA-256 `5875087f2fc05adb6c9a1e3826cd483171d81667a101107ee8b016fa1f6d628f`.
- Binding target: `/data/ukb_483356f97e1e8132_parquet/ukb_483356f97e1e8132.parquet`, same Parquet hash.

Required fields are physically present according to the inherited table/schema audit; the solver must recompute all completeness and validity denominators rather than importing audit counts:

- Key and landmarks: `eid`; `53-0.0` = T0, `53-1.0` = T1, `53-2.0` = T2. These are research-assessment dates, not laboratory order dates.
- CBC: `30000-{0,1,2}.0` WBC, `30020-{0,1,2}.0` haemoglobin, `30070-{0,1,2}.0` RDW, `30080-{0,1,2}.0` platelets.
- Baseline covariates: `31-0.0` sex, `21003-0.0` age, `21001-0.0` BMI, `20116-0.0` smoking, `30710-0.0` CRP, and calendar year derived from T0.
- Registry outcome arrays: pair same-index `40005-j.0` cancer date with `40006-j.0` ICD-10 code, j=0,...,21. Keep only parseable valid pairs and take the earliest qualifying event.
- Inpatient sensitivity arrays: for each array slot k=0,...,258, pair the same-index schema columns `41270-0.k` (ICD-10 diagnosis code) with `41280-0.k` (first-inpatient-diagnosis date). The proposal shorthand `41270-k.0`/`41280-k.0` is rendered here using the verified physical field names. This is a secondary ascertainment proxy, not a gold standard. Never cross indices and never pool the sources into one outcome date.
- Death: `40000-0.0`; `40001-0.0` is audit-only. Death is a competing event, not a cancer-type proxy.

Classify CRC as C18-C20, haematologic cancer as C81-C96, and other primary malignant cancer as C00-C97 excluding those two families and secondary C77-C79. Report invalid dates, missing pair members, duplicate eids, date ties, impossible date ordering and all code-family denominators.

The source does not contain symptoms, reason for testing, laboratory order date/source, primary-care contacts, ferritin/iron, reticulocytes, FIT, smear, marrow/pathology adjudication, stage, treatment, imaging, transfusion context, healthcare utilisation, or expert cancer adjudication. The inpatient source is selectively observed through hospitalization and may itself be severity- and healthcare-use-dependent.

## Population, windows and estimands

### Primary first-CBC population

Include unique nonmissing `eid` with parseable T0 and complete instance-0 WBC, haemoglobin, RDW and platelets. Exclude any valid qualifying registry cancer on or before T0. Do not require T1 or T2.

For the 0-2 year analysis, follow from T0 to the first CRC, haematologic cancer, other primary cancer, death, administrative censoring at 2022-12-31, or T0+2 years. For the delayed analysis, enter the risk set only if alive and free of all qualifying cancer at T0+2; follow to the first event, censoring, or T0+5 years. Events before T0+2 therefore do not become delayed events and their exclusions/counts are reported. This is a conditional delayed-risk estimand, not an unconditional five-year population risk.

### Relative D estimand

Standardize each baseline CBC variable using development-only means and scales. Fit separate cause-specific models for CRC and haematologic cancer, with other cancer and death as competing causes, using the four CBC values, age, sex, BMI, smoking, CRP and T0 calendar year. In window w:

`D_s(w) = (beta_platelet,CRC,s,w - beta_Hb,CRC,s,w) - (beta_platelet,HEME,s,w - beta_Hb,HEME,s,w)`

where s is registry (R) or inpatient (I) outcome source. Positive D means the platelet/haemoglobin contrast is relatively more CRC-associated. ### Absolute-risk / decision-facing estimand

Define two fixed, prespecified CBC profiles in development standard-deviation units:

- `g_CRC`: platelets +1 SD, haemoglobin -1 SD, WBC and RDW at their development means.
- `g_HEME`: platelets -1 SD, haemoglobin +1 SD, WBC and RDW at their development means.

The primary decision-facing contrast is the absolute-risk difference-in-differences:

- decision-scale supportive: both source-specific intervals are entirely above +1.0 percentage point, D has the prespecified positive direction, and the registry/inpatient qualitative classification agrees;
- relative-only or inconclusive: D is positive but at least one A interval overlaps [-1.0,+1.0] percentage points, or there are too few paired events for source comparison;
- adverse to the proposed interpretation: either source interval is entirely below -1.0 percentage point, a source changes from above +1.0 to below -1.0, or the D direction reverses precisely.

This boundary is a transparent reporting boundary, not evidence that a one-percentage-point difference would justify testing, referral or treatment.

Derive registry and inpatient event series independently from the exact paired arrays. Run the same cohort, delayed entry, covariates, competing events, standardization, D, A and temporal split under each source. If fewer than 50 same-class paired events are available for a class, that class's displacement and source-robustness conclusion is inconclusive. A disagreement can reflect different clinical capture, not which source is correct.

Call the delayed interpretation source-sensitive if any prespecified condition holds: D direction reverses; the delayed A classification crosses the ±1 percentage-point boundary; `|D_R(2-5)-D_I(2-5)|>0.20` log-hazard units; the absolute delayed contrast differs by >1 percentage point; or a source-by-T0-calendar-era interaction is present with a 95% interval excluding zero. Concordance is only compatibility with robustness because registry and inpatient coding may share errors. # Evolution trajectory critique: is process signal a missing temporal state?

Status: independent substantive child proposal of `candidate-b70d2895cf347ff852af08e2`. This branch reports no cohort count, fitted coefficient, prediction, metric, or scientific result. It records a pre-specified experiment for the Lead to accept or reject.

## Decision and unresolved question

The parent’s strongest evidence-supported claim is descriptive: laboratory-result and vital-recording intensity/gap features may add a transport-sensitive increment beyond demographic and latest-in-window value summaries, but the increment could reflect measured severity, discharge/EOL selection, or hospital recording practice. The parent already tightens the feature/outcome boundary to [0,360] ICU-relative minutes, makes P12 (discharge offset >720 and no recorded EOL event through 720 minutes) primary, retains S720 and S6, and uses a value-state-matched process null.

The remaining consequential rival is evolving severity inside the existing six-hour window. A single latest value can miss a transient deterioration, recovery, or instability that prompts more observations. Conversely, a trajectory representation can appear to “explain” process density simply because its missingness and timing encode the same recording process. The smallest informative test is therefore not a raw-event model: it is a fixed-bin value trajectory added to the parent’s existing latest-value state, with all explicit observation-process variables kept separate.

The falsifiable hypothesis is:

> In the parent’s P12 population, if the observed lab/vital process increment is principally an unmodeled measured temporal-state proxy, adding pre-specified fixed-bin lab/vital value trajectories from the same [0,360] window will reduce the held-out-hospital process increment beyond the parent latest-value state by more than the 0.01 AUC negligible margin, with corresponding attenuation in calibration or the 10% review net-benefit contrast and no comparable residual in a trajectory-state-matched process null. If the process increment persists after this augmentation, or remains in the trajectory-state-matched null, the available data do not support temporal-state sufficiency; workflow, selection, or unmeasured severity remain better live explanations.

This is a descriptive sufficiency/transportability test. It cannot establish physiology, a monitoring adequacy effect, an order or clinician action, or a causal effect on ICU mortality.

## Clinical importance and advance

If the increment is absorbed by measured trajectories, recording density should not be presented as a stand-alone worsening or monitoring signal; the defensible descriptive carrier is the observed state trajectory, subject to calibration. If it persists after the trajectory test but is attenuated by P12/no-EOL boundaries or concentrated in particular hospitals, the next decision is selection audit, feed harmonization, or clinical adjudication rather than a more complex predictor. If it persists in held-out hospitals and after the trajectory-state null, it is evidence that the current value trajectory is insufficient, not evidence that recording causes mortality.

This advances the parent by testing the exact latest-value weakness while preserving its hospital-held-out P12/S720/S6 estimands, state-matched nulls, lab/vital intensity-versus-gap decomposition, and clinical interpretation limits. It does not add a new source, a post-landmark treatment covariate, or a new clinical endpoint.

[K1] Rajkomar et al. supports the general value of temporally structured EHR histories for cross-center mortality prediction, but does not identify an observation-process mechanism. The present test asks whether a process increment survives a deliberately small temporal-state augmentation.

[K2] Gao et al. (abstract-only inspection) supports treating information presence/missingness as potentially predictive and transport-sensitive, but does not establish whether it represents severity, workflow, or interface behavior. The present design makes explicit value trajectories and process summaries separate channels.

[K3] Hadler et al. supports external discrimination/calibration assessment and local adaptation when EHR patterns differ across hospitals, but does not identify physiology or clinical action. The present design uses the same hospital-held-out logic to test state sufficiency and site-specific recording rivals.

## Population, time, outcome, and preserved estimands

Time zero is ICU admission and every feature offset is ICU-relative.

1. Read `patient`. Retain `unitvisitnumber=1`, `unitstaytype=admit`, numeric `age >=18` (retain `>89`), finite `patientunitstayid`, `hospitalid`, `unitdischargeoffset`, and `unitdischargestatus`. Keep unknown categorical values as levels. For duplicate qualifying rows sharing `uniquepid`, retain the smallest finite `unitadmitoffset`, then smallest `patientunitstayid), and report the duplicate count.
2. Define P12 exactly as `unitdischargeoffset >720` and `EOL12=0`. `EOL12=1` when any finite `cpleolsaveoffset` or `cpleoldiscussionoffset` is in [0,720]. A missing carePlanEOL row means no recorded event, not no EOL decision.
3. Retain S720 = `unitdischargeoffset >720` regardless of EOL12 and S6 = `unitdischargeoffset >360`; both use exactly the same [0,360] feature window. P12 remains primary. S720 and S6 are boundary/sensitivity estimands, not causal corrections.
4. Require at least 100 S720 stays per hospital before fold assignment and at least five viable hospitals. If P12 has fewer than five hospitals or fewer than 100 outcome events, report P12 as inconclusive rather than promote S720.

## State and process variables

### Parent state X

Use the parent’s fold-isolated X exactly: age, gender, ethnicity, admissionweight, up to 30 lab analytes selected by training-fold distinct-stay coverage among keys with >=1% coverage, and up to 20 qualifying vital numeric channels selected by training-fold coverage with deterministic name tie-breaks. For every retained lab/vital channel, X takes the latest valid value in [0,360], without carry-forward, with training-fold median imputation. X is a value summary, not proof of physiology.

### New temporal state T

Use the same fold-selected channels as X. For every selected lab analyte and every selected vital field, partition the fixed window into [0,120), [120,240), and [240,360] minutes. Within each channel/bin, compute the median of finite valid values. Standardize using training-fold location/scale and impute an empty channel/bin with the training-fold median for that channel/bin. Do not add missingness indicators.

T is the concatenation of X and these fixed-bin values. It uses no row counts, number of distinct offsets, first/last offset, gap length, observed-bin count, presence flag, result revision timing, treatment, care, discharge, or EOL fields. Thus the explicit recording-process block cannot be reconstructed intentionally from T. An all-empty bin is still audited, but its absence is not a modeled state feature. No carry-forward or interpolation is allowed. If a channel’s training coverage fails the parent rule it is omitted for that fold; test-fold coverage never rescues it.

This representation can reveal a direction or level change that latest X loses, while remaining small enough for a transparent additive fit. It cannot represent unobserved physiology, and imputed values do not make a missing measurement observed.

### Process P

Retain the parent’s four explicit blocks, all computed from valid rows in [0,360] independently of row values:

- lab intensity: log1p(valid row count), distinct exact offsets, distinct 30-minute bins with a valid row, and retained channels observed at least once;
- lab gap: 360 minus last valid offset, largest empty 30-minute run, and fraction of 12 bins without a valid row;
- vital intensity and vital gap: the same definitions, with a value-column observation finite and offset-valid. Duplicate channel/offset rows count for intensity but are set-based for bins/gaps.

P variables are recording proxies, not confirmed orders, specimen collection, bedside measurement, device output, clinician decisions, or interface completeness.

## Baseline, learned alternative, split, estimands, and uncertainty

The simple baseline is elastic-net logistic regression with identical preprocessing and fixed feature blocks. For each process block or full P, fit:

- X-only and X+P;
- T-only and T+P.

The substantive learned alternative is a capacity-matched histogram gradient-boosting model with the same X/T/P inputs, target, folds, preprocessing isolation, random seeds, and uncertainty. It is included because nonlinear interactions between a trajectory change and a gap/intensity block may be invisible to the additive baseline. A predictive gain alone is not evidence for the state explanation; both learners must be read through the same attenuation and null contrasts.

For model m and evaluation e, with error signs oriented so positive is better:

`Q_P^X(e)=metric(X+P,e)-metric(X,e)`

`Q_P^T(e)=metric(T+P,e)-metric(T,e)`

`A_T(e)=Q_P^X(e)-Q_P^T(e)`.

Report AUC, AUPRC, Brier, calibration-in-the-large, calibration intercept/slope, alert burden, and decision-curve net benefit at 5%, 10%, and 20%. The primary transport estimand remains the parent’s held-out contrast `D_P^T=Q_P^T(internal)-Q_P^T(external)`, plus direct held-out `Q_P^T(external)), P12-minus-S720 boundary contrasts, and domain-specific lab/vital results. The 0.01 AUC and 0.005 net-benefit negligible margins are inherited, not tuned after fitting.

Sort viable hospital IDs by SHA-256(`"eicu-transport-v2\\0"+hospitalid`) and greedily balance S720 stays into five contiguous folds. External evaluation is held-out hospital fold. Within training hospitals, reserve the fixed 20% patient-hash internal reference using SHA-256(`"eicu-internal-v2\\0"+patientunitstayid`). No patient-only split is called external validation. All analyte/channel selection, medians, standardization, class handling, risk cells, and any weights are training-fold-only.

Use 2,000 paired hospital-cluster bootstrap resamples, identical across learners, state versions, process blocks, and nulls. Report per-hospital estimates, event counts, prevalence, effective sample size for the inherited S6 measured-selection weights, and heterogeneity. The solver must first report the adult denominator, S6/S720/P12 counts, EOL12 counts, outcome prevalence, duplicate removals, hospital viability, field coverage, and all exclusions. These are required outputs, not available results.

## State-matched nulls and selection/documentation rivals

Preserve the parent’s unrestricted same-hospital process permutation, parent X-state null, and +180-minute offset displacement as secondary controls. Add one pre-specified trajectory-state null:

1. Fit the value-only T risk score within each training partition; use out-of-fold T risk for training stays and the fold-fitted score for held-out hospitals.
2. Form cells from risk quintile plus age bin, admissionweight bin, gender, and ethnicity. Merge only cells with fewer than 10 stays with the adjacent quintile, saving every merge.
3. Within hospital and cell, cyclically reassign complete P vectors using SHA-256(`"eicu-trajectory-state-null-v1\\0"+patientunitstayid`). Keep X/T, hospital, outcome, and all population flags fixed; never use outcome or P for assignment.
4. Fit/evaluate the null with the same learner, folds, predictions, metrics, and bootstrap indices. Compare observed `Q_P^T) to the null increment and retain separate lab-intensity, lab-gap, vital-intensity, vital-gap, and joint nulls.

The new null asks whether process linkage persists after a richer observed value state is matched. It is not causal matching and does not remove unmeasured severity or within-cell hospital practice.

Rival-specific observations:

- Unmeasured or evolving severity: the process increment falls materially from `Q_P^X) to `Q_P^T), with the observed trajectory-state null showing corresponding attenuation. This supports measured temporal-state sufficiency only; it does not identify physiology or eliminate unmeasured severity.
- Terminal decline/early-discharge selection: a process increment present in S6/S720 but absent or materially smaller in P12/no-EOL12, or strongly concentrated in hospitals/strata with altered boundary composition. The experiment does not infer a death time and cannot distinguish early death from early discharge when the fields do not provide that evidence.
- Hospital recording practice: persistence in the trajectory-state null, large held-out hospital heterogeneity, a gap-dominant effect, or a positive null increment despite similar T/outcome distributions. This is compatible with workflow/feed behavior, not proof of an outage or clinician practice.

## Falsification and interpretation

Support for the specific temporal-state sufficiency hypothesis requires all of the following on the prespecified P12 external estimand, with directionally coherent internal results and learner agreement:

1. `Q_P^X(external)>0.01) AUC (or corresponding calibrated/policy signal) establishes that there was a non-negligible parent process increment to explain.
2. `A_T(external)>0.01) AUC and `Q_P^T(external)<=0.01) AUC, with paired uncertainty intervals reported; the analogous 10% net-benefit attenuation exceeds 0.005 where the parent increment is present.
3. The observed trajectory-state process increment is larger than the trajectory-state-null increment, or the null attenuates comparably, and the result is not confined to one hospital.
4. The attenuation is directionally retained in S720 and S6, while P12/no-EOL12 is not rescued by changing the window, outcome, or subgroup.

This supports “the tested value trajectory explains much of the recorded-process increment” and no stronger claim.

The temporal-state sufficiency claim is falsified for this data if P12 external `Q_P^T) remains above the 0.01 AUC margin with an interval excluding the margin, or if `A_T) is below the 0.01 attenuation margin while the parent process increment is present. That result leaves residual process information, workflow, selection, or unmeasured severity alive. It does not prove a clinical mechanism. Persistence in the null, gap dominance, or one-hospital concentration strengthens the documentation/workflow rival. A positive S6/S720 increment that disappears in P12 supports a boundary-dependent selection interpretation, not an EOL causal claim.

Adverse evidence is an interval wholly below the negligible margin for the process increment with no calibration or policy support after technical checks. Inconclusive evidence includes intervals spanning the margins, fewer than five viable hospitals or fewer than 100 P12 events, excessive trajectory imputation/coverage collapse, unstable state-cell merging, unstable IPW effective sample size, material fold/channel-selection instability, Apache-label discordance that prevents a usable audit, or failed source/join/leakage checks. An imprecise null is not refutation.

## Alternative methods and resource decision

The retained baseline/alternative pair is elastic-net additive blocks versus capacity-matched histogram GBM. Inputs, target, [0,360] fitting window, hospital-held-out split, state-null assignment, metrics, and paired bootstrap are identical. The baseline exposes direction and domain attribution; the GBM can reveal nonlinear trajectory-by-process interactions that the baseline loses. The planned future solver envelope remains 16 CPUs, up to 262,144 MiB RAM, and 28,800 seconds; this is a planned estimate, not a measured full-study runtime. The current discovery verified source/schema availability but did not fit the study or measure full extraction time. A bounded readiness probe should time selected-column extraction and one outer-fold fit before execution.

CPU is selected: this is tabular gzip extraction, fixed-bin aggregation, five hospital folds, two learners, null permutations, and cluster bootstrap. An A100 would not resolve the severity-versus-workflow ambiguity; GPU use is neither prohibited nor scientifically informative here. A raw-event neural/sequence encoder is deferred because the smallest question is whether fixed-bin measured values suffice, the available fields lack order/specimen/device/interface semantics, and a larger representation would make the attribution harder. Revisit it only if the bounded diagnostic shows that fixed bins lose clinically relevant ordering and the same P12/S720/S6 estimands, nulls, uncertainty, and held-out hospitals can be preserved. A hierarchical hospital random-effects model is also deferred: it can describe heterogeneity but can absorb the site behavior that the held-out test is meant to expose. A causal monitoring/testing or EOL intervention study is unavailable without intervention assignment, order/specimen timestamps, clinician rationale, reliable death time, and adjudication.

## Missing evidence and verifier boundary

The available fields cannot establish whether a row is an order, specimen result, bedside measurement, device aggregation, interface transmission, or clinician decision; they also lack a reliable death timestamp and treatment assignment. `carePlanEOL` is a recorded care-plan field, not an adjudicated goals-of-care decision; a missing row is not proof that no decision occurred. Apache `actualicumortality` is an audit field, not an independent gold standard for the parent ICU-discharge label. Clinical interpretation requires source-level measurement validation, order/specimen/device/interface timestamps, clinician adjudication, and prospective silent-deployment/impact evaluation. No result licenses a change in monitoring, treatment, or goals-of-care practice.

The verifier can check exact source hashes, table/column bindings, joins, offsets, cohort flags, no-use of post-window fields, training-only preprocessing, channel selection, fixed bins, trajectory imputation, process definitions, fold isolation, null assignment, predictions, metrics, bootstrap intervals, and whether conclusions cite computed output rows. It cannot automatically adjudicate physiology, clinical utility, causal mechanism, terminal decline, or whether a process feature reflects hospital workflow. Those claims require the missing evidence or another study.

The solver must newly fit and save:

- a frozen cohort and exclusion manifest with P12/S720/S6/EOL12 flags, duplicate audit, hospital viability, outcome and Apache audit;
- fold-specific X and T state features, selected-channel/bin audit, imputation and coverage audit, and parent P blocks;
- paired X/X+P and T/T+P predictions for additive and capacity-matched GBM learners;
- parent X-state and new trajectory-state null predictions, plus separate and joint process blocks and inherited timing/unrestricted controls;
- per-hospital predictions, 2,000 paired hospital-cluster bootstrap metrics, Q/A/D contrasts, 10% policy metrics, and state-cell merge/weight diagnostics;
- a conclusion report linking every supportive, adverse, or inconclusive statement to saved prediction/metric rows and uncertainty intervals.

Completion is established only when these artifacts exist, all binding and leakage checks pass, and the final interpretation follows the computed P12 primary outputs while preserving the adverse and inconclusive branches. No study result is claimed by this branch.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

The deferred raw-event sequence model would become appropriate only if a bounded, pre-registered comparison shows that three fixed value bins materially lose ordering information relevant to the process attenuation contrast, not merely if it improves AUC. A richer latent trajectory model would require the same target, folds, process null, uncertainty, and a demonstrated information loss in T. A hospital random-effects model would be revisited only as a descriptive heterogeneity analysis after held-out results establish a stable residual and after confirming it does not replace external evaluation. An intervention/causal design remains deferred until order/specimen/interface and clinician-action evidence becomes available.
