# Episode 16 evolution — treatment-stream concordance after an availability/workflow stress test

Status: design only; no cohort count, fitted coefficient, prediction, metric, interval, or clinical result is claimed. Parent: candidate-98a633392db8b7ad33171630. This branch preserves the parent’s population, [0,360] predictor window, (360,720] follow-up, strict respiratoryCare start outcome, competing exits, and hospital-held-out estimand. It narrows the interpretation of the added treatment stream after stress-testing what the archive can identify.

## Scientific opening and falsifiable claim

The parent’s respiratoryCare start can be corroborated by respiratoryCharting, but both may be documentation interfaces. The treatment table adds a third stored stream with a treatment label and ICU-relative offset. The clinically important unresolved boundary is whether a later strict respiratoryCare interval-start record is reproduced in a separately stored treatment-record stream beyond generic record availability, shared workflow, timing coincidence, and exit/EOL selection.

The strongest evidence-supported claims are bounded. Pollard et al. describe eICU as a multi-center, high-granularity archive containing care documentation and treatment information, while warning that only parts of continuously streamed bedside information are archived and that table/query definitions can be ambiguous [K1]. Rajkomar et al. show that temporally ordered EHR representations can support cross-center prediction without site-specific harmonization, but this does not validate eICU treatment semantics [K2]. Tang et al. describe reproducible preprocessing for irregular structured EHR data, including an eICU proof of concept, but do not establish that a treatment row is an order, administration, delivery, or clinical event [K3]. None of these works tests the proposed three-stream concordance.

**Hypothesis.** In the unchanged adult first-ICU S6 risk set with no valid documented active respiratoryCare vent interval at minute 360, the pre-landmark parent state/process vector will show a coherent hospital-held-out increment for the strict documented respiratoryCare interval-start outcome when, and only when, the start is temporally concordant with an outcome-blind, source-labeled respiratory row in treatment. The increment must persist in treatment-observable risk sets and availability-weighted sensitivity analyses, across prespecified ±10/±30/±60-minute windows, away from ICU exit/EOL, across hospitals, and against schedule-preserving treatment-offset nulls. If the signal predicts treatment-row opportunity or generic documentation density, is explained by shared schedule, or is concentrated at exit/backfill times, the treatment stream does not add corroboration.

This is a documentation hypothesis, not a treatment hypothesis. The estimand is a recorded cross-table transition. A positive result cannot establish that therapy was ordered, administered, delivered, effective, indicated, or causal.

## Population, time, and outcomes

Time zero is ICU admission and all offsets are ICU-relative. Apply the parent exactly:

- finite patientunitstayid, hospitalid, unitdischargeoffset, and unitdischargestatus;
- patient.unitvisitnumber = 1, patient.unitstaytype = admit, numeric age >=18, retaining source >89;
- among qualifying stays with the same uniquepid, retain the smallest finite unitadmitoffset, then smallest patientunitstayid;
- S6 eligibility is unitdischargeoffset >360; do not require survival to minute 720;
- predictors use the inclusive [0,360] window;
- follow-up is strictly (360,720], truncated at the earlier of minute 720 and recorded ICU discharge.

The risk set is the parent’s operational absence group: no valid documented active respiratoryCare vent interval at minute 360. This is not clinical absence. A valid interval has finite ventstartoffset and either finite ventendoffset > ventstartoffset or a missing end treated as open; it is active at 360 when ventstartoffset <=360 and (ventendoffset >360 or open).

Define outcomes without malformed notation:

- R_start_doc: first strict, unambiguous documented respiratoryCare interval-start boundary in (360,720], with the inherited duplicate, same-start conflict, open-interval, and ambiguity rules.
- T_resp_record_doc: a treatment row whose preserved raw treatmentstring belongs to the frozen broad respiratory class T_resp_any; this means source-recorded label only.
- C_RT_doc(t) = 1 if R_start_doc occurs at t and at least one qualifying T_resp_record_doc has treatmentoffset in [t−30,t+30], the treatment offset is integer and within [0,unitdischargeoffset], and the row is not post-discharge. A same-offset row is allowed but flagged.
- T_start_doc: first qualifying respiratory treatment-record row in (360,720] before the earlier of exit and minute 720, constructed independently of R_start_doc.
- C_RCT_doc(t) = 1 if R_start_doc at t has both the parent respiratoryCharting record in its frozen ±30-minute class/window and T_resp_record_doc in its ±30-minute window. This remains secondary and is not called treatment corroboration.
- R_exit_alive and R_exit_expired: competing causes at alive or expired ICU exit before a documented start; an exit tied with an event is the exit under the parent rule.

Primary analysis uses ±30 minutes. ±10 and ±60 are prespecified sensitivity windows, not favorable-window selection. A shifted-window control uses [t+60,t+120] with the same width as the primary window; a matched pre-event shifted control [t−120,t−60] is also reported when it lies within the stay. Neither shifted control is interpreted as a clinical endpoint.

## Treatment-file semantics and outcome-blind freeze

The inherited read-only audit reports the exact treatment header as:

treatmentid,patientunitstayid,treatmentoffset,treatmentstring,activeupondischarge

with header-byte SHA-256 2e98d283b915c2defd91de0cce9f6a8a2a041b961f3a921b62e65e2ff019359a; the full source hash is 115ce152107aeab0f89f4c50c9b4b03a127a2d80618f70584d39e4b3fca4bd6b. The parent’s source audit measured 3,688,745 rows, 2,711 distinct raw strings, no blank values in the five required columns, integer-parseable offsets, negative offsets, and both True and False values of activeupondischarge. These are source-audit facts, not eligible-cohort prevalence and not clinical validation; the branch does not claim a new full-file scan.

The solver must first save a row-level audit and distinct-string manifest before constructing any endpoint or fitting any model. It must preserve raw strings, casing, whitespace, hierarchy separators and depth, treatmentid, patientunitstayid, integer treatmentoffset, activeupondischarge, exact duplicates, duplicate IDs, identical-string/identical-offset rows, negative offsets, out-of-stay rows, and post-discharge rows. No blank is converted to “no treatment”; missing rows mean unobserved corroboration.

Freeze these classes from the full distinct vocabulary before reading outcomes, model metrics, held-out predictions, or selecting hospitals:

1. T_resp_any: normalized hierarchy beginning pulmonary|ventilation and oxygenation|, plus a separately enumerated list of exact source strings for endotracheal-tube insertion, reintubation, and removal. Report exact raw members and conflicts.
2. T_support_candidate: exact raw members containing source labels for mechanical ventilation, non-invasive ventilation, CPAP/PEEP therapy, oxygen therapy, or endotracheal-tube insertion/reintubation. Exclude suctioning, physiotherapy, weaning, and removal. This is an operational candidate class, not a claim of delivered support.
3. T_nonresp_control: an outcome-blind non-respiratory class frequency- and hierarchy-matched as far as possible, used only as a workflow/documentation negative control. Its exact rule and raw members are frozen before outcome construction.

If the broad hierarchy is unstable or cannot be frozen in at least five viable hospitals, report only generic source-record concordance using T_resp_any and mark semantic corroboration unavailable. If T_support_candidate is unstable, it is secondary/omitted rather than rescued by outcome-dependent reclassification. activeupondischarge is audit-only: it is not a start/end interval, administration flag, or delivery status.

# Episode 18 endpoint-repair child: post-procedure coherence versus planned documentation

Status: design only. No cohort counts, fitted model, prevalence, effect, or clinical conclusion is claimed.

Parent: `candidate-36072d7aadd52d981721404a`. This child preserves the parent’s population, [43,181) estimand, O0/O1/O2 hierarchy, R42/R28 weighting, temporal patient-held-out split, elastic-net baseline, compact GRU alternative, uncertainty gates, and three-work evidence. It adds one endpoint-provenance repair to address the strongest remaining interpretation threat: a later literal TACE code can be planned/scheduled documentation or a care-intensity marker rather than a clinically coherent retreatment episode.

## Scientific opening and decision relevance

The supported claim at present is narrow: in the inherited first dated exact-code TACE population, a day-42 assay trajectory may predict a later operational TACE record better than a day-42 assay snapshot after accounting for baseline severity, assay opportunity, observation and care workflow. The available evidence does not support calling that record treatment failure, radiographic progression, retreatment intent, or benefit.

The unresolved claim is whether any trajectory increment persists when a later TACE record is required to have evidence of downstream same-visit activity after the procedure, and whether the increment is absent from a pre-procedure-order-only documentation pattern. The leading explanation is that a physiologically informative trajectory predicts a subsequent coherent procedure episode. The strongest rival is a workflow/selection explanation: clinicians order, schedule, document, and monitor high-intensity care in ways that create both the assay trajectory and the literal code, without the code itself identifying a completed, intended, or response-driven TACE episode.

This matters because a positive O0 result alone could encourage a clinically misleading interpretation of the assay trajectory. If O3 agrees with O0 while the planned-care negative control does not, the next decision can justify blinded chart/intent/imaging validation of a narrower operational prediction. If O0 is positive but O3 and the negative-control contrast move together, the direction should be redirected toward workflow and endpoint acquisition rather than clinical assay interpretation.

[K1] shows that longitudinal records can encode useful temporal structure while also inheriting data-collection bias. [K2] motivates explicit hazard and selection handling for longitudinal EHR occurrence processes. [K3]’s inspected supplement makes missingness, data quality, and testing-related shortcuts an explicit concern in routine clinical prediction. None of these works validates a local HCC TACE code or supplies unavailable intent/response evidence; this child adds a direct provenance check to the parent’s assay-content question.

## Fixed population, estimand, and inherited methods

Status: complete design proposal; no cohort count, fitted coefficient, prediction, metric, confidence interval, or clinical result is claimed. Parent anchor: candidate-df29ed71e2af57a3f4af639b. This child preserves the parent’s adult first-ICU S6 population, [0,360] predictors, strict (360,720] recorded respiratory-care endpoint, competing exits, hospital-held-out folds, parent state/process/availability/EOL/timing nulls, and unchanged mortality/vital modules. It repairs the treatment endpoint notation and adds an outcome-blind treatment vocabulary, an independently defined treatment-record onset, a frequency/hierarchy-matched non-respiratory workflow control, and explicit treatment-record limits.

## Scientific opening, evidence boundary, and hypothesis

The parent’s cross-stream respiratoryCare design asks whether early recorded-vital state/process information converges with a separately stored respiratory-care transition. A remaining clinically consequential boundary is whether a treatment.csv.gz row adds any respiratory-specific timing concordance beyond the opportunity to write any treatment row, shared scheduling, documentation density, and discharge/end-of-life workflow. This matters because a positive cross-table signal could otherwise be mistaken for evidence that a treatment stream independently corroborates care-state onset. Conversely, a negative result would identify that the treatment table contributes no information beyond workflow, without invalidating the parent’s narrower recorded-vital association.

The three inspected works support only bounded premises:

- [K1] Pollard et al. describe eICU as a multi-center linked ICU archive with treatment information, but emphasize that continuously streamed bedside data are only partly archived and that archive fields are not automatically bedside truth. This supports a measurement/availability stress test, not treatment semantics.
- [K2] Rajkomar et al. show that temporally structured EHR representations can support multi-center prediction and discuss semantic interoperability limits. This supports retaining a transparent temporal baseline alongside a learned alternative, not interpreting model performance as mechanism.
- [K3] Tang et al. show that structured EHR preprocessing can be made reproducible and demonstrate an eICU proof of concept. This supports frozen, fold-isolated preprocessing, not the claim that a treatment row is an order, administration, delivery, or independently timed clinical action.

The strongest claim supported by the parent and these works is therefore: linked eICU tables can support a reproducible, hospital-transportable analysis of recorded events, while data capture and field semantics may create availability and workflow artifacts. Neither the parent nor the inspected literature establishes that treatmentstring identifies a delivered therapy, that treatmentoffset is the time of care rather than a record/schedule time, or that respiratoryCare starts are physiologic deterioration.

### Falsifiable hypothesis

Among the unchanged adult first-ICU S6 risk set without an auditable active respiratoryCare interval at minute 360, the parent’s pre-landmark state/process vector has a treatment-concordant increment for the strict documented respiratoryCare interval-start endpoint beyond the increment for generic treatment-record opportunity and a frequency/hierarchy-matched non-respiratory workflow record. Specifically, the held-out-hospital association for the independently defined composite C_RT_doc (a strict respiratoryCare start with a qualifying respiratory treatment row in a prespecified time window) will be directionally coherent with, and not materially weaker than, the association for R_start_doc, after the parent’s fixed state/process adjustment, treatment/chart availability audits, timing and exit safeguards, and schedule-preserving null.

The competing explanation is generic documentation or scheduling: the same early state/process vector predicts that a stay will generate rows, that rows are generated near routine schedules or discharge, or that the respiratory and treatment tables share an interface. Under that explanation, the process increment will be similar for T_any_record, the matched non-respiratory control, and C_RT_doc, or will disappear after availability weighting, shifted-window controls, or schedule-preserving treatment-offset permutation.

This is a descriptive recorded-documentation hypothesis. It does not test treatment effectiveness, treatment indication, a causal effect, physiologic respiratory failure, or whether a therapy was delivered.

### Why this could change clinical understanding

If treatment-specific concordance survives the negative control, schedule null, hospital holdout, and availability stress tests, the next justified step is blinded clinical adjudication of a sample of respiratoryCare/treatment pairs and validation against orders, administration/device, or ventilator data. If it fails those tests, the important finding is that apparent corroboration is a workflow/recording phenomenon; future work should improve measurement rather than build a respiratory deterioration alert from this pattern. Either result separates a cross-table operational regularity from a clinically overinterpreted treatment claim.

## Population, time, estimands, and endpoint notation

Time zero is ICU admission and every offset below is ICU-relative minutes.

Apply the parent’s exact adult first-ICU selection:

1. From patient, require finite patientunitstayid, hospitalid, unitdischargeoffset, and unitdischargestatus; unitvisitnumber = 1; unitstaytype = admit; numeric age >=18 while retaining source value >89.
2. For qualifying stays sharing uniquepid, keep the smallest finite unitadmitoffset, then the smallest patientunitstayid. uniquepid is used only for this within-patient deduplication and is never joined to longitudinal tables.
3. Define S6 as unitdischargeoffset > 360. Do not require survival to minute 720.
4. Build every predictor from the inclusive [0,360] window. A predictor at exactly 360 is allowed; no future row, endpoint, treatment, chart, exit, or EOL value may enter it.
5. Follow each S6 stay strictly in (360,720], truncated at the earlier of minute 720 and recorded unitdischargeoffset. Rows after recorded ICU exit are excluded.

The treatment repair uses the parent’s operational risk set: no valid documented active respiratoryCare vent interval at minute 360. This means no auditable interval in the source record, not clinical absence of respiratory support.

### Primary respiratory-care endpoint

R_start_doc is the first strict documented respiratoryCare interval-start boundary in (360,720] and before recorded ICU exit for which:

- ventstartoffset is finite;
- the interval is valid if ventendoffset is finite and strictly greater than ventstartoffset, or is open if the end is missing;
- no valid interval from the same stay covers the immediately preceding minute;
- duplicate rows at the same start are one event, with all source row identifiers retained;
- contradictory, malformed, same-offset, or ambiguous source rows are retained in audit and do not get silently repaired into a start.

An event at exactly 360 is excluded. A missing end is not a verified stop. A valid ventendoffset is not combined with initiation in the primary endpoint.

The secondary R_stop_doc is the first valid end in (360,720] whose interval was active immediately before the end. It is reported separately as a documentation of a stop/weaning boundary and is not treated as a respiratory initiation.

### Independently defined treatment-record onset

Before constructing any respiratory outcome, save a complete outcome-blind treatment-string manifest and freeze raw-string classes (definition below). Then define:

- T_any_record: first row in treatment.csv.gz in (360,720] and before the earlier of recorded ICU exit and minute 720, regardless of respiratory class.
- T_start_doc: first row in that interval whose preserved raw treatmentstring belongs to the frozen broad respiratory class T_resp_any. This is defined without reading R_start_doc, respiratory outcome counts, held-out predictions, or concordance.
- T_support_candidate: secondary, narrower class for exact source labels compatible with mechanical ventilation, non-invasive ventilation, CPAP/PEEP, oxygen therapy, or endotracheal-tube insertion/reintubation. It is an operational candidate label, not delivered support.
- C_RT_doc(w): for each R_start_doc at time t, an indicator that at least one qualifying T_resp_any row has integer treatmentoffset in [t-w,t+w], within [0, unitdischargeoffset], not post-discharge, with duplicate and same-offset flags retained. The primary width is w=30 minutes; w=10 and w=60 are prespecified sensitivities.
- C_RCT_doc(w): secondary triple concordance requiring both C_RT_doc(w) and the parent’s frozen respiratoryCharting marker in its fixed chart window. It is not called treatment corroboration.
- T_nonresp_control: a non-respiratory treatment-record outcome whose raw members are frequency- and hierarchy-matched to T_resp_any as far as the full pre-outcome vocabulary permits. It is frozen before outcome construction and used only as a workflow/documentation negative control.

The primary comparison is the paired held-out-hospital process increment for R_start_doc versus C_RT_doc(30), with T_start_doc, T_any_record, C_RCT_doc(30), and T_nonresp_control as secondary or falsification outcomes. The estimand is a recorded cross-table event association, not the probability of treatment delivery.

Before a documented start, ICU exit is a competing cause:

- R_exit_alive when recorded unitdischargestatus == Alive;
- R_exit_expired when recorded unitdischargestatus == Expired.

An expired discharge is not converted into a death timestamp. A tie between an exit and a documented event follows the parent’s exit rule: the exit is the competing event. A stay present at minute 720 without an observed event is administratively event-free only for this recorded-observation estimand.

The parent’s unchanged P12/S720/S6 ICU-discharge mortality module and both parent recorded-vital endpoints are rerun as inherited modules; adding treatment does not replace or redefine those estimands.

At minute 360, classify starting respiratory documentation using only [0,360] rows:

- S_none_support_observed: a respiratoryCare or respiratoryCharting row exists in [0,360], no valid invasive interval covers 360, and no unresolved contradictory source state prevents the limited “no auditable invasive interval” description.

- raw-string counts, distinct offsets, duplicate/conflict flags, negative/out-of-stay and post-discharge counts;

## Analysis, baselines, and substantive alternative

### Fixed split and inherited modules

Use the parent’s five contiguous hospital-held-out folds. Viable hospital IDs are sorted by SHA-256("eicu-transport-v2\0"+hospitalid) and greedily balanced by S720 stays; require at least 100 S720 stays per hospital and at least five viable hospitals. Each external evaluation holds out one hospital fold. The fixed 20% patient-hash internal reference uses SHA-256("eicu-internal-v2\0"+patientunitstayid) and is not external validation.

All preprocessing, imputation, standardization, class rules, candidate vocabulary, trajectory thresholds, observation weights, and model selection are training-fold-only or fixed before outcomes. Preserve and rerun the parent’s exact state/process/availability/EOL/timing nulls, P12/S720/S6 mortality module, and both recorded-vital modules without changing their endpoints or predictor window. Treatment rows are outcomes/audit inputs only.

### Simple baseline

Fit pooled discrete-time cause-specific logistic hazards over (360,480], (480,600], and (600,720], with alive and expired ICU exits as competing causes. The transparent baseline is elastic-net regularized and receives exactly the parent’s X/T/P state, process, and availability representation. Fit the same locked baseline for R_start_doc; C_RT_doc(30); secondary T_start_doc, T_any_record, T_nonresp_control, and C_RCT_doc(30); and inherited mortality and recorded-vital outcomes unchanged.

The primary scientific contrast is the held-out-hospital process increment for C versus R, not raw predictive superiority. Report paired differences in AUROC/PR-AUC where estimable, cause-specific Brier score, calibration slope/intercept and reliability, and fixed clinical net-benefit analysis only if the parent’s threshold is estimable. Retain the inherited negligible incremental margin of 0.01 AUC where AUC is defined, but do not treat it as a clinical-utility threshold. Use paired hospital-cluster bootstrap with 2,000 replicates and fold variation; save uncertainty and positivity rather than only point estimates.

### Scientifically substantive learned alternative

Fit capacity-matched histogram gradient boosting with the same X/T/P inputs, targets, competing-exit encoding, hospital folds, fold-isolated preprocessing, observation-weight sensitivity, and uncertainty procedure. Lock the feature set and hyperparameter budget from training folds. This alternative can reveal nonlinear state-by-process, state-by-availability, and starting-stratum interactions that the additive elastic-net baseline can lose—for example, whether treatment concordance appears only in a narrow documented-support state or only when recording opportunity is high. Such an interaction would change the workflow-versus-independent-concordance interpretation even if average discrimination changes little.

The comparison is scientific only if the alternative changes the substantive pattern across R, C, T-any, and the non-respiratory control. A boosting-only small predictive gain without a stable C-versus-R or negative-control distinction is not evidence for independent treatment concordance. A model disagreement is reported as model-sensitive/inconclusive rather than selected for confirmation. Neural raw-sequence modeling is deferred because the present question requires auditable class and timing nulls, and adding unstructured sequence representation would make it harder—not impossible—to attribute a difference to treatment concordance. A causal treatment-effect model is deferred because the source lacks order/administration/device exposure, indication, and treatment assignment evidence; it would answer a different question. Revisit either if treatment provenance and a clinical indication/administration crosswalk become available.

### Resource plan

The future solver planning envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB RAM, up to 8 GPUs, and 28,800 seconds. This is a planning limit, not a measured runtime or a result. The study is gzip extraction, interval/string auditing, tabular fitting, hospital folds, null permutations, and 2,000 cluster bootstraps; CPU is provisionally adequate and no GPU is required or scientifically rewarded. The estimate is unverified because no full fit is run in discovery. If a bounded readiness timing identifies matrix fitting as the bottleneck, an allocated GPU may be requested explicitly and code must use only the allocated cuda:0; ordinary shell CUDA visibility is not evidence of hardware absence. No proposer/solver training is authorized. Discovery here claims no completed fitting.

## Actual scientific deliverable

Completion means newly estimated, not merely packaged, outputs:

1. Source/hash/header audit for every bound table, with ordinary gzip/member status and fail-closed checks.
2. Frozen adult first-ICU S6 manifest; parent P12/S720/S6 manifests; deduplication, exit, Apache, EOL, no-post-360, and hospital-fold audits.
3. Complete treatment raw-string vocabulary, class map, frequency/hierarchy matching, anomaly/opportunity manifest, and audit-only activeupondischarge report.
4. RespiratoryCare interval audit, R_start_doc, R_stop_doc, starting strata, respiratoryCharting vocabulary/entry-time audit, and R observation flags.
5. Independently computed T_any_record, T_start_doc, T_nonresp_control, C_RT_doc at ±10/±30/±60, C_RCT_doc, exact pair lags, shifted controls, schedule-null outputs, exit/EOL strata, and availability weights/positivity/ESS.
6. Fold-isolated elastic-net and capacity-matched boosting predictions and estimates for R, C, and controls, plus unchanged parent mortality/vital outputs.
7. Paired 2,000-hospital-cluster bootstrap intervals, calibration/Brier/AUROC/PR-AUC/net-benefit outputs where estimable, per-hospital and per-stratum results, and a conclusion table whose every claim points to exact output rows.

The key scientific output is whether a treatment-record-specific process increment remains after the availability, negative-control, timing, schedule, hospital, duplicate, and exit/EOL tests. Readiness, schema validation, or a positive association alone does not complete the objective.

## Prespecified interpretation and falsification criteria

### Supportive pattern

Call the recorded-concordance hypothesis supportive only if all gates are satisfied:

- source/header/hash checks pass; raw treatment classes are frozen before outcomes; at least five viable hospitals remain with positive R and treatment-concordance opportunity;
- treatment and respiratory event semantics are computationally auditable, with adequate positivity and ESS;
- C_RT_doc(30) and R_start_doc show directionally coherent held-out-hospital process increments in both elastic-net and boosting, with uncertainty excluding the inherited negligible margin where the metric is estimable;
- C-versus-R distinction persists after availability weighting, ±10/±60 sensitivity, shifted timing controls, schedule-preserving permutation, duplicate/conflict audit, discharge-adjacency restriction, and non-exit-adjacent analysis;
- T_nonresp_control and T_any_record do not show the same process increment, and the result is not dominated by one hospital, one baseline stratum, one raw-string vocabulary, or one documentation-time convention;
- conclusion is limited to independently concordant recorded respiratory documentation and does not call it delivered therapy.

Support would justify a next study with blinded respiratory/critical-care adjudication and order/administration/device linkage. It would not justify a treatment recommendation, alert deployment, physiologic deterioration claim, or causal claim.

### Adverse pattern

Treat these as evidence against treatment-specific corroboration, while preserving any narrower recorded association:

- the increment predicts T_any_record or generic availability but not C;
- C disappears after observation weighting, schedule permutation, shifted controls, exit/EOL safeguards, or hospital holdout;
- T_nonresp_control has the same magnitude and timing pattern;
- concordance is unstable across ±10/±30/±60, broad/candidate vocabulary, duplicate handling, or clinical-entry versus documentation-entry time;
- the association is discharge-adjacent, EOL-associated, one-hospital, one-stratum, or appears only in boosting;
- the parent’s R association persists but treatment adds no independent evidence.

This supports revising toward archive/interface and observation-process validation, not concluding that treatment was absent or ineffective.

### Inconclusive or deferral pattern

Do not call a null a refutation when it is imprecise. Defer if fewer than five viable hospitals remain; strict starts or C opportunities are too rare; positivity or ESS is inadequate; treatment vocabulary is unstable; offset meaning is unresolved; documentation lag dominates; intervals span both meaningful and negligible effects; or independent treatment provenance is unavailable. Retain the parent’s bounded recorded-vital result if this treatment module fails.

## Verifier-checkable claims and clinical limits

A verifier can check exact source paths and hashes; the treatment header and required fields; read-only joins; ordinary gzip/member status; first-ICU deduplication; [0,360] and (360,720] boundaries; strict interval-start logic; competing exits; raw-string preservation and outcome-blind freeze; independent T onset; concordance windows; negative-control matching; schedule and shifted nulls; no future leakage; fold isolation; predictions, metrics, uncertainty, positivity, ESS; and whether conclusions point to computed output rows.

A verifier cannot establish that a treatment row is an order, administration, delivered therapy, ventilator action, or clinical indication; that treatmentoffset is care time rather than documentation or schedule time; that respiratoryCare intervals are complete or represent actual bedside support; that the sources are institutionally independent; that a recorded transition is physiologic respiratory failure, clinically necessary, beneficial, or causal; or that a treatment or alert should change practice.

Those claims require order/administration/device or ventilator data, reliable indication and event timestamps, interface provenance, expert adjudication of a blinded sample, and external or prospective validation. No private clinical notes, unavailable supplementary methods, fitted result, or clinical conclusion is claimed here.

## Alternatives not selected and revisit conditions

The selected design is the smallest check that can distinguish treatment-specific recorded concordance from generic workflow while preserving the parent estimand. The alternatives are explicit:

- Additive elastic-net is retained as the interpretability and transport baseline.
- Capacity-matched histogram boosting is retained because nonlinear state/process/availability interactions are scientifically relevant, not because a small score gain is valuable.
- A neural raw-sequence model is deferred until raw sequence, vocabulary, and compute/interpretation dependencies can be justified; revisit if tabular models show a stable heterogeneous pattern that sequence order could discriminate.
- A causal treatment model is deferred until treatment assignment, indication, order/administration/device exposure, and clinically meaningful confounders are available; prediction from recorded rows cannot supply them.
- If no valid treatment class survives the outcome-blind vocabulary audit, abandon semantic corroboration and retain only the predeclared generic-record negative-control analysis, or stop the treatment branch.

Evidence to continue is a stable cross-hospital, treatment-specific, schedule-robust recorded signal. Evidence to revise is a generic availability or workflow signal. Evidence to defer is inadequate event support or unresolved source semantics.

## Three inspected key works

Exactly three distinct inspected works are attached in this branch and mapped in key-references.json:

1. **[K1]** Pollard TJ, Johnson AEW, Raffa JD, Celi LA, Mark RG, Badawi O. “The eICU Collaborative Research Database, a freely available multi-center database for critical care research.” Scientific Data. 2018;5:180178. DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2018.178. Full-text Nature HTML relevant sections inspected. Supports multi-center linked-table scope and the archived-versus-continuously-streamed data limitation; does not validate treatment semantics or delivered therapy.
2. **[K2]** Rajkomar A, Oren E, Chen K, et al. “Scalable and accurate deep learning with electronic health records.” npj Digital Medicine. 2018;1:18. DOI: 10.1038/s41746-018-0029-1. Full-text Nature HTML relevant sections inspected. Supports temporally structured multi-center prediction and semantic-interoperability caution; does not establish eICU treatment meaning or this concordance.
3. **[K3]** Tang S, Davarmanesh P, Song Y, Koutra D, Sjoding MW, Wiens J. “Democratizing EHR analyses with FIDDLE: a flexible data-driven preprocessing pipeline for structured clinical data.” Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association. 2020;27(12):1921–1934. DOI: 10.1093/jamia/ocaa139; PMCID: PMC7727385. Europe PMC full-text XML inspected. Supports reproducible structured-EHR preprocessing and an eICU proof of concept; does not establish treatment-row clinical meaning.

The attached files are accurately labeled excerpts, not claims that an original PDF or supplementary appendix was inspected. Receipt hashes in key-references.json are hashes of the attached UTF-8 bytes, not URLs.

Status: complete design proposal; no cohort count, fitted coefficient, prediction, metric, confidence interval, or clinical result is claimed. Parent anchor: candidate-df29ed71e2af57a3f4af639b. ## Scientific opening, evidence boundary, and hypothesis

The parent’s cross-stream respiratoryCare design asks whether early recorded-vital state/process information converges with a separately stored respiratory-care transition. A remaining clinically consequential boundary is whether a treatment.csv.gz row adds any respiratory-specific timing concordance beyond the opportunity to write any treatment row, shared scheduling, documentation density, and discharge/end-of-life workflow. This matters because a positive cross-table signal could otherwise be mistaken for evidence that a treatment stream independently corroborates care-state onset. Conversely, a negative result would identify that the treatment table contributes no information beyond workflow, without invalidating the parent’s narrower recorded-vital association.

The three inspected works support only bounded premises:

- [K1] Pollard et al. describe eICU as a multi-center linked ICU archive with treatment information, but emphasize that continuously streamed bedside data are only partly archived and that archive fields are not automatically bedside truth. This supports a measurement/availability stress test, not treatment semantics.
- [K2] Rajkomar et al. show that temporally structured EHR representations can support multi-center prediction and discuss semantic interoperability limits. This supports retaining a transparent temporal baseline alongside a learned alternative, not interpreting model performance as mechanism.
- [K3] Tang et al. show that structured EHR preprocessing can be made reproducible and demonstrate an eICU proof of concept. This supports frozen, fold-isolated preprocessing, not the claim that a treatment row is an order, administration, delivery, or independently timed clinical action.

The strongest claim supported by the parent and these works is therefore: linked eICU tables can support a reproducible, hospital-transportable analysis of recorded events, while data capture and field semantics may create availability and workflow artifacts. Neither the parent nor the inspected literature establishes that treatmentstring identifies a delivered therapy, that treatmentoffset is the time of care rather than a record/schedule time, or that respiratoryCare starts are physiologic deterioration.

### Falsifiable hypothesis

Among the unchanged adult first-ICU S6 risk set without an auditable active respiratoryCare interval at minute 360, the parent’s pre-landmark state/process vector has a treatment-concordant increment for the strict documented respiratoryCare interval-start endpoint beyond the increment for generic treatment-record opportunity and a frequency/hierarchy-matched non-respiratory workflow record. Specifically, the held-out-hospital association for the independently defined composite C_RT_doc (a strict respiratoryCare start with a qualifying respiratory treatment row in a prespecified time window) will be directionally coherent with, and not materially weaker than, the association for R_start_doc, after the parent’s fixed state/process adjustment, treatment/chart availability audits, timing and exit safeguards, and schedule-preserving null.

The competing explanation is generic documentation or scheduling: the same early state/process vector predicts that a stay will generate rows, that rows are generated near routine schedules or discharge, or that the respiratory and treatment tables share an interface. Under that explanation, the process increment will be similar for T_any_record, the matched non-respiratory control, and C_RT_doc, or will disappear after availability weighting, shifted-window controls, or schedule-preserving treatment-offset permutation.

This is a descriptive recorded-documentation hypothesis. It does not test treatment effectiveness, treatment indication, a causal effect, physiologic respiratory failure, or whether a therapy was delivered.

### Why this could change clinical understanding

If treatment-specific concordance survives the negative control, schedule null, hospital holdout, and availability stress tests, the next justified step is blinded clinical adjudication of a sample of respiratoryCare/treatment pairs and validation against orders, administration/device, or ventilator data. If it fails those tests, the important finding is that apparent corroboration is a workflow/recording phenomenon; future work should improve measurement rather than build a respiratory deterioration alert from this pattern. Either result separates a cross-table operational regularity from a clinically overinterpreted treatment claim.

## Population, time, estimands, and endpoint notation

Time zero is ICU admission and every offset below is ICU-relative minutes.

Apply the parent’s exact adult first-ICU selection:

1. From patient, require finite patientunitstayid, hospitalid, unitdischargeoffset, and unitdischargestatus; unitvisitnumber = 1; unitstaytype = admit; numeric age >=18 while retaining source value >89.
2. For qualifying stays sharing uniquepid, keep the smallest finite unitadmitoffset, then the smallest patientunitstayid. uniquepid is used only for this within-patient deduplication and is never joined to longitudinal tables.
3. Define S6 as unitdischargeoffset > 360. Do not require survival to minute 720.
4. Build every predictor from the inclusive [0,360] window. A predictor at exactly 360 is allowed; no future row, endpoint, treatment, chart, exit, or EOL value may enter it.
5. Follow each S6 stay strictly in (360,720], truncated at the earlier of minute 720 and recorded unitdischargeoffset. Rows after recorded ICU exit are excluded.

The treatment repair uses the parent’s operational risk set: no valid documented active respiratoryCare vent interval at minute 360. This means no auditable interval in the source record, not clinical absence of respiratory support.

### Primary respiratory-care endpoint

R_start_doc is the first strict documented respiratoryCare interval-start boundary in (360,720] and before recorded ICU exit for which:

- ventstartoffset is finite;
- the interval is valid if ventendoffset is finite and strictly greater than ventstartoffset, or is open if the end is missing;
- no valid interval from the same stay covers the immediately preceding minute;
- duplicate rows at the same start are one event, with all source row identifiers retained;
- contradictory, malformed, same-offset, or ambiguous source rows are retained in audit and do not get silently repaired into a start.

An event at exactly 360 is excluded. A missing end is not a verified stop. A valid ventendoffset is not combined with initiation in the primary endpoint.

The secondary R_stop_doc is the first valid end in (360,720] whose interval was active immediately before the end. It is reported separately as a documentation of a stop/weaning boundary and is not treated as a respiratory initiation.

### Independently defined treatment-record onset

Before constructing any respiratory outcome, save a complete outcome-blind treatment-string manifest and freeze raw-string classes (definition below). Then define:

- T_any_record: first row in treatment.csv.gz in (360,720] and before the earlier of recorded ICU exit and minute 720, regardless of respiratory class.
- T_start_doc: first row in that interval whose preserved raw treatmentstring belongs to the frozen broad respiratory class T_resp_any. This is defined without reading R_start_doc, respiratory outcome counts, held-out predictions, or concordance.
- T_support_candidate: secondary, narrower class for exact source labels compatible with mechanical ventilation, non-invasive ventilation, CPAP/PEEP, oxygen therapy, or endotracheal-tube insertion/reintubation. It is an operational candidate label, not delivered support.
- C_RT_doc(w): for each R_start_doc at time t, an indicator that at least one qualifying T_resp_any row has integer treatmentoffset in [t-w,t+w], within [0, unitdischargeoffset], not post-discharge, with duplicate and same-offset flags retained. The primary width is w=30 minutes; w=10 and w=60 are prespecified sensitivities.
- C_RCT_doc(w): secondary triple concordance requiring both C_RT_doc(w) and the parent’s frozen respiratoryCharting marker in its fixed chart window. It is not called treatment corroboration.
- T_nonresp_control: a non-respiratory treatment-record outcome whose raw members are frequency- and hierarchy-matched to T_resp_any as far as the full pre-outcome vocabulary permits. It is frozen before outcome construction and used only as a workflow/documentation negative control.

The primary comparison is the paired held-out-hospital process increment for R_start_doc versus C_RT_doc(30), with T_start_doc, T_any_record, C_RCT_doc(30), and T_nonresp_control as secondary or falsification outcomes. The estimand is a recorded cross-table event association, not the probability of treatment delivery.

### Competing exits

Before a documented start, ICU exit is a competing cause:

- R_exit_alive when recorded unitdischargestatus == Alive;
- R_exit_expired when recorded unitdischargestatus == Expired.

An expired discharge is not converted into a death timestamp. A tie between an exit and a documented event follows the parent’s exit rule: the exit is the competing event. A stay present at minute 720 without an observed event is administratively event-free only for this recorded-observation estimand.

The parent’s unchanged P12/S720/S6 ICU-discharge mortality module and both parent recorded-vital endpoints are rerun as inherited modules; adding treatment does not replace or redefine those estimands.

### Fixed split and inherited modules

Use the parent’s five contiguous hospital-held-out folds. Viable hospital IDs are sorted by SHA-256("eicu-transport-v2\0"+hospitalid) and greedily balanced by S720 stays; require at least 100 S720 stays per hospital and at least five viable hospitals. Each external evaluation holds out one hospital fold. The fixed 20% patient-hash internal reference uses SHA-256("eicu-internal-v2\0"+patientunitstayid) and is not external validation.

All preprocessing, imputation, standardization, class rules, candidate vocabulary, trajectory thresholds, observation weights, and model selection are training-fold-only or fixed before outcomes. Preserve and rerun the parent’s exact state/process/availability/EOL/timing nulls, P12/S720/S6 mortality module, and both recorded-vital modules without changing their endpoints or predictor window. Treatment rows are outcomes/audit inputs only.

### Simple baseline

Fit pooled discrete-time cause-specific logistic hazards over (360,480], (480,600], and (600,720], with alive and expired ICU exits as competing causes. The transparent baseline is elastic-net regularized and receives exactly the parent’s X/T/P state, process, and availability representation. Fit the same locked baseline for R_start_doc; C_RT_doc(30); secondary T_start_doc, T_any_record, T_nonresp_control, and C_RCT_doc(30); and inherited mortality and recorded-vital outcomes unchanged.

The primary scientific contrast is the held-out-hospital process increment for C versus R, not raw predictive superiority. Report paired differences in AUROC/PR-AUC where estimable, cause-specific Brier score, calibration slope/intercept and reliability, and fixed clinical net-benefit analysis only if the parent’s threshold is estimable. Retain the inherited negligible incremental margin of 0.01 AUC where AUC is defined, but do not treat it as a clinical-utility threshold. Use paired hospital-cluster bootstrap with 2,000 replicates and fold variation; save uncertainty and positivity rather than only point estimates.

### Scientifically substantive learned alternative

### Supportive pattern

Call the recorded-concordance hypothesis supportive only if all gates are satisfied:

- source/header/hash checks pass; raw treatment classes are frozen before outcomes; at least five viable hospitals remain with positive R and treatment-concordance opportunity;
- treatment and respiratory event semantics are computationally auditable, with adequate positivity and ESS;
- C_RT_doc(30) and R_start_doc show directionally coherent held-out-hospital process increments in both elastic-net and boosting, with uncertainty excluding the inherited negligible margin where the metric is estimable;

- T_nonresp_control and T_any_record do not show the same process increment, and the result is not dominated by one hospital, one baseline stratum, one raw-string vocabulary, or one documentation-time convention;
- conclusion is limited to independently concordant recorded respiratory documentation and does not call it delivered therapy.

# UKB muscle quantity versus quality/function: critical alternative

Status: planned Harbor experiment; no fitted result or clinical conclusion is claimed.

## Question, evidence, and hypothesis

The strongest inspected evidence supports narrower claims. EWGSOP2 makes low strength central, uses low quantity/quality to confirm sarcopenia, and treats poor physical performance as severe disease [K1]. In UKB MRI, adverse thigh composition and especially high muscle-fat infiltration (MFI) were associated with later mortality after adjustment including low grip [K2]. A recent UKB MRI study reports cross-sectional associations of a posterior/anterior thigh-muscle ratio with weak grip and falls beyond total muscle mass [K3]. None establishes that the available MFI and grip fields predict a strictly later mobility change in the same MRI-anchored people, or that such a signal is biological rather than pain/arthritis/neurologic weakness, body-size/MRI measurement confounding, or selective repeat assessment.

Hypothesis:

> Among UKB adults aged at least 50 with complete bilateral thigh MRI quantity, posterior-thigh MFI, and contemporaneous grip at assessment instance 2, after matching on the same quantity and observed body-size/current-function covariates, higher MFI and lower grip increase the calibrated absolute risk of a later worsening in usual walking pace and of a later falls outcome. A muscle-quality/function interpretation is supported only if the increment persists in diagnosis-restricted and repeat-attendance sensitivity analyses, with the same direction at a 730-day lag.

The leading explanation is that quantity and quality/function encode different lower-limb reserve. The strongest rival is an indication/measurement explanation: painful hand or joint disease and neurological disease lower grip, MRI values are confounded by body size and unavailable sex, and return for a later assessment is selected. Persistence is compatible with prognostic information, not proof of mechanism, causality, treatment effect, or clinical utility.

This advances [K2] from mortality to later mobility, and [K3] from cross-sectional distribution associations to a date-ordered test using different available quality/function fields. It is an adaptation, not a reproduction.

Later pace code counts were 1/2/3 = 173/2,190/2,171; later falls counts were 1/2/3 = 3,795/540/199. These are availability observations only. The solver must resolve Data-Coding 100313 and 100539 before naming pace ordering or a no-fall category; failure makes that endpoint inconclusive rather than permitting a new definition.

For each endpoint, the primary population is the unique anchor with age >=50, valid T0, complete Q/MFI/grip, valid baseline outcome, first strictly later valid endpoint, and T1-T0 >=365 days. The >=730-day population is locked sensitivity. T1 is date-based, never instance-number based.

## Exposures and estimands

Fit transformations in development only.

- Q is the sum of the four bilateral anterior/posterior thigh fat-free volumes; preserve all four components.
- MFI is the bilateral mean of `23355-2.0` and `23356-2.0`.
- Grip is the maximum valid left/right grip; bilateral-complete is primary, side-specific/discordant analyses are sensitivity.
- Baseline pace/falls are baseline state, not dated incident events.

After coding resolution, primary pace outcome is later category lower than baseline, reporting worsening/unchanged/improvement. Primary falls outcome is later value above the verified no-fall category, with full ordinal counts secondary. Falls asks about the last year and is not a dated fall event.

The main estimand is population-standardized absolute risk difference under quantity matching: MFI +1 development SD and grip -1 SD versus both at development means, holding Q and observed baseline covariates at each person's value. Also report nested Q-only -> Q+MFI, Q-only -> Q+grip, and Q-only -> Q+MFI+grip risk contrasts, component risks, and 95% intervals. A 1 percentage-point lower-bound marker is a scale descriptor, not a treatment threshold. This is prognostic/descriptive, not causal.

## Baseline, learned alternative, split, and uncertainty

Primary transparent models are endpoint-specific ordinal/multinomial regression for pace transitions and logistic regression for falls, with ordinal/logistic sensitivities. Models include Q, age, BMI, weight, height, smoking, baseline outcome, and a prespecified missingness rule; no post-T0 variable is allowed. Diagnosis families define pre-T0 restriction and code-adjusted sensitivity, not casual mediator adjustment. Post-T0 codes are descriptive only.

Use a patient-level temporal split: earliest 70% of T0 for development/tuning and latest 30% as locked holdout. Each `eid` is in one split. Standardization, imputation, coding thresholds, and tuning are development-only. Report holdout calibration intercept/slope, plots, Brier score, log loss, secondary rank metrics, standardized risks, and 500 participant-bootstrap intervals (or a documented substitute). Require at least 100 holdout events, class support, finite estimates, stable calibration and positivity; otherwise endpoint is inconclusive with no split/outcome changes.

Matched learned alternative: CPU gradient-boosted trees for each endpoint using exactly the same participants, inputs, missingness policy, T0/T1 rule, split and outcomes. It can reveal Q-by-MFI, Q-by-grip, thresholds, and side/compartment interactions that additive regression loses. It is substantive only if a held-out quantity-matched risk contrast or rival interpretation changes; a small rank-metric gain is not enough. Report uncertainty-bearing accumulated-local-effect or partial-dependence summaries descriptively, never as mechanism.

The transparent model is primary because it exposes the estimand and is auditable with roughly 4,500 endpoint pairs. The learned model is retained to test nonlinear scientific structure. A deep image model is deferred because no image payload exists; a trajectory model is deferred because only one verified later assessment exists; causal mediation is rejected because pain severity, neurologic examination, actual fall timing and treatment are unavailable.

Planning estimate: 8 CPU cores, 32–64 GiB RAM, 2–4 hours for selected-column parsing, exact joins, two baselines/boosted fits and bootstrap. Unmeasured planning estimate; GPU is not needed for this tabular question.

## Rival falsification

Pain/arthritis/neurologic rival: repeat the primary analysis in participants without prespecified pre-T0 inpatient code families, report each diagnosis stratum and same-index code-adjusted model. A grip signal that disappears while MFI remains stable supports the rival; a persistent result is only compatible with a quality signal because outpatient pain and examination remain missing.

MRI/body-size/sex rival: adjust using the available age/BMI/weight/height fields; compare bilateral and side/compartment estimates, and report body-size sensitivity. Sex cannot be adjusted or stratified from this verified table; a result is explicitly limited by that missing evidence. Strong attenuation or side-specific instability is adverse for the biological interpretation.

Repeat-selection/reverse-timing rival: compare unweighted results with baseline-only inverse-probability weighting for having a valid later assessment, report weights/positivity, and repeat at >=730 days and by early/late T1. Do not condition on post-T0 variables. A large weighting shift or short-lag-only signal is adverse; an imprecise weighted result is inconclusive.

Supportive evidence requires at least one endpoint passing support/positivity/calibration gates, a positive held-out Q+MFI or Q+grip increment beyond Q-only with 95% interval above zero and lower bound at least 1 point for a prespecified endpoint, compatible direction across pace/falls or lag sensitivity, no diagnosis-clean collapse, and no large return-selection shift. This supports validation/adjudication research, not deployment, causality or mechanism.

Adverse evidence is a held-out null/reversal, Q-only equivalence, baseline-only association, body-size attenuation, diagnosis-restricted collapse, large weighting shift, short-lag-only pattern, or a learned rank gain without the prespecified risk contrast. It weakens this data-bound claim, not all muscle-quality hypotheses.

Inconclusive evidence is unverified outcome coding, failed code/date pairing, fewer than 100 holdout events, missing class support, unstable calibration/positivity, or intervals spanning zero and the scale marker. An imprecise null is not refutation.

## Deliverable and limits

The solver must output a frozen cohort audit; exact model and holdout prediction files for Q-only, Q+MFI, Q+grip, Q+MFI+grip and boosted models; calibration/Brier/log-loss/risk/interval tables; rival sensitivity outputs; learned interaction summaries; and a conclusion file labelling each endpoint supportive, adverse or inconclusive with links to computed outputs.

Computationally checkable claims are source/hash/namespace compliance, exact joins, date ordering, cohort counts, exposure construction, split integrity, fit success, calibration/uncertainty and rule-following. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for pain severity, outpatient arthritis, neurologic examination, MRI segmentation validity, actual fall timing/severity, treatment effects, mechanism, transportability and clinical utility. No participant-level rows or fitted results are included here.

Revisit if same-namespace sex or validated sex-specific MRI normalization, outpatient pain/arthritis and neurologic examination, or repeated post-MRI muscle/function measures become available. Preserve unfavorable diagnosis-restricted, 730-day, side-discordance and return-selection branches.

## Three inspected key works

- [K1] Cruz-Jentoft et al. (EWGSOP2), 2019: consensus separation of strength, quantity/quality and performance; abstract-only inspection.
- [K2] Linge et al., 2021: UKB MRI MFI/composition and mortality; full-text XML inspection.
- [K3] Kim et al., 2026: UKB thigh MRI distribution, grip and falls; full-text XML inspection.

The catalog has no participant-level MRI images, gait recordings, pain scores, neurologic examination, or dated fall ledger.

## Verified temporal audit

I independently read only the selected Assessment Center columns and wrote `audit/temporal-audit.json` (SHA-256 `3b9f17d25ff059fd4b20d2c958b8179a74bfdf8278cf1ef274780f98dc16c9a2`). Date strings were parsed as dates; numeric special codes `-1,-3,-7,-10,-11` were treated as missing.

The audit found 502,370 rows and unique keys; 37,242 age >=50 anchors with complete bilateral Q, MFI, grip and T0; 4,577 strictly later dates; and 4,311 later dates at least 730 days after T0. Lag min/median/max was 366/828/3,177 days. A valid later pace or falls value was present for 4,534 anchors; valid baseline-plus-later pairs numbered 4,516 and 4,515 respectively. Later pace code counts were 1/2/3 = 173/2,190/2,171; later falls counts were 1/2/3 = 3,795/540/199. These are availability observations only. The solver must resolve Data-Coding 100313 and 100539 before naming pace ordering or a no-fall category; failure makes that endpoint inconclusive rather than permitting a new definition.

For each endpoint, the primary population is the unique anchor with age >=50, valid T0, complete Q/MFI/grip, valid baseline outcome, first strictly later valid endpoint, and T1-T0 >=365 days. The >=730-day population is locked sensitivity. T1 is date-based, never instance-number based.

## Exposures and estimands

Fit transformations in development only.

- Q is the sum of the four bilateral anterior/posterior thigh fat-free volumes; preserve all four components.
- MFI is the bilateral mean of `23355-2.0` and `23356-2.0`.
- Grip is the maximum valid left/right grip; bilateral-complete is primary, side-specific/discordant analyses are sensitivity.
- Baseline pace/falls are baseline state, not dated incident events.

After coding resolution, primary pace outcome is later category lower than baseline, reporting worsening/unchanged/improvement. Primary falls outcome is later value above the verified no-fall category, with full ordinal counts secondary. Falls asks about the last year and is not a dated fall event.

The main estimand is population-standardized absolute risk difference under quantity matching: MFI +1 development SD and grip -1 SD versus both at development means, holding Q and observed baseline covariates at each person's value. Also report nested Q-only -> Q+MFI, Q-only -> Q+grip, and Q-only -> Q+MFI+grip risk contrasts, component risks, and 95% intervals. A 1 percentage-point lower-bound marker is a scale descriptor, not a treatment threshold. This is prognostic/descriptive, not causal.

## Baseline, learned alternative, split, and uncertainty

Primary transparent models are endpoint-specific ordinal/multinomial regression for pace transitions and logistic regression for falls, with ordinal/logistic sensitivities. Models include Q, age, BMI, weight, height, smoking, baseline outcome, and a prespecified missingness rule; no post-T0 variable is allowed. Diagnosis families define pre-T0 restriction and code-adjusted sensitivity, not casual mediator adjustment. Post-T0 codes are descriptive only.

Use a patient-level temporal split: earliest 70% of T0 for development/tuning and latest 30% as locked holdout. Each `eid` is in one split. Standardization, imputation, coding thresholds, and tuning are development-only. Report holdout calibration intercept/slope, plots, Brier score, log loss, secondary rank metrics, standardized risks, and 500 participant-bootstrap intervals (or a documented substitute). Require at least 100 holdout events, class support, finite estimates, stable calibration and positivity; otherwise endpoint is inconclusive with no split/outcome changes.

Matched learned alternative: CPU gradient-boosted trees for each endpoint using exactly the same participants, inputs, missingness policy, T0/T1 rule, split and outcomes. It can reveal Q-by-MFI, Q-by-grip, thresholds, and side/compartment interactions that additive regression loses. It is substantive only if a held-out quantity-matched risk contrast or rival interpretation changes; a small rank-metric gain is not enough. Report uncertainty-bearing accumulated-local-effect or partial-dependence summaries descriptively, never as mechanism.

The transparent model is primary because it exposes the estimand and is auditable with roughly 4,500 endpoint pairs. The learned model is retained to test nonlinear scientific structure. A deep image model is deferred because no image payload exists; a trajectory model is deferred because only one verified later assessment exists; causal mediation is rejected because pain severity, neurologic examination, actual fall timing and treatment are unavailable.

Planning estimate: 8 CPU cores, 32–64 GiB RAM, 2–4 hours for selected-column parsing, exact joins, two baselines/boosted fits and bootstrap. Unmeasured planning estimate; GPU is not needed for this tabular question.

## Rival falsification

Pain/arthritis/neurologic rival: repeat the primary analysis in participants without prespecified pre-T0 inpatient code families, report each diagnosis stratum and same-index code-adjusted model. A grip signal that disappears while MFI remains stable supports the rival; a persistent result is only compatible with a quality signal because outpatient pain and examination remain missing.

MRI/body-size/sex rival: adjust using the available age/BMI/weight/height fields; compare bilateral and side/compartment estimates, and report body-size sensitivity. Sex cannot be adjusted or stratified from this verified table; a result is explicitly limited by that missing evidence. Strong attenuation or side-specific instability is adverse for the biological interpretation.

Repeat-selection/reverse-timing rival: compare unweighted results with baseline-only inverse-probability weighting for having a valid later assessment, report weights/positivity, and repeat at >=730 days and by early/late T1. Do not condition on post-T0 variables. A large weighting shift or short-lag-only signal is adverse; an imprecise weighted result is inconclusive.

Supportive evidence requires at least one endpoint passing support/positivity/calibration gates, a positive held-out Q+MFI or Q+grip increment beyond Q-only with 95% interval above zero and lower bound at least 1 point for a prespecified endpoint, compatible direction across pace/falls or lag sensitivity, no diagnosis-clean collapse, and no large return-selection shift. This supports validation/adjudication research, not deployment, causality or mechanism.

Adverse evidence is a held-out null/reversal, Q-only equivalence, baseline-only association, body-size attenuation, diagnosis-restricted collapse, large weighting shift, short-lag-only pattern, or a learned rank gain without the prespecified risk contrast. It weakens this data-bound claim, not all muscle-quality hypotheses.

Inconclusive evidence is unverified outcome coding, failed code/date pairing, fewer than 100 holdout events, missing class support, unstable calibration/positivity, or intervals spanning zero and the scale marker. An imprecise null is not refutation.

## Deliverable and limits

The solver must output a frozen cohort audit; exact model and holdout prediction files for Q-only, Q+MFI, Q+grip, Q+MFI+grip and boosted models; calibration/Brier/log-loss/risk/interval tables; rival sensitivity outputs; learned interaction summaries; and a conclusion file labelling each endpoint supportive, adverse or inconclusive with links to computed outputs.

Computationally checkable claims are source/hash/namespace compliance, exact joins, date ordering, cohort counts, exposure construction, split integrity, fit success, calibration/uncertainty and rule-following. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for pain severity, outpatient arthritis, neurologic examination, MRI segmentation validity, actual fall timing/severity, treatment effects, mechanism, transportability and clinical utility. No participant-level rows or fitted results are included here.

Revisit if same-namespace sex or validated sex-specific MRI normalization, outpatient pain/arthritis and neurologic examination, or repeated post-MRI muscle/function measures become available. Preserve unfavorable diagnosis-restricted, 730-day, side-discordance and return-selection branches.
