The EHR demonstration methods are not biologically transferable here: Delphi needs dated patient histories, Oncoformer needs longitudinal EHR and imaging, and Aladynoulli concerns longitudinal disease/genetic structure. Their method lessons were considered, but no such modalities/population are bound in these four molecular assays; they are not method bans or evidence for this hypothesis. No expert-seed claim is treated as evidence.

## Computable experiment and methods

**Time/population boundary:** Cross-sectional E-MTAB-8322 samples recorded as RA remission versus treatment-naive RA, sampled at their single biopsy/assay time. No temporal ordering, paired transition or post-cessation outcome is inferred. The donor is the independent unit (7 versus 6). Before fitting, resolve exact sample/donor/run mapping and count alignment; freeze QC, state-label rules and any expert-defined material-effect thresholds. Report age, sex, run/library, cell-yield/depth, and processing metadata by group; do not overfit adjusted covariates with 13 donors. Treat them as descriptive/sensitivity covariates, not proof of exchangeability.

**Outcome and estimand:** Estimate donor-level macrophage state proportions and donor-state MERTK pseudobulk expression from raw counts. Define states using macrophage features excluding MERTK (including its aliases) and response labels; verify state markers and alignment without using either outcome gene or group label. Decompose remission-minus-naive aggregate MERTK into (i) a composition component using a common/reference state-conditional MERTK profile and differing state proportions and (ii) a within-state component using differing state-conditional MERTK profiles at a common/reference proportion. Predeclare a symmetric/Shapley decomposition so parts sum to total contrast and report the reference convention. Report all components on the same normalized/log-expression scale, donor-level values, donor support and uncertainty. The estimand is descriptive, not causal.

**Baseline (primary):** From the 13 raw cell matrices, perform documented per-cell QC with frozen minimum coverage/doublet rules, pseudobulk raw counts by donor and MERTK-independent state, compute donor-state proportions and state-conditional MERTK, then estimate the decomposition. Use donor bootstrap and donor-level permutation/leave-one-donor-out as uncertainty and influence summaries; never use cell-level p-values. Repeat across predeclared defensible annotation resolutions, QC/depth matching, and donor/run/yield sensitivities. Report if too few cells/donors support a state rather than collapsing groups post hoc. Because there is no cell recovery denominator or gold-standard state labels, do not present observed recovered-cell proportions as absolute in-vivo tissue abundance.

**Learned/mechanistic alternative (same estimand, secondary and gated):** Fit a low-dimensional probabilistic latent-state mixture from the exact same MERTK-excluded cell-by-gene input, donor-balanced so high-yield donors do not dominate and without using response labels. Outer leave-one-donor-out folds hold out all cells/runs from one donor; fit signatures/mixture on remaining donors, align states using MERTK-excluded features, and estimate soft state membership for the held-out donor. Compute the identical composition and within-state components using soft proportions and conditional MERTK. Evaluate held-out state assignment/reconstruction and cross-fold state alignment, and compare component estimates/uncertainty to the fixed-label baseline using a full donor-resampled refit. The purpose is to expose assignment uncertainty that hard-label pseudobulk loses, not improve remission prediction. Defer or omit this alternative if state alignment is unstable, folds leak donors, groups are used to learn states, or the 13-donor sample cannot identify latent components; no GPU is selected. Alternative resource estimate is unmeasured planning only: CPU 4–8 cores, 16–32 GiB, likely <1–4 hours for QC, folds and donor bootstrap, depending on retained cells/features. The baseline is expected CPU 2–4 cores, 8–16 GiB, minutes to hours; no timing probe was run. A100 hardware exists but allocation is not needed absent a measured matrix bottleneck.

**Why this comparison matters:** The baseline yields transparent, donor-level components but assumes hard state labels and can conceal uncertainty in borderline cells. The soft latent alternative can reveal whether a seemingly dominant composition component is an artifact of label assignment. With only 13 independent donors, however, a flexible model may manufacture unstable states and precision from cell count; it cannot compensate for missing clinical or recovery data. Keep it as a sensitivity comparator, not the scientific winner based on model complexity or small predictive gains.

## Outcomes, falsification and interpretation

- **Supportive of composition-dominant hypothesis:** a nontrivial composition component exceeds the within-state component by the prespecified expert-adjudicated material margin; donor-level uncertainty supports that ordering; direction and ordering remain stable under donor deletion, label resolution, QC/depth and yield/run sensitivities, and the latent alternative (if estimable) does not reverse it. This would support prioritizing state/niche abundance or spatial-recruitment follow-up in this cohort, not causal recruitment, MERTK protection, or therapeutic benefit.
- **Adverse to composition-dominant hypothesis:** within-state MERTK is the larger, robust component, or the composition component is near zero/opposite with intervals sufficiently narrow relative to a material margin and insensitive to plausible labels/recovery. This redirects next work toward within-state regulation; it does not prove that MERTK is causal or clinically actionable.
- **Inconclusive/mixed:** wide donor-level intervals, near-zero total contrast (unstable component ratios), opposing components, few state-supporting donors/cells, failed cell/gene alignment, unstable learned states, or conclusions that track yield/depth/processing indicate insufficient resolution or a mixed model. Do not call nonsignificance equivalence or claim falsification from an imprecise null.

The numeric minimum meaningful MERTK contrast/state-fraction difference is not established by available files; a rheumatology/immunology/statistics panel must adjudicate and freeze these margins before outcome computation. If no defensible margin is obtained, report component estimates and uncertainty without a categorical “dominant” claim. Automatic verification can check file joins, MERTK feature identity, donor aggregation, formulae, split isolation, output linkage and consistency of supportive/adverse/inconclusive language with computed intervals. It cannot adjudicate state biology, recovery bias, causal mechanisms, functional protection, or clinical benefit. Conclusions beyond descriptive decomposition need source/assay expert review; target-specific causality requires a separate prospective donor-crossed MERTK loss/rescue and target-engagement study with distinct inflammatory, efferocytosis/repair and viability endpoints. Clinical recommendations require further translational studies.

## Scientific deliverable and decision record

Newly fit/estimated outputs required: exact sample/gene/barcode QC manifest; per-donor and per-state cell counts and MERTK pseudobulk; state proportion table; total/composition/within-state effects with donor-level uncertainty and leave-one-donor-out, state-label and recovery/depth sensitivities; learned soft-state comparator diagnostics/effects only if its predeclared gate passes; and a report stating which result category is supported with links to these outputs. These computations establish completion of the proposed Harbor analysis, not completion of the biological question.

**Deferred alternative:** A donor-held-out probabilistic mixture is retained only as a gated sensitivity analysis because its possible information is membership uncertainty, while 13 donors make learned states weakly identified; revisit only if stable held-out state alignment materially changes component uncertainty. The four-source pooled analysis and the prior E-MTAB-8316 inhibitor signature screen are not selected: neither supplies a comparable donor-resolved remission cohort or validates MERTK function.

## References

The closest inspected work already reports macrophage states and MerTK-associated remission/repair [K1]; this proposal adds no claim that such states or a MerTK association are novel. Independent macrophage heterogeneity [K2] and spatial matrix/routing [K3] bound the cell-intrinsic interpretation. All three are abstract-only inspected; see attached `key-references.json` and exact UTF-8 excerpts.

# MERTK cell-context therapeutic-window hypothesis: archival RNA update

**Status: hypothesis plus one completed descriptive reanalysis; no causal or wet-lab test has been executed.** The clinically consequential unresolved question is whether selective MERTK inhibition can reduce inflammatory macrophage-to-fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) signaling in an inflammatory context without impairing resolution-associated macrophage functions, or whether apparent compound-linked effects reflect off-target action, exposure/toxicity, carry-over, donor composition, or assay artifacts. The result could guide whether MERTK merits cell-restricted preclinical development versus deferral; it cannot justify systemic inhibition or clinical use.

# MERTK-state dependence of synovial fibroblast responses

## Question, hypothesis, and importance

**Untested hypothesis:** In the 48-hour ex-vivo rheumatoid arthritis synovial tissue macrophage–fibroblast co-culture, macrophage pretreatment with the MerTK inhibitor UNC1062 attenuates the measured matrix/TGF-response profile induced by MerTK/CD206-positive macrophages in FLS, relative to untreated Mpos co-culture; a shift toward measured inflammatory features is a prespecified secondary prediction. This is a bounded test of MERTK-inhibitor-associated macrophage-state dependence, not a claim that MerTK signaling between a named ligand and FLS receptor is proven.

This matters because MerTK-positive macrophage subsets have been linked with remission-associated, inflammation-resolving profiles and induction of FLS repair responses [K1]. If pharmacologic perturbation of that cell state weakens an FLS matrix/TGF-response program, it is a consequential warning about which synovial macrophage states should be preserved or altered in future therapeutic research. The available data are ex-vivo and extremely limited in independent paired units; no drug, disease-modifying benefit or patient treatment decision is supported.

## Evidence and unresolved claim

Alivernini et al. report MerTK-positive macrophage subsets with remission-associated signatures and FLS repair-response induction [K1]. Kuo et al. established a different RA macrophage-to-FLS pathway, HBEGF–EGFR, that increases FLS invasiveness [K2]. That pathway is not being relabeled as a novel finding here; HBEGF and EGFR are absent from E-MTAB-8873. Zhang et al. identify extensive inflammatory cell-state heterogeneity in RA synovium and associations with treatment response [K3], limiting any generalization from a small ex-vivo assay.

**Strongest supported claim:** prior work establishes that synovial macrophage states can influence fibroblast responses, including repair and invasiveness. **Unresolved claim being tested:** whether UNC1062 pretreatment of the Mpos compartment in this particular assay is associated with attenuation of a measured FLS matrix/TGF-response profile beyond sample-pair variation or nonspecific inflammation. Neither the literature nor the data currently establish such an effect. The substantive advance is a tightly bound, treatment-relevant boundary test of a known cell-state hypothesis, rather than discovery of a new ligand–receptor pathway.

Strongest rivals: differences in contributing donor or experimental run; inconsistent inhibitor-label/dose/washout; compound carryover directly affecting FLS; macrophage toxicity or generic change in activation rather than on-target MERTK action; an inflammatory stimulus response unrelated to the repair/matrix program; and a transcript shift that does not translate to protein or functional tissue effects.

## Bound data and population

Use the prepared E-MTAB-8873 table `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz` (445 measured transcript-feature rows × 33 sample columns) with `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json` (33 records). Matrix column names join exactly to design `sample_id`; retain `feature` identifiers and use design `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `cells`, and nested `source_metadata` fields for contributors, growth condition and stimulus. Prepared table SHA-256 `d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f`; design SHA-256 `fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4`; registered in `[private-path]/assay-registry.json` (SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`). Source lineage is E-MTAB-8873 `repository.json`, `E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt`, and the sample-specific `RSEC_MolsPerCell` archives listed in `datasets/disease_mechanisms/README.md`; data are read-only. Values in the prepared matrix are RSEC molecules-per-cell, not ordinary bulk-RNA counts.

Original source record/protocol `P-MTAB-95052` describes 3,000 FLS plus 3,000 sorted MerTK/CD206-positive or -negative STMs, co-cultured for 48 hours. It says MerTK/CD206-positive STMs were pretreated with 250 nM UNC1062; the positive inflammatory comparator used MerTK/CD206-negative STMs pretreated with 10 ng/ml LPS for 1 hour and washed three times before co-culture. The source protocol reports technical triplicates and five active RA/five sustained-remission patients in five same-day pairs, while the prepared analysis matrix has only 33 sample columns. The protocol text also refers to 446 assay genes (399 immune panel plus 46 custom) while the prepared matrix contains 445 feature rows. Resolve these provenance/count discrepancies and column-to-patient mapping against original sample-level source records before inferential interpretation; technical replicates are not independent donors. No time course is available: 48 hours is the recorded endpoint, not repeated temporal measurements.

Primary population is only the two contributor-matched untreated-versus-inhibitor Mpos blocks in the prepared table, conditional on validating matched IDs and same protocol:

- R2: `R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos` versus `R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor` (recorded FLS/macrophage contributors SA257A/SA266A).
- R5: `R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos` versus `R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor` (recorded contributors SA266A/SA277A).

R1 `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos` / `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos` plus inhibitor conditions form a donor-distinct descriptive sensitivity block, not an additional matched pair. R1 also records negative-STM and LPS controls. R1 inhibitor is labeled `Inhibitor` while R2/R5 use `preInhibitor`; protocol review must verify compound, dose, timing, washout, sample and run equivalence before pooling. Despite donor strings, the assay registry explicitly cautions that contributors may be shared/reused and disables ordinary donor t-tests. Sample columns and assayed cell counts are not independent n.

The primary matrix/TGF-response feature set is restricted to verified measured features: `COL1A1|NM_000088.3|PolyA_1`, `COL1A1|NM_000088.3|Reference_end`, `COL1A2|NM_000089.3|PolyA_1`, `COL3A1|NM_000090.3|PolyA_1`, `TGFBI|NM_000358.2|Reference_end`, `TGFB3|NM_003239.3|Reference_end`. The secondary inflammatory set is `IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end`, `CXCL8|NM_000584.3|Reference_end`, `CCL2|NM_002982.3|Reference_end`, `IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end`, and both `TNFAIP3|NM_001270508.1|PolyA_1` and `TNFAIP3|NM_001270508.1|Reference_end` features, retained separately. The matrix also contains `MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end`; no matched macrophage expression values are supplied in this prepared table. `GAS6`, `PROS1`, `HBEGF`, `EGFR`, `IL10`, `PTGS2`, ACTA2, secreted protein, receptor engagement and phosphosignaling are not measured here. A transcript name is not evidence of ligand secretion or pathway activity.

E-MTAB-8316 is not the FLS endpoint: its prepared 12 samples are LPS-exposed monocytes, none are FLS or co-cultures. E-MTAB-8322 contains macrophages only. GSE95588 co-culture data are deferred because the domain guide flags unresolved donor-to-column inference and duplicate/date-like feature labels; not independent confirmation. Do not join source datasets by coincident donor IDs.

## Estimand, analysis, and deliverables

Primary estimand: within each valid R2/R5 matched contributor block, the difference in log2(RSEC molecules-per-cell + 1) between UNC1062-pretreated and untreated Mpos co-culture for each fixed matrix/TGF-response feature; report both block estimates and their unweighted mean descriptively. The mean is not a population-level effect estimate with two blocks. The secondary inflammation-feature contrast is analyzed identically. A prespecified FLS-only and Mneg comparison can describe the Mpos context but does not establish a randomized comparator. Do not claim a result until a future analysis is run.

**Simple baseline:** per-feature paired differences and fixed feature-set average. **Substantive alternative on the same question:** fit a blocked, multivariate measured-panel condition contrast for the fixed matrix/TGF set and inflammatory set, and an exploratory Mpos-versus-Mneg/LPS condition-by-treatment specificity contrast where the recorded design permits. It could distinguish a coordinated measured fibroblast state response from isolated markers and compare that pattern with general inflammatory activation, which a single-marker baseline loses. However the specificity interaction has only R1 context, the primary contrast has only two matched blocks, and the assay is targeted. This is an estimative/mechanistic-pattern alternative, not a learned predictor or causal mediation test. Preserve features/transcript identifiers, display each block, report effect sizes and uncertainty, and perform leave-one-block-out sensitivity. No random cell/sample split and no false independent validation; no p-value-only decision. If protocol or sample map fails, output a documented block/contrast audit and mark the test inconclusive rather than improvising a population.

The solver must newly fit/estimate and deliver: (1) `effect_estimates.tsv` with feature ID, block, contrast, transformed values and effect; (2) `response_summary.json` with exact fixed feature sets, block-specific effects, descriptive mean and uncertainty limits; (3) `specificity_sensitivity.tsv` for R1 Mpos/Mneg/LPS and R1-excluded analyses, if metadata supports them; (4) an interpretation report linking claims to these computed outputs. All post-hoc 445-feature scans must be labeled exploratory and multiplicity-adjusted. No discovery screening job or molecular analysis has been executed in this proposal.

No GPU is needed. Resource estimate is unmeasured but the 33 × 445 table is small; plan ≤2 CPU cores, ≤4 GiB RAM and ≤10 minutes for the future fit. This sits inside the solver planning envelope (16 CPUs, 256 GiB, up to 8 GPUs and 8 hours). A broad learned model is deferred, not categorically prohibited: only two usable pairs and 445 targeted features cannot support its training/held-out donor validation. Revisit with protocol-harmonized independent donor pairs and a separate donor-level validation set.

## Falsification and decisions

- **Supportive:** both verified R2/R5 blocks show attenuation of the Mpos-associated fixed matrix/TGF-response set under macrophage UNC1062, not dominated by one feature; secondary inflammatory changes are reported separately, and the exploratory pattern is not merely the available LPS-control pattern. This supports an inhibitor-associated FLS transcript shift in these conditions and merits an independent replication. It does not prove on-target MERTK specificity, direction through a ligand/receptor, matrix function, FLS repair, clinical disease modification or patient benefit.
- **Adverse:** both valid blocks show no attenuation or an opposite effect, or the apparent change is driven by one block/feature and resembles nonspecific LPS response. This down-ranks the predicted transcript-level effect in this assay, not MerTK biology generally.
- **Inconclusive:** donor/sample mapping or inhibitor-label equivalence fails, fewer than two valid blocks remain, block effects disagree materially, or uncertainty/technical provenance is too weak. A wide interval or imprecise null does not refute the hypothesis.

Before interpreting, expert/protocol adjudication must verify actual FLS/STM identities, sorted phenotype, contributor/donor map, raw sample-to-tag mapping, the protocol's 446-vs-445 count discrepancy, technical replicate relation, UNC1062 administration/washout and R1/R2/R5 label equivalence. If results warrant continuation, conduct an independent donor-paired experiment randomizing Mpos macrophage vehicle vs macrophage-restricted genetic or pharmacologic MERTK perturbation/rescue; include inhibitor washout and direct FLS-only inhibitor exposure controls, Mneg and LPS controls, macrophage viability/target engagement, and FLS-only/conditioned-medium/transwell/direct-contact comparisons. Measure secreted GAS6/PROS1 and cytokines, FLS RNA/protein/phosphosignaling, and a functional matrix/invasion/repair outcome over a prespecified time course. Only a named ligand/receptor blockade/rescue with independent donors can establish directional communication; tissue localization plus clinical outcomes would be required for claims about patient disease or treatment choice.

## Method alternatives and precedent disposition

The simple paired baseline is chosen for transparency and the tiny donor-level information available. The alternate multivariate measured-panel model is retained as a scientifically substantive check for coherent, treatment-context-specific FLS response rather than chasing predictive gain. A neural predictor, unconstrained pathway search or detailed mechanistic simulation is deferred because the sample units are too few and key inputs (matched macrophage panel, ligand/protein concentrations, target engagement and functional outcomes) are absent; added complexity cannot resolve the claim. Revisit with those dependencies and independently held-out donor pairs. No new model has been fitted during discovery.

The three clinical demonstration methods are not adapted in this molecular assay: Delphi requires dated longitudinal disease histories; Oncoformer’s multimodal EHR/imaging data and main methods were unavailable in the reference bundle and do not map to the synovial assay; ALADYNOULLI is an EHR/genetic longitudinal model, not applicable here. The verified methods-and-compute note was read; no reproduction claim or GPU requirement follows from it.

Computationally checkable claims include sample/feature binding, transformation, contrast calculations, fixed-set construction, per-block effects, and whether conclusions faithfully report outputs and uncertainty. Clinical and mechanistic claims require protocol review and independent experiments. An automatic verifier cannot certify actual cell identity, inhibitor specificity, causal communication, functional tissue repair, disease modification or clinical benefit.

# Synovial macrophage remission signal: composition or within-state regulation?

## Question, hypothesis, importance

**Falsifiable hypothesis:** Among the captured synovial tissue macrophages in the E-MTAB-8322 rheumatoid arthritis remission-versus-treatment-resistant comparison, most of the aggregate transcriptomic difference is explained by differences in the proportions of stable macrophage expression states, rather than by expression changes within states shared across groups. This is a hypothesis about the measured cell compartment and a single biopsy time, not proof of cell-state transition or treatment causality.

This distinction changes the next scientific decision. If composition dominates, future work should examine recruitment, retention or survival of macrophage states; if a robust within-state component dominates, prioritize a reprogramming/perturbation experiment. Either result helps avoid treating one average-tissue signature as a unique mechanism. The precise clinical remission/resistance labels and therapy history need adjudication; no immediate treatment choice follows.

## Evidence, unresolved claim, closest prior work

Prior knowledge supports macrophage heterogeneity in RA and reports different cluster frequencies plus remission-associated macrophage programs [K1]. A second macrophage subset, HBEGF-positive and pro-invasive to fibroblasts, illustrates a plausible inflammatory rival rather than a one-dimensional pro-resolution/anti-resolution model [K2]. Synovial matrix and fibroblast niches can spatially pattern immune entry and disease activity [K3], a tissue-level rival that this macrophage-only dataset cannot resolve.

**Strongest evidence-supported claim:** prior work has observed remission-associated macrophage subsets and functional macrophage–fibroblast effects; these data are not evidence that a remission subset causes remission. **Untested claim:** whether, within E-MTAB-8322, the total remission-versus-resistant expression difference is quantitatively dominated by captured-macrophage state proportions or remains after standardizing state proportions. The advance is a donor-aware decomposition of the clinical-state contrast to distinguish state representation from within-state regulation, not an independent replication or a new cell marker. K1 is closely related and may use this dataset; its abstract/data availability were inspected, not all methods or supplements. The proposal does not imply the decomposition has not appeared in detailed source results.

Strongest rival is within-state transcriptional reprogramming; both can coexist. Other rivals include current disease activity, treatment class/history, age, biopsy selection, sequencing run/library differences, dissociation/capture bias and spatial stromal context. Existing prepared metadata cannot adjust for most of these. Failure to resolve these confounders narrows interpretation, rather than warranting a mechanistic conclusion.

## Data, population, temporal boundaries

Source snapshot `core-molecular-20261003`; relevant bindings are the assay registry `[private-path]/assay-registry.json` (SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`) and source catalog `datasets/disease_mechanisms/metadata.json`. The exact source files are read-only.

Primary sample-level table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz` (SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`), tab-separated feature-by-sample counts with `feature` row key and 27 sample-ID columns; registry lists 33,694 feature rows. Match each matrix sample column exactly to the JSON `sample_id`, retaining feature identifiers; inspect scale/lineage before selecting a count model. The table holds pseudobulk macrophage expression, not whole tissue or state-resolved values.

Sample annotations: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json` (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`), 27 records with `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, and `cells`. Use `donor_id` as biological unit. For source reconciliation, read `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `b87005a9eefff1beb2d12de2e9f945e2a0b6330aa59207f61f0ecaba180fa237`) and `E-MTAB-8322.idf.txt` (SHA-256 `3755fdf0db73c3dca32e0b4b70aeec2e91df16a737137933de2064aeb1bfe069`). Join SDRF `Source Name` to design `source_name` and verify `Characteristics[individual]`, disease and response annotations. SDRF is run-level (106 rows) with varying technical sequencing-run/lane counts per donor; run rows are not independent subjects. Verified annotations report remission n=7 (SA132, SA159, SA160, SA161, SA168, SA174, SA225) and resistant-to-treatment n=6 (SA144, SA145, SA151, SA166, SA222, SA227), all RA, synovial membrane macrophage samples. Exclude healthy, naive, undifferentiated arthritis, and SA149/SA149P related-or-repeated identity records from the primary contrast.

For the learned alternative, use original per-donor files at `[private-path]/{prefix}.matrix.mtx`, `{prefix}.genes.tsv`, and `{prefix}.barcodes.tsv` for the 13 named donors above. Matrix row i joins to row i in its genes file; cell column j joins to barcode row j. Examples verified in the source registry include `RemSA132` and `ResistantSA144`; all remaining exact sample prefixes are in the prepared design/assay registry. Preserve donor boundaries and join no identities across other assays.

Temporal target is one cross-sectional biopsy/library per donor. There is no donor-specific date, pre/post-treatment measure, treatment start/stop time, remission duration, or clinical outcome time field in the inspected design. `treatment` is null for these group records. Source label definitions, medication class/dose/duration, biopsy activity scores, concomitant steroids and detailed batch/capture context require source-record or clinician adjudication.

## Analysis and substantive alternative

**Simple baseline:** construct donor-level pseudobulk expression from the prepared feature-by-sample matrix, check its lineage and count semantics, and estimate a remission-versus-resistant contrast using a prespecified count model with donor as unit. Report per-gene effects/FDR and a sample-level total-expression contrast using a fixed, reproducible representation; show each donor, age sensitivity and sequencing-run/library sensitivity. Do not treat cells, genes or SDRF lanes as independent replicates. Maximum effective n is 13, so donor bootstrap intervals and leave-one-donor-out influence are essential; narrow covariate models are not credible at this n.

**Mechanistic alternative on the same question:** fit an unsupervised, donor-aware macrophage-state mixture model to the 13 original sparse cell matrices, learning a shared set of states without using remission/resistance labels. In leave-one-donor-out folds, learn state representations on other donors and project the held-out donor; keep all cells from one donor together. Estimate donor-level state fractions and state-specific expression, then decompose total group contrast into captured-state proportion and within-shared-state components using a common reference state distribution. Evaluate cluster/program stability across donor-held-out fits and donor-cluster bootstrap uncertainty. This can reveal a compositional explanation masked by sample averages, which the baseline cannot separate from within-state change. It is exploratory and requires common states and crossed processing/run structure; if states are unstable or group and technical batch are aliased, stop and mark inconclusive. No clinical prediction model or random-cell split is warranted.

Resource plan: baseline CPU 2 cores/8 GiB, estimated under 30 minutes (not benchmarked). Cell-state decomposition CPU 4 cores/16 GiB, estimated 1–2 hours for sparse donor-held-out fits and 1,000 donor bootstrap replicates (unmeasured, package-dependent); no GPU is scientifically useful at this size. Solver planning envelope <=16 CPU, 32 GiB RAM, <=4 hours. These estimates are future workload estimates, not measured discovery results. Discovery performed source/schema inspection only; no transcriptomic analysis or model fit was run.

## Falsification and outcome interpretation

Support for the directional composition hypothesis requires (a) donor-level remission/resistant total expression contrast, (b) reproducibly different proportions of shared, stable macrophage states, and (c) the within-state standardized contrast materially attenuated relative to the total contrast, without a single donor or observed run/lane pattern accounting for the result. This is cross-sectional association only.

- **Supportive:** the total contrast is mainly accounted for by state proportions; standardized within-state effects are smaller and uncertain; learned states are stable in donor-held-out fits. Prioritize orthogonal validation of the captured-state composition explanation, not whole-tissue abundance or causality.
- **Adverse:** stable shared states show a precise within-state contrast that is not attenuated by standardization, while state fractions are similar; this weakens the composition-dominant hypothesis and prioritizes independent perturbation of state regulation.
- **Inconclusive:** wide donor-level uncertainty, unstable clusters, no common states, sensitivity to a single donor, unmeasured group/run alias, poor gene/barcode alignment, or unresolved labels. This is not evidence that states are equivalent.

Falsification requires adequate cell/gene coverage, stable common-state assignment and a precise within-state component not materially attenuated by proportion standardization; otherwise claim only failure to resolve. Computationally checkable: sample/donor flow, joins, matrix alignment, state-fit stability, group contrasts, decomposition, uncertainty and whether conclusions match outputs. Expert adjudication needed for remission/resistance definitions, medications, severity, biopsy context, sequencing/capture confounding, and biological relevance of inferred states. Longitudinal persistence/transition requires prospective repeated samples; whole-tissue abundance/spatial effects require unsorted or spatial data; causality and intervention relevance require perturbation and functional outcomes; clinical treatment selection requires prospective external validation.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” *Nature Medicine* (2020), DOI `10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8`. The inspected abstract reports 32,000 STMs, remission-associated MerTK-positive subsets, and different cluster frequencies across clinical states. This is closely related prior work and likely overlaps this dataset; it constrains novelty and does not constitute independent replication. Abstract and limited article context inspected, not full methods/supplements. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K1-alivernini-abstract.txt`.

[K2] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” *Science Translational Medicine* (2019), DOI `10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587`. The inspected abstract supports macrophage heterogeneity, stromal conditioning, and a distinct inflammatory macrophage-to-fibroblast path as a serious biological rival. Full-text acquisition was unavailable; abstract only. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K2-kuo-abstract.txt`.

[K3] Richard JB et al. “Synovial matrix turnover controls immune cell spatial patterning in inflammation resolution.” *Molecular Systems Biology* (2025), DOI `10.1038/s44320-025-00149-7`. The inspected abstract reports fibroblast/myeloid matrix interactions and collagen-VI-associated spatial immune ingress, reinforcing that proportions in isolated macrophages cannot resolve spatial/stromal causes. Abstract only. Attached excerpt: `references/episode2/K3-richard-abstract.txt`.

## Unchosen alternatives and revision gates

D3-M1's broad whole-tissue composition question is not answerable from macrophage-only expression; the learned cell-state decomposition is a narrower, measured version. D3-M3 transition/persistence claims remain blocked by the cross-sectional single sample. Episode-1 MERTK/FLS UNC1062 study remains separate context and is not an independent validation dataset for this question. E-MTAB-8316/E-MTAB-8873/GSE95588 remain configured and accessible, but their distinct assay populations and donor namespaces are not joined here. Historical EHR demonstrations are not adapted because the molecular sources do not contain longitudinal EHR diagnoses, dates or outcomes.

Revisit/defer if K1 full text/supplements already resolve the same within-state decomposition; if exact remission/resistance criteria and medications cannot be reconciled; if run/batch is perfectly confounded with group; or if held-out state mapping is unstable. A supportive result warrants only orthogonal state-composition validation; another study is required for causal claims.

## New scientific deliverable

The solver must newly fit the donor-level expression contrast and, if identity/batch/stability prerequisites pass, the donor-held-out cell-state mixture decomposition. Completion outputs: cohort flow and exclusions, source scale/lineage QC, per-donor expression/state fractions, total and state-standardized contrast estimates with donor-level uncertainty, held-out state stability, sensitivity results, and an interpretation classified supportive/adverse/inconclusive and justified from these outputs. No reference solution or discovery result is claimed.

# Synovial macrophage remission signal: composition or within-state regulation?

## Research objective

Test the frozen hypothesis that, among captured synovial tissue macrophages in the E-MTAB-8322 rheumatoid arthritis remission-versus-treatment-resistant contrast, the aggregate expression difference is mainly explained by differing proportions of stable shared macrophage states rather than within-state regulation. This is cross-sectional, donor-level, and specific to the captured macrophage compartment; it is not evidence of cell transition, treatment causality, tissue-wide abundance, or clinical utility.

The strongest evidence-supported claim is that prior work reports remission-associated macrophage programs and frequencies [K1], macrophage-to-fibroblast effects [K2], and spatial matrix/myeloid context [K3]. The unresolved claim is the quantitative composition-versus-within-state decomposition in this dataset. K1 may overlap this cohort, so this is not independent replication and novelty is limited to the proposed decomposition. A substantive rival is within-state transcriptional regulation; other explanations include disease severity, drug history, biopsy selection, technical run/library differences, capture bias, and spatial stromal context.

## Inputs and cohort

All bound data are read-only under `/data`. Use only E-MTAB-8322; do not join donor identifiers across assays. The prepared matrix is `/data/prepared/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz`, a feature-by-sample TSV with `feature` plus 27 sample-ID columns (33,694 feature rows). Join each sample column exactly to `sample_id` in `/data/prepared/E-MTAB-8322.design.json`; required design fields include `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, and `cells`. Biological unit is donor, not cell, lane, run, gene, or sample replicate.

Reconcile labels using `/data/E-MTAB-8322/E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt` and `/data/E-MTAB-8322/E-MTAB-8322.idf.txt`. Join SDRF `Source Name` to design `source_name`; check `Characteristics[individual]`, disease and response fields. SDRF contains 106 run-level records and repeated technical runs; never count them as independent subjects. Primary cohort: 7 verified remission donors (SA132, SA159, SA160, SA161, SA168, SA174, SA225) and 6 verified treatment-resistant RA donors (SA144, SA145, SA151, SA166, SA222, SA227), all synovial membrane macrophages. Exclude healthy, treatment-naive, undifferentiated arthritis, and SA149/SA149P related/repeated records. Preserve sample IDs as present in the prepared matrix; verify alignment rather than assuming naming equivalence.

The alternative model uses per-donor sparse count triplets in `/data/E-MTAB-8322/{prefix}.matrix.mtx`, `{prefix}.genes.tsv`, `{prefix}.barcodes.tsv`, with prefixes `RemSA132`, `RemSA160`, `RemSA161`, `RemSA174`, `SA159`, `SA168`, `SA225`, `ResistantSA144`, `ResistantSA145`, `ResistantSA151`, `ResistantSA166`, `SA222`, and `SA227`. Matrix row i maps to row i of the matching genes file; matrix column j maps to row j of the matching barcodes file. Verify dimensions/order and retain actual filtering/QC logs. No validated state-label table is supplied; states must be learned. There is no individual sample date, remission duration, response assessment time, medication history, or disease-activity score verified in these bindings. Do not invent temporality or clinical covariates. No archive members are needed; inputs are independent files.

## Required new computation

This is a research task, not a reference-answer task. Newly estimate (1) donor-level remission-versus-resistant pseudobulk expression contrasts, and (2), only if data alignment, common-state stability, and group/run identifiability allow it, a label-blinded, donor-held-out state-mixture decomposition of the same contrast. Deliver cohort flow and exclusions; scale/lineage QC; donor-level expression and state fractions; total contrast; state-proportion and within-shared-state contributions; common-state-standardized contrast; uncertainty and leave-one-donor-out influence; state stability across donor-held-out fits; and sensitivity to observed run/library structure. Keep every cell from a donor in the same fold. Learn states without response labels, fit on other donors, and map held-out donors. Report how the decomposition metric is defined before interpreting it; preserve signed components and uncertainty. If shared states cannot be robustly mapped or technical structure is aliased with clinical group, stop the decomposition and report inconclusive rather than substituting another estimand.

**Baseline:** donor-level pseudobulk from prepared matrix, after confirming scale/lineage and count-model suitability. Report gene-level effects/FDR and the prespecified overall contrast, donor-level uncertainty, all donors, and age/run/library sensitivities; do not overfit covariates at n=13. **Substantive alternative:** shared unsupervised state mixture on original sparse cell matrices; estimate donor state proportions and state-specific expression, then standardize to a common state distribution and decompose the total contrast. This may identify a compositional component hidden by averages that pseudobulk alone cannot distinguish. Use donor-cluster bootstrap uncertainty and leave-one-donor-out stability. Do not split cells randomly or predict clinical labels.

Proposed solver resource envelope is at most 16 CPU, 262,144 MiB RAM, 8 GPUs, 28,800 seconds. The proposal estimates the baseline at 2 CPU/8 GiB/<30 min and mixture model at 4 CPU/16 GiB/1–2 h plus 1,000 donor bootstrap replicates; these are unmeasured estimates, not benchmarked. CPU is appropriate for this small sparse dataset; no GPU is required. Readiness only checks packaging, imports, and input headers, not study completion.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive evidence requires a measurable total donor-level contrast, reproducibly different proportions of stable shared states, and a smaller common-state-standardized within-state component with uncertainty reported, not driven by one donor or observed run/lane structure. Report continuous estimates and uncertainty; do not create a post hoc numerical cutoff. This would prioritize orthogonal validation of captured-state composition, not establish tissue-wide abundance or causality.

Adverse evidence is a precise within-state contrast not attenuated by standardization together with similar state fractions; it weakens composition dominance and supports prioritizing independent state-regulation/perturbation work. Inconclusive evidence includes wide donor uncertainty, unstable or non-shared states, influential single donors, label/alignment failures, or group/run aliasing. Imprecision is not equivalence and is not refutation.

The automatic assessment can check source joins, donor flow, matrix alignment, preprocessing, held-out fit structure, decomposition calculations, uncertainty, sensitivity, and consistency of conclusions with outputs. It must reject correct numbers paired with claims of cell transition, mechanism, treatment effect, causality, or clinical choice. Clinical label validity, drug exposure, severity, biopsy context, processing confounding, and inferred-state biological identity need clinical/expert review. Longitudinal samples are needed for persistence/transition; spatial or unsorted tissue for tissue-wide composition; perturbation and functional assays for mechanism; and prospective external outcomes for treatment utility. These are outside this computational task.

## Key references

[K1] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” *Nature Medicine* (2020). DOI: 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Inspected abstract/limited article context reports remission-associated programs and subset frequency differences; likely overlaps this cohort, constraining novelty and not serving as independent replication. Full methods/supplements were not inspected. Public source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-020-0939-8

[K2] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, Zhang F, Zhang F, Wei K, Rao DA, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” *Science Translational Medicine* (2019). DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract only; reports an inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast rival. Full-text acquisition was unavailable. Public source: https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC6726376

[K3] Richard JB, Hoyle A, Bower M, Wu S, Worthington L, Davidson S, et al. “Synovial matrix turnover controls immune cell spatial patterning in inflammation resolution.” *Molecular Systems Biology* (2025). DOI: 10.1038/s44320-025-00149-7. Abstract only; bounds interpretation because this macrophage-only design lacks spatial/stromal evidence. Public source: https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12583461

## Output and verifier contract

Write `/workspace/results.json` and `/workspace/report.md`. JSON must include `cohort`, `qc`, `baseline`, `decomposition`, `uncertainty`, `sensitivity`, `interpretation`, and `limitations`. `cohort.remission_donors` and `cohort.resistant_donors` must list the exact eligible donor IDs above once each; `cohort.remission_sample_ids` and `cohort.resistant_sample_ids` must list their exact matching matrix sample IDs once each. `qc.sample_design_join_verified` must be true and `qc.biological_unit` must be `donor`. `baseline.computed` must be true; `baseline.total_contrast` must include a numeric `estimate` and finite two-number `interval`.

When the decomposition is computable, set `decomposition.computed=true`, `state_stability=stable`, `assessment` to `composition_supported` or `within_state_supported` only when the corresponding pattern and uncertainty above are supported, and provide numeric estimates and finite intervals for `proportion_component`, `within_state_component`, and `standardized_contrast`. Otherwise use `computed=false`, `assessment=unresolved`, and a specific `stop_reason`; unresolved maps to `interpretation.status=inconclusive`. The other status mappings are `composition_supported` → `supportive` and `within_state_supported` → `adverse`. These labels summarize the reported evidence, not causal truth.

`interpretation.justification` must identify computed evidence; `evidence_fields` must list existing dotted JSON paths used for the conclusion. Use only scoped claims in `interpretation.claims`: `cross_sectional_association`, `captured_macrophage_compartment`, `composition_validation_priority`, `within_state_perturbation_priority`, and/or `inconclusive_due_to_prerequisite_or_uncertainty`. Provide nonempty `uncertainty`, `sensitivity`, and `limitations`. The report must map every conclusion to named output fields/tables and state that the finding is cross-sectional, does not establish causality, and requires expert review for clinical interpretation. The verifier checks cohort/structure, numerical fields, status consistency, conclusion links, and prohibited structured claims. It cannot validate biological identity, clinical labels, causal validity, or clinical utility. Do not submit canned values, citations-only prose, or a hypothesis-confirming conclusion unsupported by computed outputs.

# Do remission-associated macrophage averages reflect captured state representation?

## Question, hypothesis, and deliverable

**Question:** Among rheumatoid-arthritis synovial membrane macrophages sampled once in E-MTAB-8322, does the observed remission-versus-treatment-resistant average-expression contrast have a robust, estimable component attributable to differences in captured macrophage expression-state proportions, or is within-state expression change at least as large?

**Falsifiable hypothesis (untested):** Conditional on the prespecified technical-overlap and state-support gates, more than half of the squared multigene remission/resistant macrophage-expression distance is attributable to state-proportion differences rather than state-conditional expression differences, and that attribution is stable to donor resampling and leave-one-donor-out state fitting. The 50% threshold defines “dominant” before analysis. Composition and within-state regulation may coexist. “State” means a reproducible expression cluster inferred in this assay, not a stable lineage, transition, or mechanism.

**Deliverable:** newly fitted train-only, leave-one-donor-out (LODO) expression-state maps and held-out assignments; per-donor state proportions and conditional expression vectors; a signed two-factor Shapley decomposition and donor-level uncertainty/influence outputs; plus an equal-donor pseudobulk baseline on the same response-blind gene universe. No screening has been executed and no result is claimed.

**Clinical importance:** An average synovial signature alone can motivate the wrong next experiment. Robust composition dominance would motivate a follow-up measuring recruitment/retention and tissue localization; within-state dominance would motivate targeted cell perturbation or functional testing; an unstable/unidentifiable decomposition means obtain clinical, spatial, or technical evidence before choosing either direction. No result alone selects or changes a patient’s treatment.

## Evidence boundary and competing explanations

The strongest evidence-supported claim remains limited to the inspected abstract-level literature: synovial macrophage heterogeneity and remission-associated macrophage observations [K1], HBEGF+ macrophage–fibroblast invasiveness as a plausible within-state/tissue-crosstalk alternative [K2], and a spatial LYVE1+ macrophage network associated with treatment response in another spatial/longitudinal study [K3]. These works establish plausibility and boundaries, not the decomposition tested here. All three attached works remain abstract-only; no full text or supplementary methods are claimed. This source cohort may overlap the closest remission literature [K1], so novelty of the cohort biology or an unreported result is not asserted.

The unresolved claim is whether the mean expression contrast in these specific 13 donors is quantitatively composition-dominant by the prespecified signed decomposition, conditional on the assay-level gates. The strongest biological rival is within-state transcriptional regulation. A more fundamental rival is response-linked disease severity, therapy/history, biopsy selection, cell recovery/capture, or sequencing/library structure. These can affect both cell-state proportions and expression. The prepared `treatment` annotation is empty/null and disease-activity scores and longitudinal clinical records are unavailable. Spatial niches are unmeasured. Stable adjusted association would not establish causality, recruitment, a transition, mechanism, or treatment effect. A clinician must adjudicate response-label meaning and biopsy/therapy timing before stronger clinical interpretation.

## Population, time, and exact sources

Snapshot: `core-molecular-20261003`. Keep all sources read-only. Population: the 13 RA synovial membrane macrophage donors reconciled in the parent from sample design and SDRF: remission (n=7: SA132, SA159, SA160, SA161, SA168, SA174, SA225) and treatment-resistant (n=6: SA144, SA145, SA151, SA166, SA222, SA227). Exclude healthy, untreated/naive RA, undifferentiated arthritis and SA149/SA149P related-or-repeated identity records. One donor is the independent unit; cells and sequencing runs are nested. One biopsy/assay time point per donor; no longitudinal response window or follow-up is inferred.

**Primary state-analysis files:** for each of those 13 donor prefixes, read exactly `private/data/E-MTAB-8322/{prefix}.matrix.mtx`, `private/data/E-MTAB-8322/{prefix}.genes.tsv`, and `private/data/E-MTAB-8322/{prefix}.barcodes.tsv` from the configured `core-molecular-20261003` snapshot. Matrix is feature-by-cell; matrix row order binds to that donor’s `genes.tsv`, column order to that donor’s `barcodes.tsv`. Keep donor-specific identity namespaces separate; no cross-dataset joins.

**Sample and technical reconciliation:** `private/data/prepared/E-MTAB-8322.design.json` (SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`), 27 sample records with `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, `cells`; join matrix columns to `sample_id` exactly. `private/data/E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt`: join `Source Name` to design `source_name`; use only its available donor/run/library/assay/platform/processing fields for technical-overlap reporting. Do not use assay run rows as donor replicates. The assay registry and catalog (`datasets/disease_mechanisms/README.md`, `datasets/disease_mechanisms/metadata.json`) define allowed source bindings; the prepared profile is `private/data/prepared/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz` (feature-by-sample, row ID `feature`, sample columns; registry reports 33,694 features and 27 samples; SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`) and is used only for lineage/count-scale reconciliation, never as an alternate selectable primary result. `private/data/E-MTAB-8322.idf.txt` is experiment-level date metadata only, not donor follow-up. Verify the listed frozen hashes before use; report hash/shape mismatch and stop rather than substitute.

## Locked feature universe and transformations

1. Verify each donor’s feature identifiers are unique, stable and consistent; take the intersection across all 13 `genes.tsv` files. Preserve identifier strings; do not silently map aliases. Apply one response-blind detection filter on raw counts: retain a feature if count is at least 1 in at least 10% of cells in at least 3 of the 13 donors. This uses all donors without response labels, before group summaries or state fits. Freeze and report the exact IDs, retained count, and donor/cell detection summaries. A failed identifier/count-scale reconciliation stops the analysis; do not substitute “detected in both groups.”
2. For each cell, divide raw counts by that cell’s total over the full measured feature set, multiply by 10,000, and `log1p`; restrict the resulting matrix to the fixed genes for state fitting and state-conditional means. The full-measured-feature library size avoids making normalization depend on the retained subset.
3. Baseline pseudobulk: sum raw counts per donor over captured macrophage cells, divide by each donor sum’s total over its full measured feature set, multiply by 10,000, then `log1p`; restrict to the same fixed genes. Compare remission and resistant group means with equal donor weights, and report the total squared Euclidean distance and donor-deletion influence. Do not treat its total distance as the composition attribution.

## LODO learned-state alternative and leakage controls

Fit 13 folds, holding out one entire donor each time. All data-adaptive feature scaling, variable-gene ranking, PCA and clustering are fit using training donors only; the held-out cells never enter these fits. Per fold, among the frozen genes rank training-cell variance after the shared log normalization (deterministic tie-break by feature ID), select the top 2,000 or all if fewer; compute training-only gene means/SDs and apply those parameters to training and held-out cells; fit centered PCA with 30 components or the available numerical rank if lower; construct a k=15 nearest-neighbor graph and Leiden clusters at resolution 0.5, seed 0. Assign each held-out cell to the nearest training-cluster centroid in the fitted PC space (Euclidean distance; deterministic tie-break by cluster ID). Record software/package versions and seeds, training sizes, cluster sizes, held-out assignment distances and unmatched/low-support assignments. Never tune these choices by response or by inspecting the primary attribution.

For cross-fold state naming only, align training-cluster centroids in the common fixed-gene transformed expression space to the reference fold’s centroids by maximum Pearson-correlation assignment using the Hungarian algorithm; perform this after each fold’s fit and held-out assignment. This post-fit naming does not alter assignment or refit a held-out donor. Retain unmatched clusters as unmatched; do not force biological labels. Report matched-cluster fraction and cross-fold centroid concordance. A fold that cannot fit, a donor with no mapped cells for a required common state, or a common mapped state with fewer than 20 held-out cells in any donor where its proportion is needed is a state-support failure: stop the primary attribution and label inconclusive. No resolution search or favorable clustering replacement is allowed.

## Technical-overlap gate

Before examining the expression contrast, tabulate the 13 donors by response for every available categorical donor/run/library/assay/platform/processing field in SDRF and design, and report age and captured-cell yield distributions and sex. Collapse run-level values to donor-level sets; a donor with multiple values retains all observed values, but is still one donor. For each categorical field, “perfect separation” is present exactly when no observed category is represented by at least one donor in each response group (ignore missing as a category; separately report missingness). Perfect separation on any such field is a technical stop: no biological attribution; report the result as inconclusive. Otherwise the limited categorical gate passes, but is not evidence of balance. Flag sparse overlap if fewer than two donors per group share any category. For age, report observed ranges and range intersection; for yield report donor values, without inferential cell-level tests or an unsupported adjustment. Missing age/sex, therapy history and disease activity do not count as successful clinical confounding control. Clinician review of status labels and timing remains necessary.

## Estimand: explicit signed two-factor Shapley decomposition

Let R denote remission and S treatment-resistant. For donor i, `p_ik` is the fraction of its captured, mapped cells assigned to aligned state k; `m_ik` is its mean transformed expression vector over cells assigned to k and fixed genes. First average donors equally within each group to obtain `p_gk` and `m_gk`; do not weight donors by cell number. Use the common aligned state set; failed support is not silently dropped. Let `mu(p,m)=sum_k p_k*m_k` and `F(p,m)=||mu(p,m)||_2^2` on the fixed gene universe. Compute all four counterfactuals:

- `F_RR = F(p_R,m_R)` (remission proportions, remission conditional means).
- `F_SS = F(p_S,m_S)` (resistant proportions, resistant conditional means).
- `F_RS = F(p_R,m_S)` (remission proportions, resistant conditional means).
- `F_SR = F(p_S,m_R)` (resistant proportions, remission conditional means).

Total observed squared distance `D = F_RR + F_SS - 2*F_RS` is not the valid distance formula for a generic counterfactual; therefore instead define the contrast function `Q(p,m)=||mu(p,m)-mu(p_S,m_S)||_2^2` for all counterfactuals, where the resistant profile is the fixed origin. Denote `q_RR=Q(p_R,m_R)`, `q_SR=Q(p_S,m_R)`, `q_RS=Q(p_R,m_S)`, and `q_SS=Q(p_S,m_S)=0`. This gives total `T=q_RR=||mu_R-mu_S||²`, the exact observed squared distance. Signed composition Shapley is `C=0.5*((q_RR-q_SR)+(q_RS-q_SS))`; signed within-state Shapley is `W=0.5*((q_RR-q_RS)+(q_SR-q_SS))`. Thus `C+W=T` algebraically. The primary scalar is `C/T`, without clipping; cancellation can yield values below 0 or above 1, so never describe it as an ordinary percent explained in those cases. Report C, W, T and each q, and verify `|C+W-T| <= 1e-10*max(1,|T|)`; failure is a computation error. If `T <= 1e-12` on this transformed scale, ratio is undefined and classification inconclusive; still report component outputs. These equations use both factor-swap orders and a fixed resistant-origin squared-distance game; they preserve signed attribution, not an assumption that both components are nonnegative.

## Uncertainty, influence, and decision rules

Use 10,000 deterministic group-stratified donor bootstrap draws (resample 7 remission and 6 resistant donors with replacement; seed 8322). For computationally bounded, transparent uncertainty, the primary bootstrap resamples donor-level cross-fitted `(p_i,m_i)` summaries and recomputes equal-donor group means, all four q values, C, W, T and C/T. This is conditional on the 13 fitted cross-fold maps; it is not 10,000 nested refits and must be labeled “donor-resampling uncertainty conditional on fitted state maps.” Estimate state-fit uncertainty separately, not folded into that interval: report the 13 LODO fold fits, assignment/matching/support diagnostics, and the full-data point estimate alongside 13 delete-one-donor influence analyses. Each deletion recomputes group donor means/decomposition after removing that donor’s held-out summary; additionally show each donor’s held-out assignment and fold diagnostics. A full refit bootstrap is not silently claimed or required by this bounded plan. The exact estimand remains the cross-fitted 13-donor decomposition; conditional intervals quantify donor sampling variation given those fitted maps, while mapping variability is assessed by the prespecified LODO stability/influence gates and is a limitation of the interval.

Report percentile 95% intervals for T,C,W,C/T and bootstrap state-support failure fraction; report the 13 donor-deletion point estimates and gate status. Also report exact two-sided donor-label permutation results for the baseline total squared distance over all 1,716 assignments of 7 of 13 donors to remission; this is secondary descriptive evidence, not a causal test or test of the Shapley threshold.

- **Supportive for composition dominance:** technical gate has no perfect categorical separation; all state fit, common-state support and matching gates pass; T exceeds `1e-12`; conditional-bootstrap 95% interval lower endpoint of C/T is strictly above 0.50; and no donor deletion changes the point estimate to `<=0.50`.
- **Adverse to composition dominance in this cohort:** the same validity gates pass; T exceeds the floor; interval upper endpoint is strictly below 0.50; and no deletion changes the point estimate to `>=0.50`. This weakens the specific composition-dominance hypothesis, not all composition contribution.
- **Inconclusive:** interval includes 0.50; T is at/below floor; any technical/state/common-support/matching gate fails; any required fit fails; a bootstrap draw fails support; or any donor deletion crosses 0.50. A wide interval is not evidence of equality. If categorical fields show sparse but non-perfect overlap, mark result “inconclusive—technical overlap weak” even if interval threshold otherwise clears. No subgroup rescue or post hoc threshold change.

## Methods compared and compute limits

**Simple baseline:** equal-donor log-CP10k pseudobulk group profiles on the fixed gene universe; donor-level deletion and exact label permutation. It answers whether an average contrast exists and how donor-sensitive it is, but cannot partition state representation from conditional expression.

**Substantive alternative:** train-only LODO expression-state fitting and held-out centroid assignment on the same donors, features and normalization, then the signed Shapley decomposition. It can reveal whether the aggregate contrast is carried primarily by captured expression-state proportions or by expression conditional on state, information the baseline necessarily discards. It remains descriptive and vulnerable to response-linked technical capture and state instability. Both approaches are retained.

**Resources:** CPU only is currently appropriate for 13 sparse donor matrices and modest PCA/clustering; no GPU evidence or need. Estimated solver envelope from the audit is 2–4 CPU, 8–16 GiB, and up to 7,200 s. These are planning estimates, not measured. The 13-fit LODO core and 10,000 donor-summary bootstrap algebra are unbenchmarked in this branch; request 4 CPU, 16 GiB, 7,200 s, write per-fold/checkpoint outputs, and record wall time/peak memory. This is not a claim that nested 10,000x13 refits fit; that workload is explicitly not the chosen bootstrap because it is unverified and needlessly conflates donor sampling with repeated map refitting. If the summary-bootstrap or LODO core cannot complete in the configured envelope, stop with partial checkpoint and report unresolved feasibility to Lead—do not reduce donors, feature threshold, bootstrap draws, estimand, or claim without Lead review. The conditional interval’s limitation is explicit; if future evidence requires full refit uncertainty, benchmark/authorize that separately.

## Interpretation and next decision

Supportive output prioritizes spatial/recruitment-retention measurement in an independently collected, clinically adjudicated study; it does not establish recruitment. Adverse output redirects the next experiment toward within-state regulation/function, without proving it. Inconclusive output defers biological prioritization and identifies whether technical overlap, mapping stability, denominator, donor leverage or interval width blocks interpretation. Clinical response validity, therapy/severity/biopsy confounding, actual tissue abundance versus capture, spatial localization, lineage/transition, mechanism and treatment benefit require adjudication or a separate spatial/prospective/perturbation study. A verifier can check source accounting, no held-out leakage, equations, bootstrap implementation, gate application, output uncertainty and whether prose matches computed values; it cannot adjudicate those clinical/biological claims.

## Key references

[K1] Existing inspected abstract-level synovial macrophage/remission work: supports biological context only; source-cohort overlap may limit novelty. This proposal tests a quantitative, prespecified decomposition in the 13 bound donors and does not claim independent replication.

[K2] Existing inspected abstract-level HBEGF+ macrophage–fibroblast work: bounds an equally plausible within-state/tissue-crosstalk explanation; the current macrophage-only dataset cannot resolve the fibroblast interaction.

[K3] Existing inspected abstract-level spatial LYVE1+ macrophage/treatment-response work: bounds interpretation by showing spatial/longitudinal evidence not available here; it does not adjudicate this cross-sectional decomposition.

The three distinct frozen references and receipts are inherited unchanged from the valid parent candidate; key-reference claims remain mapped as above. They are abstract-only, not full-text inspections.
