# Episode 18 — posterior-thigh MFI, falls recall timing, and measured response selection

## Scientific question and clinical importance

Among UK Biobank participants with visit-2 MRI and observed posterior-thigh muscle fat infiltration (MFI), is higher bilateral posterior-thigh MFI associated with a classifiable visit-3 report of any fall in the preceding year, after the same measured baseline adjustment as the valid parent? Does that respondent-conditional association remain materially similar when the visit-3 recall window is nominally separated from visit-2 MRI by a ≥730-day visit gap, rather than the primary ≥366-day gap? Separately, among participants with visit-2 MRI/MFI and complete baseline covariates, how sensitive is the observed complete-case association to measured selection into a timely return and classifiable response under a missing-at-random (MAR) response model?

Falls matter because they can cause injury, fracture, disability, and loss of independence. A stable, precise positive association would justify independent prospective study with dated/adjudicated falls; a precise adverse result would lower the priority of posterior-thigh MFI as a falls-risk phenotype. This analysis does not produce a screening tool, treatment effect, causal effect, or estimate of true fall-event risk.

## Evidence supported versus tested

Three inspected works delimit what is known. The UK Biobank analysis reports broad associations of thigh MFI with mortality and disease, but its abstract does not establish falls [K1]. The closest MRI-thigh overlap associates posterior/anterior muscle-volume ratio with falls, but measures volume distribution rather than MFI and does not resolve the recall timing here [K2]. Roe et al. summarize cross-sectional and longitudinal population evidence of age-related myosteatosis, while noting few studies in diverse populations and unresolved contributions of disease and disuse [K3]. This review bounds the age-versus-disease/disuse interpretation; it does not establish either explanation for this cohort. The closest overlap means novelty is not claimed for “thigh MRI and falls” generally. The substantive advance is a bounded MFI-specific, two-timepoint association with an explicitly tested recall-window boundary and a distinct measured-response-selection sensitivity.

**Hypothesis under test:** within the fixed ≥366-day respondent-conditional cohort, one SD higher visit-2 mean bilateral posterior-thigh MFI has a positive adjusted association with a classifiable visit-3 report of any fall; in the nested ≥730-day cohort, the association remains directionally and materially compatible after the longer separation of the nominal recall window from MRI.

**Strongest rival explanation:** MFI marks pre-existing frailty, illness, inactivity/disuse, prior falls, or body composition, while differential visit attendance, response, and recall/reporting shape the observed association. The ≥730-day restriction may weaken recall-window overlap, but it also selects a different set of returners and cannot distinguish timing effects from cohort composition, survivor/participation selection, or other differences in elapsed time. Measured-response weighting tests only measured selection under MAR among MRI/MFI-observed participants. Adjustment or weighting cannot identify a mechanism or remove unmeasured confounding, selection on MRI attendance, MNAR response, differential recall, or outcome misclassification.

## Data binding and source checks

Snapshot: `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`. Unit/key: one participant `eid`, namespace `ukb672073`; no cross-namespace linkage.

Primary source is read-only ordinary CSV `UKB/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, source ID `ukb_d61ec821b81b9034`, exact source path `[private-path]/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, SHA-256 `77cad853153b1fdc9b6b9c83b6fff19691681cdee3b0822210bc5c875e1db94c`, schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-fb278a0d71d3a688.json`. It is an ordinary delimited file; no archive member applies. Exact relevant columns, present in the source schema: `eid`; visit date fields `53-2.0`, `53-3.0`; posterior MFI fields `23355-2.0`, `23356-2.0`; visit-2 falls `2296-2.0`, visit-3 falls `2296-3.0`; visceral adipose tissue (VAT) `22407-2.0`; thigh fat-free volume fields `22403-2.0`–`22406-2.0`; body fat `23099-2.0`; BMI `21001-2.0`; age `21003-2.0`; smoking `20116-2.0`; activity `884-2.0`; walking pace `924-2.0`; and grip `46-2.0`, `47-2.0`. Dictionary metadata labels field 2296 “Falls in the last year” and states the touchscreen wording, “In the last year have you had any falls?” (metadata `Path`=Assessment centre > Touchscreen > Health and medical history > General health; field ID 2296; coding 100539; four instances). Thus, visit date is the survey/report date; no date of each fall is present in this field.

Sex `31-0.0` is joined only from read-only ordinary CSV `UKB/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, source ID `ukb_ce68812c3a782e09`, exact source path `[private-path]/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, SHA-256 `cd2e004a78b20a8606d70ab2cb3b32de82c44264383a34960b0cd29bc2963f0e`, schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-0f3b3a4749849a80.json`, on unique same-namespace `eid`. ### Temporal cohorts and outcome

Use the same eligibility and fixed covariate-complete/respondent definition for all matched estimates. Parse `53-2.0` and `53-3.0` as ISO-safe calendar dates (no `dayfirst=True`); report absent/invalid/malformed dates, duplicate `eid`, impossible order, and each exclusion count. The targeted nested sensitivity is the subset of those same eligible individuals with a gap ≥730 days. Define nominal recall start for interpretation as `visit3_date − 365 days`; this is an arithmetic representation of “last year,” not a known exact recall interval. At a 366-day gap that nominal interval begins about one day after the visit-2 date; at a 730-day gap it begins about 365 days afterward. Calendar-year phrasing and recall behavior may differ; no record supplies individual fall dates.

Exposure is the mean of `23355-2.0` and `23356-2.0`, standardized by one SD using the fixed ≥366 primary analysis cohort once and held on that scale in the ≥730 subset and all model comparisons. Audit observed units/range, impossible/special values, left/right agreement, and any source-exposed quality-control fields before interpreting MFI; no numeric range/QC threshold is inferred from the label alone. Outcome is `2296-3.0`. Preserve original values and frequencies. The inherited parent classification is code 1=no falls and codes 2/3=any falls; the inspected UKB field page confirms the question and data-coding ID, while available attached coding evidence specifically verifies -3 as “Prefer not to answer” and does not display every label. Before outcome fitting, verify the complete code table for codes 1/2/3 and any other encountered values. Fail closed if this verification is unavailable: do not misclassify unknown codes; report them separately and do not fit the primary binary outcome until resolved. Exclude refusal/unclassifiable responses from the respondent estimand and report them separately. No report is clinically adjudicated.

Preserve the parent’s prespecified adjustment set and data construction: baseline falls (`2296-2.0`), age (`21003-2.0`), sex (`31-0.0`), BMI (`21001-2.0`), smoking (`20116-2.0`), physical activity (`884-2.0`), walking pace (`924-2.0`), grip (`46-2.0`, `47-2.0`), VAT (`22407-2.0`), body fat (`23099-2.0`), and a nonredundant thigh muscle-distribution measure derived from `22403-2.0`–`22406-2.0`. Verify metadata labels, units, visit-2 measurement and categorical special codes, then specify the mapping before estimation. The matched logistic and shrinkage-GAM use identical people, exposure scale, outcome and covariates; no model-specific complete-case deletion is allowed. Do not condition the target on post-exposure variables.

## Estimands and computation

### Primary ≥366-day respondent association

Estimate adjusted association—not a causal risk—using a multivariable logistic regression of binary any-falls report (`2296-3.0`, 2/3 vs 1) on standardized bilateral posterior MFI and the fixed covariates. Report the MFI log-odds coefficient, odds ratio per SD with 95% CI, model-based and participant-bootstrap uncertainty, covariate and event counts, calibration/descriptive predicted probabilities, and standardized risk contrast between MFI −0.5 SD and +0.5 SD (average over observed cohort covariates). Do not call prediction performance clinical utility. Keep this primary estimand and cohort frozen.

### Nested ≥730-day recall-window sensitivity

Re-fit the exact primary logistic model, with unchanged coding, scaling, covariate formula, and interpretation, in the nested subset with visit gap ≥730 days. Report its event/non-event support and 95% uncertainty. Show the primary estimate both in all ≥366-day eligibles and restricted to the ≥730-day subset (the restricted estimate is the actual boundary sensitivity); tabulate the two nested cohorts’ composition and row flow. A materially different restricted estimate is compatible with a recall-window/timing explanation, but cannot establish it: longer-gap participation, survival, response, disease progression and measured/unmeasured composition also change. A similar estimate weakens concern that the minimum 366-day rule alone drives the association but cannot prove that reported falls occurred after MRI or eliminate recall error. Do not compare the two point estimates as an independent randomized exposure to lag.

**Support/precision gate:** before interpreting this sensitivity, require both outcome classes to have at least 10 observations per effective model degree of freedom, no separation/non-convergence, and sufficient covariate overlap; for the response-weighted analogue require effective sample size (ESS) ≥50% of the unweighted classifiable-returner count and no material weight positivity failure. For interpretive precision, predeclare OR=1.20 per SD only as an operational “potentially consequential association” benchmark (not an established clinical threshold): call the ≥730 result decision-informative only if its 95% CI can distinguish OR=1 from OR=1.20 in the relevant direction. If support fails or the interval spans both, report estimate/CI as inconclusive and do not infer absence or persistence. Keep the threshold and all gate outcomes visible; do not change subgroup/cut point after looking at results.

### Measured-response-selection sensitivity (parent estimand retained)

Target population for response weighting is **only participants with visit-2 MRI and observed MFI, complete prespecified baseline covariates, and valid baseline timing data**. Define `R=1` for this frame when the individual has an eligible visit-3 return ≥366 days after visit 2 and a classifiable response; all other people in this already-MRI-observed frame are `R=0` for return/classifiable-response selection. Fit a prespecified, cross-fitted response model `P(R=1|X)` using exposure and the same baseline covariates, with folds assigned by `eid`; assess calibration and overlap, then compute stabilized inverse-probability-of-response weights among `R=1`. Predefine truncation at the 1st/99th percentile and show untruncated plus truncated results; report probability distribution, extreme weights, truncation fraction, weighted/unweighted covariate balance, ESS, and bootstrap uncertainty. Use weights to estimate the MAR-standardized MFI/falls association in the MRI/MFI-observed complete-covariate frame, not among all UKB participants.

Repeat response-selection diagnostics and weighted estimate within the ≥730-day restriction only if its event and weight-support gates pass. State that this extra contrast remains a sensitivity analysis in selected MRI attendees, with changing returner composition; it is not a correction for MRI nonattendance, MNAR response, undocumented recall behavior, or latent confounding. Report unweighted and weighted ORs, standardized risk contrasts, their CIs, absolute and relative shifts, and support/positivity diagnostics. A weighted shift is evidence of sensitivity to measured response patterns conditional on MAR/model specification, not proof selection caused the association. Lack of shift is not proof absence of selection bias.

### Logistic baseline versus shrinkage-GAM alternative

Both are fitted on the exact same fixed ≥366-day respondent cohort, then repeated in the ≥730 subset only when its support gate passes. Baseline: the above adjusted logistic model with linear MFI term and linear continuous covariate terms (categoricals as prespecified factors). Alternative: a penalized shrinkage-GAM logistic model on the identical target, with a shrinkage smooth for standardized MFI and penalized smooths for age, grip and VAT; any MFI-by-grip smooth interaction must be prespecified, penalized toward zero, and counted in the support gate. It targets a scientifically relevant uncertainty lost by the baseline’s linear MFI log-odds restriction: a threshold/plateau or effect heterogeneity across measured functional capacity, consistent with either biological gradients or nonlinear measurement/selection patterns. It does not identify muscle mechanism or causal effect. Compare penalized and linear fits via held-out participant folds nested within the fixed cohort, log loss and calibration as supportive diagnostics only; primary comparison is curve shape and marginal standardized risk contrasts with bootstrap bands. Report concur/smooth departures, uncertainty and effective degrees of freedom; shrinkage toward linear/null is not evidence of no nonlinear physiology if support is weak. No tuning on the ≥730 outcome followed by redefining the cohort or endpoint.

## Readiness and falsification criteria

Before fitting any outcome model, the solver must: (1) resolve raw CSV delimiter/encoding and verify row counts, unique `eid` and selected column names against the frozen table schema; (2) verify the separate population-characteristics file has unique `eid`, `31-0.0`, and acceptable match/duplicate rates within the same `ukb672073` namespace; (3) audit raw and special codes, full Data-Coding 100539 labels for all values used, exact date parsing, and measurement units/ranges; (4) report duplicate rows, exclusions by reason, eligible counts/events/non-events for ≥366 and nested ≥730; (5) report baseline covariate completeness, MRI/MFI observed denominator, response indicator counts, and missingness; (6) verify nonredundant muscle distribution parameterization, no algebraic redundancy, and no source field is silently dropped; (7) test response-model convergence, calibration, overlap, positivity, ESS, weight truncation and balance; and (8) write only derived outputs to workspace. No data or clinical notes may enter public search.

The positive hypothesis is not supported if the primary adjusted association is precise and adverse (95% CI excludes OR=1 in the inverse direction), or if a reasonably precise primary estimate is null and excludes the operational OR=1.20 benchmark. A primary association that is positive but loses direction/magnitude under the ≥730 restriction with adequate support would falsify robustness to the stricter temporal boundary, not prove temporal bias. A materially shifted response-weighted estimate with adequate overlap would show sensitivity to measured selection assumptions and qualify the primary complete-case finding. A non-significant estimate with wide intervals, low events, separation, unstable weights or failed support gate is inconclusive, not negative evidence. Results may support, weaken or leave undecided the prespecified association; they cannot establish causal effects, biological mechanism, true event dates, event validity, or population-wide screening value.

## Interpretation and claims requiring future evidence

Supportive results: a positive, reasonably precise ≥366 estimate, compatible ≥730 restricted estimate, and no material well-supported measured-MAR weighting shift would support a temporally bounded, respondent-conditional association robust to these two measured sensitivities. Next step is independent replication using prospectively dated/adjudicated falls and explicit follow-up ascertainment.

Adverse results: a precise inverse/null result or an adequately supported ≥730 incompatibility with the primary estimate would lower confidence in the association or its recall-boundary robustness. It does not prove MFI is unrelated to actual falls; misclassification, power, selection and construct differences remain.

Inconclusive results: wide intervals, sparse events or failed overlap/weight gates do not refute the hypothesis. Continue only if an independent data source can improve event timing, adjudication or response support; otherwise defer rather than add exploratory subgroups.

Unavailable/essential evidence: exact participant fall dates, falls severity/context and clinical adjudication; MRI attendance/quality beyond available records; validated MFI measurement range/QC thresholds if absent; complete category codebook if not available at execution; and evidence on MNAR/nonresponse. Stronger causal or mechanism claims require a separate longitudinal design with repeated exposures, event-dated outcomes and confounding control, ideally independent replication and expert adjudication. No automated verifier can certify these clinical claims; only computation, estimands, consistency of reports with outputs, and uncertainty calculations are computationally checkable.

## Method and compute choice; alternatives deferred

The actual scientific deliverable is newly estimated matched linear-logistic and shrinkage-GAM outcome contrasts, the nested ≥730 boundary estimates and uncertainty, and unweighted/weighted MAR response estimates with complete support diagnostics. No association, cohort count, outcome fit, or feasibility result is claimed in this draft.

**Selected matched alternatives:** logistic baseline uses the fixed response cohort; shrinkage-GAM uses exactly the same records and target. Model fitting target is binary visit-3 falls report; validation folds are participant-level, nested/held-out within the primary fixed cohort, while bootstrap uncertainty resamples participants. Evaluate uncertainty with CIs/bootstrap bands, support, calibration and event counts, not a small predictive-score gain alone. A CPU envelope of 4 vCPUs, 16 GiB RAM, and up to 2 hours for data preparation, cross-fitting, bootstrap and model fits is proposed (estimate, not measured); no GPU is needed for this moderate tabular model. The 730-day subgroup is estimated only as prespecified sensitivity, not tuned as a discovery subgroup.

**Not chosen / revisit criteria:**
- Delphi sequence adaptation: not chosen because current scope is dated single-exposure MRI with one later recall item; longitudinal disease-history tokens are not needed to distinguish the visit-2/visit-3 recall-window rival. Revisit only if a defined decision-relevant question uses sufficient dated disease trajectories and a held-out comparator.
- Oncoformer lab/image adaptation: not chosen because the endpoint is falls self-report and this question gains no relevant information from chest imaging/labs. Revisit only if relevant modalities and a competing measurable clinical question become available.
- ALADYNOULLI: not chosen because latent disease-course inference cannot resolve visit-2 exposure versus visit-3 one-year recall timing or the MRI-attendee measured-response target better than the bounded estimands above. Revisit only if repeated disease-state observations enable a separate, decision-relevant latent trajectory question.
- More complex causal, deep learning, genetic, proteomic, or multimodal alternatives: deferred; the source bindings either do not measure the timing/clinical adjudication uncertainty or add no discriminating information for this question. No unavailability of all four configured datasets is implied: only the bound UKB tables are needed here.
- A strict ≥730-day-only primary or standalone >1-year lag direction was considered and not selected because it would replace the valid parent estimand and further reduce/alter the cohort; retained only as nested, support-gated sensitivity.

## Key works

[K1] Zhang Y et al. “Integrative Analysis Uncover the Effects and Multi-Omics Features of Thigh Muscle Fat Infiltration.” Aging Cell (2026). Abstract inspected only. It supports broad UKB MFI/disease relevance, not falls or the temporal estimand here.

[K2] Kim HS et al. “Neck-to-knee dixon MRI thigh volume as a superior mass biomarker for Sarcopenia: evidence from the UK biobank.” npj Digital Medicine (2026). Publisher HTML text extraction inspected for abstract and results/discussion passages. Closest thigh-MRI/falls prior; exposure is volume distribution, not MFI.

[K3] Roe LS, Zmuda JM, Miljkovic I. “Myosteatosis: an emerging biomarker of aging.” Frontiers in Aging (2026). Retrieved full-text HTML excerpt inspected for the Discussion on longitudinal population evidence and age versus disease/disuse. It supports longitudinal age-related myosteatosis but highlights unresolved disease/disuse contributions; it does not test this study’s falls, response-selection, or timing questions.

## Reference evidence package

The exact parent key-reference receipts and source snapshots are attached unchanged for K1–K3; the separate UK Biobank 2296 coding excerpt is also attached unchanged. Receipt timestamps are retrieval times and precede this repair. No fit, outcome, cohort count, or scientific result is claimed.

# Task: Posterior-thigh MFI and later falls reports

## Objective and claim boundaries

Complete the frozen Episode 18 investigation in this task. Do not change its population, timing, estimands, outcomes, covariates, model comparison, nested sensitivity, response-selection target, support gates, or falsification criteria. The study is an observational, respondent-conditional association analysis—not a causal-effect estimate, mechanism test, validated risk score, or estimate of true fall-event risk.

Among UK Biobank participants with visit-2 body MRI and observed bilateral posterior-thigh muscle fat infiltration (MFI), estimate the adjusted association between one-SD higher MFI and a classifiable visit-3 report of any fall in the preceding year, when visit 3 is at least 366 days after visit 2. Test the prespecified nested >=730-day timing sensitivity and measured-response MAR sensitivity among MRI/MFI-observed participants with complete baseline covariates. The question matters because falls can cause injury, fracture, disability, and loss of independence; a robust association would justify an independent study using dated/adjudicated falls, while a precise adverse result could deprioritize this phenotype. A positive finding would not by itself change clinical screening or treatment.

### Evidence and hypothesis

Existing evidence supports broad UK Biobank thigh-MFI associations with mortality and disease, but the inspected abstract does not establish falls [K1]. A close UK Biobank overlap reports cross-sectional associations between posterior/anterior thigh-volume ratio and falls, but it studies volume distribution rather than MFI and does not establish temporal ordering [K2]. The inspected myosteatosis review summarizes age-related evidence while leaving contributions of disease and disuse unresolved [K3]. The substantive advance is a bounded MFI-specific, two-timepoint report association, with explicit nominal-recall-window and measured-response sensitivities—not a claim of novelty for thigh MRI and falls generally.

**Hypothesis under test:** within the fixed >=366-day eligible respondent cohort, one SD higher visit-2 mean bilateral posterior-thigh MFI has a positive adjusted association with a classifiable visit-3 report of any fall; within the nested >=730-day cohort, that association remains directionally and materially compatible.

**Strongest rival:** MFI marks pre-existing frailty, illness, inactivity/disuse, prior falls, or body composition; attendance, response, and recall/reporting produce or distort the observed association. The >=730-day restriction also selects a different cohort and cannot isolate elapsed-time effects. MAR weighting addresses only measured response selection in the MRI/MFI-observed, complete-covariate frame. Adjustment and weighting do not establish mechanism or remove unmeasured confounding, MRI-attendance selection, MNAR response, recall error, or outcome misclassification.

### Data and exact bindings

All source files mount read-only. Put only derived outputs, logs, sampled rows, and code in `/workspace`; never modify or copy source data into public task assets. Do not send participant data or clinical notes to public search. Retain direct access to all four configured dataset families, but this experiment uses only the following bound UKB files; do not join other datasets or identifier namespaces.

- Assessment Center participant table: `/data/ukb_d61ec821b81b9034/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, source `[private-path]/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, SHA-256 `77cad853153b1fdc9b6b9c83b6fff19691681cdee3b0822210bc5c875e1db94c`, schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-fb278a0d71d3a688.json`. Ordinary CSV; no archive member. Unit and join key: unique `eid` in namespace `ukb672073`. Required columns: `eid`, `53-2.0`, `53-3.0`, `23355-2.0`, `23356-2.0`, `2296-2.0`, `2296-3.0`, `22407-2.0`, `22403-2.0` through `22406-2.0`, `23099-2.0`, `21001-2.0`, `21003-2.0`, `20116-2.0`, `884-2.0`, `924-2.0`, `46-2.0`, and `47-2.0`.
- Population Characteristics participant table: `/data/ukb_ce68812c3a782e09/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, source `[private-path]/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, SHA-256 `cd2e004a78b20a8606d70ab2cb3b32de82c44264383a34960b0cd29bc2963f0e`, schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-0f3b3a4749849a80.json`. Ordinary CSV; join `31-0.0` by unique same-namespace `eid` only. Audit duplicate/missing keys and match rates.
- UKB dictionary: `/data/ukb_dd10bf7e2be6e7d0/metadata.csv`, source `[private-path]/metadata.csv`, SHA-256 `9189b21c052ee3715448b1715e5700b297b7377b57278ccb747b7dfc5fa558bd`. ### Population and temporal boundaries

Start from participants with visit-2 MRI and observed bilateral MFI. Define date gap as visit-3 date (`53-3.0`) minus visit-2 date (`53-2.0`). Audit malformed/absent dates, duplicates, impossible order, and exclusions. The primary eligible respondent cohort requires valid dates, gap >=366 days, observed bilateral MFI, complete prespecified baseline covariates, and a verified classifiable visit-3 falls answer. The nested timing cohort is the subset with gap >=730 days. Preserve and report participant flow and event/non-event support in both cohorts.

The field asks about falls “in the last year.” For interpretation only, represent nominal recall start as visit-3 date minus 365 days. This is arithmetic, not a known event interval; actual event dates, calendar-year interpretations, and recall behavior are unavailable. At a 366-day gap the nominal interval begins around visit 2; at 730 days it begins around a year afterward. The longer-gap cohort also differs in returner composition, survival, participation, disease progression, and measured/unmeasured characteristics.

Exposure: mean of `23355-2.0` and `23356-2.0`, standardized using the mean and SD of the fixed >=366-day primary analysis cohort. Reuse this scale unchanged for every subset and model. Audit units, observed range, special/impossible values, side agreement, and available quality-control fields; do not invent thresholds. Outcome: verified binary any-falls report from `2296-3.0`, codes 2/3 versus 1.

Prespecified visit-2 adjustment set: baseline falls `2296-2.0`; age `21003-2.0`; sex `31-0.0`; BMI `21001-2.0`; smoking `20116-2.0`; activity `884-2.0`; walking pace `924-2.0`; grip `46-2.0` and `47-2.0`; VAT `22407-2.0`; body fat `23099-2.0`; and one nonredundant thigh muscle-distribution representation derived from `22403-2.0` through `22406-2.0`. Verify metadata labels, units, instance, and category special codes first. Document and freeze the parent-compatible nonredundant muscle parameterization before fitting; do not include algebraically dependent volumes and ratios together. Both outcome models use identical participants, exposure, outcome and covariates; no model-specific complete-case deletion. Do not adjust for post-exposure variables.

### Required analyses and outputs

1. **Primary association:** multivariable logistic regression on the fixed >=366-day cohort, binary any-falls report on standardized MFI and the complete prespecified adjustment set. Report coefficient, OR per SD, 95% CI, participant-bootstrap uncertainty, counts, model convergence/separation, calibration/descriptive predicted probabilities, and average standardized risk contrast comparing MFI -0.5 SD with +0.5 SD over observed covariates. Calibration and prediction are diagnostics, not clinical utility.
2. **>=730-day boundary sensitivity:** Fit the unchanged primary logistic formula and exposure scale in the nested >=730-day cohort. Report the primary estimate for both the entire >=366-day cohort and only the >=730-day subset; the latter is the boundary comparison. Show cohort composition, flow and class support. Do not treat the cohorts as randomized lag groups. A different estimate is compatible with timing but also cohort selection/composition; a similar estimate only weakens concern about the minimum boundary and does not prove event timing.
3. **Measured-response MAR sensitivity:** target only participants with visit-2 MRI and observed MFI, complete prespecified baseline covariates, and valid baseline timing data. In this frame define R=1 as eligible >=366-day visit-3 return with classifiable response, and R=0 otherwise. Fit a prespecified cross-fitted response model `P(R=1|X)` using exposure and the same baseline covariates, with folds assigned by `eid`; assess calibration/overlap, then compute stabilized inverse-probability response weights among R=1. Predefine 1st/99th percentile truncation and report both truncated and untruncated analyses, predicted probabilities, extreme weights, truncation fraction, balance, ESS, and participant-bootstrap uncertainty. Estimate MAR-standardized association only in the MRI/MFI-observed complete-covariate frame, not all UKB. Report weighted and unweighted ORs, standardized risk contrasts, CIs, absolute/relative shifts and diagnostics. Repeat within >=730 only if support gates pass. Weight shifts indicate sensitivity to measured response assumptions, not proof selection caused the association; no shift does not prove absence of selection bias. This cannot correct MRI nonattendance, MNAR, unmeasured factors, or recall error.
4. **Scientifically substantive alternative:** matched penalized shrinkage-GAM logistic fit versus the linear logistic baseline on identical records/outcome/exposure/covariates. The GAM has shrinkage smooths for standardized MFI, age, grip and VAT. Include MFI-by-grip only if prespecified before outcome inspection and penalized toward zero. Compare curve shape, effective degrees of freedom and bootstrap bands/marginal standardized risk contrasts; participant-fold held-out log loss/calibration are supportive diagnostics only. It tests whether linear MFI log-odds loses threshold/plateau or functional-capacity heterogeneity information; it does not establish a mechanism. Apply to >=730 only if gates pass. Do not tune the scientific question on that subset.

Use the proposal's predeclared interpretation gates: both classes need at least 10 observations per effective model degree of freedom; no separation/non-convergence; adequate covariate overlap. For weighted analyses additionally require ESS >=50% of unweighted classifiable returners and no material positivity failure. OR=1.20 per SD is an operational potentially-consequential precision benchmark, not a validated clinical threshold. Call >=730 decision-informative only if its 95% CI distinguishes OR=1 from OR=1.20 in the relevant direction; if support fails or CI spans both, label inconclusive. Preserve all gates and do not change subgroups/cutoffs after results.

### Falsification and interpretation

- **Supportive:** positive, reasonably precise primary association; compatible >=730 estimate with adequate precision/support; no material, well-supported measured-MAR shift. This supports only an association robust to these measured sensitivities in selected MRI respondents. Next step: independent prospective replication with dated/adjudicated falls and explicit ascertainment.
- **Adverse:** precise inverse association, or a reasonably precise null that excludes the operational OR=1.20 benchmark, weakens the proposed association. Adequately supported incompatibility in the >=730 subset weakens robustness to the stricter boundary, not proof of timing bias. It does not establish no relationship with actual falls.
- **Inconclusive:** wide intervals, sparse events, failed support, separation, unstable weights, or failed overlap do not refute the hypothesis. Defer or seek independent data with better event timing/adjudication/response support; do not substitute exploratory subgroups.
- A material weighted shift qualifies the complete-case association as sensitive to measured selection assumptions. Null shifts do not rule out selection.

Conclusions must quote and link each claim to the corresponding computed output (table/field/file), provide uncertainty, and identify gates that passed/failed. Do not reward or require confirmation. The complete codebook and expert confirmation of field semantics, MFI QC/units if unavailable, falls event timing/severity/context, clinical adjudication, MRI attendance/quality, and MNAR evidence are missing or require review. Strong causal/mechanistic/population-screening claims require a separate design with repeated exposures, event-dated outcomes, confounding control, independent replication and expert adjudication. Automated checks can verify input/header access, computations, consistency of reported values with generated outputs, uncertainty and bounded interpretation fixtures; they cannot certify clinical validity, causal validity, novelty, or clinical adjudication.

### Required deliverable

Write `/workspace/results.json` plus a concise `/workspace/report.md`. `results.json` must contain source/schema/coding audit; actual row/participant counts and exclusions; cohort definitions and support; frozen variable/code mappings and MFI scale; all primary, nested, GAM and response-weighted estimates with uncertainty and diagnostics; and conclusion class (`supportive`, `adverse`, or `inconclusive`) with output references and limitations. If the codebook cannot be verified, include the audit and explicitly record that outcome fitting was blocked; do not fabricate estimates or label the scientific hypothesis adverse. Include analysis code, logs, sampling/filtering decisions, and derived files in `/workspace`. Do not submit source rows or private clinical notes in outputs. Report no result that was not computed.

## References

[K1] Zhang Y et al. “Integrative Analysis Uncover the Effects and Multi-Omics Features of Thigh Muscle Fat Infiltration.” Aging Cell (2026). Abstract inspected only. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/

# Episode 17 — posterior-thigh MFI and temporally separated falls reports

## Unresolved question and clinical importance

Among UK Biobank `ukb672073` participants with visit-2 thigh MRI and a classifiable visit-3 falls response, is higher bilateral posterior-thigh muscle fat infiltration (MFI) at visit 2 positively associated with a fall report for the year before visit 3 when the visits are at least 730 calendar days apart? Does that association remain after adjustment for visceral adiposity, thigh muscle distribution, prior falls and measured function, and is it sensitive to measured item-response selection among MRI/MFI-observed returnees?

Falls can cause injury, fracture, disability and loss of independence. A stable association would justify independent prospective validation of muscle-quality phenotyping; a precise null or adverse association would lower its priority. The principal advance is not that thigh MRI or falls are novel: it asks whether posterior MFI adds an association beyond muscle distribution/function after a full reported recall year has elapsed following MRI. This is a selected-returnee association, not an estimate of true-event incidence, causality, screening utility or treatment benefit.

## Evidence, hypothesis and strongest rival

The UKB thigh-MFI VTE cohort supports relevance of MFI to disease outcomes, not falls [K1]. The closest direct overlap reports a cross-sectional posterior/anterior thigh-volume association with “falls in the last year” [K2]; therefore broad thigh-MRI/falls novelty is not claimed. The myosteatosis review describes unresolved aging versus disease/disuse explanations and a need for longitudinal evidence [K3]. None establishes the proposed posterior-MFI association with a full post-MRI recall window.

**Hypothesis being tested:** in the prespecified 730-day selected-returnee population, one SD higher visit-2 bilateral posterior-thigh MFI has a positive adjusted association with classifiable visit-3 any-fall report, beyond measured VAT, muscle distribution and baseline falls/function.

**Strongest rival:** MFI is a marker of pre-existing frailty, illness, inactivity/disuse, adiposity or prior falls; those factors and reporting/return behavior may generate the association. The longer lag resolves recall-window overlap by construction only if the item’s “last year” wording and assessment dates are correct. It does not remove confounding, time-varying illness, conditioning on MRI/return, recall error or MNAR selection. Persistence after adjustment or weighting does not identify a biological mechanism. The cited review’s etiologic uncertainty is not resolvable with these data.

## Population, timing and variables

Use snapshot `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`, participant unit `eid`, identifier namespace `ukb672073`. Bind read-only ordinary source `UKB/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, source `ukb_d61ec821b81b9034`, exact path `[private-path]/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, SHA-256 `77cad853153b1fdc9b6b9c83b6fff19691681cdee3b0822210bc5c875e1db94c`, schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-fb278a0d71d3a688.json`; ordinary file, no archive member. This raw table is required because the prepared Assessment Center Parquet omits VAT field `22407-2.0`. Do not join Olink, `ukb671626`, `dta`, or other ID namespaces without a documented crosswalk.

Fields from that Assessment Center table: dates `53-2.0` and `53-3.0`; visit-2 posterior MFI `23355-2.0` (left) and `23356-2.0` (right); visit-3 falls item `2296-3.0`; prior falls `2296-2.0`; VAT `22407-2.0`; thigh fat-free muscle volumes `22403-2.0` through `22406-2.0`; age `21003-2.0`; BMI `21001-2.0`; body fat `23099-2.0`; smoking `20116-2.0`; activity `884-2.0`; walking pace `924-2.0`; grip `46-2.0` and `47-2.0`. Join sex `31-0.0` only from ordinary `UKB/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, source `ukb_ce68812c3a782e09`, exact path `[private-path]/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, SHA-256 `cd2e004a78b20a8606d70ab2cb3b32de82c44264383a34960b0cd29bc2963f0e`, schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-0f3b3a4749849a80.json`, using audited same-namespace `eid`. Use read-only `metadata.csv`, source `ukb_dd10bf7e2be6e7d0`, key `Path`, SHA-256 `9189b21c052ee3715448b1715e5700b297b7377b57278ccb747b7dfc5fa558bd`, for field definitions/units/special values, never for participant joins. Audit duplicate keys, unmatched sex joins, impossible/special values and row flow. Sources remain read-only; derived files go in the workspace.

Eligibility: ordered valid visit dates with `(visit3 - visit2) >= 730` calendar days; both visit-2 MFI sides; recognized visit-3 outcome; and all prespecified adjustment fields. Parse the UKB ISO dates without `dayfirst=True`; report missing/malformed dates and exclusions. Mean the bilateral MFI values and standardize once in the fixed primary complete-case cohort. Derive posterior/anterior distribution from posterior volumes (`22404`,`22406`) divided by anterior volumes (`22403`,`22405`), all at visit 2; report component measures and handle zero/invalid denominators by a prespecified exclusion gate. Outcome codes 1=no falls, 2/3=one or more falls, based on the previously inspected UKB coding evidence; `-3` is prefer-not-to-answer and is not a negative response. Keep other, unrecognized, special and missing values separately tabulated; never infer their meaning. Reconfirm attached codebook evidence in the execution package before classification. The item is retrospective self-report, not adjudicated events.

A bounded aggregate diagnostic on the frozen Parquet derivative `ukb_d61ec821b81b9034_parquet` (exact path `[private-path]/ukb_d61ec821b81b9034.parquet`, SHA-256 `e69705f71f6a4f263371bec081d50a7d9482291d73cde09873634b327936a841`, schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-6fc0a334db7f533b.json`) read only `eid`, dates, outcome and both MFI fields from 502,370 rows. It found 5,409 date-lag rows at >=366 days and 4,988 at >=730 days; among classifiable response plus bilateral-MFI rows, the corresponding counts were 4,929 (798 fall reports) and 4,640 (762 fall reports; codes 2/3: 563/199). Four other nonmissing outcome values were not classifiable and were excluded. These are aggregate availability counts, not the complete analytic cohort: no VAT/full-covariate, global-key, MRI-quality or sex-join audit was performed. Earlier episode scans report different date-eligible totals under other filters; do not reuse them as denominators. The 730-day threshold retains substantial preliminary event support before covariate filtering, but complete-case support remains to be computed.

## Estimands, analyses and comparisons

Primary estimand: adjusted respondent-conditional odds ratio (OR) for classifiable any-fall report (codes 2/3 versus 1) per 1-SD higher visit-2 bilateral posterior MFI among eligible complete cases with >=730 days between visits. Prespecify adjustment for age, sex, BMI/body fat, smoking, activity, walking pace, grip, prior falls, VAT and posterior/anterior thigh-volume distribution; use a fixed covariate set with explicit special-value handling. Report complete-case N/events and all exclusions before estimates.

**Simple baseline:** logistic regression with linear MFI effect and the fixed covariate set; report OR, 95% CI and two-sided p-value, plus absolute standardized predicted-risk contrast as a descriptive model-based quantity. **Substantive learned alternative:** same-row, shrinkage-penalized GAM/logistic model with a prespecified smooth for MFI and shrinkage smooths for selected continuous confounders, plus prespecified MFI-by-prior-falls and MFI-by-grip terms. It tests whether the association is nonlinear or concentrated in measured frailty/function strata—information a linear log-odds slope loses—not whether prediction improves by itself. Compare models on the same cohort using likelihood-based fit and bootstrap uncertainty for the MFI curve/contrast; control effective degrees of freedom before outcome inspection, and report calibration and sensitivity to influential observations. No post-hoc subgroup search.

Retain the parent’s measured-response sensitivity only as a separate, MAR-dependent estimand: among participants with visit-2 MRI/MFI, complete baseline predictors and a valid >=730-day visit-3 date, model classifiable-item response (codes 1/2/3 versus missing/unclassifiable) from visit-2 predictors using cross-fitting; apply stabilized inverse response weights to classifiable respondents. Report propensity calibration, overlap, weight distribution/truncation, effective sample size and balance before/after weighting, then weighted OR/CI alongside the unweighted primary estimate. This sensitivity is conditional on having a timed visit-3 date; it does not correct MRI attendance, missing visit dates, nonreturn, MNAR or event/report validity. If positivity/ESS or balance gates fail, label weighting uninterpretable rather than rescue the primary result.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive: positive primary OR with CI excluding 1, no influential-data dependence, a compatible GAM curve, and materially similar weighted estimate with adequate overlap. This supports a reproducible association in selected returnees and motivates independent validation with prospective fall surveillance; it does not establish causality, mechanism, true-event risk or clinical utility.

Adverse: precise primary estimate at/below null (CI excludes a positive association), or a positive signal that disappears under prespecified frailty/distribution adjustment or is highly sensitive to measured-response weighting with sound overlap. This lowers priority for MFI as an additional falls phenotype in this cohort; it does not prove no effect in other populations or exclude measurement error.

Inconclusive: wide intervals spanning null and a potentially useful positive association, insufficient covariate-complete event support, model instability, failed codebook/quality/positivity gates, or divergent models without clear precision. Report uncertainty and do not call an imprecise null a falsification. If the stricter cohort proves unestimable, do not revert silently to 366 days; return to the Lead for a substantive design decision.

Computationally checkable: exact filters/joins, row-flow counts, fitted models, estimates/intervals, bootstrap/calibration diagnostics, weighting overlap/ESS, and whether narrative claims match output. Requires expert review or another study: outcome-code adjudication beyond inspected codes, MRI segmentation/quality, falls-event truth and recall accuracy, residual frailty/disuse/treatment explanations, MNAR selection, transportability and clinical utility. A verifier must reject correct computation paired with unsupported causal/event-truth claims and recognize appropriately limited supportive, adverse and inconclusive interpretations; automated verification cannot establish clinical truth.

## Alternatives, compute and delivery

The simple logistic baseline is retained because its conditional OR directly tests the prespecified question. The GAM is retained for a scientifically substantive uncertainty—nonlinearity or measured frailty-stratum concentration—not a marginal predictive gain. A sequence transformer/Delphi-style disease-history model is deferred: the tested signal is a single MRI exposure with one later retrospective endpoint, not dated disease sequences; no sequence adds the missing event adjudication or resolves confounding. No GPU is justified for this tabular model; CPU fits/bootstraps suffice. A bounded Parquet scan was measured at 3.6–3.9 seconds on 4 CPUs using selected columns. Full raw CSV extraction/fitting time is unmeasured; estimate budget up to 4 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, 2 hours for one selected-column extraction plus paired logistic/GAM fits and 500 bootstrap replicates, to be verified in solver. Solver planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 256 GiB RAM, 8 GPUs and 8 hours, but this study requests no GPU. Discovery diagnostics are not a completed scientific analysis.

New scientific deliverable: newly fit the prespecified logistic and GAM outcome models and the measured-response propensity/weighted sensitivity, reporting the complete-case flow, coefficients/curve, uncertainty, model comparison, propensity and diagnostics, plus output-linked interpretation. Independent positive and negative verifier fixtures must cover correct computation with an overclaim, an adverse result, and an inconclusive result. Readiness/package checks alone do not complete the research objective.

# Hypotension duration versus nadir for early AKI in eICU

## Proposed relationship
Among adults in eICU with a qualifying ICU stay and at least one valid systolic blood-pressure measurement below 65 mmHg during the first 24 hours, greater cumulative time below 65 mmHg is associated with higher risk of new or worsening acute kidney injury during the next 48 hours, after accounting for baseline illness severity, prior vasopressor exposure, and hospital. The duration signal is expected to add reproducible information beyond the admission nadir alone.

This is an association hypothesis, not a causal claim that lowering blood pressure causes AKI or that 65 mmHg is a treatment target.

## Clinical importance and unresolved question
A single nadir may be transient or artifact-prone, whereas sustained hypotension may represent a different exposure burden. The unresolved question is whether duration and trajectory add clinically meaningful information about subsequent AKI beyond the nadir, rather than merely reflecting severity, measurement frequency, or treatment response. Resolving this could inform whether early AKI risk assessment should use duration/trajectory rather than a single minimum value.

## Evidence supporting the opening
The closest inspected work reports that duration/recurrence-based intraoperative hypotension trajectories were associated with major postoperative complications and improved prediction beyond conventional hypotension measures [K1]. A recent ICU AKI review emphasizes that AKI is heterogeneous and should be considered with urine-output trajectories, hemodynamic phenotyping, and contextual measures rather than as a single creatinine event [K2]. A methods paper warns that covariate-driven observation times in electronic health records can create spurious exposure-outcome associations if not explicitly modeled [K3]. These works motivate, but do not answer, the proposed eICU duration-versus-nadir test.

## Exact data bindings
Use the read-only eICU sources listed in datasets/eicu/README.md. The patient table is `patient` (source `baidu_downloads/eicu_mimic/eicu数据库/EICU 2.0数据/patient.csv.gz`, ordinary file), with `patientunitstayid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, `uniquepid`, `hospitalid`, `age`, `gender`, `unitadmittime24`, `unitdischargeoffset`, and `unitdischargestatus`. Join all longitudinal tables by `patientunitstayid); no cross-dataset identity matching is permitted.

Use `vitalPeriodic` (source `vitalPeriodic.csv.gz`, ordinary file), columns `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, and `systemicsystolic`; use `vitalAperiodic` (source `vitalAperiodic.csv.gz`, ordinary file), columns `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, and `noninvasivesystolic`. Derive valid systolic BP, cumulative minutes below 65 mmHg, nadir, and measurement counts in ICU time 0–24 hours. Use `lab` (source `lab.csv.gz`, ordinary file), columns `patientunitstayid`, `labresultoffset`, `labname`, `labresult`, `labmeasurenamesystem`, and `labresultrevisedoffset`, selecting the verified creatinine item(s) and defining baseline and post-exposure creatinine. Use `infusionDrug` (source `infusionDrug.csv.gz`, ordinary file), columns `patientunitstayid`, `infusionoffset`, `drugname`, `drugrate`, `infusionrate`, and `drugamount`, for prior vasopressor context after verifying drug labels. Use `hospital` (source `hospital.csv.gz`, ordinary file), joined by `hospitalid`, for hospital-held-out evaluation. The `intakeOutput` table (source `intakeOutput.csv.gz`, ordinary file; `intakeoutputoffset`, `outputtotal`, `celllabel`, `cellvaluenumeric`) is a secondary urine-output outcome only if item semantics, weight, and timing are verified.

All source files are ordinary-file archive members under the exact paths above; source rows remain read-only and derived files go under the branch workspace.

## Population, timing, exposure, and outcome
Qualifying population: adults (age >=18 at admission) in a single qualifying ICU admission with a valid ICU start time and at least one valid systolic BP <65 mmHg in the first 24 hours. Exclude records lacking the required admission identifier or with impossible/ambiguous timestamps. The primary exposure window is ICU time 0–24 hours; the primary outcome window is 24–72 hours, so the outcome is assessed after the exposure window is complete.

Define baseline as the last valid creatinine before or at ICU time 0 when available; otherwise use the first creatinine in a prespecified pre-exposure window, with missingness reported rather than silently imputed as normal. Define hypotension burden as cumulative minutes with systolic BP <65 mmHg in 0–24 hours using piecewise-linear interpolation between valid measurements, with no extrapolation beyond the first/last observed measurement. Report sensitivity analyses using no interpolation, a shorter interpolation gap, and adjustment for measurement count/observation intensity. Exclude or flag physiologically implausible values using a prespecified range and do not let a single artifact dominate the exposure.

Primary outcome: new or worsening AKI by KDIGO-compatible creatinine criteria, assessed from timestamped creatinine in 24–72 hours: creatinine increase >=0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours from baseline, or >=1.5 times baseline if the rise is documented within the outcome window. Use the earliest qualifying event and retain time to event. A secondary urine-output AKI outcome is included only if `intakeOutput` item semantics, weight, and timing are verified; otherwise report it as unavailable rather than substitute a proxy.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative
The simple baseline is a prespecified hospital-stratified logistic model using nadir systolic BP in 0–24 hours, age, sex, baseline creatinine, and available baseline severity/vasopressor context. The substantive time-aware alternative adds cumulative hypotension minutes, time below threshold in prespecified intervals, last BP before window end, and a simple recovery/trajectory feature, while retaining nadir. The alternative can reveal whether sustained exposure, recovery after the nadir, or observation density carries information that a single minimum discards. It is scientifically useful only if those features are stable and not merely proxies for measurement intensity or treatment; otherwise the baseline remains preferred.

Evaluate both models on the same rows, with a hospital-held-out split and the same outcome definition and uncertainty procedure. Report duration effect estimates and confidence intervals, calibration, and hospital-held-out discrimination as secondary descriptive outputs. Compare direction and uncertainty across hospitals. A complex sequence model is deferred because the available data cannot distinguish hypotension-mediated kidney injury from severity, treatment, and observation artifacts; revisit it only if a bounded diagnostic shows that trajectory information is materially unavailable to the simpler representation.

## Falsification and interpretation
The hypothesis is supported if duration adds reproducible information beyond nadir with a prespecified direction and uncertainty, and the result is not explained solely by observation density or a single hospital. It is adverse if duration adds no information, reverses after prespecified adjustment, or is confined to artifact-prone measurements. It is inconclusive if AKI ascertainment, timestamp validity, or sampling is too sparse to estimate the comparison reliably. Any causal interpretation, treatment threshold, or mechanism requires additional clinical adjudication, richer treatment/etiology data, and prospective or quasi-experimental evidence.

## Scientific deliverable and limitations
The actual deliverable is a newly fitted baseline and time-aware analysis with a frozen cohort, exposure/outcome timing, uncertainty, hospital-held-out evaluation, and interpretation tied to computed outputs. No full study result has been computed in discovery. Clinical adjudication of AKI, reasons for missing measurements, interface interruptions, discharge/transfer, and end-of-life treatment limitations are not assumed available. The three inspected works are abstract-only evidence here; no unavailable full text is claimed.

# Episode-3 provisional hypothesis: persistent discordant AKI recovery beyond current severity

Status: provisional research task, not a completed result. No cohort count, effect estimate, or clinical conclusion is claimed.

## Proposed relationship

Among adults with an ICU stay and a prespecified creatinine-defined AKI episode who remain observable at a fixed 48-hour landmark, persistent creatinine improvement without concurrent urine-output improvement will identify higher subsequent risk of renal deterioration or in-hospital death than concordant recovery, after adjustment for the same landmark severity, treatment state, and observation intensity.

The clinically consequential unresolved claim is incremental prognostic information: whether the ordering and persistence of discordance adds information beyond current creatinine, current urine output, and current illness state. This is not a causal claim about fluid status, renal physiology, or treatment benefit.

## Why this matters and what is unresolved

The expert seed observes that creatinine and urine output can recover discordantly and that a creatinine-only recovery label may miss persistent renal vulnerability. Existing evidence supports the measurement concern, not the proposed association: Haines et al. found that eGFR creatinine systematically overestimated measured kidney function after prolonged critical illness, while eGFR cystatin C was closer to measured GFR in 38 ventilated patients [K1]. Li et al. identify the 2012 KDIGO framework as the highest-quality AKI guidance and emphasize standardization alongside implementation and population-applicability gaps [K2]. Tang et al. used a strict 24-hour MIMIC-IV/eICU landmark with creatinine, AKI stage, urine output, and severity to predict observed CRRT initiation, but explicitly treated CRRT as clinician-driven rather than objective necessity and reported limited external calibration and incremental value [K3]. None establishes that discordant recovery predicts subsequent outcomes. The leading explanation is that discordance reflects a real persistent vulnerability; the strongest rival is that it is a proxy for current severity, diuretic/vasopressor exposure, differential urine measurement intensity, or noise in a single creatinine or urine summary. A matched current-state baseline versus a persistent trajectory analysis can distinguish these explanations in a falsifiable way, although neither can establish mechanism.

The Bayesian longitudinal demonstration is not reproduced because its genetic inputs are unavailable; the compact EHR-only trajectory alternative is a bounded adaptation, not a reproduction. # Hypotension duration versus nadir for early AKI in eICU

## Proposed relationship
Among adults in a qualifying eICU ICU stay with at least one valid systolic blood-pressure measurement below 65 mmHg during ICU time 0–24 hours, greater cumulative time below 65 mmHg is associated with higher risk of new or worsening acute kidney injury during the subsequent 24–72 hours, after accounting for baseline illness severity, prior vasopressor exposure, and hospital. The duration signal is expected to add reproducible information beyond the admission nadir alone.

This is an association hypothesis, not a causal claim that lowering blood pressure causes AKI or that 65 mmHg is a treatment target.

## Clinical importance and unresolved question
A single nadir may be transient or artifact-prone, whereas sustained hypotension may represent a different exposure burden. The unresolved question is whether duration and trajectory add clinically meaningful information about subsequent AKI beyond the nadir, rather than merely reflecting severity, measurement frequency, or treatment response. Resolving this could inform whether early AKI risk assessment should use duration/trajectory rather than a single minimum value.

## Evidence supporting the opening
A perioperative study used time-weighted MAP <65 mmHg as a reference hypotension burden and found that waveform morphology did not improve postoperative AKI prediction beyond that burden; it does not answer the eICU duration-versus-nadir question [K1]. An ICU AKI review describes AKI as heterogeneous and dynamic, with creatinine-centered diagnosis necessary but insufficient and urine-output and hemodynamic context important [K2]. An EHR methods study shows that missingness and observation processes can affect dynamic prediction and compared missing-indicator and imputation strategies [K3]. These works motivate the proposed test but do not establish it. No computed eICU effect estimate is claimed.

## Exact data bindings
Use only eICU rows and documented eICU identifiers; no cross-dataset identity matching is permitted. All source files are ordinary-file archive members under the exact read-only paths in `datasets/eicu/README.md`.

- `patient` (`patient.csv.gz`): `patientunitstayid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, `uniquepid`, `hospitalid`, `age`, `gender`, `unitadmittime24`, `unitdischargeoffset`, `unitdischargestatus`.
- `vitalPeriodic` (`vitalPeriodic.csv.gz`): `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `systemicsystolic`.
- `vitalAperiodic` (`vitalAperiodic.csv.gz`): `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `noninvasivesystolic`.
- `lab` (`lab.csv.gz`): `patientunitstayid`, `labresultoffset`, `labname`, `labresult`, `labmeasurenamesystem`, `labresultrevisedoffset`; select the verified `creatinine` item.
- `infusionDrug` (`infusionDrug.csv.gz`): `patientunitstayid`, `infusionoffset`, `drugname`, `drugrate`, `infusionrate`, `drugamount`; verify vasopressor labels before use.
- `intakeOutput` (`intakeOutput.csv.gz`): `patientunitstayid`, `intakeoutputoffset`, `outputtotal`, `celllabel`, `cellvaluenumeric`; use urine-output AKI only if item semantics, weight, and timing are verified.
- `hospital` (`hospital.csv.gz`): `hospitalid`, `numbedscategory`, `teachingstatus`, `region`; use for hospital-held-out evaluation.

Join longitudinal tables by `patientunitstayid`; join hospital context by `hospitalid`. Source rows remain read-only; derived cohort, exposure, outcome, and analysis files go under the branch workspace. Direct source-header inspection confirmed the listed headers. A full source dictionary scan confirmed 1,277,760 `creatinine` lab rows, common norepinephrine/vasopressin/phenylephrine/epinephrine infusion labels, and urine/weight labels in `intakeOutput`; this establishes availability, not clinical validity.

## Population, timing, exposure, and outcome
Qualifying population: adults (`age >=18` at admission) in a single qualifying ICU admission with a valid ICU start time and at least one valid systolic BP <65 mmHg in the first 24 hours. Exclude records lacking the required admission identifier or with impossible/ambiguous timestamps.

Primary exposure window: ICU time 0–24 hours. Derive valid systolic BP from both vital tables, cumulative minutes below 65 mmHg, nadir, and measurement counts. Use piecewise-linear interpolation between valid measurements, with no extrapolation beyond the first/last observed measurement. Flag or exclude physiologically implausible values using a prespecified range. Sensitivity analyses use no interpolation, a shorter interpolation gap, and adjustment for measurement count/observation intensity.

Primary outcome window: 24–72 hours, so the outcome is assessed after the exposure window is complete. Define baseline as the last valid creatinine before or at ICU time 0 when available; otherwise use the first creatinine in a prespecified pre-exposure window, with missingness reported rather than silently imputed as normal. Primary outcome is new or worsening AKI by KDIGO-compatible creatinine criteria: creatinine increase >=0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours from baseline, or >=1.5 times baseline if the rise is documented within the outcome window. Use the earliest qualifying event and retain time to event. Secondary urine-output AKI is included only if `intakeOutput` item semantics, weight, and timing are verified; otherwise report it as unavailable rather than substitute a proxy.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative
The simple baseline is a prespecified hospital-stratified logistic model using nadir systolic BP in 0–24 hours, age, sex, baseline creatinine, and available baseline severity/vasopressor context. The substantive time-aware alternative adds cumulative hypotension minutes, time below threshold in prespecified intervals, last BP before window end, and a simple recovery/trajectory feature, while retaining nadir. The alternative can reveal whether sustained exposure, recovery after the nadir, or observation density carries information that a single minimum discards. It is scientifically useful only if those features are stable and not merely proxies for measurement intensity or treatment; otherwise the baseline remains preferred.

Evaluate both models on the same rows, with a hospital-held-out split and the same outcome definition and uncertainty procedure. Report duration effect estimates and confidence intervals, calibration, and hospital-held-out discrimination as secondary descriptive outputs. Compare direction and uncertainty across hospitals. A complex sequence model is deferred because the available data cannot distinguish hypotension-mediated kidney injury from severity, treatment, and observation artifacts; revisit it only if a bounded diagnostic shows that trajectory information is materially unavailable to the simpler representation.

## Falsification and interpretation
The hypothesis is supported if duration adds reproducible information beyond nadir with a prespecified direction and uncertainty, and the result is not explained solely by observation density or a single hospital. It is adverse if duration adds no information, reverses after prespecified adjustment, or is confined to artifact-prone measurements. It is inconclusive if AKI ascertainment, timestamp validity, or sampling is too sparse to estimate the comparison reliably. Any causal interpretation, treatment threshold, or mechanism requires additional clinical adjudication, richer treatment/etiology data, and prospective or quasi-experimental evidence.

## Scientific deliverable and limitations
The actual deliverable is a newly fitted baseline and time-aware analysis with a frozen cohort, exposure/outcome timing, uncertainty, hospital-held-out evaluation, and interpretation tied to computed outputs. No full study result has been computed in discovery. Clinical adjudication of AKI, reasons for missing measurements, interface interruptions, discharge/transfer, and end-of-life treatment limitations are not assumed available. The attached works were inspected through returned abstract/article excerpts and are labeled abstract-only; no unavailable full text is claimed.

# Episode 7 provisional hypothesis: persistent discordant AKI recovery beyond current severity and observation intensity

Status: provisional successor to candidate-adbf70880eec2e5dcf215dec; no cohort count, effect estimate, or clinical conclusion is claimed.

## Proposed relationship

Among adults with an ICU stay and a prespecified creatinine-defined AKI episode who survive to a fixed 48-hour landmark, persistent creatinine improvement without concurrent urine-output improvement will identify higher subsequent renal deterioration or in-hospital death than concordant recovery, after adjustment for the same landmark severity, treatment state, and observation intensity. The unresolved claim is incremental prognostic information, not a mechanism, causal treatment effect, or proof of true renal recovery.

## Evidence boundary and opening

The inspected evidence supports a measurement concern: creatinine-based eGFR overestimated measured kidney function in a small critical-illness cohort [K1], while a systematic review identifies the 2012 KDIGO framework as standardizing AKI diagnosis using creatinine and urine output but notes implementation and population-applicability gaps [K2]. A strict-landmark MIMIC-IV/eICU study predicted observed CRRT initiation using creatinine, AKI stage, urine output, and severity, but explicitly treated CRRT as clinician-driven rather than objective renal necessity [K3]. Those sources do not establish prevalence, an outcome association, or that discordance is biologically protective or harmful. The substantive rival is that the apparent signal is current severity, illness trajectory, treatment intensity, or documentation/measurement intensity. A persistent pre-landmark trajectory comparison can distinguish ordered discordance from a noisy cross-sectional mismatch; it cannot establish mechanism without measured GFR, cystatin C, fluid adjudication, or RRT indication.

# Timing-anchored eICU hypotension-duration hypothesis

## Proposed relationship

Among adults in a qualifying eICU ICU admission with at least one valid systolic blood-pressure measurement below 65 mmHg during ICU time 0–24 hours, greater cumulative time below 65 mmHg is associated with higher risk of a new or worsening creatinine-defined AKI event during the subsequent 24–72 hours, after accounting for baseline illness severity, prior vasopressor exposure, and hospital. Cumulative duration is expected to add reproducible information beyond the admission nadir alone.

This is an association hypothesis, not a causal claim that lowering blood pressure causes AKI or that 65 mmHg is a treatment target.

## Evidence and unresolved question

The inspected evidence motivates but does not establish this eICU question. [K1] reports that, in a perioperative cohort, arterial waveform morphology did not improve postoperative AKI prediction beyond a model containing time-weighted MAP below 65 mmHg and baseline covariates; it does not answer whether systolic-BP duration adds information beyond nadir in ICU admissions. [K2] describes ICU AKI as heterogeneous and dynamic, with creatinine-centered diagnosis necessary but insufficient and urine output nonspecific without clinical context. [K3] compares missing-data handling in dynamic EHR prediction and cautions that missingness patterns can affect performance and transportability. None validates the local eICU fields or the proposed effect.

The unresolved claim is whether duration is a reproducible incremental signal after the timing and ascertainment constraints below. No computed eICU effect estimate is claimed.

## Exact data bindings

Use only eICU rows and documented eICU identifiers; no cross-dataset identity matching. Source files are read-only:

- `patient.csv.gz`: `patientunitstayid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, `uniquepid`, `hospitalid`, `age`, `gender`, `unitadmittime24`, `unitdischargeoffset`, `unitdischargestatus`.
- `vitalPeriodic.csv.gz`: `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `systemicsystolic`.
- `vitalAperiodic.csv.gz`: `patientunitstayid`, `observationoffset`, `noninvasivesystolic`.
- `lab.csv.gz`: `patientunitstayid`, `labresultoffset`, `labresultrevisedoffset`, `labname`, `labresult`, `labmeasurenamesystem`; select the verified creatinine item.
- `infusionDrug.csv.gz`: `patientunitstayid`, `infusionoffset`, `drugname`, `drugrate`, `infusionrate`, `drugamount`; verify vasopressor labels before use.
- `intakeOutput.csv.gz`: `patientunitstayid`, `intakeoutputoffset`, `intakeoutputentryoffset`, `outputtotal`, `celllabel`, `cellvaluenumeric`, `cellvaluetext`; use urine-output AKI only after semantic and timing validation.
- `hospital.csv.gz`: `hospitalid`, `numbedscategory`, `teachingstatus`, `region`.

Join longitudinal tables by `patientunitstayid`; join hospital context by `hospitalid`. Derived cohort, exposure, outcome, and analysis files belong in this branch.

## Population, exposure, outcome, and analysis

Qualifying population: adults (`age >=18`) in a single qualifying ICU admission with valid ICU start time and at least one valid systolic BP <65 mmHg in ICU time 0–24 hours. Exclude records lacking the required admission identifier or with impossible/ambiguous timestamps.

Exposure: derive valid systolic BP from both vital tables, cumulative minutes below 65 mmHg, nadir, and measurement counts in 0–24 hours. Use piecewise-linear interpolation between valid measurements, no extrapolation beyond first/last observed measurement, and prespecified physiologic-range filtering. Sensitivity analyses use no interpolation, shorter interpolation gaps, and measurement-count/observation-intensity adjustment.

Primary outcome: a creatinine-defined event in 24–72 hours. Define baseline as the last valid creatinine at or before ICU time 0 when available; if unavailable, use the first valid creatinine in a prespecified pre-exposure window and report missingness rather than imputing normal. Define the event as the earliest creatinine increase >=0.3 mg/dL from that baseline within 48 hours, or >=1.5 times baseline if the rise is documented within the outcome window, retaining time to event. Do not use a post-exposure creatinine as baseline. If the required pre-exposure baseline or outcome-window measurements are absent, classify the endpoint as unavailable/indeterminate rather than silently treating it as negative.

Secondary urine-output endpoint: retain only after a bounded semantic check of `intakeOutput` labels, numeric/text values, entry versus event offset, duplicate/cumulative behavior, and weight/availability. If semantics cannot be established, report urine-output AKI as unavailable rather than substitute a proxy.

The simple baseline is a prespecified hospital-stratified logistic model using nadir systolic BP in 0–24 hours, age, sex, baseline creatinine, and available baseline severity/vasopressor context. The substantive time-aware alternative adds cumulative hypotension minutes, time below threshold in prespecified intervals, last BP before window end, and a simple recovery/trajectory feature while retaining nadir. Evaluate both models on the same rows with a hospital-held-out split and the same outcome definition and uncertainty procedure. Report duration effect estimates and confidence intervals, calibration, and hospital-held-out discrimination as secondary descriptive outputs. A complex sequence model is deferred because the available data cannot distinguish hypotension-mediated kidney injury from severity, treatment, and observation artifacts; revisit only if a bounded diagnostic shows trajectory information is materially unavailable to the simpler representation.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive: duration adds reproducible information beyond nadir with a prespecified direction and uncertainty, and the result is not explained solely by observation density or a single hospital. Adverse: duration adds no information, reverses after prespecified adjustment, or is confined to artifact-prone measurements. Inconclusive: creatinine ascertainment, timestamp validity, or sampling is too sparse to estimate the comparison reliably; an imprecise null is not decisive refutation. Any causal interpretation, treatment threshold, or mechanism requires additional clinical adjudication, richer treatment/etiology data, and prospective or quasi-experimental evidence.

## Deliverable and limitations

The deliverable is a newly fitted baseline and time-aware analysis with a frozen cohort, explicit pre-exposure baseline and post-exposure event timing, uncertainty, hospital-held-out evaluation, and interpretation tied to computed outputs. No full study result has been computed in discovery. Clinical adjudication of AKI, reasons for missing measurements, interface interruptions, discharge/transfer, and end-of-life treatment limitations are not assumed available. The attached works are inspected as abstract-only evidence; no unavailable full text is claimed.
